attribution: Yu.E. Berezkin, E.N. Duvakin. The Electronic Analytic Catalogue of Folklore and Mythology Motifs

A1.definition_eng: Another sun, usually less benevolent and/or powerful, existed before the present one

A10.definition_eng: The sun gets his bright eye or eyes from an animal

A11A.name_eng: Eyes of the Sun and the Moon: coolness and night
A11A.definition_eng: Visible sun and/or moon are the Sun's and/or the Moon's eyes. If these eyes were not injured, light and heat would be more intense

A11B.definition_eng: The Sun or the Moon is one-eyed (usually another eye was knocked or sucked out but sometimes this defect is not explained

A11C.name_eng: The Sun, the Moon and monster’s eyes
A11C.definition_eng: The Sun and the Moon kill a monster whose eyes are unequally bright. The Moon takes the brighter eye but gives it back to the Sun

A12.definition_eng: Some creature or creatures regularly (sunrise and sunset, summer and winter, lunar phases) or irregularly (solar and lunar eclipses, eschatological events) attack the luminaries or shade their light

A12A.definition_eng: During an eclipse or at other circumstances the Sun or the Moon are attacked by a predator animal (a bear, a feline, a canine, a racoon)

A12B.definition_eng: During an eclipse or at the sunset the Sun or the Moon are attacked by a frog or toad

A12C.name_eng: Eclipses: reptile or fish produces eclipses
A12C.definition_eng: During an eclipse or at the sunset the Sun or the Moon are attacked by a reptile (a snake, a lizard, a dragon, a crocodile) or a fish

A12C1.definition_eng: A lizard produces eclipses (alone or with other beings)

A12D.definition_eng: A bird or birds attack or shade the Sun or the Moon during an eclipse or at the sunrise and sunset

A12E.name_eng: Spider is enemy of celestial bodies
A12E.definition_eng: A spider attackes the Sun or the Moon (usually produces lunar eclipses)

A12F.definition_eng: A creditor comes from time to time to the Sun or the Moon to claim back his money producing eclipses

A12G.name_eng: Revenge on the Moon for his denunciation
A12G.definition_eng: Person tries to eclipse the Moon because the Moon has reported on the person’s crime

A13A.definition_eng: A raven steals (hides) the Sun or tries to do it

A13A1.definition_eng: Raven (crow) gets the hidden or stolen Sun (daylight)

A13B.definition_eng: During an eclipse or during the first night ants shade or shaded the Sun

A14.name_eng: Eclipses: relations between the Sun and the Moon
A14.definition_eng: Coming together of the Sun and the Moon is the reason of their eclipses

A14A.name_eng: The conflict between the Sun and the Moon
A14A.definition_eng: The Sun and the Moon are or were enemies, either permanently or in particular situations

A15.definition_eng: The lunar (and solar) eclipse or spots on the lunar disc are expained by the fact that the Sun or the Moon came to a wrong path or that their paths crossed

A16.definition_eng: Every night the Sun passes by creatures or objects which try to destroy them

A17.name_eng: The Sun’s relax at the midday
A17.definition_eng: After passing half of the its way across the sky (in the day time) or in the underworld (in the night time), the Sun stops to have a rest

A18.definition_eng: During the day and/or the night (in the underworld, beyond the horizon etc.) the Sun and/or the Moon regularly travel in a boat.

A19A.name_eng: By horse in the morning, by ox in the evening
A19A.definition_eng: During its everyday travel across the sky, the Sun changes its draught animals (usually in the morning the Sun rides a slow animal and in the evening a quick one)

A19B.name_eng: By snail in summer, by bird in winter
A19B.definition_eng: For its sky voyage, the Sun chooses draught animals according to the season, riding a slow one in the summer time and a quick one in the winter time. Or a young man carries the Sun in the winter time and the old man in the summer time

A19C.definition_eng: The Sun is associated with a horseman or rides in a cart driven by horses (equids)

A19C1.definition_eng: The sun or the moon moves in a cart or sledge

A19D.name_eng: One carries the Sun, another the Moon
A19D.definition_eng: The sun or the moon are carried by two different persons or creatures

A19E.name_eng: The summer sun and the winter sun
A19E.definition_eng: Sun of the summer and sun of the winter are two different persons

A1A.name_eng: Parrot was the sun before the Sun
A1A.definition_eng: A big bird with bright feathers (parrot, tucan) had been the source of light before the real Sun appeared

A2.definition_eng: In a certain time in the past three or more suns were on the sky simultaneously

A20.name_eng: Childhood and youth of the Sun and Moon
A20.definition_eng: The Sun and the Moon (rare: the Sun and a star, the Moon and a star) are two siblings who live on earth and then ascend to the sky being still young persons

A21.name_eng: Luminaries are objects fixed in the sky
A21.definition_eng: The sun and/or the moon are inanimate objects thrown up to the sky or fixed in the sky

A21A.definition_eng: The Moon is an object which its owners released by chance or which was stolen from them and ultimately ascended to the sky

A22.name_eng: To the sky from a bonfire
A22.definition_eng: After getting into the fire or boiling water, one or two persons ascend to the sky and turn into the Sun and/or Moon

A22A.name_eng: The hot Sun and its cold companion
A22A.definition_eng: After two persons burn up, one turns into the present Sun and another into a less important sky object

A22B.definition_eng: Person who becomes the Sun burned up in a hot fire while his companion burned up in the less hot fire or threw himself into the ashes. He (she) turns into the Moon or a star which gives no warmth

A22C.definition_eng: To make the Sun rise above the horizon, to send him to the right distance from the earth, to make him move across the sky, etc. a person has to be sacrificed

A22D.name_eng: The burned up persons turn into constellation
A22D.definition_eng: The burned up persons turn into a constellation or into the dark spot on the Milky Way

A23.name_eng: Elections of the Sun to be
A23.definition_eng: The primeval ancestors come together to choose the best candidate to become the Sun and/or to send the Sun to the sky or to see how the Sun rises to the sky for the first time

A23A.name_eng: Who will see the Sun first?
A23A.definition_eng: Two persons or animals argue about who of them will be the first to see the rising sun. One who seemed to have less chances wins

A23B.name_eng: First beams on the tree tops
A23B.definition_eng: Two persons or animals argue who will see the rising sun first. One who got to see not the sun itself but its reflection or the first beams on trees or mountain tops wins

A23C.definition_eng: Birds argue who of them will fly higher. One who seemed to have less chances wins (he hides himself in feathers of a strong bird using it as a vehicle)

A23D.name_eng: Who will be the first in the calendar cycle?
A23D.definition_eng: Animals argue which of them should stand at the beginning of the calendar cycle (twelve months or years). Mouse obtains the first place

A24.definition_eng: In the beginning it is dark. When the Sun first appears on the sky, primeval beings or part of them perish or turn into animals, spirits, stones

A24A.name_eng: The first day or night: transformed into spirits
A24A.definition_eng: At the moment when the first day or the first night come, (some) people turn into supernatural beings

A25.definition_eng: When people see light of day for the first time, they are prohibited to look at it immediately. Those who break this taboo are ruined

A26.definition_eng: A bird incorporates the Sun or the day light. It can be caught, let free, killed

A27.name_eng: Crowns of the Sun and Moon
A27.definition_eng: Light and/or heat of the Sun and/or Moon originate from their crowns, necklaces or clothes (of feathers, of animal teeth)

A28.name_eng: The smart Sun and the unwise Moon
A28.definition_eng: The Sun and the Moon are men. The unwise Moon tries to repeat dangerous tricks of the Sun but fails to do it successfully

A29.name_eng: The Sun and a demon compete for the hero
A29.definition_eng: Two persons one of which is connected with the upper and another with the lower or middle world, both are eager to possess another person and pull him or her to his or her side. One or both rivals are female. Person connected with the upper world and/or the object of the competition are luminaries – the Sun, the Moon, or Venus

A29A.name_eng: Torn in half by two women
A29A.definition_eng: The sky wife and the woman from the earth (the demon) each pull the man to her side, As a result he turns into the night luminary

A29B.definition_eng: Person, connected with the upper world and another person connected with the lower world or the earth both are eager to possess a hero or heroin who is associated with the Moon

A2A.name_eng: The sun is a source of distructive heat
A2A.definition_eng: The world was or will be (almost) burned when several suns had (will) appear(ed) simultaneously; or the only sun was too hot (or bright)

A2A1.name_eng: The Moon was as bright as the Sun
A2A1.definition_eng: Initially, the Moon was as bright and hot as the Sun

A2B.definition_eng: Other suns or moons besides present ones had been in the sky and were later annihilated

A2B1.definition_eng: Two or more suns shine in the sky. When the extra suns had been annihilated, there was a risk of the last one being destroyed too

A2C.name_eng: Extra suns are children of the present one
A2C.definition_eng: Extra suns who almost burned or could burn the world are children of the present one

A2C1.name_eng: The Sun abandons his marriage plans
A2C1.definition_eng: The Sun plans to have children. One of the animals sais that if the Sun (marries and) has children, the earth will burn. The Sun has to abandon his plans.

A2C2.definition_eng: The catastrophy that is dangerous for the earth is related to the simultaneous appearance of not only several suns but also several moons

A2D.definition_eng: Different suns illuminate different worlds or will appear successively in the future

A2E.name_eng: The Sun and the Moon are cut off heads
A2E.definition_eng: The Sun and/or the Moon are cut off heads of anthropomorphic beings

A3.definition_eng: The Moon is female or bisexual, the Sun is male

A30.definition_eng: Moon descends to earth to eat children, corpses or bones of the dead

A31.definition_eng: As a result of some intimate contacts and/or love affair, the Moon acquires its present appearance (often, the stains on his face) and/or ascends to the sky

A31A.definition_eng: When a woman gets know that her husband or lover did something against accepted rules of behavior, she cuts off her breast and shows it to him

A32.definition_eng: A figure or an imprint of some being or object are seen in the Moon. (For statistical analysis motifs A32A – A32J are also included into A32)

A32A.definition_eng: Rabbit or hare are seen in the moon

A32B.definition_eng: Frog or toad are seen in the moon or the Moon is associated with them

A32B1.name_eng: Jumps on the face of the Moon
A32B1.definition_eng: A woman sits (jumps) on the face (back) of the Moon man and now is seen as the shadows on the lunar disc

A32C.name_eng: A man and a dog in the Moon
A32C.definition_eng: A human being and a dog together are seen in the moon

A32C1.definition_eng: A predator animal (fox, wolf, dog, coyote, jaguar, lion) or its imprint is seen in the Moon

A32D.definition_eng: Human being or imprint of human being is seen in the moon

A32D1.name_eng: Cain and Abel in the Moon
A32D1.definition_eng: Cain and Abel are related to the Moon, usually are seen (both or Cain only) in the shadows of the lunar disc

A32D2.name_eng: Person with pitchfolk in the Moon
A32D2.definition_eng: Person with a pitchfolk in hands is seen in the shadows of the lunar disc

A32DD.definition_eng: Person who carries a bundle of brushwood or firewood is seen in the moon.

A32E.name_eng: Person with an object in hands
A32E.definition_eng: Person who holds some object in his or her hands is seen in the moon (rare: in the sun)

A32F.definition_eng: Person who went to fetch water and/or holds in hands a container for liquid is seen in the moon

A32G.definition_eng: Person who had been carried up to the moon took hold of a bush or a small tree and is seen now on the lunar disc together with this bush

A32H.definition_eng: A tree or bush is seen in the moon

A32I.definition_eng: A shepherd or herdsman (alone or with a girl, with his herd, dogs) is seen in the moon

A32J.definition_eng: A shaman with his drum ascends to the moon and remains there, his figure is seen in the moon

A32K.name_eng: First to the Sun, then to the Moob
A32K.definition_eng: Person seen in the Moon initially had to get to the Sun or the Sun and the Moon argue who of them should get the person

A32L.definition_eng: The figure of a person or creature is visible in the Sun or it is told that a person got to the Sun and remained there

A32M.definition_eng: The Moon is called the “Gypsy Sun”

A33.definition_eng: The Sun has appearance of a big terrestrial mammal (bull, ram, antilope, pig, rhinocero, etc.) or rides such an animal

A34.definition_eng: Jackal, coyote, or fox are connected with the Moon (usually with the origin of spots on the lunar disc)

A35.definition_eng: Dark spots on the lunar disc are dirt, blood, paint, traces of beating, burning, scratching, etc. on the Moon person's body or face (Kiliwa: spots on the Sun) and do not form any particular figure

A35A.definition_eng: Spots on the lunar disc are dirt thrown into the Moon's face by his/her sister/brother or mother

A35B.name_eng: To smear the Moon with pitch
A35B.definition_eng: To make the Moon less bright, some person tried to smear it with pitch

A35B1.definition_eng: A criminal attempts to make the Moon’s light as weak as possible because it irritates him or prevents him to make evil

A35C.name_eng: Scars and wounds on the Moon’s face
A35C.definition_eng: Dark spots on the Moon are scars and wounds on her face

A36.definition_eng: The Moon, unlike people, revives or rejuvenates every month; or those who live in the Moon are immortal; or the Moon makes decision if people should die forever or regularly revive

A36A.definition_eng: The Sun, unlike people, is immortal; is responsible for the mortal nature of humans

A37.name_eng: The Sun is attacked with weapons
A37.definition_eng: Person intentionally and with special equipment (usually shooting arrows) attacks the Sun (or several suns if they were many)

A37A.definition_eng: Small animal (marmot, rabbit, mole, toad, frog) or person who turns into this animal tried to hit the Sun with arrows and since then has been hiding from the Sun in underground holes or in the water

A37B.definition_eng: A small animal (marmot, rabbit, mole, toad, frog) or person who turns into this animal tried to hit with his arrow an aim in the sky (the Sun or a bird) but remains without thumb as a result

A37C.definition_eng: Person is going to hit the celestial body or deity but his arrow hits an obstacle that screens his aim for a moment

A38.definition_eng: Person prepares a snare, loop, noose, etc. to catch the Sun and/or the Sun is caught in a snare, tied by a rope, etc.

A38A.definition_eng: The Sun is caught into snare made of the pubic hair of hero's female relative

A38B.definition_eng: After the Sun is caught into snare only mouse, shrew or other small animal is able to cut it open

A38C.definition_eng: A boy or a girl has a cloak. The Sun spoils it or gives instead a better one

A38D.definition_eng: Because the Sun does damage to a person or animal (spoils, burns his cloak, skin, etc.), the person or animal kills him or catches him in a snare

A39.definition_eng: Suns are born and die every day

A39A.definition_eng: Each of calender units (usually the months) that make the year is a separate object or person

A4.definition_eng: The Sun is female, the Moon is male or (more rare) also female

A40.name_eng: The Sun or Moon marry toad
A40.definition_eng: Frog or Toad is a wife of the Sun or Moon

A41.definition_eng: Two persons have children (younger siblings, mothers). One of them proposes to another that they should kill (eat, bake, etc.) their children (mothers, etc.) but hides his or her own. The opponent actually kills his or her own kin. One of the persons or/and the only survived child is the Sun

A42.name_eng: Phaethon: false Sun fails to fulfill his duty
A42.definition_eng: Person comes to the sun, attempts to fulfill the sun's duty but intentionally or because of a lack of skill does it wrong and the earth suffers from heat etc. (Cf. Earth burned because the bearer of the sun came too low, Boas 2002: 664)

A42A.name_eng: The Sun’s imitator falls to earth (Phaethon)
A42A.definition_eng: When a person arrives to the sky his attempt to fulfill the sun's duty fails and he falls to earth (is thrown down to earth)

A43.name_eng: Person with a shoe on one foot
A43.definition_eng: While being transformed into a bird or ascending to the sky a person was in a hurry and put a footwear only on one foot, or somebody attempted to seize him grasping his foot. Now the corresponding bird or a sky-person is believed to have different feet

A43A.definition_eng: The Moon-person runs out of the lodge and flies up. He forgets to put his footwear on one foot, or somebody attempts to seize him grasping his foot or cuts the foot off. Now the Moon-person lacks one foot or footwear on one of his (or her) feet

A44.definition_eng: A person pursued by an enemy or tyrannized by others asks the Moon to take her or him to the sky. The request is granted and the person is now seen in the Moon

A45.definition_eng: Person who teases or insults the Moon is punished

A46.name_eng: The Sun and Moon emerge from the eyes of a being
A46.definition_eng: The Sun and Moon (Rig-Veda: the Sun only) appear from eyes of an anthropomorphic being

A46A.name_eng: The Sun and Moon are eyes of a deity
A46A.definition_eng: The Sun and Moon (Rig-Veda: the Sun only) are associated with eyes of an anthropomorphic being (the motif of their emergence, creation from his eyes is not obligatory)

A47.name_eng: The Sun is born from an egg
A47.definition_eng: The Sun is born or created from an egg

A4A.definition_eng: Modest Sun-woman dazzles (usually pricks with needles, i.e. the sun rays) eyes of those who look at her

A4B.name_eng: The Sun is afraid of the night
A4B.definition_eng: Being afraid of the night, the Sun decided to travel across the sky only at the day time

A4E.definition_eng: An anthropomorphic person associated with the thunder and rain rides on the clouds (uses them as a vehicle)

A5.name_eng: The Sun and the Moon are males
A5.definition_eng: The Moon is male, the Sun is also male or (rare) has no sex

A5A.name_eng: Elder brother is the boy, younger one is originally a doll
A5A.definition_eng: A boy is lost. A doll to replace him is made. It revives and becomes younger brother of the original boy. Borhters meet each other and act together

A6.name_eng: The Sun and the Moon are females
A6.definition_eng: Both the Sun and the Moon are considered to be females (incl. cases when the gender is not directly specified but both emerge from parts of the body of a female person)

A7.definition_eng: The Sun and the Moon are two persons one of which is pursuing another in the sky or pursued him or her when they were rising to the sky from the earth

A7A.name_eng: Torches in hands of celestial bodies
A7A.definition_eng: Light of the Sun (Moon, Venus) is a torch in hands of the celestial body

A8.name_eng: The Sun, the Moon and the Star are three siblings
A8.definition_eng: The Sun, the Moon and the star (stars) are three sisters or three brothers

A8A.name_eng: The Sun, the Moon and the star: released by the hero

A8B.name_eng: The Sun in the land of the dead
A8B.definition_eng: When the Sun descends below the horizon, it shines to the anthropomorphic denizens of the netherworld (the dead, dwarfs, etc.)

A9.definition_eng: Female moon does not permit her husband or son to destroy people

B1.definition_eng: Two male anthropomorphic creators compete in producing things. One of them is or becomes master of the underworld and/or spirits while another is associated with humans

B10.definition_eng: Person drinks a lake or all the water in the world or all the water is originally inside person's belly. When a hole is made in it, the water pours out

B100.definition_eng: Formerly or in a certain country the sleep was not known; certain person possesses sleep, is its incarnation or teaches to sleep; the sleep is a particular substance

B101.definition_eng: Angry against the birch, person beats or cuts it, whence scratches and slashes on its bark

B102.definition_eng: Clouds are formed from smoke that ascends from the earth

B102A.definition_eng: Clouds are associated with cattle (and rain is the milk of the cloud coes)

B103.definition_eng: Person (a devil or a bear) thinks that because the Cornus mas tree (European cornel, male cornel) blossoms before all other fruit trees do, it also brings its fruits early. The cornel fruits become ripe very late, so the person is disappointed and gets no fruits

B104.definition_eng: When a guest comes, a host hides from him a cooked chicken. When the host is going to eat it himself, he finds the chicken transformed into the tortoise (origin of tortoises) or a toad

B104A.name_eng: Meat springs as toad on the face of an ungrateful son
B104A.definition_eng: A couple (son) intends to eat a roasted chicken (meat). When the man’s old father passes by unexpectedly, they hide the chicken in order not to share it with him. When the old man continues on his way and they replace the chicken on the table, it has turned into a toad (snake) and humps onto the son’s face where it stays until his death

B104B.name_eng: Woman is changed in a woodpecker
B104B.definition_eng: A woman does not want to share bread with God who came to her in guise of a poor man and is transformed into a woodpecker

B105.definition_eng: Father- or mother-in-law gets to see his or her daughter-in-law in an improper situation (combing her hair, taking a bath, etc.). She is ashamed in turns into a bird (usually a hoopoe) or a turtle

B106.definition_eng: When the sky cock cries (or the underground cocks cry), all the cocks on earth cry after him, not before

B107.definition_eng: During a (world) fire oyster was burned, nor now oyster shells are black

B108.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic person broken into small particles turns into the snow that shines under the sun

B109.definition_eng: Person turns into a bear (origin of bears)

B109A.definition_eng: Initially the bear(-person) lived in the sky and then descended to the earth (and turned into the bear)

B110.name_eng: If by back, the ravines, if by head the red flowers
B110.definition_eng: Person dragged on the ground disintegrates or touches the ground with different parts of her or his body producing particular features of landscape, different plants, etc.

B110A.name_eng: Falling person turns into snow and wind
B110A.definition_eng: Being dragged on the ground or falling from the sky, peprson turns into atmospheric phenomena

B111.definition_eng: Bees or wasps fly out of the corpse the body of a big animal (lion, bull). Usually the episode explains the origine of bees

B112.name_eng: Bird helps to return property and is decorated
B112.definition_eng: Person suggests to do some work (usually to ferry people's property across river) but carries away the property that he was entrusted to control, A woodpecker or tit helps to return the property. The owner decorates the bird, thence the color of its plumage

B113.name_eng: Bottoms of women and knees of men
B113.definition_eng: Because of certain events of the time of creation, the women’s bottom and the men’s knees (or vice versa) are cold

B114.definition_eng: Old man or old woman turns into anteater (origin of anteaters)

B115.definition_eng: Coniferous or some other trees or shrubs (subshrubs) became evergree when the life elixir was spilled on them by chance

B115A.definition_eng: Person (St. Peter), angry at carpents, wants another (Christ) to make wood (trees) with iron knots (branches, nails) but the latter makes the branches only of hard wood

B116.definition_eng: An animal or a person eats up the first book (writing, important document). (In some of European traditions the eating up of the book is not directly described but follows from the context)

B116A.definition_eng: Person or animal swallows sacred book or its remains. During rituals this knowledge is actualized in the oral text, in sounds of musical instruments made of the animal body parts or in animal body parts used for divination

B116B.definition_eng: Becasue sacred book gets wet or sinks when people were crossing a river, it is lost or the text becomes unreadable. Or it is destroyed when people try to dry it or when they go to bath and let it lie on a shore

B116C.definition_eng: In the past a particular groups of people possessed scripture and knowledge that were later lost or the people missed opportunity to obtain them

B116D.name_eng: The “book” as a part of the stomach
B116D.definition_eng: A special part of the ruminants’ stomach is named “the book”

B117.definition_eng: The animals (usually dogs) got a certificate which was lost because of the cat (is swallowed by the cat, burned, eaten by mice). Since them dogs and cats are enemies, usually also cats and mice

B118.name_eng: One who remained on earth turns into the owl
B118.definition_eng: Person who was unable to ascend to the sky or had returned from the sky to the earth turned into the owl

B118A.name_eng: The owl was wife of the Moon
B118A.definition_eng: Wife of the Moon turned into the owl

B119.name_eng: Husband of magic wife turns into the cock
B119.definition_eng: Mortal man tries to get back his magic wife but ultimately turns into a cock (explanation of the appearance of the cock or the reason why he cries)

B11A.definition_eng: Mammoth described as an underground fish-related creature moves across the earth while it is still wet creating the present landscape

B11B.definition_eng: In the beginning of times or during the flood, mammoth had drowned or sank under the ground. Since then, he is absent on the earth

B12.definition_eng: The river bed follows the way of a snake, fish, dragon or crab; pieces of the snake’s body turn into rivers; a river is a snake

B120.definition_eng: There are creatures who hibernate having frozen snot under their noses

B121.name_eng: A bird is eager to fill up the sea
B121.definition_eng: There are creatures who hibernate having frozen snot under their noses

B122.definition_eng: Birds (usually storks or geese) carry small children to the other world or bring them from there

B123.name_eng: The flies instead of nails on Christ’s heart
B123.definition_eng: Flies look like nails and prevent more nails being driven in

B124.definition_eng: Since a piece of flesh was torn off from somebody’s foot, there is a depression beteen toes and heel

B125.definition_eng: During the time of creation particular species of animals (rare: plants) exchanged certain organs or traits or one animal borrowed an organ from another one but never brought it back. Thence the characteristics of these animals now. In rare cases the back exchange and restoring of the initial situation or the passing of certain organ from one animal to another without compensation are described

B125A.definition_eng: The nightingale (more rare somebody else) borrows the blindwoms’s eye and does not return them, the blindworm becomes blind

B125B.name_eng: The party and the borrowed organ
B125B.definition_eng: Going to the feast, party, etc., animal person borrows from another one a part of the body that must make him more attractive

B125C.definition_eng: The beaver had tail which the muskrat has now and vice versa

B13.definition_eng: Person or creature makes (usually intentionally) rivers, digging or tracing them, pouring water while running, and the like

B13A.definition_eng: A stream of water (with a monster in it) pursues person who tries to escape from it

B14.name_eng: To regulate the river current, person creates rapids and falls

B14A.definition_eng: Rain (dew) is tears of certain person who is weaping above the earth

B14B.name_eng: Tears turn info bodies of water
B14B.definition_eng: Person’s tears fill seas (lakes, rivers, springs) or overflood the earth

B15.definition_eng: A river flows from the body of a female person

B16.name_eng: Water is salty being polluted by alive being
B16.definition_eng: Sea, river or spring is salty or turbid because it was created from a body liquid of some alive being or polluted with such a liquid

B16A.definition_eng: The sea is produced from urine or blood

B16B.definition_eng: The sea is alty because the wolverine or the fox bathed in it or urinated into it

B16C.definition_eng: Magic mill is ordered to grind salt but not ordered to stop. It sinks into ocean and continues to work making the water salty

B17.definition_eng: Darkness is a particular object that can be carried (usually brought from its original owner in a container)

B18.definition_eng: Day light (also warmth, the sun, the moon) is kept as a particular object in a container, under a cover, etc.

B19.name_eng: The night and the married life
B19.definition_eng: People had trouble making love before night came into being

B1A.name_eng: Three worlds: the universe divided between gods
B1A.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic persons agree to divide between them levels of universe (upper world, earth, lower world)

B1B.definition_eng: Two supernatural females compete in producing things. One has positive, another negative characteristics

B1C.definition_eng: Two creators agree that whose object will be found in a certain condition (usually: whose tree or flower will grow or blossom first) should be recognized as a senior one. While one of the creators sleeps or is absent, another replaces the objects and so achieves the priority by deceit

B1D.definition_eng: Two persons are creating the world, one is a good and and another a bad worker, that’s because separate parts of the world look differently

B1F.name_eng: Two brothers: a winner and a failure
B1F.definition_eng: Two brothers (companions) live In the epoch of the creation. One of them is smart and selfconfident, another is weak and makes mistakes. They are not enemies and demonstrate their qualities in two or more episodes

B1G.definition_eng: Four travelling brothers transform the world, annihilating monsters, changig the habits and appearance of different creatures and acquiring valuables (water, fire, cultivated plants and the like). Usually one of them is the main actor, and they often have one name for all the four

B20.definition_eng: People regularly ascend to the sky for hunting, fishing or gathering; do not give honey, fish or proper meat to the old person remained below; she or he makes their return impossible, they remain in the sky

B21.definition_eng: People ascend the tree to hunt, fish, or gather food in the sky. The tree is destroyed, people fall to earth or remain in the upper world

B22.definition_eng: People who have climbed up a tree do not share food with a person who remained below. He or she revenges on them destroying the tree. The events have cosmic dimensions

B22A.definition_eng: Boys climb a tree to eat fruits. Tapir asks them to give some fruits to him, they refuse to do so. Tapir tries to kill the boys

B23.definition_eng: God prohibits making fire for cooking and punishes breakers of this taboo

B24.definition_eng: After being engaged into a conflict or breaking a tabou, people are transformed into wild pigs or peccaries

B24A.definition_eng: Person makes a circle of bird feathers around a group of people or throws feathers into their dwelling, people turn into wild pigs

B25.definition_eng: Persons climb a tree or liana and fall turning into wild pigs and other game animals

B26.name_eng: Human person joins the wild animals
B26.definition_eng: Human person who follows the wild animals turns into one of them or into their master

B27.definition_eng: Persons ponders over what object, feature, or creature it would be appropriate for him or her to turn into. When the choice is made, the persons transforms himself or herself

B27A.definition_eng: Persons ponders over what object, feature, or creature it would be appropriate for them to turn. When the choice is made, persons turn into thunder and/or lightning

B27B.definition_eng: Persons ponders over what object, feature, or creature it would be appropriate for them to turn. When the choice is made, persons turn into stars

B28.definition_eng: The transformer walks along coming across different persons and creatures, transforming them into birds, animals, stones, shrines, etc. (or transforming monstrous animals into present day ones) and introducing cultural norms, landscape features, etc.

B28A.definition_eng: Person is riveted to the ground with a pole or spear, removed to the far away place and is associated with an object that continues to influnce life of the people

B28B.definition_eng: Hero comes to a country where inhabitants are afraid of objects or plants who attack them. He easily overcomes these objects and transforms them in what they are now

B28C.name_eng: Lice grasp a man and pull him into the sea
B28C.definition_eng: Lice grasp a man and pull him into the sea

B28D.definition_eng: Persons do not understand with whom they are talking and tell the Transformer that they are making weapons to kill such and such a person or thinking about how to hide from him. The Transformer kills them of transforms them into animals

B28D1.name_eng: Man transformed into deer, his knives into antlers
B28D1.definition_eng: Unrecognized Transformer meets a man who tells him that he prepares knives (a spear) to kill Transformer. The latter transforms him into deer, his knives or spear into deer antlers

B28E.definition_eng: The Moon (alone or together with the Sun) transforms the original abnormal world establishing present day norms and forms

B29.definition_eng: People turn into animals, birds or stones at a feast, after the feast, after performing a ritual or after a victory over dangerous enemy

B2A.definition_eng: The earth is a female person (alone or together with a male person); she is female being or associated with a woman

B2B.definition_eng: The earth devours bodies of the people when they die and are buried

B2C.name_eng: The earth is a human body, is born by the woman
B2C.definition_eng: The earth, elements of the landscape or the fertile soil are the transformed body of a person or the earth (islands) were born by a woman

B2D.name_eng: Marriage of the sky and the earth
B2D.definition_eng: The male Sky (the Sun, the Thunder, the creator of the sky) marries the female Earth (or its female creator) or the female Sky marries the male Earth

B2E.definition_eng: The earth or the world as a whole is a male person (alone or together with a female person)

B2F.definition_eng: (While the earth is still absent or liquid), a bird buries its relative in its own head that usually explains its appearance (a swell on its beak, a crest of feathers) or unpleasant smell

B2F1.definition_eng: (While the earth is still absent or liquid), a bird buries its relative in its own head that usually explains its appearance (a swell on its beak, a crest of feathers) or unpleasant smell

B2F2.definition_eng: Person carries a dead body for a long time having no possibility to bury it or being ignorant how to do it but ultimately buries the corpse in the earth

B2G.name_eng: Chameleon walked while the earth was still soft
B2G.definition_eng: Chaeleon is a premordial animal and walked on the earth while its was not still solid

B3.definition_eng: Initially the earth is a swamp, water and dry land are not separated from each other

B30A.definition_eng: Fish emerges from remains of a killed person or creature

B30B.name_eng: Murdered person turns into game animals
B30B.definition_eng: Different game animals emerge from remains of a murdered person

B31.definition_eng: A woman (usually after a conflict with a man or remaining alone) or a man and a woman (married couple, lovers, brother and sister) turn into water mammals

B32.definition_eng: After a conflict with their husbands women turn into fish

B32A.definition_eng: Enemies of a person who rides a ship turn into seals or dolphins

B33.definition_eng: Female person is incarnation of wind, mother of winds, etc.

B33A.name_eng: Person dies of cold in the spring
B33A.definition_eng: When it becomes warm, a person or animal (bird) decides that the winter is over (most often an old woman goes to graze her animals) but dies of cold or the animals that had been deiven to the pasture die

B33A1.definition_eng: Person or animal, bird teases, offends March or other month and are punished

B33B.definition_eng: In the late winter or early spring a bird (usually a thrush) flies out before time and dies of cold or her nestlings die of cold

B33C.definition_eng: When the winter ends and the spring begins certain month (usually March) borrows (rare buys, steals) several days from a neighbor month

B33D.definition_eng: Old woman is incarnation of winter, is associated with snow, or there are several cold days between winter and spring (or fall) associated with a certain old woman

B33D1.definition_eng: In folk narratives days of week (usually Friday and Wednesday) are (female) persons of more or less recognizable demonic nature

B33E.definition_eng: The last cold month wishes he were longer or would come earlier. In such a case he would freeze everybody to death

B33E1.name_eng: To freeze an embryo in the womb
B33E1.definition_eng: To describe the extreme cold, it is said that it is able to frees boiling water, an embryo in its mother womb and the like

B33E2.definition_eng: To describe the extreme cold in early spring, it is said that it brakes cattle’s horns (

B33F.definition_eng: Thanks to activity of a person (usually the old woman who winds or unwinds yarn, threads, etc.), the night and the day alternate with each other

B33F1.definition_eng: Committing particular acts, an (old) woman defines alternation of night and day

B33F2.name_eng: In search of the fire, hero ties up an old woman
B33F2.definition_eng: At night, the fire fades away, and the hero goes in search of it. On his way, he ties up an old woman or an old man (usually, they are responsible for the duration of night and day)

B33G.name_eng: Three horsemen (the Sun, the Moon, the Night)
B33G.definition_eng: Horsemen or horses symbolize luminaries or parts of the day cycle

B33H.definition_eng: The Sun has the mother who shares with him (rare: her) his dwelling place

B34.definition_eng: When night escapes from container where it was originally preserved, men surprised by the darkness turn into birds or animals

B35.definition_eng: Being in a hurry, the bear puts his left shoe on his right foot and vice versa. Now is lumbering

B35A.name_eng: Tree fulfills wishes and then transforms into bear
B35A.definition_eng: Tree grants a man the fulfillment of his wishes but ultimately transforms him into a bear

B36.definition_eng: Birds, fish, reptiles, mammals intentionally or by chance are smeared with colorful substances or divide among themselves parts of somebody's body thus acquiring their present characteristics

B36A.definition_eng: Two zoomorphic personages decorates each other or somebody decorates each of them

B36B.definition_eng: Birds obtain their voices after pecking big reptile and smearing themselves with liquids from its body

B36C.definition_eng: Animals get meat and fat extracted from some original creature or created otherwise. Some get a lot, some remain lean

B37.name_eng: Creatures are made appear as they are now
B37.definition_eng: Person decorates different birds (rare: fish), share fat between anomals. Since then, the corresponding species acquire present characteristics

B38.definition_eng: Person paints birds or animals or they paint each other. Some of them are not satisfied with the result

B38A.definition_eng: Two birds decorate each other, one becomes worse than it was before

B38B.definition_eng: Two mammals or reptiles (or a mammal or raptile and other creature) decorate each other or somebody decorates each of them

B38C.name_eng: Raven and loon paint each other
B38C.definition_eng: Raven and loon paint each other

B38D.name_eng: Raven and owl paint each other
B38D.definition_eng: Raven and owl paint each other

B38E.definition_eng: Person kicks loon or other water bird. Since then this bird has flat tail base and it walks on dry land with difficulty

B39.definition_eng: Insect-person knows the source of food (cultivated plants) and water but does not share his knowledge. To make him speak, ancestors tie a rope around his waist and pull it till the waist becomes narrow (origin of narrow place between breast and belly of insects)

B3A.definition_eng: Water is the original element, the dry earth appears later

B3B.definition_eng: Original earth was small and later increased in size or the fertile soil grew from a small amount of original substance

B3C.definition_eng: When dry land is created, Creator takes a rest and sleeps. His antagonist decides to drown him and drags him to the edge of the earth. The dry land grows in size as long as the antagonist drags the Creator's body, the edge never reached

B3D.definition_eng: A worm obtains the earth (from the underworld), it emerges from the worm's excrements, is extracted from inside of the worm

B3E.definition_eng: In the beginning there are only air and water. 1) Person descends from the sky, creates the dry land or a hard support created for her or him grows into the earth. 2) The earth is sent or dropped from the sky, put on the surface of the water. 3) The earth is brought from somewhere (not from the underworld) and put on the water

B4.definition_eng: Islands or continent are fished out of the ocean or pulled to their present place by rope

B40.definition_eng: Hare or rabbit is a false deer or it was deer in the past or a close kin of the deer or had horns or antlers or missed opportunity to get them, its ears are the false horns

B40A.definition_eng: Animal who has no horns now had them before or missed opportunity to get them

B40B.definition_eng: The horse exchanges some parts of his body with the cow, usually gives her horns and/or obtains teeth

B41.definition_eng: Because the dog was spreading some information, altercated with its masters, was talking in a wrong time, etc. it lost the ability to speak

B41A.definition_eng: The dog or other domestic animal speaks aloud about those details of its masters' life that they would prefer to conceal. He is punished by depriving his ability to speak

B42.definition_eng: Certain stars or constellations are interpreted as hunters, their dogs and game that the hunters pursue

B42A.name_eng: Blood or fat drops to earth
B42A.definition_eng: Hunters pursue a bear across the sky, kill it in August – October. Its blood or fat drops to earth as a dew or painting leaves of the trees in red

B42B.definition_eng: In the cosmic hunt tale the game pursued by the hunters is an ungulate (elk, deer, mountain sheep, etc.)

B42C.definition_eng: In the cosmic hunt tale the game pursued by the hunters is a bear

B42D.definition_eng: In the cosmic hunt tale the game pursued by the hunters is a tapir

B42E.definition_eng: In the cosmic hunt tale the game pursued by the hunters is a rhea bird (Rhea americana)

B42F.definition_eng: Ursa major (seven stars or only four stars of a dipper) is identified with an ungulate (elk, deer, mountain sheep, etc.)

B42G.name_eng: Ursa major is attacked or persued
B42G.definition_eng: Ursa major (Dipper with Handle or Dipper only) is associated with an animal (animals), persued / attacked by other participants of the tale

B42H.name_eng: The Belt of Orion is the game, other star is the hunter
B42H.definition_eng: The Belt of Orion is the animal or three animals, other star (of the Orion or outside of this constellation) is the hunter

B42H1.definition_eng: In context of the Cosmic Hunt myth one of the stars (group of stars) is an arrow or a bullet which hit the animal or three animals identified with the Belt of Orion

B42H2.definition_eng: A big reddish star (Betelgeuse or Aldebaran) is associated with an arrow

B42HH.definition_eng: Constellation of Orion is related to the Cosmic Hunt tale

B42I.definition_eng: Cassiopea (the Lady in the Chair) is associated with the deer or elk

B42K.definition_eng: In the cosmic hunt tale either hunters or game is identified with the Pleiades

B42L.name_eng: Animal is the dipper, hunters are the handle
B42L.definition_eng: Stars of the handle of the Big Dipper are identified with the hunters, the dipper itself with the game (bear or elk) or a neat-barn ravaged by bear

B42M.definition_eng: Three stars of the Dipper’s handle of Ursa Mayor are three men (hunters, thieves) who are eager to get an animal (an elk or a bear) or an object (a cot). Alkor (a weak star near Mizar) is a receptacle in possession of the second man

B42M1.definition_eng: Three main stars of the Big Dipper’s handle are associated with three men of different ethnic afiliation

B42M2.name_eng: The boaster and the hurried one
B42M2.definition_eng: Stars of the handle of the Big Dipper are three hunters who pursue an animal and demonstrate particular psychological characteristics (one is a boaster, another is a hurried one, etc.). In Siberia the hunters belong to different ethnic groups and in the North American Northeast they are different species of birds

B42MN.name_eng: One hunter chases the sky elk
B42MN.definition_eng: In the cosmic hunt tale only one hunter (not many) pursues an animal (elk or bear) associated with a circumpolar constellation but not with Orion or the Pleiades. (In Kalevalaic tradition the association with particular sideral objects is absent

B42N.definition_eng: Constellation of Orion or the Belt of Orion is identified with only one male person, usually with a warrior or hunter

B42O.definition_eng: Certain constellation is a male person whose back is broken or wounded

B42O1.definition_eng: Ursa major is identified with a fisher (mustela pennati)

B42P.definition_eng: Ursa major is identified with a bear

B42Q.definition_eng: Ursa major is identified with a carriage, a cart

B42R.name_eng: The Belt of Orion: one runs after another
B42R.definition_eng: Three stars of the Belt of Orion are three persons or animals who pursue each other

B42S.definition_eng: Ursa major or Polaris are identified with a middle size animal (ermine, fisher, woodchuck) or with a basically anthropomorphic person (with some animal characteristics) hit with a dart or an arrow

B42T.name_eng: Ursa major is a big mammal
B42T.definition_eng: Seven main stars of Ursa major are interpreted as a figure of a mammal: bear, deer, mountain sheep, camel, dog

B42U.name_eng: Big Dipper’s handle are three persons
B42U.definition_eng: Three stars of Big Dipper’s handle are three persons. Four stars of the Dipper itself are an object or an animal (rare: animals)

B43.definition_eng: Parts of the body of the primeval person or creature are transformed into different elements of the landscape and parts of the universe

B43A.definition_eng: A person or creature is created from several different materials or objects or from material brought from different places

B44A.name_eng: Council on seasons: units of time
B44A.definition_eng: Animals (Melanesia: persons) discuss the number of discrete units of time that should be in a certain calendar period or in the night

B44B.name_eng: Council on seasons: toes, claws, hairs, feathers
B44B.definition_eng: Toes, claws, feathers, hairs, color stripes, etc. are counted and compared to establish the number of period of time or particular way of alternation of periods

B44C.definition_eng: It is discussed if darkness or light, cold or warm periods should exist

B44D.name_eng: Black-an-white animal is night and day
B44D.definition_eng: There are both night and day because spotted (or otherwise black and white) animal has been killed

B44E.definition_eng: The primeval ancestors (usually birds and animals) participate in discussion concerning the desired predominance or wamth/light or cold/darkness, number of the units of time in a tempoi cycle, etc.

B44F.definition_eng: In a dispute about should it be dark or light, the fox stands for the light

B44F1.definition_eng: In a dispute about should it be cold (dark) or warm (light), the bear stands for the cold; or the world is dark because the bear hides the sun in his house

B45.definition_eng: Interaction between the warm (light, abundant, etc.) and the cold (dark, barren, etc.) seasons is associated with the relations between a man and a woman

B45A.definition_eng: Alternation of seasons and/or differences between climates of particular areas is interpreted as a struggle betwee two persons, one being related to the warmth and another to the cold

B45B.definition_eng: Bull or cow are related to winter and cold, responsible for existence of the cold season

B46.definition_eng: Every one of the seven main stars of the Ursa mayor is a an adult man

B46A.definition_eng: One of the stars of the Pleiades was separated from others (usually abducted) by stars of Big Dipper and now is seen among them)

B46A1.name_eng: Stars of Big Dipper are robbers
B46A1.definition_eng: Stars of Big Dipper are thieves, robbers

B46B.definition_eng: Every one of the seven main stars of the Ursa major is a female person

B46C.name_eng: Big Dipper is seven persons or animals
B46C.definition_eng: Every main star of the Big Dipper is interpreted as a particular person or animal

B46D.definition_eng: Several men each of whom is an expert in a particular sphere turn into stars

B47.definition_eng: In former times or regularly the Pleiades or other group of stars produced or produce till now severe cold. (The heliacal set of the Pleiades is in May-June while in the Northern Hemisphere they are seen best of all in the winter time)

B47A.definition_eng: Cow steps on the stars of the Pleiades which were dangerous being and lived on earth. Some of these stars slipped through its split hoof

B48.definition_eng: Weak or herbivorous animals were dangerous predators but have been transformed

B48A.definition_eng: Particular pieces of flesh or inner organs in the bodies of animals, birds, or fish originally belonged to other creatures

B48B.definition_eng: Some game animals have a piece of human flesh in their body that remained since the time when these animals were anthropomorphic

B48C.definition_eng: In the pike’s head are (seen) tool used by people

B48D.definition_eng: Persons or objects swallowed by pike become part of its body (bones in its head, liver)

B49.definition_eng: Animals of particular species do not hear well the instructions concerning their way of life or the ask God for some benefit but muddle their request. Thanks to this they acquire their present habits. (In the Toraja tale the motif is used to explain the mortal nature of human beings)

B49A.name_eng: How many cubs in a year
B49A.definition_eng: Mighty animals lost opportunity to have many children and now give birth only once in several years

B49B.definition_eng: Initially cow had more teats than now

B4A.name_eng: Islands cut off by a fish
B4A.definition_eng: A fish struggles and knocks its tail against ground cutting off Islands from a mass of land

B50.definition_eng: An insect feeds on human blood (flesh). Dangerous person asks it where it had sucked blood or whose blood (flesh) is the most delicious. Usually the insect lies or cannot answer (its tongue is cut off) and thanks to this dangerous person attacks certain plants or animals and not people

B51.definition_eng: Thanks to intentional misinformation, Thunder did not get know that bloodsucking insect has sucked human blood

B51A.name_eng: The snake is an enemy of the swallow
B51A.definition_eng: The snake is an enemy of the swallow (usually because swallow does not let snake to destroy people; the snake sends mosquito or other bloodsucking insect to get know whose blood is the most delicious; the insect flies back to report that human blood is the sweetest; swallow bites its tongue off and the snake gets to pull off feathers from the swallow's tail)

B52.name_eng: Waters of deluge create the mountains
B52.definition_eng: When waters of the world flood withdraw with a rush, they create mountains and valleys

B52A.definition_eng: Flying above the earth and flapping its wings, a bird (usually a vulture) makes it dry after the flood or otherwise creates present landscape

B52B.definition_eng: Person spits out earth that he swallowed or concealed otherwise. This way the broken landscape is created

B52C.definition_eng: When the earth was created it proved to be bigger than the sky and had to be squeezed. This way mountains or swamps have appeared

B53.name_eng: Creatures or objects from cut off genitals
B53.definition_eng: Supernaturally big genitals are cut off and turn into snakes or other creatures and objects

B54.definition_eng: Chips of wood, branches or pieces of bark thrown or fallen into the water turn into fish and/or aquatic animals

B55.definition_eng: Fish grows on branches of a tree or leaves of a tree turn into fish

B56.definition_eng: After the crocodile or caiman swallows or loses fire (that he possessed before), he remains without his tongue; or the crocodile's tongue is cut off to make something related to celestial fire (thunderbolt, sun beams, etc.

B57.definition_eng: When some person or animal is killed, blood paints the sky (origin of the sunrise or sunset, of reddish colors of Aurora borealis) or other natural objects (Moon, autumn vegetation)

B57A.definition_eng: When person gets to see that the sky becomes red he or she understands that another person's blood is shed or that another person spilled a red liquid

B58.definition_eng: After the original fire is stolen by the ancestors, a partridge size forest bird (Penelope sp.; Anhima cornuta; etc.; jacu, paujil) swallows burning coal and (besides the Andoque) its neck becomes red

B59.name_eng: A group of dancers ascends to the sky
B59.definition_eng: A group of people (usually children, brothers or sisters) play, dance, ascend to the sky and turn into Pleiades or other compact constellation

B5A.definition_eng: In the beginning of time, a male and a female persons meet each other and become engaged into the dialogue

B5B.name_eng: The universal mother and female creator
B5B.definition_eng: A female deity creates the world (alone of with the help of a male companion); woman (alone or with her companion) gives birth to or creates not only people but also different creatures and objects {Versions with the female creator and the primeval mother are diffiocult to separate from each other}

B5B1.definition_eng: A woman gives birth to animals of different species (but not to humans of natural objects)

B5C.definition_eng: There are two women in the beginning of time, an old and a young one. One or both conceive in a supernatural way. A son or twins are born, they establish natural order and social rules

B6.name_eng: A man and a woman move around a post and meet each other
B6.definition_eng: The first or the only survived man and woman move in different directions around a post, a hill, etc. When they come together they marry each other

B60.definition_eng: Children conflict with their parents who do not pay them enough attention, condemn their sexual behavior, do not give them enough food, clothes, etc.; the children abandon their parents and become birds, bats, atmospheric phenomena, or stars (usually the Pleiades)

B61.definition_eng: Mole had to support the sky or the Sun that had fallen down. Usually its paw (hand) remained crooked after this

B62.definition_eng: Man thinks that buzzard or hawk has better life than he. They exchange clothes. The bird lives with the man's wife as her husband, the man usually does not enjoy his bird life

B63.definition_eng: Young people, usually siblings, tell other person, usually their mother, that they have been doing agricultural work though it is not the case. When the deceit is discovered, they turn into atmospheric phenomena

B64.definition_eng: Bones of fresh-water fish are result of a fighting or military expedition. The bones are arrows that have pierced the fish bodies (gill openings are pierced by arrows) or the small bones are fragments of originally big ones

B64A.name_eng: Small bones: war between fish and birds
B64A.definition_eng: Fish and birds shoot arrows into each other. Since then there are many small bones inside the fish

B64B.name_eng: Small bones: war between the fish
B64B.definition_eng: Fish of two species shoot arrows into each other. Since then there are many small bones in the fish or some bones are forked

B64C.name_eng: Small bones: fish fall from the sky
B64C.definition_eng: Fish in company of other earth dwellers ascend to fight with the sky dwellers. They fall to earth and break their bones. Since then there are many small bones in the fish

B64D.definition_eng: Certain bones in the body of living creatures (usually birds and fish) are arrows that were shot into them

B65.definition_eng: Person plays imitating other animal person. His belly is cut open as a result and intestines turn into vines

B66.definition_eng: Persons climb to the sky up a rope or an arrow ladder; fallen down rope turns into forest vines

B67.definition_eng: People fell giant tree. The fallen tree and/or its stump turns into mountain(s) or rocks

B68.definition_eng: Hazel-grouse was big and dangerous. He is torn to pieces which are shared between other birds and animals. What remains is the present grouse

B68A.name_eng: A punished bird: must carry a weaker one on its back
B68A.definition_eng: Birds quarrel and one who pretended to obtain a high position badly beats a weaker one. Other birds decide that the offender must carry another one on his back

B68B.name_eng: One who tried to scare the God
B68B.definition_eng: (Animal) person who tried to scare the God (people) with his/its, behavior, strange look or sudden appearance is punished being transformed into an animal (of different characteristics than it was before)

B69.name_eng: Chipmunk's back scratched: hence his stripes
B69.definition_eng: To thank or to punish a small mammal like chipmunk or (ground) squirrel, animal or person scratches or paints it producing stripes on its back

B69A.definition_eng: Chipmunk or an animal of similar size (weasel, pika) is engaged into argument with another animal person (bear, elk, puma, snake) if it should be warm and light or cold and dark

B69B.name_eng: Frog’s back scratched: hence its stripes
B69B.definition_eng: To thank or to punish a frog, animal or person scratches it producing stripes on its back

B6A.definition_eng: Female ancestor gives birth to several eggs. One or two of them do not hatch for a long time, thought to be rotten are thrown into the river. However just from them emerge (or had to emerge) high status characters

B70.definition_eng: Person beats hares, foxes or other medium size animals who became helpless (usually closed in his house). Tale explains why tips of the animals' ears or tails have a particular color

B71.definition_eng: Aurora borealis is spirits (of the dead) who run holding burning torches, play or fight with each other

B72.definition_eng: Because children do not give water to their mother, she turns into a bird, usually a cuckoo, and flies away

B72A.definition_eng: Мать (мачеха, приемный отец) не дает еды девочке или (реже) мальчику. Ребенок просит перелетных птиц взять его с собой, те (Step)parent does not share his or her food with a child. The child (usually a small girl) asks the migrating birds (swans, geese, etc.) to take her or him with them. The birds give the child feathers (wings, etc.) and the girl (boy) flies away with the birds

B72B.name_eng: An offended one flies away as a bird
B72B.definition_eng: A girl or more rare a boy turns into a bird and flies away when her or his mother (father or other adult person in whose house she lives) does not give her or him food, water or makes her feel offended in other way

B72C.name_eng: The blood of the running children paints objects
B72C.definition_eng: Running after their mother, the children injure themselves, their blood paints red plants, ground, sky

B72D.definition_eng: A woman makes wings (a beck, a tail) from her dress-making tools and turns into a bird or a flying squirrel

B73.definition_eng: Person turns into the cuckoo so quickly that one of his or her legs remains bare or one of her braids not plaited. Now it is believed that the cuckoo has different legs or wings

B73A.name_eng: The cuchoo: in search of lost horse
B73A.definition_eng: A girl (with her brother; two small brothers) is (are) in search of the horse or cattle or the girl is in search of her lost brother. She (alone or with her brother; both brothers) turns into a bird (usually a cuckoo; or both siblings turn into birds) that cries in specific way

B73B.name_eng: The cuckoo: in search of lost family member
B73B.definition_eng: Two teenagers or young people are in search of each other, call each other (or one of them call another): a girl in search of her lost (or dead) brother or sister ir brother’s wife, a boy in search of his brother or sister, young parents in seach their child. One or both of them turn into birds with particular cry

B73C.name_eng: If the food is smaller in volume, you has eaten it
B73C.definition_eng: One of the members of a household accuses another that she or he has eaten part of the food though the volume decreased because of the heating

B74.definition_eng: Eyes of wood-grouse became red because it shed tears

B74A.definition_eng: After they sew red rags or threads to person’s eylids or paint them in red (or he does it himself), he sees everything in red color or his eye become red forever

B74B.name_eng: The marriage of the owl and the Moon
B74B.definition_eng: The (proposed) marriage of the owl and the Moon broke up or has never been realized

B75A.name_eng: Sounds of the time of creation: voice of a person
B75A.definition_eng: Voice of a person who lived in the bygone times is still heard (most often it is an echo)

B75B.name_eng: Sounds of the time of creation: a creaking of trees
B75B.definition_eng: Creaking of trees is a voice of a transformed person

B75B1.name_eng: Sounds of the time of creation: voice of a wife or mother-in-law
B75B1.definition_eng: Man pushes his mother-in-law or his wife into a tree hollow, she turns into the creaking of trees or into echo

B75C.name_eng: Sounds of the time of creation: a sound of the surf
B75C.definition_eng: The sound of the surf or of the river rapids is heard from the time of creation

B75D.name_eng: Sounds of the time of creation: a murmur of the forest
B75D.definition_eng: The murmur of the forest or grass swayed by the wind is heard from the time of creation

B76.definition_eng: Waves of the sea petrified and turned into dry land with mountain chains

B77.definition_eng: Originally the sky was close to the earth, then it has risen up

B77A.definition_eng: One or several (animal)-persons push sky up to its present height

B77B.name_eng: Sky touched with a long object
B77B.definition_eng: The sky rose to its present height and/or the direct relations of the sky deity with the people were broken off when the sky or the deity was touched or struck with a long object (a pestle, a broom, etc.)

B77B1.definition_eng: The sky rose to its present height and/or the direct relations of the sky deity with the people were broken off when the sky or the deity was pushed up, touched or struck with a pestle or with a ladle during the preparation of food

B77B2.definition_eng: The sky rose to its present height and/or the direct relations of the sky deity with the people were broken off when the sky or the deity was pushed up, touched or struck with a broom

B77C.definition_eng: Serpent-like creature pushes the sky far away from the earth

B78.definition_eng: When person or creature shakes himself or itself, shakes his or her bed, clothes, plucks birds, etc., snow falls down to earth

B79.definition_eng: From the primeval egg, eggs, or egg-like ball emerge the earth, the sky, sky bodies, different animals (all or part of the items of this list)

B79A.definition_eng: In the beginning of time a bird flies, lays an egg or eggs, different objects and creatures emerge from them or a bird drops some solid substance on the waters and the dry land or an island appear

B79A1.name_eng: A bird dropped hard substance on water
B79A1.definition_eng: In the beginning of time, a bird flies and drops (puts) some solid substance on the waters and the dry land or an island appear. Sometimes the precise nature of the substratum on which the solid piece falls is not defined

B7A.definition_eng: Somebody is the only possessor of water or certain beverage. Another person drinks it, escapes and spits out making it available for the people

B7B.definition_eng: Sea, river, waters of flood flow out of a small receptacle

B7C.definition_eng: Person or creature possesses all the fresh water. Another person splashes it out of a container or pond making it available for everybody

B7D.definition_eng: Water flows from a broken bone (of a bird) producing a flood

B8.definition_eng: Frog hides all the water but other person makes it available for everybody

B80.definition_eng: The process of world creation includes the measuring of its size

B81.definition_eng: Creator and his opponent ponder upon should the dog be able to use a bow or fire-arms

B82.definition_eng: Raven or other carrion-eating bird of dark color and a similar size was originally white

B83.name_eng: Bag too heavy to be lifted up
B83.definition_eng: Person tries to pick up a small object or creature but it proves to be of enormous weight (and size)

B84.definition_eng: When a demonic person (usually an ogress pursuing a man) dies, her or his flesh turns into objects that are found on trees, like fungi, pitch, fruits or nuts

B85.definition_eng: Wind is too strong, hero makes it to blow more calmly

B85A.definition_eng: Wind stops to blow (after blowing too much). Person comes to him and creates the desirable balance. Since then, wind blows but usually not too much

B85B.definition_eng: Wind was or is in a particular enclosure (bag, cave, etc.). It was released from it or comes out from time to time

B86.definition_eng: To reach the sky (the Sun, Moon, particular star), people build a ladder or tower that consists of separate modules (bricks, logs, sticks, etc.). This construction collapses

B86A.name_eng: To get the Moon from the sky
B86A.definition_eng: People try to get the Moon from the sky

B87.definition_eng: Alcor (a weak star near the second star of the handle of the Big Dipper) is selected as a particular sky object

B87A.definition_eng: A weak star near the second star of the handle of the Big Dipper (the Tibetans: Small Dipper) is interpreted as a dog

B87B.definition_eng: Big Dipper is a cart with a harnessed wolf or bear. Usually it is explained that the handle of the Big Dipper is not straight because a wolf or a bear (identified with Alcor or with the last star of the handle, η) attacked an ox that was dragging a cart and was harnessed instead of it

B87C.definition_eng: Alcor (a weak star near Mizar, the second star of the Big Dipper’s handle) is a rider, a driver

B87D.definition_eng: Alcor (a weak star near Mizar, the second star of the Big Dipper’s handle) is a baby

B87E.name_eng: Alcor is a young girl or woman
B87E.definition_eng: Alcor (a weak star near Mizar, the second star of the Big Dipper’s handle) is a young girl or woman

B88.definition_eng: All person's children die. He or she addresses God and asks him why he or she suffers so much

B89.name_eng: Owl as a king of birds
B89.definition_eng: Owl was or wanted to be king of birds or it behaved itself in a wrong way during the elections of the king. Now it avoids other birds and/or other birds chase it

B9.definition_eng: There is enormous amount of water inside a trunk of a tree or a tree turns into water

B90.definition_eng: There is an anthropomorphic patron or patroness of wolves. Usually he or she gives instructions to wolves on particular day of the year

B91.definition_eng: Snail had (the) sharp(est) eyes. Another animal person borrows them and never returns

B91A.definition_eng: (Animal) person who became blind borrows eyes but never returns them to the owner

B92.definition_eng: Person whose body is extraordinary hard and invulnerable or (rare) a small object is broken to pieces that turn into flints or other hard stones (the origin of flints)

B93.name_eng: Meeting in the sky once a year
B93.definition_eng: Once a year or once in several years sky dwellers or messegers of the deity who are seen among the stars meet each other

B93A.name_eng: The bird bridge over the sky river
B93A.definition_eng: Once a year birds make a chain of their bodies to serve as a bridge щмук the celestial river. Usually feathers on their heads are worn down as a result

B94.definition_eng: Trees (and animals) could talk and asked people not to cut or kill them

B95.definition_eng: Human posterior looks in particular way because certain person burned it

B95A.definition_eng: Trickster burns his own anus to punish it for improper behavior

B96.definition_eng: The heroe's enemy turns into a big fish (usually a sturgent) or (rare) a water mammal that are fished or hunted by people

B97.name_eng: Grateful person makes the bird pretty
B97.definition_eng: Grateful person decorates (rare: punishes) a bird who lives near water (kingfisher, loon, goose), thence its appearance (crest, beak, feathers)

B97A.name_eng: The necklace of bird or animal
B97A.definition_eng: A strip of light or dark feathers or hair on the neck of a bird or animal is its necklace

B98.name_eng: The bat between birds and animals
B98.definition_eng: Bat (rare: ostrich) makes attempts to join sometimes animals and sometime birds or is excluded from both categories

B98A.definition_eng: The bat becomes an outcast among other creatures (usually after it makes attempts to join first animals and then birds or vice versa)

B98B.definition_eng: Bat is in conflict with other creatures because of the incident related to somebody's death or funerals

B98C.name_eng: The bat is deceived by God
B98C.definition_eng: The sky deity could cure the mother or child of the bat but did not do it and they have died

B99.name_eng: Person turned into the nest of insects
B99.definition_eng: Person (his/her head) who was abandoned in a tree or falls on a tree turns into a nest of insects

C1.definition_eng: Catastropic displacement of layers of the univers in the past or in the future is mentioned. Among variants (sometimes combined): the sky fell on the earth; the earth (the underworld) and the sky interchanged their positions; the earth turned upside down; the layers of the universe collapsed in one after another; they will change their place during the future cataclysm

C10.definition_eng: During the flood birds or animals escape to some place (mountain, tree, boat, sky). Tips of their tails or other body parts get covered with water or foam and acquire their present color and form

C10A.name_eng: The flood: birds cling to the sky
C10A.definition_eng: During the flood some birds survive clinging to the sky with their beaks

C11.definition_eng: Person uses his supernatural powers to destroy a large group of people who have offended or insulted his son

C12A.name_eng: The dog and the world cataclysm
C12A.definition_eng: A dog warns people about approaching flood or world conflagration, instructs them what should be done

C12B.definition_eng: In the beginning of time or after the flood man marries a bitch. Present people descend from them.

C13.definition_eng: During or before the world cataclysm (deluge, darkness) or (Suruí) in particular place at night, household objects and/or stones, trees, domestic animals turn into wild beasts and monsters

C14.definition_eng: During or before the world catastrophe (deluge, darkness) wild beasts and monsters attack and destroy people

C15.definition_eng: Monstrous puma or jaguar is imprisoned in a cave or tree trunk

C16.definition_eng: Against person's will, butchered, dried or cooked meat, tanned hides, etc. turn back into animals or fish and escape.

C16A.definition_eng: Mistress of animals or fish revives them after being offended

C17.definition_eng: The men of primeval community destroy most of the people and/or themselves in a fire pit or on the bonfire

C18.definition_eng: Person who incarnates or owns the sun hides himself or herself or is hidden. To return or to get heath and light, his or her interest is attracted or diverted by way of singing, dancing, playing music, provocative behavior, offering of unusual gifts, sex or alcohol

C18A.name_eng: The cock lures out the Sun from its hiding place
C18A.definition_eng: The cock lures out the Sun from its hiding place or people beliefe that the Sun will not rise if the cock would not cry

C19.definition_eng: The Sun (the day light) that was absent, stolen or hidden appears (again)

C2.definition_eng: Inhabitans of the Middle World are (partly) destroyed (or will be destoyed) once by fire or draught, another time by a flood or the world is destroyed with a flood of fire or boiling water

C21.definition_eng: In the beginning of time, the wife of a man who is not back for long creates a tiger and send him to return her husband

C22.definition_eng: In time of severe drought or the world conflagration birds and animals go to the master of the rain and bring him back or make him send the rain

C23.definition_eng: Growth and falling of giant tree defines the condition of the sky with luminaries on it (tree eclipses the light of the sun, can destroy the sky, tears the sun off the sky, etc.)

C24.name_eng: The world in danger of falling down
C24.definition_eng: A tree or pillar supports the sky or the earth. If it collapses, people perish

C25A.definition_eng: The destiny of creation depends on a person (usually an old woman) who is cooking soup somewhere outside of our world (in the sky, in the Moon, etc.)

C25B.definition_eng: In the sky, on the Moon (rare: on the Sun), i.e. somewhere outside of our world certain person is spinning, weaving, plaiting, or embroidering

C25C.name_eng: The Big Dipper and the end of the world
C25C.definition_eng: Change in configuration of the stars of certain constellation (usually Big Dipper) or its disappearance from the sky will be a signal of approaching world cataclysm

C26.name_eng: Guardian at the border of the non-human world
C26.definition_eng: Monsters or ghosts try to invade our world. Powerful person or creature is on guard and prevents the invasion

C27.definition_eng: A horned monster breaks ice on river or lake. Usually people walk across frozen body of water, get to see a horn protruding from the ice and try to cut it off. The monster breaks the ice, many people drown

C28.definition_eng: A demon obtains valuables essential for another person's (and for all the people) survival but is tricked to return the valuables

C29.definition_eng: People or God get know a secret thanks to listening in its possessor when he speaks aloud with himself or with his relations. The received knowledge is related to cosmogony or acquisition of cultural values

C2A.definition_eng: Two persons meet a woodpecker and as a consequence, the earth burns. The strong and smart person survives, the weak and stupid is burned

C2B.definition_eng: The Sun and Moon get into conflagration. The Sun survives, the Moon is burned

C3.name_eng: Snakes stops up a hole in the Noah’s arch
C3.definition_eng: When a hole is opened in the arch (rare: in the ground) from which a torrent of water flows, a snake (eel, frog) stops it up with its own body

C30A.definition_eng: A contract entitles the lender of a sum of money to cut a certain amount of flesh (or eye, head, limb, etc.) from the debtor’s body if the load is not repaid in time. The lender cannot cut out the flesh being unable to fulfill a condition that looks logical but is practically absurd

C30B.name_eng: To clean traces off the field
C30B.definition_eng: When an animal or a spirit claims certain field to be his own or suggests an impossible task for a person, the person asks him to delete from the ground traces of his feet or to walk not leaving any traces. The spirit cannot do it

C30C.definition_eng: Person must drink all the water in the sea (count all drops of sea water) but asks his opponent first to separate the sea water from the water of rivers that flow into it

C30D.name_eng: Not to spill a drop of urine
C30D.definition_eng: Person gives his permission to pollute his place with excrements but only on condition that not a drop of urine would be spilled. To fulfill this condition proves to be impossible

C31.definition_eng: A hedgehog proves to be smarter than gods and than other animals; he possesses the knowledge that is of crucial importance for survival of humans

C31A.name_eng: Celestial bodies or fire are promised to Devil
C31A.definition_eng: The master of the underworld receives or is going to receive the celestial bodies of fire but thanks to a trick or a chance, they are not given to him (her) or returned back

C31B.definition_eng: An owl proves to be smarter and wiser than other beings

C31C.definition_eng: A bat proves to be smarter and wiser than other beings

C32.definition_eng: Demons will make a ship of the cut off nails.

C32A.name_eng: Cut off nails indispensable after death
C32A.definition_eng: The cut off nails (and hair) will be indispensable after death (to climb a mountain, to reach the sky, to build a bridge, etc.)

C32B.name_eng: Cut off nails used by Devil
C32B.definition_eng: From the cut off nails (and hair) the demonic persons can make something profitable for them (and harmful for people)

C32C (MOTIF IS NOT IN THE CORRELATION TA.definition_eng: The cut off nails (and hair) have special significance for the fate of the soul in the beyond or for the future of the entire world

C33.definition_eng: A strong man who ventured to confront God is for a long time (for eternity) chained to a mountain or to a post

C33A.definition_eng: During a year somebody tries to break, to make thinner a chain or rope with which the person himself or somebody else is tied. In a certain day when the chain is almost broken it is restored or a post to which the person is tied sinks into the ground again

C33A1.name_eng: A bird comes to peck the enchained man
C33A1.definition_eng: Every day a predator bird comes to peck inner organs of the enchained man. During the day the organs are restored and everything repeats again

C33B.definition_eng: The primordial race perishes when the wind blows for the first time

C34.name_eng: The deluge because of a wounded creature
C34.definition_eng: Killing (injuring, offending) of some cruature (usually related to water) triggers deluge
