C34A.definition_eng: A supernatural person comes to people who fish. They bury him on the beach or throw him into river or marsh. Somebody saves him. He or his father sends the flood

C35.definition_eng: It becomes known that if the Sun or the Sky marry, great calamity is inevitable. The marriage plans are given up

C35A.definition_eng: A zoomorphic person gives wise advise concerning the ways that the Sun should follow. His advise is accepted but he himself is punished by the Sun

C35B.name_eng: Frog is the enemy of the Sun
C35B.definition_eng: The frog (toad) prevents situation in which more than one Sun there were in the sky

C36.definition_eng: Gods fight with their powerful adversaries at the decisive battle that changes fate of the world

C37.definition_eng: A sloth produces the world catastrophe or saves people from it

C38.definition_eng: Those who inhabited the world in the time of creation were saying that real people were to come and so they had to do this and that

C39.definition_eng: When part of the sky was broken, the hole was filled up with stones or pieces of ice

C39A.definition_eng: A crack in the sky or a fissure in the earth was repared with ice. Because of this the northern (northwester, northeatsren) wind is cold

C4.name_eng: The flood: fruits fall from a tree
C4.definition_eng: During the flood or in the beginning of times fruits, seeds or other objects are dropped into water one by one, usually by a person who has climbed a tree. As far as the objects fall, water recedes and the dry land appears

C40.definition_eng: In the beginning rocks were falling from the sky killing people

C41.definition_eng: In the beginning the sky has no particular colour. When certain person covers it with a blue cloth or makes something else, the sky acquires its present colour

C4A.name_eng: The flood: survival in a tree
C4A.definition_eng: During the flood some persons survive in a tree

C5A.definition_eng: Birds or humans later changed to birds are sent to explore the earth (is it dry, are any survivals, to investigate why smoke rises to the sky, etc.) or to bring some soil to make the land that would be good for living

C5B.definition_eng: During the creation of the world or after the world cataclysm animals run around making the earth big, reporting about its condition or they are sent to report the size of the growing earth

C6.name_eng: Valuables brought from the lower world
C6.definition_eng: Persons or animals dive or otherwise decend to the lower world to get a desired object and to bring it to earth (besides episodes in the fairytales, cf. motif k27x9)

C6A.name_eng: The diver is turtle or frog
C6A.definition_eng: A turtle or a frog (toad) brings the desired object from the bottom of the water body or from the lower world

C6B.definition_eng: A muskrat (more rare beaver or otter) brings the desired object from under the water

C6C.definition_eng: An aquatic bird dives and brings the desired object from the bottom

C6C1.definition_eng: Two or more different birds (often a loon and a duck) dive one after another to get earth from under the ocean. Only one of them is successful

C6C2.definition_eng: Birds must dive to get mud from the bottom of the waterbody, this mud will turn into the dry land. The loon is unable to reach the bottom, refuses to dive or attempts to hide the mud that brought by him (usually he is punished for this)

C6C3.definition_eng: The loon dives and brings a piece of earth (a blade of grass etc.) that is transformed into the dry land or it brings other object which everybody is eager to get (the loon is the only or the only successful diver)

C6C4.definition_eng: The duck (or an aquatic bird similar to the duck) dives and brings a piece of earth that is transformed into the dry land (it is the only or the only successful diver)

C6D.name_eng: The aquisition of the earth from the lower world
C6D.definition_eng: The dry land (the earth) grows from a small amount of solid substance (sand, clay, dirt and the like) brought from the lower world (usually from the bottom of the ocean)

C6E.definition_eng: A crustacean brings the earth from the bottom of the ocean or from the lower world

C6F.definition_eng: Persons or animals dive to get from under the water a drowned person or creature or part of its body

C6G.name_eng: The diver is a wild boar
C6G.definition_eng: A wild boar brings the earth from under the water and/or spills it over the water

C6H.definition_eng: An insect brings the earth (from under the water, from a lower world or from a far-away place)

C6H1.name_eng: Earth is extracted from the belly of an invertibrate
C6H1.definition_eng: The earth brought from the lower world was in the belly of a worm or an insect and extracted from their

C6I.name_eng: Dirt stuck to body turns into the earth
C6I.definition_eng: Bird or animal returns from the lower world smeared with dirt. It shakes itself or the dirt is scraped off. The dirt turns into the earth

C6I1.name_eng: A heap of mud arises above the water
C6I1.definition_eng: Mud from the bottom of the ocean is gathered up forming a heap which suppit emerges over the surface of the water and becomes the earth

C6J.name_eng: The acquiring of the earth linked to the creation of man
C6J.definition_eng: The acquiring of the earth from the sea bottom or from the lower world, the creation of humans and attempt to spoil it are successive episodes of the same narrative

C6J1.name_eng: The earth is brought by the God's enemy
C6J1.definition_eng: God sends his enemy to bring earth from the bottom of the waterbody. In the beginning, the enemy or also the god can have guise of birds. When the earth is brought up and dry land created, two persons, now always anthropomorphic, are engaged into confrontation

C7.definition_eng: In the beginning of times or after the flood a dam of earth, person or creature does not let water to recede. The dam is broken or opened, waters withdraw

C8.name_eng: The couple of close relations originates the mankind
C8.definition_eng: In the beginning of time or after the natural disaster brother and sister, mother and son, or father and daughters are the only human beings. They marry and the present day people are their descendents

C8A.definition_eng: Being alone and having no other marriage partners, brother and sister agree to marry each other if a highly improbable event or a series of events will take place. Among the events that take place (alternatively or one after the other) are 1) the siblings let two grinding stones roll from two mountains, the brother's stone falls on the sister's one; 2) brother and sister throw two swords from two mountains, both swords get into one sheath; 3) they throw some objects up, the objects get together; 4) they kindle two fires, columns of smoke get together; 5) they put to grow two stems of bamboo, tops of the stems get together

C8A1.name_eng: Thread should enter the needle’s eye
C8A1.definition_eng: Being alone and having no other marriage partners, brother and sister agree to marry each other if a highly improbable event will take place: a thread that is far from a needle has to enter the needle’s eye.

C8A2.definition_eng: The lion (often the stone lion) helps to suvive the flood

C8AA.name_eng: Brother and sister beget the people
C8AA.definition_eng: In the beginning of time or after the natural disaster brother and sister are the only human beings. They marry and the present day people are their descendents

C8B.name_eng: Siblings change their looks and marry
C8B.definition_eng: In the beginning of time or after the world catastrophe brother and sister or mother and son are the only humans. They reject marriage or only the man does not want to marry his sister or mother. After their looks are changed (or only the sister or mother changes her face) they take each other for strangers, marry and beget the new race

C8C.definition_eng: After the world cataclysm, in the beginning of time or coming to a new land a woman marries her son and produce people

C8C1.name_eng: Father and daughter beget the people
C8C1.definition_eng: In the beginning of time or after the world cataclysm, a man marries his daughter(s) and the present day people are their descendents

C8D.name_eng: The smallpox breaks tabou for incestuous marriage
C8D.definition_eng: Brother and sister avoid incestuous relations but marry after getting over the smallpox and because of this being unable to recognize each other

C8E.name_eng: Survival in the floating bottle gourd
C8E.definition_eng: During the flood or in the beginning of times persons (usually brother abd sister) are floating in a big bottle gourd

C8F.definition_eng: During the flood or in the beginning of times persons (usually brother abd sister) are floating in a big drum

C9.definition_eng: God, animal, some person warns one of the people about the catastrophy (usuallly the flood) that will become soon and in which most of the people must perish

C9A.name_eng: The flood: people turn into toads
C9A.definition_eng: During a flood or when crossing a river those people who drowned (or those who survived) turn into water animals

D1.definition_eng: Fire is personified as an (elder) woman, alone or with her husband, master of fire

D10.definition_eng: A male and a female persons personify fire-sticks

D11.definition_eng: Before fire became known, people prepared food using warmth of their bodies (usually putting food in their armpits); or a person keeps fire in his or her armpits

D12.definition_eng: First people or inhabitants of a distant country cook food in the sun; or fire owner lies that he or she cooks food in the sun

D12A.name_eng: At the sunrise, heat of the sun is enough for cooking
D12A.definition_eng: People who live at the Eastern or Western horizon cook their food using the heat of the sun which comes near them

D13.name_eng: Laughter as a trigger for change
D13.definition_eng: Person’s guise, nature or status are changed when he or she laughs or hears laughter

D13A.name_eng: The obscene dance for the Sun
D13A.definition_eng: To make a character who controls fire or the sun or embodies them laugh, others perform obscene acts in front of him or her (simulate intercourse, show off their genitals, relieve themselves, etc.)

D13C.name_eng: Trickster makes his brother’s wife laugh
D13C.definition_eng: Two companions or brothers live together. The elder conceals his wife from the younger. In his absence, the younger tries to make the woman laugh and this way to get know her hiding place

D13D.definition_eng: To find a person who is hiding somewhere inside the house, another one tries to make her or him laugh

D13E.definition_eng: Hunters perish because they were laughing at the killed (and revived) animal

D13F.definition_eng: Laughter triggers emergence or spread of fire. Usually fire is obtained from a creature when it bursts out laughing

D13G.definition_eng: When person laughs, people see his or her monstrous mouth (many teeth, human meat on teeth). They kill the monster or escape from it

D13H.definition_eng: Person should not laugh in the world of the dead

D13HH.name_eng: Not to laugh visiting the dead
D13HH.definition_eng: Person who visits the other world should not laugh or demonstrate his surprise seeing strange and funny things

D13I.definition_eng: Person knows that the deceiver and trickster has one of his teeth broken. To identify him, person makes others laugh and thus open their mouths

D13I1.name_eng: Showing his teeth, person betrays himself
D13I1.definition_eng: Person’s (demonic) nature becomes clear when he or she laughs and shows his or her teeth

D1A.definition_eng: Girl marries man whose mother is Fire

D1A1.name_eng: Mistress of fire carries away woman’s baby
D1A1.definition_eng: Because a woman offended the fire, its mistress carries the woman’s baby away

D1A2.name_eng: The borrowed object is not burned
D1A2.definition_eng: House of a person who insulted the fire is destroyed but an object or a child of another person (or this person himself) who was nice to the fire has not been burned though it was in the house of the first person

D1A3.definition_eng: A man marries a woman who is the incarnation of fire. She is offended or does not fit the man, their marriage is ruined

D1A4.definition_eng: Two fires from different dwellings meet each other and chat

D1B.definition_eng: The fire is personified as an elder man (alone or with his wife, mistress of fire)

D2.name_eng: Woman gives birth to the fire
D2.definition_eng: A woman gives birth to a son who is very hot (usually the fire or Sun)

D2A.name_eng: Woman dies giving birth to the Sun or the fire
D2A.definition_eng: A woman gives birth to the Sun or the fire and dies because of burns

D4A.definition_eng: Fire is stolen from its original owner or brought back to the people from somebody who had stolen it before

D4AA.name_eng: Moth tries to steal fire from people
D4AA.definition_eng: Moths try to steal fire which the people posess

D4B.definition_eng: Person or people who have stolen fire or asked its owner to share the fire are punished by God

D4C.definition_eng: Warm season is obtained from its original owners

D4C1.definition_eng: Animal-people come to steal summer from its owner. One of them in guise of an elk or caribou diverts the owners' attention or puts to float a log that the owner takes for an elk and pursues. The summer is successfully stolen and brought to the people

D4E.definition_eng: Coyote or fox bring people the fire, the daylight or the Sun

D4E1.definition_eng: Dog obtains fire, daylight or the Sun or steals them

D4F.name_eng: Beaver or fish let themselves to be roasted
D4F.definition_eng: Beaver (in North American) or a small fish (in South America) lets fire owners catch and roast it, then revives and carries the fire away

D4G.name_eng: Hummingbird discovers where the fire is (and brings it to people)
D4G.definition_eng: Hummingbird discovers where the fire is (and brings it to people)

D4H1.definition_eng: A small singing bird (robim, wren) steals fire for people

D4J.definition_eng: Fire owner, stealer, or stealer's companion is a rabbit, a hare or (among the Ofaie) a guinea pig

D4L.definition_eng: The first fire or warmth (summer) are sent to earth from the sky; the ancestors (animal-people) ascend to the sky and bring from there the fire or warmth

D4M.definition_eng: Person comes to the owners of fire or light. They feast and dance. He joins them and in a proper moment carries away the valuables

D4N.definition_eng: A boy or (among the Kutenai) a woman weeps, asking for an element that is absent, i.e. for summer, fire, or rain

D4O.name_eng: Fire stealer pretends to be wet and cold
D4O.definition_eng: To steal fire from its owner, person pretends to be wet or cold and is granted permission to sit near the fireplace. In a proper moment the stealer carries the fire away and brings it to people

D4P.definition_eng: Parrot or parakeet steals fire for people. (Australian data not computed because historically definitely unrelated to the Tropical American data)

D4Q.definition_eng: Fly(-woman) obtains fire by "washing" her hands like a fire-drill twirler

D5.name_eng: Woman as the owner of the fire
D5.definition_eng: Female person is the owner or inventor (but not the personification) of the fire

D5A.definition_eng: First fire was hidden in genitals or anus of a woman

D6A.definition_eng: Crocodile or cayman is an original or temporary owner of fire or lighting

D6B.definition_eng: Badly burned person turns into caiman or crocodile

D7.definition_eng: Frog or toad possesses the fire, steals it from original owner, tries to extinguish or to save it

D7A.definition_eng: Spider possesses the fire or steals it from original owner (texts in which spider acts together with other animals and does not play the leading role are not included)

D8.definition_eng: Fire or summer is stolen from a big predator: a lion (in Africa), a tiger (in Asia), a bear (in Siberia and North America) or a jaguar (in South America)

D9.definition_eng: Raven or other big dark-feathered bird scavenger is the owner, personification, spouse, obtainer or stealer of fire, daylight, or the Sun

E10.definition_eng: A lonely woman or married couple surprises childred who live nearby in guise of animals (plants, objects). After this the children preserve their human guise

E11.definition_eng: Magic person reveals his true nature and/or remains with the real people after the object responsible for preserving the non-human appearance (usually an animal skin) is destroyed (usually burned)

E12.definition_eng: Person draws an object or creature and it becomes alive

E13.definition_eng: The shaman’s drum is likened with a lake

E13A.name_eng: Sacred knowledge from under the water
E13A.definition_eng: Sacred knowledge, objects and rituals are initially obtained from the denizens of the underwater world

E14.definition_eng: People obtain sacred knowledge, objects and rituals from ghosts

E14A.definition_eng: People prepare ritual costumes and masks coping the features from the real demons whom they have killed

E15.definition_eng: People learn from aquatic birds how to make canoes or how to paddle; or the first canoe is a transformed bird or is made of bird bones

E15A.definition_eng: Frame of canoe is made according to breast bone of a bird

E15B.definition_eng: While man is asleep, birds turn into girls and sew covering of his canoe

E16.definition_eng: Riding in canoe, people first turn paddles edgewise, then learn the correct way to use them

E17.definition_eng: Humans acquire (the idea of) ornamentation of the vessels, baskets, body, etc. or the idea of the system of signs after somebody gets to see the pattern on the body of zoomorphic and/or supernatural creature

E17A.name_eng: The ornament: imprint on the skin of a swallowed one
E17A.definition_eng: When serpent swallows a man, his skin becomes decorated with ornament

E18.definition_eng: People learn how to decorate ceramics or baskets (usually learn decorated patterns) thanks to a water creature

E19.name_eng: Origin of drugs: person torn to pieces
E19.definition_eng: Narcotic plants emerge from the body parts of a person who was torn to pieces by others

E1A.definition_eng: First human beings are made of unstable materials (mud, wax, fire, honey, etc.) and unviable

E1A1.name_eng: Becoming sodden under the rain (origin of cripples)
E1A1.definition_eng: Deity or ancestor makes people from mud. Some figures become sodden under the rain and this is the reason why some people have physical defects

E1B.definition_eng: Certain person is made of improper material and proves to be short-lived or unfit for fulfilling his functions

E1B1.definition_eng: A man who had married an unusual girl is warned that she should avoid work or food. Some other members of his household make her violate the raboo and she dies or disappears

E1C.definition_eng: Certain person is made of human excrement or carrion

E1D.definition_eng: First canoes were made of unfit materials

E1E.definition_eng: First human pair has a son who initially is the stalk of a plant

E2.definition_eng: Making people, creator does not reach perfection immediately. First variants of creation are rejected, then proper form and material found

E20.definition_eng: Entering water, certain person makes fish die. From parts of his body or from his grave grows plant used to prepare fish poison (timbo)

E21.definition_eng: Child fishes with poison or his or her body produces fish poison. Fish or water snake kills him or her. The perished child is avenged

E22.definition_eng: Getting into the body of certain being, person obtain knowledge of rituals, songs, ornaments, poison or drugs and then brings it to people

E23.definition_eng: A handful of fleas or lice is thrown into people or into particular person. It was the only way to make him, her or them move and live

E24.definition_eng: Human arms and legs become pliant (get joints) when a primeval ancestor(s) fall from height and break his arms and legs

E25.definition_eng: The art of weaving people get from a spider or from a person who turns into spider afterwards; a spider is weaving for people

E26.name_eng: People (women) transformed into fish become humans again
E26.definition_eng: People or only women disappear under the water and turn into fish. They are caught using fishing tools and become humans (women) again. (Narratives that tell about a man who caught only one fish who because his wife are not included; see motig F7)

E27.definition_eng: People emerge from drops of blood that fall from the sky

E28.definition_eng: People shoot into the Moon person, his blood drops to earth

E29.definition_eng: Two persons (usually Coyote and Lizard) argue if people's hand has to be like a paw or people should have fingers

E3.definition_eng: After destruction of previous world, new people (rare: new earth) are made from the bones of the perished race

E30.definition_eng: Person does not have a spouse, uses wooden fakes for his wife or her husband

E30A.name_eng: Make-believe spouse replaced with alive person
E30A.definition_eng: Person does not have a spouse, uses wooden fakes for his wife or her husband till alive person comes to replace it

E30B.definition_eng: A man makes or receives a figure of a woman. It becomes alive and he marries her

E31.definition_eng: Man makes a wooden doll and pretends that it is alive. Really it is not or it is half-alive. A real woman takes place of a doll, marries the master

E31A.name_eng: Creators and rescuers of a girl
E31A.definition_eng: Several men take part in rescuing, creation or reanimation of a girl (rare: a bird) or several women take part in the reanimation of a dead man or they differetly express their grief. It is asked whose role was crucial (who behavior more noble) and/or who should be the spouse of the reanimated person. Or three men make something valuable and it is asked whose role in the corresponding enterprise was more important

E31A1.name_eng: Three men construct a woman which becomes alive: to whom does she belong?
E31A1.definition_eng: Three (rare two or four) men take part in creation of a girl: one cuts her body of wood, another puts clothes on her, the third one makes her alive. To whom does she belong?

E31A2.name_eng: That one is like her father, another is like her brother but this one is her husband
E31A2.definition_eng: Only one of several men can marry a girl. The girl herself or somebody else explains that somebody among suiters is like a father to her, somebody else is like her brother and only one of the men suits the role of the girl’s husband

E31B.definition_eng: Several women take part in the reanimation of a dead man. They argue whose role was crucial and/or who of them should be the spouse of the reanimated person

E31C.definition_eng: Every one of several men had learned a unique skill thanks to which they save a girl abducted by demon or animal

E32.definition_eng: First people are born by trees or come out of a tree, flower, reed

E34.definition_eng: Ogre is killed. Musical instruments used in male rituals and taboo for women emerge from his remains

E35.definition_eng: First people or people made by Creator's rival were imperfect, not completely anthropomorphic (often: had webbed fingers)

E36.definition_eng: Human body was or could be protected with a hard layer (rare: with hair) but it has been preserved only on fingers and toes (on the head)

E36A.name_eng: Nails as a priviledged part of the body
E36A.definition_eng: Nails grow permanently or human body is covered with a hard layer only on the tips of fingers and toes because only these parts were rinsed with the water of life

E37.definition_eng: Creator takes many small sticks, transforms them into people of both sexes and all ages

E38A.name_eng: Woman gives birth to many embryos
E38A.definition_eng: Woman gives birth to a gourd, a bag (with eggs), a piece of meat. The flesh is cut into pieces which turn into people or many people come out of the gourd or bag

E38B.definition_eng: After the world cataclysm or in the beginning of times a gourd survives or appears, new people come out of it

E38C.definition_eng: First people are dumb but begin to speak when they hear something unusual, are made to laugh, etc.

E39.definition_eng: A pig is an ancestor of a particular group of people

E39A.name_eng: Female animal conceives from man’s urine
E39A.definition_eng: A female animal (snake, pig) conceives from the uruine of a man and gives birth to human child(ren)

E4.name_eng: Creation from dirt of the skin
E4.definition_eng: Supernatural person creates the entire earth, human or other beings of dirt taken from his or her skin, from under the nails, etc.

E40.definition_eng: First people have noses with nostrils upside and are in trouble when it rains

E41.name_eng: Smith kneads iron with his bare hands
E41.definition_eng: A skillful smith has a power to take and knead the hot iron with his bare hands producing the desired form. Usually the smith breaks some taboo and his power is lost

E41A.definition_eng: Crossed legs of a dog or jaws of a snake served as a model for the first pincers

E5.name_eng: Half-made man attempts to stand up
E5.definition_eng: God makes the first man of clay. The man must wait till he is dried up but makes attempts to stand up before time

E5A.definition_eng: The first people (or only the first men or the first women) are not created but come to earth from the underworld (from a cave) or from a small enclosure under the earth or on its surface (tree trunk, rock, gourd, etc.). Many people of both sexes and of different ages or people and different species of animals come out together

E5AA.definition_eng: The first people grew or crawled out of the earth like a grass, mushrooms, worms, etc.

E5B.definition_eng: First man (a group of brothers) or first human couple come out from the underworld (a cave) or from a small enclosure on its surface (tussock, reed, tree, rock, gourd)

E5C.definition_eng: The first people or first anthropomorphic divine beings descend to earth from the sky.

E5D.definition_eng: People live underground or in a small enclosure. When they come out they are attacked by monster or dangerous animal. Monster is killed or transformed

E5E.name_eng: The two-headed being is not allowed to come to the earth
E5E.definition_eng: First people or animals ascend or descend to earth. The two-headed monster attempts to follow them but is prevented from coming to the earth

E6.name_eng: Because of a woman worlds become isolated
E6.definition_eng: When a woman of the child-bearing age tries to come from one world to another (e.g. from sky to earth), the communication between the worlds is blocked or broken forever

E6A.definition_eng: To reach their present country, people had to pass (frozen) water body. Part of the migrants remain on the opposite side or is drowned

E7.name_eng: Person stuck in a cosmic hole
E7.definition_eng: To descend from the sky, ascend from the underworld or come out of the cave, people must pass through narrow hole. A person is stuck in the hole blocking forever communication between different parts of the universe

E8.definition_eng: The first people or (the first) woman (wife of a primeval ancestor) are made of wood

E8A.definition_eng: Women or people in general come out of the fruits (orten the coconuts) or (more rare) leaves of the cocos palm spontaneously turn into women

E8B.definition_eng: A woman hides in a fruit that was brought to house and comes out when nobody is nearby or when the fruit is cut open

E8C.definition_eng: A woman hides in a chip of wood (in a twig) that was brought to house and comes out when nobody is nearby

E9.definition_eng: Person observes traces of some activity that takes place in his (rare: her) house in his (her) absence and then takes by surprise the responsible one

E9AA.definition_eng: In search of his lost fox-wife man comes to a den. Different animal- or bird-women come out and ask him if he would mary them. He refuses and they let him in

E9B.definition_eng: A man marries a woman who can acquire the image of an elephant or appears from the elephant’s tusk

E9C.definition_eng: A man marries a woman who initially has guise of an ungulate animal (buffalo, elk, derr, etc.)

E9D.definition_eng: Man marries a girl who initially has guise of a dog

E9E.definition_eng: Youth gets to supernatural beings, rejects any treasure, asks for a puppy, a dog's skin, a fruit, etc. When he returns home, the puppy (skin, etc.) turn into magic wife

E9I1.definition_eng: A man marries supernatural woman who is a swan

E9I2.definition_eng: A man marries supernatural woman who is a duck

E9I3.definition_eng: A man marries supernatural woman who is a goose

E9I4.definition_eng: A man marries supernatural woman who is a (white) crane

E9I5.definition_eng: A man marries supernatural woman who is a snail

E9J.definition_eng: Man marries monkey-woman; supernatural woman takes form of a monkey or the man pretends that the house-keeper is a monkey

E9J1.definition_eng: It is told how some monkeys changed their habits and appearance and became humans

E9K.definition_eng: A man or a woman is incarnation of the honey or a bee-person

E9M.definition_eng: Man marries a polar bear or grizzly who becomes a woman or a woman who becomes a bear

E9N.definition_eng: Man marries a seal, dolphin or porpous who takes guise of a woman and lives with her in the human world

E9P.definition_eng: Man marries a bee who becomes a woman or a woman who becomes a bee

F1.name_eng: First woman is a transformed man
F1.definition_eng: Woman, female supernatural or animal females are created by changing the sex of a man (or male animals)

F10.definition_eng: Woman has another toothed mouth (usually in vagina) or biting animals in vagina. Man inserts there a stone, bone, stick, etc. breaking or knocking out the teeth or extracting from there dangerous animals

F100.name_eng: Test of chastity (a queen and a servant girl)
F100.definition_eng: A magic medicine demonstrates that the only chaste woman is not the one who was supposed to be

F100A.definition_eng: To revive a man or to extract an arrow point from his body, a chaste woman or girl must touch his body or step over him

F100B.definition_eng: Thanks to her chastity, a woman is able to do something that others cannot do but she does it only when a minor misdeed of her youth comes up to her

F101.name_eng: The rival woman tries to prevent the heroine to give birth
F101.definition_eng: Using magic, the rival woman tries to prevent the heroine to give birth

F11.definition_eng: Penis is biting, stinging, eats food

F12.name_eng: Man kills his wife with her lover’s penis
F12.definition_eng: Man kills his wive inserting into her body the cut off penis of her lover

F13.definition_eng: Human or monkey's genitals becomes red after being injured during copulation with the girl who had toothed vagina or had not any vagina

F14.name_eng: Son of a man and a rock
F14.definition_eng: Hero is born by a rock that was impregnated by a man

F14A.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic person appears from a rock, is born by a it

F15.name_eng: Person’s penis sticks out of the ground
F15.definition_eng: Person sticks out of the ground his penis that looks like a plant (provoking a woman to sit on it)

F16.name_eng: Men and women: exchange of anatomical characteristics
F16.definition_eng: Initially men possessed women's biological traits and vice versa (beard, menses, breasts, bearing children)

F16A.definition_eng: Men had menstruations or it was planned to be so

F16B.name_eng: Men fed babies with the breast milk
F16B.definition_eng: Men fed babies with their breast milk

F16C.definition_eng: Women had beard and/or men had not

F16D.definition_eng: n the past, babies were born by the men and not by the women

F17.definition_eng: Originally, humans had (had to have; can have under some special confition) their genitals not on the place where they are now; the genitals were absent, or people did not know know their function and used for copulation other parts of the body

F18A.definition_eng: Penis is so long that he can turn it round his waist or send into a woman who is at a long distance from him. (Only texts considered to describe real events and beings and not anecdotes are included)

F18B.definition_eng: After contact with a non-human or prohibited partner (close kin, animal, spirit) man's penis becomes so long that he had to carry it in a basket, etc.

F18C.definition_eng: Seeing a girl on the opposite bank of a river, person uses tricks to have sex with her: sends his long penis, transforms his penis into a bridge or a dam, dives and copulates with a girl from under the water

F18D.definition_eng: Female genitals are as long as a big snake

F19.definition_eng: After copulation with a frog, man's penis is injured

F2.definition_eng: Child is born from a tumor or swelling on person's body (on thigh, knee, finger, etc.) or is temporarily placed there or child grows from blood that flew out from a cut

F20.definition_eng: Man and woman embrace each other forever or for a long time

F20A.definition_eng: Initially, people copulated like dogs and dogs did it like now do humans

F21.name_eng: Woman turns into a tree, penis captured
F21.definition_eng: Man copulates with a woman who turns into tree or rock, his penis is captured in it

F22.definition_eng: Person asks another person of the opposite sex about destination or place of her or his genitals. Usually it is made after putting questions about function of other body parts; or person tries to use for sex different parts of the partner's body or tests them before reaching the best place where the genitals should be put

F23.definition_eng: Women menstruate because they bled in primeval time after the first defloration

F24.definition_eng: Women bleed because fish or snake bites them. Usually it is invisible fish inside their body

F25.name_eng: Origin of menses: girl smeared with blood
F25.definition_eng: Woman is smeared with blood or red paint. Since then women menstruate

F26.name_eng: Origin of menses: sacred objects lost
F26.definition_eng: The transition of sacred sound instruments (bull-roarers, big trumpets, etc.) from women to men is connected with beginning of menses among the women

F27.definition_eng: For girls and young women it is dangerous to come near water. Water creatures swallow them or drag away; a girl can die or become pregnant from a spirit; she can trigger a flood (rare: other cataclysm). Water spirits can come themselves to a girl who has her periods

F28.definition_eng: The penis is a particular monstrous being with whom copulate the primeval women, the amazons, or a certain woman

F28A.name_eng: Primeval penis grows from the ground
F28A.definition_eng: There is only one monstrous penis, a husband of primeval women or the amazons, which grows out of the ground or out of the water in a lake

F28A1.definition_eng: Alive penis exists as a separate being able to move and attack people

F28A2.definition_eng: The owner of a field answers (intentionally or because he does not hear well) that he is cultivating penises. After this penises grow on his field instead of plants

F28A3.name_eng: Nice for the girl, dangerous for the people
F28A3.definition_eng: An object possessed by a girl (woman) is nice (useful) for her but getting to somebody’s hands it becomes harmful (dangerous)

F28A4.definition_eng: Penises are fruits or shoots of plants

F28B.definition_eng: Certain woman masturbates with a penis made of wax, gourd, wood, radish, etc. Usually her husband or male relative smears it with chile; the woman is hurt or killed

F28C.name_eng: Bear penis in hands of old woman
F28C.definition_eng: Woman masturbates with penis of a big animal killed by a man of her household

F28D.definition_eng: Woman conceives after masturbating with an artificial penis

F29.definition_eng: A girl or young woman who is usually occupied with domestic work (is cooking, weaving, etc.) sits on the ground and copulates with a penis-like creature that crawls from below into her vagina

F29A.definition_eng: To kill snake or worm paramour of a woman or girl, person pours on it boiling water, resin or spills live coals

F2A.name_eng: The wrong way to be born
F2A.definition_eng: Child is born not in a normal way but intentionally cutting his mother’s body. It is a sign of his malicious and/or supernatural nature

F3.name_eng: A man eats woman’s pregnancy medicine
F3.definition_eng: A man gives birth after accidentally eating pregnency medicine. The child appears from a swelling on his leg or otherwise but the man remains alive

F30.definition_eng: A woman or a girl takes a snake, an eel (i.e. Pacific snake-eel), a lizard, or a worm for husband or paramour. People kill or badly injure him, the woman and/or her progeny or the woman herself is transformed into snake. Cf. motif k76b: the snake-husband becomes and remains a handsome man

F30A.definition_eng: Woman is nursing a worm (caterpillar, reptile, fish) as her baby. People kill the monster

F31.definition_eng: Girl or woman is imperceptibly impregnated by snake when the content of a broken egg of a snake flows into her vagina or when she touches a dead snake

F32.definition_eng: Baby child or children who come out of mother's womb and turn themselves into adult men or a snake who lives in her womb climb up a tree and help the woman to gather fruits, bark, edible fungi, etc. Usually the child who is a snake returns to his mother's womb and adult man turns back into a baby; or the girl's love affair with a snake is discovered when her father climbs a tree to gather fruits for her

F33.definition_eng: Certain woman or a group of women take for paramour a big water animal (caiman, otter, sea-lion, whale, anaconda; rare: water bird, crab), water spirit or monster. Husbands, brothers or (adoptive) children kill or maim paramour and/or (sometimes) the woman

F34.definition_eng: Certain woman or a group of women takes for a paramour a big land animal. Husbands, brothers or (adoptive) children kill or maim paramour and (sometimes) the woman

F34A.definition_eng: Women of the primeval community or amazons have one non-human paramour for all or simultaneously copulate with animals of particular specie whom they summon using special sygnal

F34B.name_eng: The paramour is an animal or a monster
F34B.definition_eng: A girl (a woman, a group of women) intentionally takes a penis-being, a snake, an eel, a lizard, a worm, a big water animal or water monster or a big terrestrial mammal for paramour. People kill or maim the paramour, the woman and/or her progeny or she is transformed herself into an animal. She is blamed for her behavior

F34B1.name_eng: Strange marriage: the woman and the bear
F34B1.definition_eng: A woman takes a bear for paramour. A man (several men) kill or mame it

F34B2.name_eng: Strange marriage: the woman and the deer
F34B2.definition_eng: A woman takes a deer for paramour. A man (several men) kill of mame it

F34B3.name_eng: Strange marriage: the woman and the tapir
F34B3.definition_eng: A woman takes a tapir for paramour. A man (several men) kill of mame it

F34B4.name_eng: Strange marriage: the woman and the jaguar
F34B4.definition_eng: A woman takes a jagyar for paramour. A man (several men) kill of mame it

F34B5.name_eng: Strange marriage: the woman and the crocodile (cayman)
F34B5.definition_eng: A woman takes a crocodile (cayman) for paramour. A man (several men) kill of mame it

F35.definition_eng: Person feeds another with the meat of his or her sexual partner who cooks or eats it without knowing whose meat it is

F35A.definition_eng: Person does not know that he or she eats or cooks the meat of the member of his or her household (blood relation, more rare a spouse or servant) or serves it to his or her friends, or uses her or his bones for everyday needs, or slowly kills him ort her

F36.definition_eng: The (adoptive) children or grandchildren and not person's spouse or brother kill the paramour of their (step)mother or father

F37.name_eng: Gourd vessel put on the surface of water
F37.definition_eng: Person knocks the gourd vessel (that floats above the water) to call water monster or serpent. Usually a woman calls this way her monstrous paramour

F38.definition_eng: Women were possessors of the sacred knowledge, sanctuaries or ritual objects which are now taboo for them or they made attempts to acquire such a knowledge or objects

F39.definition_eng: The women dominated over the men in the past or in a far away land, were the active part in marriage relations, practiced activities which now are reserved of the men only. Or the women could obtained supremacy but failed to do it for some reason

F3A.definition_eng: A man carries a child like a woman

F4.definition_eng: In the beginning of times, a particular person or children in general was or were conceived and grown up in pots, heaps of mud, etc. and not in a womb

F40A.definition_eng: An anthropomorphic male or an androgyne is the only possessor or leader of women

F40B.name_eng: A man in a village of women
F40B.definition_eng: A man gets into the village of women. Usually he has to satisfy every woman against his will or every woman claims him for herself

F40C.definition_eng: A powerful man kills every baby boy born by his wives or by his sister

F41.definition_eng: The men of primeval community kill the women because of their unsocial behavior

F42.definition_eng: The men feel themselves offended by the women and abandon them

F42A.name_eng: Men or women turn into birds
F42A.definition_eng: Either young men and boys or women turn into birds or bats and fly away

F43.definition_eng: The women of the ancestral community kill or abandon the men

F43A.definition_eng: The women of the ancestral community kill, try to kill or transform the men

F43B.definition_eng: When women of the ancestral community abandon the men, they disappear in the opening that leads underground

F43C.definition_eng: Marriage partners of the primeval women, the amazons or a solitary woman are small animals (usually flying foxes)

F44.definition_eng: The women and the men of the primeval community quarrel and abandon each other

F45.definition_eng: There are (or were) women who live apart from men in their own village or villages

F45A.definition_eng: A woman or a female animal is impregnated deliberately exposing her genitals to the wind

F45A1.definition_eng: A woman is impregnated by wind in defiance of her wish

F45B.definition_eng: A woman gives birth to a son after being impregnated by the sun(shine) or sun(beam)

F46.definition_eng: In the beginning of time two or more men (animal people) have only one woman

F46A.definition_eng: Men (animal people) discover a woman in a tree and copulate with her there

F47.name_eng: Pieces of flesh turn to people
F47.definition_eng: A living creature or a lump of alive flesh is cut into pieces which are diepersed around. After some time every piece turns into human being

F47A.name_eng: Men use pieces of woman’s flesh
F47A.definition_eng: Every man uses for copulation certain part of an only woman or takes a part of her body after it was cut into pieces

F47B.name_eng: New people on the old place
F47B.definition_eng: To create the new people (new women) instead of those who were destructed, person puts down in every empty hut (hearth, hammock) something (feathers, pieces of flesh) from which new people (new women) emerge

F48.definition_eng: Different women are not similar physically because pieces of the first woman's flesh distributed between men were of unequal quality or because males who copulated with her had different nature

F49.definition_eng: Cesarean operation upon a woman at childbirth as a custom

F49A.name_eng: Animal explains how to give birth
F49A.definition_eng: A small animal (mouse, rat, rabbit, opossum, a bird) explains a woman how she can deliver her child in a natural way

F5.definition_eng: Person cannot or do not want to give his daughters in marriage to all the men who claim them for wives and transforms animals into girls. (Usually in the beginning of times or after the flood many men come to marry the only daughter of God or patriarch)transforms animals into girls

F50.definition_eng: Child or children come out of mother's womb and return back

F51.definition_eng: Person who conceals his or her identity comes to his or her lover (at night). Next time, the lover puts a mark on the stranger's face, body or clothes doing this intentionally (to recognize him or her) or by chance (that leads to the identification)

F51A.definition_eng: When incest relations with her brother come to light, the sister openly claims her brother for a husband, turns into monster, kills people

F51B.definition_eng: To get know the nature or locality of a person, another fastens a thread to his body and follows it

F51C.definition_eng: When a girl gets to know that her night visitor was her own brother, she demonstrates him her genitals or her nake breasts and suggests to take what he had been desired so much. After this she runs away and he pursues her

F51D.definition_eng: The ginseng roots are boys or girls who help the hero

F52.name_eng: Pubic hair for a bird’s crest
F52.definition_eng: A bird person gets his crest putting on his head a pubic hair of a woman or part of her genitals

F53.definition_eng: An ugly man marries a girl but conceals his face. Marriage is ruined after his face is seen

F53A.name_eng: Bat or owl hides his face
F53A.definition_eng: A man hides his face from his wife because she does not know that he is a nocturnal being (a bat or an owl)

F54.definition_eng: A young man and a woman (Konkani: a young girl and a man) marry and later get to know that they commited incest

F54A.definition_eng: After a rather long marriage, wife discovers some minor traits in her husband guise that help her understand that he is not a proper marriage partner but her close kin (brother, son or father) or a transformed animal; or a man getting to notice a scar on his wife’s head understands that she is his sister

F54B.definition_eng: A youth or boy decorated with feathers and paint copulates incognito with his mother or sister. They discover his identity noticing on his body traces of feathers or paint

F54C.definition_eng: Husband notices imprints of finger-nails on his wife’s face and assembles all the men to recongize the culprit

F54D.definition_eng: Woman gives birth to a boy after unwittingly drinking urine of a he-animal or she-animal gives birth to a boy drinking urine of a man

F54E.definition_eng: A young man kills somebody and later gets to know that ut was his father

F55.definition_eng: A woman cannot understand what does her partner want. She points at, names or suggests different things. At last she points at, names or exposes her genitals. This is the right answer

F55A.name_eng: To put an object on her naked body (the demon and the woman)
F55A.definition_eng: A demon forces a woman to show him a particular part of her body because certain object should be put only there. He kills the woman pulling this part of her body out. Usually the woman serves or names different places and the demon rejects each one before the the place he wants is opened

F56.definition_eng: A man or boy thinks about incest when he gets to see his daughter(-in-law)'s, sister's, or mother(in-law)'s vagina

F56A.definition_eng: To create opportunity to see female genitals, a man throws something combustible into the fire which makes the woman fall on her back and expose her vagina

F57.definition_eng: A girl or her father (rare: mother) picks a plant (usually a flower) and because of this encounters a person who has non-human guise and/or is related to the underworld. The girl marries him. In some cases the flower is the person’s hair but more often it’s not so

F58.definition_eng: A man cohabits with a group of women (or with several women in succession) concealing his identity and/or intentions. He is either eventually exposed and punished by women or escapes to continue his tricks

F59.definition_eng: To make believe that he is a female, a trickster transforms particular objects or creatures into female body parts or into a baby child

F5A.definition_eng: When God intends to create Eve from Adam’s rib, an animal (dof, cat, monkey, fox, snake) or a devil steals it. God (or his angel) pursues it and catches its tail. The tail tears off, God creates Eve from it. Or God made Eve from edible material and a dog devoured it, so God had to make Eve from Adam’s rib. Or God cut off Adam’s tail and made Eve from it.

F5B.definition_eng: Person suffests another a woman but does not have any or does not want to give her. He makes artificial girl (of wood, snow, etc.), sends servant girl instead of his daughter, turns into a woman himself, or recognizes his fault when he feels that it is save to do so

F6.definition_eng: Woman has no vagina and it is later made by bird or animal

F60.definition_eng: A girl gets sick. A man comes to cure her but only copulates with her or makes an attempt to do so

F61.name_eng: Trickster rapes a woman who carries him on her back
F61.definition_eng: A man pretends to be weak, ill or injured, asks a woman to carry him on her back. When she agrees, he makes attempt to copulate with her

F62.definition_eng: An (ostensibly) sick (ugly, weak, poorly clad) person remains at home when others go to the feast. The person comes by himself or herself looking like a handsome man or beautiful girl. The man (woman) does not recognize him (her) and feels against her (him) sexual interestю (All texts with motif k57, Chinderella, are also included into f62)

F63.name_eng: Trickster poses as woman and marries man
F63.definition_eng: A male person turns into woman and marries a man. He is either unmasked or abandons his "husband" by his own will

F64.definition_eng: Person changes his or (rare) her guise to marry his or her close relative in descending or (rare) ascending line

F64A.definition_eng: Going away or pretending to die, a person bids his or her relative to marry another person who resembles him (her) or has some special traits; or he describes a man who should be met as a dear guest; person comes himself unrecognized and is taken for one whom he had described

F64B.definition_eng: A woman pretends to be a stranger to have sexual relations with her (grand)son, daughter or brother

F65.definition_eng: To realize his or her secret desire (illicit sex, refusal to share food with relations), person pretends to die and is abandoned at a burial place

F65A.definition_eng: Person pretends to die. His or her wife or husband abandons him or her on a burial place. He or she marries his or her paramour

F65B.name_eng: Death feigned to eat burial food
F65B.definition_eng: Man pretends to die because he does not want to share food with the others and eats it alone at his burial place

F65C.name_eng: The feigned burial: boy exposes deceit
F65C.definition_eng: A man feigns death to marry his daughter or to eat burial food. One of the younger children recognizes the (adoptive) father or gets to see that the false dead is alive (escapes from the burial pyre, laughs, etc.)

F65D.name_eng: The feigned burial: wife does not believe
F65D.definition_eng: A man feigns death and is abandoned at the burial place. His wife (mother, aunt) gets to know about the deceit and provokes the man to show that he is alive

F66.definition_eng: Person’s father, grandson, brother, or sister pretends to be a stranger to commit incest (accordingly with the daughter, grandmother, sister, or brother), or a husband shams to be his wife’s brother because he wants to be taken by her as her blood relative. To realize his or her stratagem, the hero imperceptibly runs to another house where the object of his or her interest later comes and takes him or her for a stranger

F67.name_eng: Old woman pretends to be man
F67.definition_eng: An old woman makes herself false penis and testicles, marries or attempts to marry her (step)daughter

F68.name_eng: Death feigned: woman dresses up as a man
F68.definition_eng: A woman pretends to die or really dies. Her (former) paramour comes to her grave. She revives and goes with him. Not to be recognized, she dresses up as a man

F69.definition_eng: A woman's husband or male relative asks her (grand)children to invite her to make love with him. The invitation is expressed in an allegoric form. She understands, comes to him

F7.definition_eng: Man takes or attempts to take a wife who is connected with the underwater world (fish, crab, snake, water animal and the like)

F70.name_eng: Potiphar's wife: false accusation of sexual abuse
F70.definition_eng: Woman makes vain overtures to young man and/or falsely accuses him of sexual abuse. Her husband believes that the young man is guilty, kills or tries to kill him

F70A.name_eng: Disordered clothes as evidence against innocent man
F70A.definition_eng: To accuse a man or boy of (sexual) abbuse, a woman tears her clothes, smears or scratches her body pretending to be attacked

F70B.definition_eng: A woman revenges on a man who rejected her love but necessary not pretends to be an object of sexual harassment from his part

F70C.name_eng: The castrated youth becomes a man again
F70C.definition_eng: A young man is castrated but his member is restored by magic (and he marries happily)

F70D.definition_eng: A castrate or girl pretends to be a man or a cripple girl conceles her injury or a man pretends to be a girl. Some person gets to know about it and plans to expose the deception. At the last moment the hero or heroine magically becomes a real man (or girl; gets back the lost members) and the informer is disgraced

F70E.name_eng: A girl turns into a man
F70E.definition_eng: A girl poses as a man, her sex is magically transformed and the man is happily married

F70E1.name_eng: A daughter instead of a son
F70E1.definition_eng: An old man needs a son to accomplish a man’s work or service. (Only the youngest) daughter sets to do it (successfully passing her father’s test and) guised as a man

F70E2.name_eng: Father tests his daughters or sons
F70E2.definition_eng: Father sends his daughters or sons to carry out a difficult task. At the very beginning their courage is tested. Only the youngest son or the youngest daughter passes the test successfully. Usually father takes guise of a robber or a predator animal and charges but only the youngest son or the youngest daughter is not scared.

F70F.definition_eng: Getting into a far away place, person discovers that his or her sex is changed

F71.name_eng: Susan and the old men (the innocent slandered maiden)
F71.definition_eng: An innocent girl or young woman rejects a man who attempts to seduce her. The man accuses her of loose conduct, ultimately the truth comes to light

F72.definition_eng: A woman asks a man to tie her before copulation in such a way that a watcher would think she is raped

F73A.name_eng: Vulva is or thought to be wound
F73A.definition_eng: Vulva is a unhealed wound on the body of the primeval women or the primval people had no sex mistaking vulva for a wound

F73B.name_eng: The bear beliefs that vulva is a wound
F73B.definition_eng: The bear (wolf, lion, dragon) beliefes that vulva is a wound.

F74.definition_eng: When a person sees a dangerous enemy, he or she shams dead taking his or her clothes off, or the enemy takes off them himself. The enemy believes that it is a corpse, lets it alone

F75.definition_eng: A hunter watches tapir who calls a water woman from the river or lake and copulates with her. Hunter does the same, becomes the woman's lover

F76.definition_eng: People learn to copulate after they see birds, fish or animals doing it

F77A.definition_eng: Penis is stretched across a body of water as a pole or bridge

F78.definition_eng: Person or creature has toothed anus or second head in place of the anus

F79.definition_eng: Person marries several non-human wives in succession, every time (besides the last one) is disappointed

F8.definition_eng: Initially women and men live apart from each other. Later they meet each other and become to live together

F80.definition_eng: The first men and/or women have no genitals

F80A.definition_eng: Genitals exist by themselves as separate beings, they can be stuck to the human body, remove, etc.

F81.definition_eng: A man mistakes his own reflection in river for a beautiful woman and makes attempts to marry her

F82.definition_eng: A man uses a trick to have opportunity to make love to his mother-in-law or woman uses a trick to make love to her son-in-law. Usually a man takes with him on a hunt not his wife but her mother

F82A.definition_eng: To lure prohibited sexual partner into his or her hammock, person imitates or interpretes in a certain way voices of birds and animals

F83.definition_eng: Person commits something shameful, obscene. Presumably, nobody could see him doing it. When he asks people, "What's the news?", they answer that so-and-so (this person) has done such a thing

F83A.definition_eng: Animal person comes to children of a big predator and tells them that he will copulate with their mother (or that he will beat her)

F83B.name_eng: The stuck between trees she animal is raped
F83B.definition_eng: A strong she animal pursues a weaker one male but is stuck netweem trees or stones. The male taunts (usually rapes) her

F84.definition_eng: Person has sex with the wife of his host or brother. Trying to conceal his deed, he puts ashes or juice of a fruit on his glans that has to prove his long celibacy

F85.name_eng: The Moon: contra men and pro women
F85.definition_eng: The Moon (female or male) is the leader of women in their struggle against the men or leads the women away from the men

F86.definition_eng: Person summons with a certain signal a non-human being (usually his or her sexual partner or his or her protégé). Another person spies, uses the same signal or pronounces the same words and kills the being who comes to him (or uses this being sexually himself)

F86A.definition_eng: Person take care for a fish, crab or other small creature. Another person spies on him or her, kills the pet and eats it up or try to do it

F87.definition_eng: A serpent creates stuation when a girl must promise to marry him, and takes her to his realm. After some time she comes with her children to visit her relations. Her close kin (father, mother, brother) gets to know from her children how their mother calls her husband, summons the serpent with the same signal and kills him. Seeing her husband dead, the woman transforms her children (and herself) into birds or trees

F87A.name_eng: Snake’s wife and her children: transformation into birds
F87A.definition_eng: A snake crawls on the clothes of a bathing girl and lets her take them not before she gives a promice to marry him. He takes her to the underwater world. She is happy and they have children. She visits her kin taking her children with her. Her relations summon the snake and kill him. After this his wife transforms their childred and/or herself into birds

F87B.name_eng: Snake’s wife and her children: transformation into trees
F87B.definition_eng: A snake crawls on the clothes of a bathing girl and lets her take them not before she gives a promice to marry him. He takes her to the underwater world. She is happy and they have children. She visits her kin taking her children with her. Her relations summon the snake and kill him. After this his wife transforms their childred and/or herself into trees

F88.definition_eng: Initially women's genitals were fragrant or had no smell. Because of a bad chance they acquire unpleasant odor or do not acquire fragrant odor

F89.definition_eng: Sister and brother live alone. The brother rejects the incest. The sister makes him take her for unknown girl, marries him

F9.definition_eng: For different reasons, sexual contact with a woman is deadly dangerous for a man

F90.definition_eng: Brother and sister marry each other. When their children get to know about the incest, they kill their parents, or father kills children, or parents suicide, or wife/sister suicides when her husband/brother has died

F91.definition_eng: A man lets his wife to be eaten up by worms. She either dies or has a narrow escape

F92.definition_eng: A male person is tricked into being used sexually by another man

F93.definition_eng: After a man commits some act, his penis begins to speak (often: repeats all his words)

F93A.definition_eng: A man's member speaks and can be silenced only by his mother-in-law

F94.definition_eng: A man gets to the sky where he has a choice to marry one of two women, one of them being connected with life and another with death

F95.name_eng: Wife of one of two brothers
F95.definition_eng: Two companions or brothers live together. One has a wife which he conceals. Another suspects her existence, destroys her or tries to get a wife also for himself

F96.definition_eng: A girl (wife) rejects an ugly youth (her husband). He becomes handsom (usually thanks to the help of a supernatural person). Those who were evil to him are punished

F97.name_eng: The prohibited fruit: origin of sex
F97.definition_eng: After eating certain fruit, berry, tuber, etc. people become sexually aware

F97A.name_eng: Snake is deprived of its limbs
F97A.definition_eng: Being responsible for breaking food tabou by humans, snake lost its limbs as a punishment

F98.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic god descends from the sky and copulates with a cow

F99.definition_eng: A baby son turns into an adult man, copulates with his mother, then acquires his baby guise

F9A.definition_eng: There are teeth, blades or sharp stones in woman’s genitals, vagina is the biting mouth. (Only texts that are believed to correspond to reality are considered but not anecdotes and jokes)

F9A1.definition_eng: A woman pretends that her vagina is a mouth with teeth. (It is not suggested that women’s genitals are really dangerous)

F9B.definition_eng: Biting piranha is in woman's genitals

F9C.definition_eng: Snake (Pacific snake-eel in Polynesia) is in vagina; around the woman's thighs; vagina is a mouth of a snake; a woman with toothed vagina is associated with a snake; a snake crawls out of woman's mouth to bite off the man’s penis during the copulation

F9D.definition_eng: Small creatures in female or male genitals are dangerous for the partner

F9E.definition_eng: There are small mammals with sharp teeth in woman's genitals.

F9E1.definition_eng: Woman is dangerous because biting or stinging animal or animals is (are) inside her genitals (and not only the head of such an animal)

F9F.definition_eng: Demon (snake) regularly kills woman’s husbands during the first night, the woman herself being ignorant about the reason of their death

F9F1.definition_eng: Poisonous snake (snakes, scorpions) comes out of the mouth of a woman {Motif F9f1 and K100c are almost identical but F9f1 links to a cluster of etiological/cosmological motifs related to the idea of a dangerous woman while K100c is related to adventures}

F9F2.name_eng: Hood of cobra in wife's bag
F9F2.definition_eng: Woman’s snake paramour is killed. She puts part of his body into her bag and gets a right to kill her husband if he woulod not guess what is inside. At the last moment the husband gets to know the secret and kills the woman

F9G.definition_eng: A strong woman overcomes and kills suitors. Hero or his helper tames her (usually whips in the wedding night). The hero marries her

F9G1.name_eng: A heavy hand of the bride
F9G1.definition_eng: In the first marriage night, the bride that has supernatural strength thrusts her weight upon her bridegroom to suffocate him

G1.definition_eng: Valuables (earth, soil, sun, crops, fire, sacred knowledge, hunting luck) are got or returned when son or daughter is stolen from his or her parent

G10.definition_eng: A tree which trunk is cut through do not fall because it is hold from above

G11.definition_eng: A squirrel plays crucial role in felling the gigantic tree

G12.definition_eng: A giant tree (often with water inside it or with different cultivated plants on its branches) grows out of the human body or is transformed person

G12A.definition_eng: Cultivated plants emerge from drops of blood or spill from cuts on the body of a person or animal

G12B.definition_eng: Star-person is a giver of cultivated plants

G12C.name_eng: Fox brings plants from the sky
G12C.definition_eng: Fox or coyote returns from the sky and disperses seeds or shoots unknown on earth before

G13.definition_eng: Before acquisition of cultivated plants people ate rotten or soft (Ceiba L., Ochroma Sw.) wood; some people eat rotten wood

G13A.definition_eng: Before acquisition of cultivated plants (fire, hunting skills) people ate dirt, mud or stones

G13B.definition_eng: Before acquisition of cultivated plants people ate fungi. Fingi is a food of non-human beings. Fungi is a false food of inferior quality

G13C.name_eng: Bad food of the pre-agricultural epoch
G13C.definition_eng: Before the cultivated plants or edible wild plants become known, people ate (decomposed) wood, bark, mud, stones, fungi

G14.definition_eng: A man is swallowed by a water monster and comes out from its belly in the land of the supernatural beings. He receives from them cultivated plants and brings them to people

G15.definition_eng: In the other world or in the time of the ancestors food products or materials used by people looked as persons

G16.definition_eng: Ants are the first who find cultivated plants (corn or manioc) which are concealed from the others in particular place

G17.definition_eng: Serpent (snake-eel in Oceania) or alligator is the original possessor or the source of cultivated plants or wild staples

G18.definition_eng: A person asks people to abandon him or her in the forest, to burn or drag him or her around the future garden plot, to burn her in her house, etc. People fulfill the person's wish and find cultivated plants growing on the place

G19.definition_eng: After a conflict in primeval community, a group of men or youths (Paresi: a boy and a girl) burned themselves in a bonfire (or leap over it, etc.). As a result, people acquire cultivated plants, especially corn

G2.definition_eng: Person who is the incarnation of fertility and life first disappears and then (reriodically) returns

G20.definition_eng: Food crops emerge from remains of a woman or girl

G21.name_eng: Coconut palm from a human head
G21.definition_eng: Coconut palm grows out of the human head

G22.definition_eng: Frog or toad is related to acquisition of cultivated plants

G23.name_eng: Alive being turns into many objects
G23.definition_eng: Person or creature is transformed. Separate parts of its (his, her) body give origin to different objects or creatures (only etiological narratives are considered)

G23A.definition_eng: Person or creature is transformed. Separate parts of its (his, her) body give origin to different plants, mostly edible or cultivated

G23B.definition_eng: Different body parts of a being turn into people of different ethnic affiliation or such people receive their names and characteristics according to body parts that they got

G24.definition_eng: First seeds (sprouts, tubors) of cultivated plants or of important edible wild plants are brought from the sky (received from the sky-dwellers)

G24A.name_eng: Seeds of plants hidden on the body
G24A.definition_eng: Person steals cultivated plants for the people hiding the seeds on/in his body

G25.definition_eng: Seeds of cereals have been spilled over the earth, now people cultivate them

G26.definition_eng: Food products were swallowed or hidden in person's mouth. Thanks to this people got them

G27.definition_eng: Person urinates producing the first cultivated plants

G28.definition_eng: Tree contains fish in its trunk

G29.definition_eng: Demonic person turns into or consists of different household objects or tools (and into elements of a landscape)

G3.definition_eng: Cultivated plants or fertile soil to plant them are hidden inside a rock. Birds or Thunders get them destroying the rock

G30.definition_eng: A cut off long penis turns into many edible plants or fifferent trees

G31.name_eng: Trees tied up with a rope
G31.definition_eng: Persons put a rope around many trees and fells them all together or pretends to do it

G3A.definition_eng: Original grains of rice or corn were burned to different degree and because of this different sorts of cultivated plants have grains of different colour

G4.definition_eng: Cultivated plants are found above or inside a mountain

G5.definition_eng: Fruits and shoots of different cultivated plants grow on the branches of one tree (on one vine) or certain plant has a tree form that is alien to it in nature

G6.definition_eng: One of the trees is the principal, original one (emerged before all the other; ancestor of wild or cultivated plants; ocean or rivers inside it; world axis; higher than all the others; overshadows sky)

G6A.definition_eng: Year is described as a tree with the number of branches, twigs, leaves etc. corresponding to the number of seasons, months, days, etc.

G7.definition_eng: Ancestors try to fell a tree (more rare a high rock) that has different useful fruits on its branchs (on its top) or contains water and fish in its tunck. The notch disappears as soon as the woodcutters abandon their work for a while or periodically

G8.definition_eng: A deep notch in the tree (or in the sky support) is magically restored as soon as persons or creatures who cut or gnaw it stop working

G8A.name_eng: Cutting tree to make a canoe
G8A.definition_eng: To make some object (usually a canoe), person cuts a tree, goes away, returns, finds the tree intact. Usually another person who was restoring the tree by magic fells it down himself and makes a canoe for the hero

G8B.name_eng: Cutting tree to get a person
G8B.definition_eng: Person hides in a tree. Somebody tries to fell it but the notch disappears and the tree becomes intact

G8C.definition_eng: (Animal-)people try to fell a tree that contains water and fish or has cultivated plants on its branches. The notch disappears and the tree becomes intact

G8D.name_eng: Falling or growing up of a tree is dangerous to the world
G8D.definition_eng: To save the world (gods, king, etc.) certain persons or creatures try to cut or gnaw a tree (post, mountain) or do not permit the others to do. The notch disappears and the tree (post, etc.) becomes intact

G8E.definition_eng: Person tries to cut down the tree in the Moon but the notch disappears and the tree becomes intact

G8F.definition_eng: A deep notch in the tree is magically restored when persons or creatures who cut it go away to take a rest. They get to fell the tree after they begin to burn the cut off chips or to carry them far way

G8G.definition_eng: There is a tree, one of its kind, that should be cut or bended down. Particular creatures or beings live in its different parts and/or special objects of top significance are made from its wood

G9.definition_eng: People fell trees to make a garden. In the morning, the forest is intact again

G9A.name_eng: Cultivated field turns into the virgin soil
G9A.definition_eng: People break ground but in the morning it is intact again

G9B.name_eng: Abandon your work, flood is coming
G9B.definition_eng: A man fells trees to clear ground for a garden or breaks ground. Certain person or animal revives vegetation, makes the soil virgin again. He or she explains that the flood is coming, there is no sense to work and advices to prepare a floating device

H10.definition_eng: People are mortal because stone thrown into the water sank. They have missed a chance to be like wood or other organic matter that floated

H11.definition_eng: People become mortal because they do not hear or answer a call of a being who promises them immortality (or do not pronounce his name) or answer a call (pronouns the name) of a being who brings death

H12.name_eng: The alive person comes to the land of the dead after somebody’s death
H12.definition_eng: The alive person comes to the land of the dead to bring back somebody who has recently died (besides stories about shamans who journey to the other world to bring back the soul of a sick person) or, having no particular aim, goes there in company of somebody who had recently died or following his or her tracks

H12A.definition_eng: Wife dies, husband comes after her or he kills his untrue wife. The dead wife turns into monster and pursues him

H12B.definition_eng: Inhabitants of the land of the dead eat excrements

H12C.name_eng: Orpheus: to return the dead wife
H12C.definition_eng: Husband follows his dead wife to the other world but is unable to bring her back or succeeds to do it but loses her once again

H13.name_eng: Dead person is returned and revives
H13.definition_eng: Person comes to the land of the dead and brings back somebody who has recently died or brings his remains. The dead one becomes alive and lives normal life (for some time)

H14.name_eng: Woman flies back to the land of the dead
H14.definition_eng: A dead woman returns to earth but flies back as a bird or a fly

H15.definition_eng: If called in a loud voice, ghosts do not hear an alive person but hear whisper, yawning, etc.

H16.definition_eng: Rivers of tears exist in the other world. Tears shed on earth fill there big containers

H16A.definition_eng: Rivers (lakes) of blood (also of puss, bones, sweat or water used for washing of corpses) are mentioned in narratives (in different context)

H16B.definition_eng: A river (wave, lake, basin) of milk that exists on earth (and not among the stars) is mentioned in narratives (in different context)

H17.name_eng: Ring of defenders around the chief
H17.definition_eng: Ancestors surround their (dead) chief trying to defend him or his corpse. A trickster gets to go through the ring, kills the chief or steals and devours his heart

H18.definition_eng: Game animals were concentrated in one single place. Certain person lets them disperse in the world

H18A.definition_eng: The owner of game animals conceals them underground. One of the ancestors turns into pup, is adopted by owners' children, lets the animals lose

H18B.definition_eng: After getting domestic animals from supernaturals a person immediately loses the animals or most of them (usually because of a broken taboo like to look, to speak in a loud voice, etc.; the animals disappear in water, remain in the sky, scatter in various directions, etc.)

H19.definition_eng: Raven hides or scares game animals preventing hunters to kill them. People outwit him

H1A.name_eng: The originator of death the first sufferer
H1A.definition_eng: One person wants man to live forever, another wants man to be mortal. When somebody dear to the latter one dies, he or she is eager to accept the suggestion of his or her opponent but the original decision cannot be changed

H1B.definition_eng: Person does something that makes death inevitable because the death of a child or a woman beloved by another person is indifferent or desirable for him or her

H1BB.definition_eng: Person refuses to revive a dog which is dear to another person, and this conflict is related to the missed opportunity to revive people

H1C.definition_eng: People do not come back to life after somebody buries the dead in the grave or stamps down the earth on the grave

H1D.name_eng: The first dead is rejected by the alive people
H1D.definition_eng: Person dies and returns soon but people send him or her back, refuse to accept as a member of their community or bury again. Since then death becomes permanent

H1E.name_eng: The first dead opens the road
H1E.definition_eng: After the first death the road to the realm of death remains open; certain person makes a road to the realm of death; the first person who had died becomes the ruler of the guard of the realm of death

H1F.name_eng: People learn how to bury the dead
H1F.definition_eng: People get to know what they should do with the dead body observing the behavios of a raven (crow)

H2.definition_eng: Animals ask God to make people mortal because people would be too numerous and step on the animals, deprive them of their food and habitat, or because the animals want to feast on the human corpses

H20.definition_eng: All the fish or (rare) shellfish) was concentrated in one place. Certain person lets it lose or puts it into the rivers or sea

H20A.definition_eng: A woman (a girl, several women) keeps all the fish for herself. Man comes and lets fish escape into rivers or sea.

H21.name_eng: Animals or fish kill a child
H21.definition_eng: Person possesses game animals or fish. A boy or a girl knows this secret or is used as a luring device. Another person asks or forces the boy or girl to serve him the same way or the boy himself makes an attempt to hunt or fish. As a result, the boy or girl is killed or carried away by animals or fish

H21A.name_eng: Not to kill a big fish

H22.definition_eng: Big game animals obtain sense of smell and/or become to escape from hunters after a person makes them olfactory organs or lets them feel strong odor

H22A.name_eng: Animals disperse after being touched by people
H22A.definition_eng: Big game animals were concentrated in one place, had no fear of people. They escape and disperse after somebody slightly strikes or stains them

H23.definition_eng: Objects (animal horns, tree fungi, heartwood) that are now stiff and inedible consisted of fat

H24.definition_eng: Container with valuables or with dangerous creatures is opened (before time). Its content goes out of control or disappear

H24A.definition_eng: Person opens a bag with stars which ascend to sky in disorder

H24B.name_eng: Souls disappear from the opened container
H24B.definition_eng: Person receives a container with the soul of a dead person and has to open it not before he gets to particular place or after particular time interval. He opens it too early, the soul fly away

H24C.definition_eng: People open container with death or disease inside and become mortal

H24D.name_eng: Still picks up what was let lose
H24D.definition_eng: Animal person who let lose the content of a container entrusted to him or her (darkness, insects, reptiles, etc.) still tries to pick up what was let lose (etiology of behavior of certain animal species)

H24E.definition_eng: People are suggested to choose one of two objects, associated with life and death. They choose the object with death

H24F.definition_eng: Person can magically put a lot of meat or fish into a small package or vessel which is easy to carry

H24G.definition_eng: A woman brought back from another world or received there disappears as soon as the man opens the box where she was

H25.definition_eng: People are suggested to choose one of two objects, associated with life and death. They choose the object with death

H26.definition_eng: The right way to dispose of container with stinging insects would be to throw it into the river or sea or bury in a far away place, but it was not done

H27.definition_eng: Stinging insects (rare diseases) had been inside a container or some enclosure. They escaped to the world when the container or enclosure was foolishly opened

H27A.name_eng: A hole through the ground made with a pole
H27A.definition_eng: The Creator's antagonist demands for himself as much ground as would be enough to put a pole or staff

H27A1.name_eng: Plagues emerge from a hole in the ground
