H28.name_eng: Plagues from the body of a person or creature
H28.definition_eng: Killed and destroyed (often burned) person or creature (usually ogre, fierce animal, powerful shaman) turns into a multitude of biting insects or into other small molesting creatures

H28A.definition_eng: A burned person or creature immediately turns into a multitude of mosquitoes or biting flies

H28B.definition_eng: The cut off hair from the aniaml hide (ash and smoke of the burned hide) turn into blood-sucking insects

H28C.definition_eng: Person creates blood-sucking insect to influence the behavior of the (potential) sex-partner

H29.definition_eng: A woman is impregnated by an animal, usually by a snake. People of hostile nation originate or receive their culture from her progeny or from her paramour's relatives

H3.definition_eng: People become mortal because they imitated real funerals burying an animal

H30.definition_eng: Seeing two women who have come together or in succession, man has to choose one of them. Usually he takes the one who is less pretty and smart or more dangerous inflicting troubles on himself and humanity

H31.name_eng: Origin of death: man and celestial bodies
H31.definition_eng: God summons to him man and celestial bodies and makes the man mortal and others immortal

H32A.definition_eng: Supernatural woman comes to live with humans. Thanks to that, food becomes easily available. She is maltreated, goes away, temporal superfertility is lost forever

H32B.definition_eng: A small girl or boy who is a child of a deity comes to live with humans. Thanks to that, food or other resources become easily available. The child is maltreated, returns to its own world, human life becomes difficult and scanty

H33.definition_eng: Children walked or could walk from the very birth but this ability was lost or never obtained

H33A.definition_eng: A woman did not allow God to throw her baby across a hedge, roof, etc. Because of this babies lost or never got ability to walk from the very birth

H34A.definition_eng: Person has a series of suggestions how to make the world easy for living and free of hard work and death. His companion successively rejects them. Their dialogue forever defines conditions of human life

H34B.definition_eng: Rivers were flowing or according to the original plan had to flow in both directions; somewhere there is a river that flows in both directions

H34C.definition_eng: Rice could flow arriving by itself to the household

H34D.definition_eng: Animal person climbs (or attempts to climb) to the sky or to the Moon to bite off a piece of it

H34D1.definition_eng: Sky or sky objects were edible but later this source of food became inaccessible or used only by the inhabitants of the distant land where the sky and the earth meet

H34E.definition_eng: Snow was edible or something edible was falling from the sky instead of the snow

H34G.definition_eng: One cereal grain (cob, etc.) is enough to prepare a meal

H34H.definition_eng: Firewood, brushwood arrived to the house themselves, no work was needed to cut and carry them

H35.definition_eng: Human teeth are made of material subject to easy damage (etiology of tooth ache in most cases)

H36.definition_eng: Person is sent by god to bring instructions or certain objects but distorts, forgets or replaces them. This has fatal consequences for humans or for a certain species of animals. (Lithuanian case can be a mistification)

H36A.name_eng: Origin of death from the falsified message
H36A.definition_eng: Person distorts instructions that he must pass to others, intentionally lies, forgets or replaces certain objects that must be given to others. Because of this human beings become mortal (do not revive after death)

H36B.definition_eng: Chameleon is responsible for introduction of permanent death or hard life; loses object that the deity trusted him to bring to the earth

H36C.definition_eng: Lizard is responsible for introduction of permanent death. (Lithuanian case can be a mistification)

H36D.definition_eng: Hare is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H36E.definition_eng: Rat is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H36F.definition_eng: Raven is sent to deliver important object or message. It distorts message, loses object

H36FF.definition_eng: Raven is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H36G.name_eng: Muddled message: how many meals a day
H36G.definition_eng: God sends his messenger to tell people that they should eat only rarely (once in three days or the like). The messenger tells them that they should eat often (three times a day)

H36G1.definition_eng: When the bull (ox, cow) is sent to deliver important message, he distorts them intentionally or by chance

H36G2.definition_eng: When person who was later transformed in the dung beatle was sent to the people to deliver important message, he distorted it

H36GG.definition_eng: Coyote is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H36H.definition_eng: Some beings, frog and toad among them, have to overcome an obstacle. This is realized not the way it was planned and as a consequence, people become mortal

H36HH.definition_eng: Frog or toad is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H36I.definition_eng: Goat or sheep is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H36J.definition_eng: Lark is responsible for introduction of permanent death

H37.name_eng: Magic device lost by a failure
H37.definition_eng: Magic object, device that makes hunting or fishing easy gets into possession of a person who is unable to operate it or abuses it. The device kills or injures the failure himself, other people and/or disappears

H37A.definition_eng: Person gives a trickster ability to kindle fire easily. He uses it without need, it is lost

H37B.name_eng: Charge of skunk used to no purpose
H37B.definition_eng: Person gives a trickster his power (usually skunk gives his charge) but he squanders it all to see the effect. When a real need comes, the device does not work anymore

H38.name_eng: Supernatural person comes after his property
H38.definition_eng: Supernatural person changes his guise and comes to the hero's children (more rare, to him). They hand him what he asks for and he disappears with his former property is

H39.definition_eng: Certain creatures (snakes, insects) get access to special substance that proved to be out of control and become poisonous or immortal; creatures obtain their characteristics (usually becomes poisonous) after drinking or licking a particular medicine

H4.definition_eng: Those who change their skin become young again

H40.name_eng: Dog is the guard of man
H40.definition_eng: Dog guards (successfully or unsuccessfully) the (still unfinished) physical body of man or the entrance to paradise

H40A.name_eng: Dog materializes at the moment of danger
H40A.definition_eng: When dangerous enemy is ready to attack, accidentally thrown objects or substances are transformed into a dog who drives the enemy away

H41.definition_eng: Dog is responsible for people being mortal or imperfect. Usually the antagonist bribes dog with a warm fur and the dog lets him spoil the half-ready human figures

H42.name_eng: Creator goes away for a while
H42.definition_eng: After creating the bodies of the first people or after getting a conception how to do it the Creator goes away for a while. During his absence another person, because of his or her ignorance or intentionally, spoils the creation or makes himself or herself what the Creator would make in a better way. Usually because of this people are mortal and subject to diseases

H43.name_eng: One creates the body, another the soul
H43.definition_eng: One supernatural creates the body of the first people, another revives them

H43A.name_eng: Broken figure of the first man
H43A.definition_eng: After making human body, creator goes away for a time. In his absence another person makes attempt to break human figure that was not yet alive

H43AA.name_eng: Figure of the first man smeared with filth
H43AA.definition_eng: After making human body, creator goes away for a time. In his absence another person spits on the human figure that was not yet alive, smears it with filth, etc.

H43AB.name_eng: Man is mortal because somebody spit on him
H43AB.definition_eng: Man is mortal because somebody spit on him when his figure was still in process of creation

H43AC.name_eng: Creator’s enemy animates human figures instead of him
H43AC.definition_eng: Creator made human figuers. When he goes away for a time, the anatagonist revives them instead of him. Because of this, humans are mortal (imperfect)

H44.name_eng: Demonic spouse cuts in two her offpring from human being
H44.definition_eng: Human person becomes a wife (husband) of a demonic being. When they part with each other, the demon cuts (wants to cut) their offpring in two

H44A.name_eng: Sky and Earth divide their children
H44A.definition_eng: Two persons, one of whom is connected with the sky (water, spirit world) and another with the earth (human world), divide their child or people created by them. Sky (spirit, Water) takes the imperishable part, and Earth (person), the perishable one

H45.definition_eng: A woman or child demonstrate no respect for bread soiling it with excrements. For this God punishes all the humanity

H46.definition_eng: Somebody (usually God) is going to deprive humans of their staple food (usually cereals) but does not do it thanks to the dog (and/or cat; rare – birds)

H46A.definition_eng: Properties of the cereals (usually the size of the spike) are defined by what the dog did in time of creation

H47.definition_eng: The sky (or the earth) is offended by people’s behavior in respect to it and reacts accordingly (e.g. rises higher than it was before)

H48.definition_eng: Diseases are sisters (rare: brothers), usually children of evil spirit

H49.definition_eng: A dog or other animal kills dangerous creature who was going to attack the child. The master thinks that the assailant was the pet and kills it

H49B.name_eng: The faithful dog as security for a debt
H49B.definition_eng: A man gives his dog to another man. The dog proves to be brave and intelligent (drives off thieves, finds stolen treasure). The man who received the dog sends it back with a message of thanks. The owner, thinking the dog has run away, kills it and after this finds the letter

H49C.definition_eng: A tame bird (more rare: domestic animal) seems to be aggressive against its master (usually a falcon knocks the cup from the hand of a thirsty king). The master kills the bird (animal) only to find that the it saved his life

H49D.definition_eng: A bird or a person brings fruit (seed, sprout) that makes people young (healthy). By chance or by evil intent the fruit becomes contaminated with poison. The man for whom the fruit had been brought kills (is going to kill) the helpful bird (person) and then discovers the truth

H4A.definition_eng: People do not become young (usually do not shed their skin) anymore because certain person was bothered during rejuvenation or was not recognized by his family in his new guise

H5.definition_eng: Reptiles or invertebrates possess the medicine of immortality; are contrasted with men as immortal with mortals and/or are responsible for originating of death; or a snake's bite inflicts the first death

H50.name_eng: Sky god and mistress of the dead
H50.definition_eng: A couple of deities or ancestors divorces. Man remains on earth or ascends to the sky, woman becomes the mistress of the dead or of the underworld

H51.definition_eng: A horse eats people or is associated with antagonist of the God

H52.definition_eng: Person finds a land where there is no death. Setting off to visit his home country, he does not come to this land again

H52A.name_eng: Death tricks a person to touch the ground
H52A.definition_eng: Coming back from the land of immortality, the hero should not touch the ground. However, he comes down from his horse to help an old man (old woman). It was Death in guise of an old man and he kills the hero on the spot. Rare: at the last moment the hero decides not to commit fatal acts and returns to the land of immortality

H52B.definition_eng: Setting off in search of the land of immortality, the hero comes across persons or animals who are involved in activity that needs tremendous time to be completed. However the hero is eager to obtain not the long but the eternal life and he continues his search

H53.name_eng: Wolf is the master of the dead
H53.definition_eng: Wolf takes part in creation and/or is a brother of the creator who wins demons of the lower world. Wolf is the first person who died and/or becomes the master of the dead

H54.definition_eng: Eyelids (eyelashes, eyebrows) of personage hang long down over his eyes. To make the eyes widely opened, the eyelids (eyelashes, eyebrows) should be propped up with poles, folks, sticks, etc. (rare: cut off)

H54A.definition_eng: Person comes across an old man (woman) whose face is completely covered with hair or snot. He or she cuts the hair (wipes the snot off) and receives compensation for his or her good deed

H54C.definition_eng: Person’s eyelids are stretched wide with sticks to make him impossible to close them

H55.definition_eng: Person who visits the other world gets to see different people punished or rewarded according to their behavior when they were alive on earth

H55A.definition_eng: Person gets to see husband and wife who pull their blanket from each other or have not enough space for two on their bed

H55B.name_eng: The robber who repents his misdeeds
H55B.definition_eng: A man who has visited hell (met the God) tells the robber about tortures prepared for him in the future. The robber accepts this news with resignation, does penance and ultimately is saved. Usually a hermit who decides that God is unjust in this case is punished

H56.definition_eng: After eating certain fruit, berry, tuber, etc. people become mortal (cf. motif F97: people become sexually aware)

H6A.definition_eng: Mortal humans are contrasted with (almost) immortal trees that shed their bark, become green again after winter sleep or propagate by sprouts

H6B.definition_eng: The life-medicine is accidentally spilled not on men but on plants which become evergreen, capable for regeneration or producing fruits

H6BB.definition_eng: Animal person is sent to pass to the people certain objects or substance but loses or replaces them. Because of this people miss possibility to become immortal or their life becomes difficult

H6C.definition_eng: Raven is associated with death or contrasted with people as an immortal with mortals (is sent to the medicine of immortality; drinks itself water of immortality; gives instructions concerning funeral rites; etc.)

H6C1.name_eng: Valuables in exchange for the nestling
H6C1.definition_eng: To obtain a desired object, person catches a child or spouse of an animal person (bird, snake, crab) and promises to release it as soon as its parent (spouse)) brings the object

H6C2.name_eng: Water of life in the land of darkness
H6C2.definition_eng: There is a land of darkness at the edge of the world. Those who are eager to get water of immortality or gold go there

H6C3.definition_eng: Big migratory birds who fly like a wedge (stocks, cranes, swans, geese; Zugvögel in German) are connected with the world beyond (bring babies from there, carry children away to the unhuman loci, possess the water of life and death, etc.)

H6D.definition_eng: Person obtains a remedy that makes alive beings immortal (revives them). While he is asleep or absent, the remedy is lost because of activity of other persons

H7.definition_eng: Death (also Old Age, Disease, etc.) is a particular person not identical with the Master of the Dead. He kills people usually carrying away their souls

H7A.definition_eng: Man receives from Death (Fortune, some spirit) knowledge will the patient recover or die. He becomes a doctor and receives rich rewards. Usually he gets the ability to see Death near the bed of a patient and considering a particular place where Death stands, gets to know perspectives of recovering

H7B.name_eng: The Death is stuck to a tree or a bench
H7B.definition_eng: A man lures Death (Devil) to climb a tree or sit on a bench to which they are stuck and can free themselves not before the man gives them such a permission

H7B1.definition_eng: Getting a magic sack into which any being must climb according to the wish of the owner, a man acquires power over the Death (Devil)

H7B2.definition_eng: Person called Poverty makes Death to promise him/her that he, the Death, will never come to him. Because of this poverty cannot be eradicated

H7C.definition_eng: Death promises to take a man after he has finished a prayer. The man begins to pray but does not finish his prayer and the Death cannot take him

H7C1.definition_eng: Cunning man first deceives Death (Devil) and then, also using a trich, gets into the Paradise

H7D.name_eng: The old man asks Death to help him to carry a load
H7D.definition_eng: An old man has to carry a heavy load of wood. Tired and exhausted, he wishes for death. When Death appears he asks her to help him with the load

H7E.name_eng: Humans knew the time of their death
H7E.definition_eng: In the year before they were to die, people neglected their responsibilities (they repair fences with temporary materials). Therefore, God decided that they should not know in advance when they will die

H7F.name_eng: Death asks God whom he should eat
H7F.definition_eng: God gives instructions according to which particular categories of people must die or suffer. Person who receives these instructions distors them out of sympathy for the people

H7F1.definition_eng: Death eats the dead and thus assuages his hunger

H7F2.definition_eng: The incarnation of death had a body that was visible for the people. Later Death becomes invisible

H7G.definition_eng: Person gets to see a lot of burning candles or lamps. As soon as one of them goes out, somebody dies

H7G1.name_eng: Death is more fair and rich than God
H7G1.definition_eng: Person (who is usually in search of the godgather for the newborn child) rejects God (saints) and devil but accepts Death who is more fair (or rich)

H7G2.name_eng: Failed escape from Death from the earth to the water
H7G2.definition_eng: When the day of a person’s death is near, he hopes that Death will be in search of him on the earth and makes attemt to live on or under the water. But Death finds him

H8.definition_eng: People lose immortality because they do not dare to touch or drink something loathsome, poisonous, hot or otherwise dangerous

H9.definition_eng: People are mortal because they have been likened to something subject to decay and easy destruction (e.g. to the soft wood and not to the stone)

H9A.name_eng: Who will give birth the first
H9A.definition_eng: One woman is associated with stone, another with a plant. The plant-woman gives birth the first or the stone-woman do not have children at all. That's because people have their present characteristics (are mortal, capable to speak, etc.), or offsprings of the two women are different (skillful and not, etc.)

H9B.definition_eng: People are likened to plants which are mortal but revive in their offsets

I1.definition_eng: Creatures that produce rain and/or thunderstorms are birds or anthropomorphic beings with wings; or (rare) some or all birds are connected with thunder, lightning or rain though Thunder is not a bird

I100.definition_eng: The Pleiades are a group of girls or women (with children)

I100A.name_eng: The Pleiades are mother with children
I100A.definition_eng: The Pleiades are a woman with her children

I100B.name_eng: The Pleiades are a group of people
I100B.definition_eng: The Pleiades are any people (of any ages and sex, combined data of i99-i100a)

I100C.definition_eng: God transformed man into a cuckoo, his wife and children into the Pleiades

I100D.definition_eng: The Pleiades or stars in general are associated with kids or lambs

I101.name_eng: Big Dipper is poles, a nailed skin
I101.definition_eng: Several bright stars of Big Dipper or other constellation are poles which support or stretch an object like skin, shelter, etc.

I102.definition_eng: Milky Way is a tree or a trace of a tree

I103.definition_eng: Sirius is associated with a dog or a wolf

I104.definition_eng: Stars are fragments of a bigger luminary (usually the Moon); or stars, the sun and the moon are formed from one and the same primeval person or creature

I105.definition_eng: One of constellations represents a hand with fingers

I106.definition_eng: Ursa major is only one anthropomorphic being, not several persons

I107.definition_eng: Stars are nails in the firmament or pegs, or stars are nailed to the sky

I108.definition_eng: The Pleiades are only one anthropomorphic being, not several persons

I109.name_eng: Milky Way is the path of the Sun
I109.definition_eng: Milky Way is the path of the Sun and/or Moon

I10A.definition_eng: Different sky levels or different categories of clouds have different colors

I10B.definition_eng: Particular layers or categories of the earth have different colors

I11.definition_eng: A turtle, toad, or frog supports the earth (sky) or is its embodiment

I110.definition_eng: Constellation are interpreted as agricultural tools or people occupied with agricultural works (mostly ploughing and haymaking)

I110A.definition_eng: Orion, Ursa major, or other constellation is a plough

I110B.definition_eng: (Belt of) Orion is (three) mowers or agricultural tools related to mowing and harvesting

I111.definition_eng: The earth is the body of a crocodile or a dragon

I112.definition_eng: A boat is an alive creature, a fish, a water animal

I113.definition_eng: A pig made of gold or having golden bristles is a treasure

I114.definition_eng: A ram (lamn, sheep) who has golden fleece or the skin of such a ram is described

I115A.name_eng: Orion and the Pleiades as a man and women
I115A.definition_eng: Orion and the Pleiades are opposed as a man or men and a woman or women. Orion is usually male

I116.name_eng: Milky Way is the border between the seasons
I116.definition_eng: The Milky Way is the border-line between seasons of the year or parts of the universe (the wet and the dry seasons, the sky and the earth, etc.)

I117.name_eng: Spider ferries from one world to another
I117.definition_eng: Spider person raises the hero to the sky, helps him or her to return back to earth or otherwise helps to overcome the borderlines between worlds

I117A.name_eng: Bat helps to descend from a rock
I117A.definition_eng: Bat(-woman) helps the hero to descend from a high rock

I118.definition_eng: Spider-woman (rare: spider-man) is a patron of the hero who lives in her house and marries her daughter

I119.definition_eng: The earthquakes are produced by the dead who are in the underworld or during the earthquakes the inhabitants of the lower world try to come out; try to understand are there still living beings on earth

I119A.definition_eng: Supernatural beings shake the earth because they think that no earth dwellers remained or wanting to check it, or demonstrating that they themselves are on the place

I11A.name_eng: The earth was put on the back of a turtle (frog)
I11A.definition_eng: It is described how the earth was obtained and put on the back of a turtle or frog

I12.definition_eng: A tree or post pierces and unites different layers of the universe

I120.definition_eng: Food and clothes (rare: everything) are extracted from the horn of a cow or goat

I120A.definition_eng: After entering the ear of an animal (usually a horse or a cow) and coming back person becomes handsome (sated, well clad)

I120B.definition_eng: Person takes from the ear of an animal (usually a horse or a cow) food, clothes and other valuables

I121.definition_eng: Two constellations (usually Ursa major and Ursa minor) are interpreted as twin objects of the same type (two animals, two carts, etc.)

I122.definition_eng: The Pleiades are a nest, a congestion of bees or wasps (or apiary, etc.)

I123.definition_eng: Altair or Vega with a weak nearby star are believed to appear on the sky immediately after winter solstice though really it is not so

I125.definition_eng: The Hyades are a jaw bone or a head of a big animal or anthropomorphic creature

I126.definition_eng: Ursa major or other circumpolar constellation is a stretcher on which a dead or sick person is carried, a dead body ready for the burial, a tomb

I127.definition_eng: Ursa major is a bed, a cot, a bedstead

I127A.name_eng: The bowl of Ursa major is a biar for the dead body
I127A.definition_eng: The bowl of Ursa major is a biar for the dead body, a catafalque

I128.definition_eng: Ursa major is a dipper, a ladle

I129.definition_eng: When constellation of Heron appears on the sky, the rain season begins

I130.definition_eng: One of costellations is a hunting or fishing net, trap, snare

I131.definition_eng: Life of every man is related to certain thread. When the thread is cut, the man dies

I132.name_eng: Climbing a deer antlers up to the sky
I132.definition_eng: A giant deer’s or deer-like creature’s antlers reach the upper world, a person climbs them to get there. Or person gets to the sky when he touches the deer’s antler

I132A.name_eng: A girl on the swing of the Sun
I132A.definition_eng: A girl sits on a swing and it carries her to the sky

I132B.definition_eng: A girl reaches the Sun to become his wife but at the last moment is transformed (usually becomes a bird)

I133.definition_eng: Sideral objects in different parts of the sky are identified with one and the same humanoid figure (parts of its body, decoratioons, etc.).

I133A.definition_eng: There is a constellation identified with a bird that corresponds to several big constellations in European traditions (mostly Ecuatorial and not Circum-Popar).

I134.name_eng: Long neck on the Milky Way
I134.definition_eng: Figure of a long-necked creature (llama or nandu) is seen along the axes of the Milkt Way

I135.definition_eng: The sky (Milky Way) is a skin of an animal or a cloth

I136.definition_eng: The rolling wheel (and a person who is riding it) is hostile to the hero (to the people) or a weapon used by such a person

I137.definition_eng: A constellation is associated with a shoe, usually with a (worn-out) bast shoe

I138.definition_eng: A glass mountain (tower, bridge) is mentioned as a an unusual (difficult to be reache) place

I139.name_eng: Strong men throw an axe to each other
I139.definition_eng: Two (rare: three) men or women regularly throw or give somthing to each other despite a significant distance between them. It is a sign of their strength, big size and dexterity

I13A.definition_eng: Giant water-chthonic or sky serpent or dragon has horns or antlers on its head

I13B.definition_eng: Snake of natural size has horns on its head

I13C.definition_eng: Reptiles possess treasure which a person gets or tries to get. Usually it is a crown, jewel or small horns on the snake's head

I13D.definition_eng: A man gets into the dwelling of snakes and after a long time escapes or is permitted to go. In While in the dwelling of snakes, he usually licks a special stone that allows to live without water and food

I13E.definition_eng: The serpent lets a man go on condition that he will not tell about their meeting. Under pain of death the man breaks his promise. The serpent instructs him how to dring the broth that will be made of his meat and revenges not on the man but on those who had forced him to break his word

I14.definition_eng: Person or creature has no anus opening

I140.definition_eng: A staff that was thrown on the ground turns into an alive snake

I141.definition_eng: A stick, wand is a tool to initiate processes which results have no rational explanation

I14A.name_eng: Eject digested food through the mouth
I14A.definition_eng: No-anus people eject digested food through the mouth or other orifice

I15A.definition_eng: Mouth of human being was first cut vertically

I16.name_eng: Body anomalies of the first people
I16.definition_eng: First human beings have no mouth, anus or genitals, their women do not know how to give birth

I17.name_eng: Body anomalies of inhabitants of a distant land
I17.definition_eng: Beings without mouth, anus, genitals, whose women do not know how to give birth live in the underworld, in the sky, or in a far-away land

I17A.definition_eng: Beings without anus or mouth are dwarfs

I18.name_eng: A spouse without anus or mouth
I18.definition_eng: Person visits people who have no anus or mouth. He or his sister marries or tries to marry a local dweller

I19.name_eng: People inhale the odor of food
I19.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic beings satisfy their hunger cooking food and inhaling the odor

I2.definition_eng: Lightning emerges from eyes or mouth of the being who is thought to produce thunderstorms

I20.definition_eng: Race of dwarfs lives under the ground (deep under the earth or in hills and rocks) or at the horizon where the earth and the sky meet

I20A.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic inhabitants of the upper world are giants

I20B.definition_eng: People in the upper world are different than on earth and put their belts not on the waist but higher or below it

I20C.definition_eng: Dwarfs live in the underworld that somewhat reminds the world of humans. If the dwarfs and the humans meet, it is deep under the earther

I20C1.name_eng: Dwarfes live in hills and rocks
I20C1.definition_eng: Dwarfs live not deep under the earth but in hills and rocks, usually come from there to the earth

I20C2.definition_eng: The denizens of the country at the horizon (where the sky and the earth meet) are dwarfs

I21.name_eng: Red-haired people scorched by the sun
I21.definition_eng: People who live in the underworld, at the sunrise or sunset (often dwarfs) are scorched by the Sun which moves by at a short distance from them. They are red-haired, dark-skinned, etc.

I22.definition_eng: There are objects which remaining on the same place are moving permanently or periodically (meet and part. rise and fall down, shut and open, rotate)

I22A.definition_eng: The sky is constantly moving up and down in respect to earth

I22B.name_eng: Birds fly to the outer world
I22B.definition_eng: Migratory birds (or shamans in guise of birds) fly from our world to the outer world through the narrow opening, between clashing rocks, under the edge of the sky which is rising and falling, etc. Many birds perish; and/or the person who lives at this place feeds on these birds; the person can be mistress of birds, lives on another side of the pulsating obstacle

I22B1.name_eng: Birds perish at the border of our world
I22B1.definition_eng: Some migratory birds (or shamns in guse of birds) perish when they reach the border of our world

I22C.name_eng: A plank from the stern of Argo
I22C.definition_eng: Person succeeds in getting through the opening which is going to bang shut but the stern of his boat, the tail of an animal or a bird, the body of his horse, or his own heel is flatterned, torn off, etc.

I22D.name_eng: Water of immortality behind clashing rocks
I22D.definition_eng: To get a wonderous medicine that revives (cures) living beings, one must go between clashing rocks

I22E.name_eng: Objects in permanent move on the way of the dead
I22E.definition_eng: On their way to the Beyond, souls of the dead must get between clashing rocks or other moving obstacles

I22F.definition_eng: Person must go beyond relatively small objects (trees, logs, blades) which are incessantly clashing and parting, rising and falling

I22G.definition_eng: There are mountains or rocks which permanently collide and separate again from each other or a crack (jaws) in a vertical cliff which is opening and closing

I22G1.definition_eng: Clashing stones are among strange creatures and objects, which the hero sees In the other world. They do not block his way, however

I22H.definition_eng: Person must jump over a crevise or precipice under his feet that is widening and narrowing all the time or a river which becomes now wide, now narrow

I23.definition_eng: The door of a house is opening and closing by itself crashing persons who attempt to come in or out

I24.definition_eng: Snake, lizard or worm is a bridge or a rope over the river

I24A.name_eng: A snake bridge to the other world
I24A.definition_eng: A body of water with the snake-bridge across it separates our world from the other world

I25.definition_eng: Way to the place of a certain person is guided by dangerous creatures (which often stand on the both sides of the pathway). Person placates them by gifts or nice talk, and they let him or her go the both ways, sometimes being punished for this by their master

I25A.definition_eng: Person sees that food put for certain animals is inedible for them and corrects situation (usually gives to herbivorous animals food that was given before to predators and vice versa)

I25B.name_eng: To clean an oven with her own hair
I25B.definition_eng: It is told about women who had no tools at all and were using parts of their body instead

I25B1.name_eng: They use their own hair instead of a rope
I25B1.definition_eng: It is told about women who use their own hair instead of a rope to lift bucket with water from a well

I25C.name_eng: To name bloody river the river of vine
I25C.definition_eng: On her or his way to the destination, person (on his or her way back) names dangerous or repulsive objects and beings beautiful and nice, thus securing their loyalty

I25D.definition_eng: On his or her way to dangerous person, a man or a girl comes across a gate to which he or she does something good (oils, opens, closes, etc.). On his or her way, the grateful gate refuses to catch him or her

I26.name_eng: Dangers on the way of souls
I26.definition_eng: On its way to the Beyond, a soul has to defend itself or divert attention of guards who wait for it giving presents to them

I27.definition_eng: A dog is the lord, guard or guide of/to the land of the dead; or dogs live on the way to the land of the dead

I27A.definition_eng: Souls of the dead dogs have their own towns in the Beyond or their own paths to travel there

I27B.definition_eng: A dog ferries person across a river that forms a border between the worlds

I27C.definition_eng: Dogs having spots over the eyes are called the four-eyed and believed to have special properties (e.g. to see ghosts)

I27D.definition_eng: A certain black (red) dog has a negative influence on the human life (and is associated with the night sky)

I28.definition_eng: Game animals live inside a mountain, in a cave or in the underworld where they often look like humans and have a master

I28A.definition_eng: Big game animals disappear under the earth and produce earthquakes

I29.name_eng: Animal’s hole leads to the underworld
I29.definition_eng: Person follows an animala through its hole or digs a hole himself and gets into the lower world where the animals who dig holes live

I3.definition_eng: The lightning (and thunder) is (produced with) an object (axe, sword, mirror, belt, stones, skin, etc.) in hands of anthropomorphic being

I30.name_eng: Master of the dead welcomes women
I30.definition_eng: Master or mistress of the realm of the dead copulates with every new human soul of the opposite sex who arrives to his or her realm

I31.name_eng: Master and mistress of the dead
I31.definition_eng: In the Beyond, two mythological personages, one male and another female, meet the newcomers, or the same person meet the women in the female and the men in the male guise

I32.definition_eng: There is (or was) a tree on which souls of still unborn babies grow, which leaves transform into people, or which trunk is covered with female breasts or flowers that innumerable babies are sucking

I32A.definition_eng: When a leave or a fruit of a certain tree drops, one of the people on the earth dies

I33.definition_eng: The ultimate aim of the afterlife journey is to reach certain tree

I34.definition_eng: It is necessary to approach a tree which is surrounded with fire, ejects fire, shoots sharp splints, etc.

I35.definition_eng: Thunder is produced by dragging behind a dry animal skin or (rare) a person (rare) or by shaking clothes

I35A.definition_eng: Thunder is produced by an old woman who lives in the sky

I35A1.definition_eng: Person claims to be equal to the sky god, imitating him or mocking upon him

I35A1A.definition_eng: Person claims to be equal to the high god, imitating him, mocking upon him or making attempt to kill him

I35A2.name_eng: Thunder is rolling stones or vessels
I35A2.definition_eng: Thunder is heard when stones or big vessels are rolled, dragged, overthrown in the sky

I35B.definition_eng: Sky is made of metal. The technique of its creation reminds the work of a smith

I35C.definition_eng: One of mythological characters using his skills in crafts creates for the first time tools and valuable cultural and natural objects; is a patron of craftsmen (usually of blacksmiths)

I36.name_eng: Thunder and lightning are relatives, spouses or in-laws
I36.definition_eng: Thunder and lightning (two thunders, two lightings) are close relatives, spouses or in-laws; or only one of two persons is transformed but during the interaction with another

I37D.definition_eng: Mushrooms are excrements of mythological person

I37D1.definition_eng: St. Peter eats bread (cake) secretly. When Chist talks to him he tries to hide what he ei eating and spits it out. Afterwards mushrooms grow from crumbs

I37G.definition_eng: Tree fungi are steps, small platforms, umbrellas, obstacles that make moving easier or more difficult, provide a shelter or cover

I38.definition_eng: Some beings are half-men and half-dogs (usually anthropomorphic with heads of dogs)

I38A.definition_eng: Dogs or dog-headed men are husbands of human women

I39.definition_eng: Rainbow is a road, a bridge or a ladder

I39A.name_eng: Souls of the dead walk upon the rainbow
I39A.definition_eng: Souls of the dead walk upon the rainbow to the other world; the rainbow bridge is across the river that separates the world of the dead from the world of the living

I3A.definition_eng: During the thunderstorm supernatural person beats somthing or somebody with a whip. This is the lightning

I4.definition_eng: Thunder is heard when a vehicle moves in the sky

I41.definition_eng: Rainbow is a reptile (usually a snake) or (more rare) a fish, or it is related to snake, to its tongue, breath, or to scorpion's tail

I41A.name_eng: Rainbow from anthill or termite nest

I41B1.definition_eng: Rainbow drinks and together with water swallows fish, people, etc. Sometimes this fish falls on earth from the sky

I41B2.definition_eng: Rainbow comes out of the mouth of a reptile, amphidian or in vertebrate animal

I41C.name_eng: Sky object is a reflection of a snake
I41C.definition_eng: The rainbow of the Milky Way is a reflection of a snake (fish) that is on the earth or in the sea

I42.name_eng: Rainbow is a pair of creatures
I42.definition_eng: Rainbow is two creatures or persons, usually a male and a female

I42G3.definition_eng: In the forest person comes across a house that is made, completely or partly, of edible matter

I43A.definition_eng: Giant reptilian monster (serpent, more rare fish, chain of fish) extends in the sky and/or supports the sky being associated with Milky Way or the rainbow

I43B.name_eng: Milky Way is a serpent or fish
I43B.definition_eng: Milky Way is a reptile, fish, or chain of fish

I44.definition_eng: Giant serpent lies on the perimeter of the earth or supports the earth

I45A.name_eng: Not to point at the Moon or a star
I45A.definition_eng: Person who points at the Moon or a star or looks intently at them will get sick or die or his pointing finger will rot or wither

I45B.name_eng: Not to point at the rainbow
I45B.definition_eng: It to point at the rainbow, pointing finger or entire arm will rot, wither or become crooked

I45C.definition_eng: Person who counts stars will suffer diseases and misfortunes

I46.definition_eng: Rainbow is the ornamented part of the clothes, its decoration, a belt

I46A.definition_eng: Rainbow is associated with an old woman

I46B.definition_eng: Intensity of particular colors of rainbow predicts good or bad harvest of particular crops

I46C.definition_eng: Rainbow is a rope to which a domestic animal is tied

I46D.definition_eng: Rainbow is a snare, a noose

I46E.definition_eng: Rainbow is a sword, a cutting weapon

I47.definition_eng: Rainbow is a flatulence of a demon, a spray of a skunk, is associated with spit, urine, feces, genitals, etc., causes skin diseases, is associated with death

I47A.definition_eng: Rainbow is associated with a wedding of foxes or jackals

I48.definition_eng: Certain person loses his or her freedom, is confined to a far away place (often, to the underworld) and acquires cosmic dimensions: supports the earth or the sky and/or his or her movements produce earthquakes or (rare) storms

I48A.definition_eng: At the terminal part of the narrative the antagonist of the hero descends into the underworld

I49.definition_eng: Earthquake is a person. Whenever he or she runs or walks, the earth trembles

I4A.name_eng: Thunder in trouble: falls to earth
I4A.definition_eng: Thunder falls to earth, cannot return to the sky. Usually a human person helps him to do it

I4B.name_eng: Thunder in trouble: fights with his enemy
I4B.definition_eng: A man helps Thunder who fights with his enemy

I4C.definition_eng: Thunder-god is temporarily overcome and imprisoned by his enemy

I4D.definition_eng: Thunder’s instrument is stolen from him. He or his helper comes unrecognized to the thief, gets his instrument and kills the enemies

I4D1.definition_eng: The Storm-god’s adversary steals his tendons (heart and eyes) but he gets them back and overcomes his adversary

I4E.name_eng: Storm-god as rider of the clouds
I4E.definition_eng: An anthropomorphic sky-god (associated with the thunder and rain) rides on the clouds (uses them as a vehicle)

I5.definition_eng: Thunder looks like a quadruped mammal (pig, buffalo, camel, anteater, tapir, dog, cat, leopard, monkey, etc.)

I50.name_eng: Ungulate animal with more than four legs
I50.definition_eng: An ungulate animal (a horse, an elk, a moose) with six or more legs is described or represented in art

I50A.name_eng: Torn off legs of the helpful animal
I50A.definition_eng: Demon tears off or devours one by one legs of aт animal who helps the hero, usually of his riding horse

I50A1.name_eng: Torn off legs of a dog
I50A1.definition_eng: Person tears off one by one legs of a dog but the dog continues to do what it considers to be its duty

I50B.name_eng: Predator animal with more than four legs
I50B.definition_eng: A predator animal or a zoomorphic non-reptilian monster with six or more legs is described or represented in art

I50C.name_eng: Šarabkha (animal with legs on its back)
I50C.definition_eng: An ungulate animal with an additional set of legs on its back runs using in turns legs under its belly and on its back. Thanks to this it is indefatigable

I51B.definition_eng: The earth or the sky are identified with a big quadruped mammal or are made of parts of its body

I52.definition_eng: World is supported by fish or fish-like monster or the earth itself is such a monster

I53.definition_eng: The animal or the fish which supports the earth is bothered by an insect. The animal moves and the earth tremblesThe animal or the fish which supports the earth is bothered by an insect. The animal moves and the earth trembles (or an animal being afraid of the insect does not dare to move)

I54.definition_eng: Anaconda or a water monster has live fish or animals inside; is father of the fish; all fish emerge from its body

I55.definition_eng: Stars are openings in the firmament; holes in dwelling's covering are thought to be stars

I55A.definition_eng: Stars are lakes in one of the sky levels

I55B.definition_eng: Hero pursues a deer or elk which carry the sun

I56.name_eng: Ghosts do not see people from earth
I56.definition_eng: The alive person who is travelling between the worlds is visible for inhabitants of one world and invisible for inhabitants of another

I56A.name_eng: In the land of the ghosts human being is an evil spirit
I56A.definition_eng: When a man who had got to the land of spirits touches a local dweller the latter dies or becomes sick

I57.definition_eng: Thunder's enemies are evil spirits, reptiles, animals living in burrows. They hide from him in different objects, Thunder destroys these objects

I58.name_eng: Milky Way is the way of birds
I58.definition_eng: Milky Way is the path of migratory birds (especially wild geese)

I59.definition_eng: Milky Way is a trace of people who spilled on their way something related to agriculture (straw, chaff, hay, more rare flour, peas)

I59A.definition_eng: Astral objects or lunar spots are associated with a story of a stealing and the value of the stolen objects is low (straw, firewoods, cabbage, etc.)

I59B1.name_eng: Milky Way is the road to a remote city
I59B1.definition_eng: Milky Way is the road to a remote city (Rome, Jerusalem, etc.)

I59B2.name_eng: Milky Way is the way of St, Jacob
I59B2.definition_eng: Milky Way is the way of St. Jacob (the way to Santiago de Compostela, etc.)

I59B3.name_eng: Milky Way is the way of salt traders
I59B3.definition_eng: Milky Way is the way of salt traders

I59B4.name_eng: Milky Way is snow or rime
I59B4.definition_eng: Milky Way is associated with a snow, hoarfrost, cold

I59B5.definition_eng: Milky Way is a smoke that ascended from the earth to the sky

I5A.definition_eng: Tapir is associated with the upper world, usually with the thunder

I5B.definition_eng: Flying feline produces rains and thunderstorms

I6.definition_eng: A man meets a giant bird that brings with it clouds, rain, hail, thunderstorm, etc.

I60.name_eng: Milky Way is a seam in the sky
I60.definition_eng: Milky Way is a sky seam, a concealed fissure or crack between two half of the sky vault

I60A.name_eng: Milky Way is a stripe on belly
I60A.definition_eng: Milky Way is a longitudinal streak, associated with a white line, stripe along the middle of a belly of an animal

I61.name_eng: Milky Way is a stream of secretion
I61.definition_eng: Milky Way is a stream of secretion (usually a milk) discharged from the body of some person or creature

I61A.definition_eng: Milky Way is the belt of the sky

I62.definition_eng: Milky Way is a sky river, water body, chain of beings that swim

I63.name_eng: Milky Way is a path of tapir
I63.definition_eng: Milky Way is a path of tapir, or tapir is seen in the Milky Way

I64.name_eng: Milky Way is a trace of animals
I64.definition_eng: Milky Way is a trace of big animals who were walking or running along it

I64A.definition_eng: Two different ungulates run a race in the sky. Usually Milky Way is their trace of dust

I65.definition_eng: Milky Way is the path over which souls travel to the beyond or a path of the funeral procession

I66.definition_eng: Milky Way is ashes or smoldering coals

I67.name_eng: Emu and rhea in the Milky Way
I67.definition_eng: A giant figure of an emu (in Australia) or rhea (in South America) is seen in the Milky Way

I68.definition_eng: On a certain moment, a crack, a window or the like opens in the sky vault (rains flows though it, the upper world is seen, communication with inhabitants of the upper world becomes possible)

I68A.definition_eng: Once in a year water for a short time acquires special qualities

I68B.definition_eng: In a certain night of the year any wish that was thought of or voiced is fulfilled

I69.definition_eng: Shining sky objects or atmospheric phenomena are excrements of sky dwellers

I6A.name_eng: Male and female birds: different kinds of precipitation
I6A.definition_eng: The male and the female birds bring with them different kinds of precipitations (e.g. the male comes with a hail, the female with a rain). Or (Buryats of Mongolia) one and the same bird brings different kinds of precipitations depending on is it angry or not.

I7.definition_eng: A flying reptile produces rain, thunderstorm

I70.name_eng: Person or creature with plants on its back
I70.definition_eng: Trees or reeds grow on the back of a person or reptile

I71.definition_eng: Stars are roots of the plants which grow in the upper world

I72.definition_eng: Stars are people, ghosts, anthropomorphic beings (interpretations of unique star objects like Venus or Polaris as persons not considered)

I72A.name_eng: Stars are children of the Sun and the Moon
I72A.definition_eng: Stars are children of the Moon and/or the Sun

I73.definition_eng: Stars (rare: suns and moons) are sparks or burning coals

I74.definition_eng: Stars are shining stones, spangles, beads

I75.definition_eng: Before present world, several (two or more) other worlds or races of people existed

I76A.definition_eng: After certain time a snake or fish turn into a dragon

I76B.definition_eng: After certain time aAfter certain time or thanks to some particular activity a mouse turns into a bat mouse turns into a bat

I77.definition_eng: Powerful person connected with thunder and rain is lame (usually after falling down from the sky)

I78.definition_eng: The earth is square, the sky is usually round

I7A.definition_eng: The lightning is associated with a snake

I7B.name_eng: Lightnings are fissures in the sky-vault
I7B.definition_eng: Lightnings are fissures in the sky-vault and the sky light is seen through them for a moment

I7C.definition_eng: When a person or creature who lives in the upper world urinates, it rains (dew falls) on earth

I80.definition_eng: Person who got into the place of a deity responsible for atmospheric phenomena breaks certain taboo or instructions producing excessive thunderstorm, rain, snowfall or wind

I80A.definition_eng: Man meets Thunders and becomes one of them

I80B.definition_eng: God charges a man with the task of magaging the weather. The man sends rain and heat in a due propotion but is unable to consider all relevant factors (usually forgets the wind). As a result, the man gets no harvest at all all the breads has a bad taste

I81.name_eng: Waters rush down into the underworld
I81.definition_eng: Waters of all rivers on earth run to the precipice where they rush down into the underworld

I81A.definition_eng: A giant crab produces earthquakes or floods, stops or can stop flow of the waters into the chasm or on the contrary prevents waters from being dammed.

I81A1.definition_eng: The confrontation between the crab and the serpent (eel) produces the present landscape features or has the cosmic scale

I81B.definition_eng: It is tide when a creature belches out the sea water or ousts it with its body and it is ebb when it swallows the water or lets it go back (or it is simply told that water periodically emerge and disappears into the maelstrom

I82A.definition_eng: Morning and/or Evening Star is a male personage

I82B.definition_eng: Morning and/or Evening Star is a female personage

I82C.definition_eng: Venus or some other bright star seen near the eastern or western horizon is female and wife of the Moon

I82C1.definition_eng: The Moon has two wives (usually the Morning and the Evening stars). One of them takes care of him and he becomes fat, another neglects him and he becomes thin

I82D.name_eng: Morning and Evening stars are a man and a woman
I82D.definition_eng: Morning and Evening stars are opposed as a man and a woman or vice versa

I82D1.definition_eng: Morning and Evening stars are two men (usually brothers)

I82E.definition_eng: It is told about Venus or other star that she sold her mother or father to have a beautiful attire

I82F.definition_eng: (Evening) Venus is associated with a predator animal, usually with a she-wolf

I82G.name_eng: Venus is the star of the shepard
I82G.definition_eng: Venus or other bright star (Arcturus, Sirius, etc.) is the star of the shepard (herdsman, swine-herd, etc.)

I82H.definition_eng: The name of the Venus is like Čolpan, Čolbon, Tsulmon, etc.

I82I.definition_eng: The name of an object of the night sky (usually Venus) is like Zakhra, Zukhra, Zura, etc.

I83.definition_eng: Birds, first of all vultures and eagles, live in the sky, usually at one or more layers of the upper world

I84.name_eng: Milky Way is a snow-shoes track
I84.definition_eng: Milky Way is a path of a person who was walking on snow-shoes

I84A.name_eng: Son of God frozen to death
I84A.definition_eng: In winter time despite warning son of the sky deity sets off (usually on his snow-shoes) and is frozen to death

I85.name_eng: Polaris is a pole, a nail
I85.definition_eng: Polaris is a (tethering) pole or a nail

I85A.definition_eng: Hoofed animals are walking around Polaris or the movement of stars is compared with the movement of animals around a post

I85A1.name_eng: Polaris is the hole in the sky
I85A1.definition_eng: Polaris is the opening though which one can get into the upper world

I85C.definition_eng: A person rises to the sky and finds there containers with different (two or more) types of precipitations, atmospheric phenomena, seasons and/or celestial bodies

I85C1.name_eng: The rain stored in the sky
I85C1.definition_eng: In the sky there is a special container (vessel, skin, box, etc.) for storing the rain

I86.name_eng: Hairs into animals, scales into fish
I86.definition_eng: Master of living beings sends down, hairs, scales, etc. which turn into birds, animals, fish

I86A.definition_eng: Snow is created from bird's down when certain bird in the sky shakes itself or certain person shakes his or her clothes made of bird down

I87.definition_eng: Personages use a shelter which proves to be an object related to the world of the giants (a skull, a shoulder-blade, a mitten)

I87A.name_eng: Series of creatures ever greater in size
I87A.definition_eng: Personage of gigantic dimensions in respect to normal humans and animals proves to be tiny dwarf in respect to another personage

I87A1.definition_eng: Two persons engaged into dialogue describe a series of objects and creatures as simultaneously giant and small

I87A2.definition_eng: Antagonist names numbers from one to seven (nine, rwelve) every time asking what it is. The hero gives answers that the antagonist accepts as correct ones. Or the hero names and explains numbers and the antagonist only listens him (her)

I87AA.definition_eng: Huge bull (rare: horse) is described: its head is in one field, its tail in another; a bathhouse on its tale, a lake on its back; person who is near the head walks a long time till he meets another neat the tail; etc. Usually the bull is killed and eaten (by people in Baltic Finnish traditions and in Russian bylina from Olonets area; by bird in most of southern traditions)

I87AB.name_eng: Only child was able to pick it up
I87AB.definition_eng: Strong men or a lot of people people cannot move the corpse of a killed person or creature but a child or a woman does it easily

I87AC.definition_eng: Something big or huge gets into the man’s eye but he takes it for a speck of dust. Usually a bird picks up and carries away an animal or a fish and drops its bone into an eye of a man. When the bone is found, it is dragged out with difficulty (people ride in a boat inside the eye, drag the bone with a fishnet, with many oxen, etc.)

I87AD.definition_eng: A giant hides the pursued man in his moith – usually (or always) in a hollow tooth; or a man survives after getting into the giant's mouth hiding himself in a hollow tooth

I87B.name_eng: The quest for a strong adversary
I87B.definition_eng: A man seeks a strong adversary to wrestle with and comes across person who is incomparably stronger than he

I87C.definition_eng: Animals use for shelter or transportation a small object related to the human world (skull, mitten, sieve, etc.)

I87C1.definition_eng: A mouse makes a canoe form a small object and rides in it

I87D.name_eng: Men in the time of giants
I87D.definition_eng: The earth was inhabited by the giants. One of them finds a tiny person, brings him to his parents. Usually his father or mother esplains that this is one of those men who will live on the earth in the future instead of the present day giants

I87E.definition_eng: In the future dwarfs will replace people on earth

I87F.definition_eng: A raсe of people who were bigger, stronger or otherwise different from the present day people lived in the past. They dissapeared after commiting suicide

I88.definition_eng: There is a zoomorphic being with many tails

I89.definition_eng: There is an evil star or constellation that brings death and misfortune; usually travelers mistake at night some star for Morning Star, set off, take a wrong direction and perish or get into trouble

I8C.definition_eng: The earth does not fall down or swing because it is suspended to ropes

I8E.name_eng: Four men at the cardinal points
I8E.definition_eng: Four (or eight) anthropomorphic male persons support the earth or the sky or are placed at the four cardinal points

I8E1.definition_eng: For objects, persons or beings (four groups of them) from four sides support sky or the earth; in some cases ther fifth one is at the center; or the earth is suspended on four ropes

I8F.definition_eng: Only one pole or mountain supports the earth or the sky

I8G.definition_eng: One giant supports the earth or the sky

I8H.name_eng: A man and a woman hold the earth
I8H.definition_eng: Two anthropomorphic beings, a male and a female, are in the underworld and support the earth

I8I.definition_eng: Originally the earth was unstable and swung, then it was fixed up

I9.definition_eng: Four cardinal directions and/or some objects associated with them are associated with different colors

I90.name_eng: To follow the rolling ball of threads
I90.definition_eng: To reach his or her destination, person follows a ball of threads (rare: some ball, apple) which is rolling in front of him or her

I91.name_eng: Water body at the base of a tree
I91.definition_eng: There is a source or body of water at the base of a tree which connects layers of the universe and/or has gigantic dimensions and considered to be the main tree of the world

I92.definition_eng: Person who gets to walk under, over or through the rainbow changes his or her sex

I92A.definition_eng: Anyone who jumps or steps over the rainbow will change his or her sex

I92B.definition_eng: There is a treasure under the extremities of the rainbow

I93.definition_eng: Milky Way is the backbone of the sky or of all the world

I94.definition_eng: The Pleiades are holes in the firmament

I95.name_eng: The Pleiades are a sieve for grain
I95.definition_eng: The Pleiades are a sieve to process agricultural products

I95C.definition_eng: Orion is a staff, a crook

I96.definition_eng: Rainbow is blood, associated with war and death

I98A.name_eng: The Pleiades are a hen with its chickens
I98A.definition_eng: The Pleiades are a brooding hen, hen with its chickens, chickens

I98B.name_eng: The Pleiades are a duck’s nest
I98B.definition_eng: The Pleiades are wild ducks, a nest or eggs of a wild duck

I98C.name_eng: The Pleiades is a flock of birds
I98C.definition_eng: The Pleiades is a flock of birds (in flight)

I99.name_eng: The Pleiades are boys or men
I99.definition_eng: The Pleiades are a group of boys or men, or a group of different people but predominantly males

I9A.definition_eng: The zenith and/or nadir are described together with four cardinal directions as the fifth (and the sixth) ones

J1.definition_eng: Persons avenge the death of their father, mother or other relatives who are one (rare two) generations older than they

J10.definition_eng: A woman loses her way after being bitter by insect (wasp, bee, ant). She accuses her unborn sons of being the cause of the bite and/or slaps herself on her abdomen to punish the sons or to kill the insect. As a consequence her sons are offended and do not show her the correct way anymore

J11.name_eng: Unborn child asks to pick up some flowers
J11.definition_eng: A quarrel between a mother and her sons in her womb flares up after they ask her to pick up flowers or fruits (usually the insect bites her when she picks flowers up)

J12.definition_eng: A girl (or two sisters) travel, usually in search of a proper marriage partner who lives far away or who has gone away. On her way or after reaching the place of destination the girl gets to some unpleasant suitors

J12A.definition_eng: A girl or two sisters get to old woman who suggests them to marry her son. It is a worm or alive penis preserved by its mother in a pot. The girl (the sister) rejects it, runs away

J12B.definition_eng: A suitor or husband who is a honey person or skillful honey-gatherer is attractive for a girl

J12C.definition_eng: A girl gets to see her bridegroom for the first time at a feast and then sets off to his place following instructions received from him

J12D.definition_eng: After a girl marries a valuable suitor, a rejected imposter or his relations kill him

J12J.definition_eng: In village where valuable marriage-partner lives an imposter plays the role of a buffoon

J12K.name_eng: A valuable partner and an imposter live in one house
J12K.definition_eng: A valuable partner whom a girl (two sisters) should marry and an imposter live together in one and the same house

J12L.definition_eng: A murderer of a valuable marriage-partner pretends to mourn over him. His trick is exposed, people chase him

J12M.definition_eng: A girl or two sisters marry a valuable partner. His rival kills or attempts to kill him or his wives. As a consequence, the women turn into water birds

J13.definition_eng: Two sisters (if more, only two play a significant role in the plot) travel and meet an unpleasant suitor or get to an ogre

J14.definition_eng: A girl or two sisters walk in search of the man whose beautiful voice or whose flute-play they listen

J15.definition_eng: Walking in search of her husband, boyfriend, kinsmen, shelter woman or girl gets to the house of dangerous creatures where she is injured or killed

J15A.definition_eng: Setting off (usually in search of her husband, boyfriend or kinsmen), woman gets to the place of dangerous felines

J15B.definition_eng: Setting off (usually in search of her husband, boyfriend or kinsmen), woman gets to the place of female toad or frog

J16.definition_eng: Person perishes because being forced to clean ogre's or animal’s head infected with insects, refuses to bite the insects, spits in disgust or is suspected to do it

J17.definition_eng: Instead of lice, there are other (bigger or dangerous) creatures in the hair of some persons or he or she pretends that his or her hair is infested with them

J18.definition_eng: A woman who is pregnant or has a small child falls from the sky. She or a daughter born by her dies but her (grand)son is grown up

J18A.name_eng: Mother is eaten up, children escape
J18A.definition_eng: An ogress devours a woman, gets into her house. Her daughters (daughter and son, one daughter) run away, climb a tree or a rope that hangs from the sky. Ogress pursues them and perishes

J19.definition_eng: When husband o brother leaves home to hunt, an evil spirit comes to his wife or sister. The spirit kills her or carries her away. Her baby boys extracted from her womb or born at this time survive

J19A.name_eng: To serve food on the abdomen
J19A.definition_eng: A demonic person visits a woman when she remains alone. He or she claims that needs a particular part of her body to complete a particular act that is against logic and custom. After this the demon kills the woman (extracts a child from her abdomen, pulls out her tongue)

J19B.definition_eng: An evil spirit kills a woman burning her belly through

J19C.definition_eng: An evil spirit kills a woman burning her belly through

J2.definition_eng: Husband or lover is a tree (that temporarily turns into a man)

J20.definition_eng: When husband o brother leaves home to hunt, an evil spirit comes to his wife or sister and kills or injures her being able to do it because she has broken taboo to open the door, to look at the guest or to answer him or her

J21.definition_eng: Gods, first people or founders of the royal lineages are born from eggs

J22A.definition_eng: Two men or a man and a woman appear from two halves of the cut in two anthropomorphic body or embryo; or another man appears from part of the body of the first one or from his body discharge

J22B.definition_eng: A woman is torn or cut in half, two new women appear

J22C.definition_eng: A demonic creature has a form of two women half merged like Siamese twins

J22D.name_eng: Two animals from one cut in two
J22D.definition_eng: Two halves of one animal or person which was cut in two turn into two animals of different species or into foreigners

J22E.definition_eng: A second person evolves from the placenta of the first one

J23.definition_eng: People (elder brothers, elder siblings, elder sister) disappear (one by one). A lonely woman has a baby or finds a baby or she becomes pregnant magically and gives birth to a boy or twins. The boy grows up, exterminates the antagonists, usually revives and releases those who had disappeared

J23A.definition_eng: A woman is crying, mucus from her nose (or her tear) turns into a boy who grows up, overcome powerful adversaries

J23B.name_eng: Spears put all along the path
J23B.definition_eng: To overcome a monster, the youth (twin boys) prepares spears and puts them all along the path from the monster’s den to his place. When the monster pursues him, the youth throws his spears one after another and ultimately kills the monster

J23C.definition_eng: People (elder brothers, elder siblings, elder sister) disappear (one by one). A lonely woman has a baby or finds a baby or she becomes pregnant magically and gives birth to a boy. The boy grows up, exterminates the antagonists, usually revives and releases those who had disappeared

J23D.definition_eng: People (elder brothers, elder siblings, elder sister) disappear (one by one). A lonely woman has baby twins (or more children) who grow up, exterminates the antagonists, usually revives and releases those who had disappeared

J23E.definition_eng: To become sure that the ogre is dead a bird or an insec enters his body from the mouth and flies out from the anus

J24.definition_eng: Hero is grounded to powder but resuscitates

J25.definition_eng: Heroes (usually one or two), being still babies or embryos, escape or are thrown away, often into the water. To bring them back into the human world, they are lured (persuaded) to come out or caught with difficulty

J25A.definition_eng: Mother dies or is killed. Her (still unborn) baby-son is buried with her. He comes out of the grace, meets people, then returns to the grave but ultimately agrees to remain with the people

J25A1.name_eng: Child born in grave saves his mother
J25A1.definition_eng: Woman dies but remains but remains imperishable and gives birth to a boy. He is found in her grave and he brings his mother back to life

J25B.name_eng: Dead mother fetches food for her baby
J25B.definition_eng: Mother dies and is buries. Her spirit comes out of the grave to fetch food for her baby. The baby is found and remains alive

J25C.name_eng: Baby brought up by the she-wolf
J25C.definition_eng: A she-wolf brings up an abandoned baby boy. He becomesan illustrious leader

J26.name_eng: Babies come out of the water
J26.definition_eng: Baby heroes, embryos or objects from which they emerge are found in a river or lake or come to people out of the water

J26A.definition_eng: Among woman’s childen or among children of two women who live together are a boy and a puppy or woman’s son is substituted with a pup and thrown away. This puppy lives with the woman and helps her.

J27.definition_eng: A small boy (several babies) was thrown away, born by the dead woman, lives in the water (in forest, etc.). Another boy lives with his father or mother. Ultimately the first boy comes to live in the locus of the second one. Often (see motif j25, Babies escape and return) during some time the boy who lives in the wilderness meets secretly with his brother (with other children, with pups that had been fed up by his mother) who lives with the people

J27A.definition_eng: One of two babies is thrown away and lives in the water, in the forest, etc., another lives in the house; after both of them become to live in the house, they kills their father

J27B.definition_eng: Besides his parents on earth, the baby who had been thrown into a river or lake and comes from time to time to the shore has another father (and mother) under the water. He does not want to be separated from them or they do not want let him go

J28A.definition_eng: Hero asks how one of his parents died and receives a series of false answers. Usually he successively exposes himself to the same dangers, survives and thus demonstrates that truth is still concealed from him

J28B.definition_eng: A youth gets to know that a woman (usually his mother) conceals from him important information about his father, brothers or bride. He causes her pain (usually putting hot scone, handful of hot grain, etc. into her hand) making her tell him the truth

J29.definition_eng: A murdered parent of the hero comes to him as a ghost and informs about the circumstances of his or her death

J3.definition_eng: A woman gives birth to a boy or twin boys after being impregnated without her knowledge when one of the animal persons crawls under the earth to the place where she sits on a ground

J30.definition_eng: Before the hero destroys the antagonists or escapes from them, he finds or receives the remains or possessions that belonged to the antagonists' victim

J31.definition_eng: A young hero obtains and uses weapons or other powerful objects which belonged to his murdered father

J32.definition_eng: Some valuables (foals, hay, apples, etc.) are regularly stolen. Nobody (the elder brothers) is able to catch the thief and only the hero (the younger brother) finds who it is

J32A.definition_eng: Before passing away a man asks his sons to guard his grave for a certain time or to bring something to his grave. The youngest son goes and obtains valuables

J32A1.definition_eng: Every night somebody tramples down the grain field, steals hay, etc. The hero discovers that horses do it

J32B.definition_eng: To have enough time for realizing his plans, hero makes the night longer changing behavior of the person or creature responsible for the day cycle

J32C.name_eng: Demon comes to harm to the dead
J32C.definition_eng: At night a demonic person comes to the tomb to harm the dead

J32D.name_eng: Princess in a tower (The glass mountain)
J32D.definition_eng: The girl will marry a man who (riding on a horse or otherwise) would quickly reach a place that is almost inaccessible (the top of a tower, a mountain, the upper floor of a palace, the top of a staircase, bridge, the bottom of a deep cavity, etc.). Usually the girl herself is in the corresponding place

J32E.definition_eng: Every foal to which a mare gives birth is immediately stolen. The hero identifies the thief

J32F.definition_eng: Being on guard, the hero gets to know who steals regularly fruits (usually apples) from the garden

J33.definition_eng: A youth or two siblings live in a house of an old man or woman. To produce a reaction from this older person, they kill a person or animal and stuff its skin with insects, worms, ashes, grass or blow it up

J33A.definition_eng: A youth or two siblings live in a house of an old woman. they kill her a person or animal who is her husband and make a dummy of him. The old woman is angry that her husband does not answer her, beats him and understands that it is a dummy

J34.definition_eng: After killing their enemy, heroes have fun frightening their (grand)mother or father with its dummy

J35.definition_eng: A tree-frog kills or neutralizes dangerous person or creature who chases heroes

J36.definition_eng: Hero's parents are killed by turtle who pulled them under the water

J37.name_eng: The antagonist is carried away by bird
J37.definition_eng: A man turns into powerful bird or creates it. The bird carries away his enemy

J38.definition_eng: A mighty bird thrust its talons into a big fish, whale, water monster, etc. Talons get stuck, the bird is either pulled down under the water or makes itself free with great difficulty

J39.definition_eng: Antagonist makes a girl or a woman his or her slave. The slave's brothers or sons secretly come to her, kill for her some small game. Woman tries to pursue the antagonist that she herself killed the game

J4.name_eng: Revenge for the death of the male relatives
J4.definition_eng: Heroes avenge the murder or captivity of the male relatives: (grand)father, uncles, or the elder relatives in general, the loss of the males being the most traumatic

J40.definition_eng: Beings who live in the sky descend to kill people. Usually such a being carries away to its world a person or many people (or person's cut off head or limb). The hero (usually a relation of the perished one) revenges on the dangerous being and/or brings back the victim or victims (his or her head, etc.)

J40B.definition_eng: After the hero comes back after a long absence and finds his parents enslaved, he tells them to demonstrate openly a lack of respect to their masters and punishes those who were cruel with them

J41.name_eng: Foxes jeer at the abandoned person
J41.definition_eng: When the hero returns home after a long absence, his relation does not believe at first that it is really he because all this time somebody jeered at him or her imitating the hero's voice, telling that the hero is back, etc.

J41A.name_eng: Son transforms mother into a bird
J41A.definition_eng: When hero returns, he finds his mother being tormented during his absence and transforms her (and usually himself) into a certain bird

J41B.name_eng: Son returns and burns tormentors using magic
J41B.definition_eng: When hero returns and finds his mother being tormented during his absence, he burns the tormentors producing fire and heat by magic

J41C.name_eng: Trials before confrontation with the antagonist
J41C.definition_eng: A man sets off for a confrontation with dangerous adversary. On his way, he is suggested to fulfill difficult tasks and does it successfully. Usually the same tasks had been suggested before to another man who failed to fulfill them and was killed or imprisoned by the adversary

J41D.name_eng: Strong man throws his iron cudgel and lets it fall on his head
J41D.definition_eng: To test his iron cudgel, sword or the like, strong man throws them into the air and catches (lets them fall on his head, etc.)

J42.definition_eng: When person comes to the water body, waters are split apart so the person reaches the other bank walking on the dry ground

J43.definition_eng: To kill his antagonists, hero lures them with an attractive object which is delicious to eat and is usually on the other side of a body of water or a canyon

J44.definition_eng: Person or his helper draws his enemies on the unstable bridge and destroys it. The enemies fall into water, into a precipice

J45.definition_eng: Person stretches his or her leg or neck as a bridge across water body. The fugitives or those who walk ahead cross the bridge; the persecutor or those who are behind usually fall because the person takes his bridge off

J46.definition_eng: Antagonist perishes falling into the water or trying to cross a water body

J47.definition_eng: Person ascends to the sky (rare: descends from the sky; ascends the cliff) by a rope, a ladder, etc. Another person tries to follow him or her but the rope (the ladder) is broken or severed

J47A.definition_eng: A plant (usually not a tree in nature and often a leguminous) grows in no time and person climbs by it to the sky

J47A1.definition_eng: Person gets into a house inhabited by the goats. He secretly eats the food found there but is ultimately discovered

J47B.definition_eng: A strong rope (chain, etc.) is thrown to the person pursued by a demon but a rotten rope is thrown to the pursuer. The person is saved and the demon falls down (drowns) and dies

J48.definition_eng: Person ascends to the sky or descends from the sky to earth by a rope. A parrot cuts the rope, the person falls to earth

J49.definition_eng: The Moon's wife or sister tries to follow him to the sky but is unable to do it

J4A.name_eng: Revenge for the death of the mother
J4A.definition_eng: A woman is murdered. Her son or children (rare: grandchildren, nephews) revenge for her death

J4B.definition_eng: Children (son, sons, son and daughter) of the murdered woman or man revenge on persons who have marital or close kin relations with the victom

J5.definition_eng: Two or several brothers or friends are killed by antagonists. One of them is the father of the young hero who avenges their death or all of them are his uncles

J50.name_eng: An attempt to revive the victim
J50.definition_eng: Twin heroes' parent dies or is killed, an attempt to revive him or her fails

J50A.definition_eng: Mother dies when her sons embrace or push her

J50B.definition_eng: An attempt to revive the killed father (and uncle) is only partly successful because the revived person is unable to be among the living (to be a warrior). The hero decides to abandon him (in the other world) or to let him die forever

J51.definition_eng: Person or animal is eaten up or destroyed otherwise. His bones are put together and he or it is revived. Because one bone was broken, swallowed or lost (or a drop of blood, a small piece of flesh lost), the person or animal cannot be revived or being revived misses some part of his or its body

J51A.definition_eng: To climb a rock, person must insert into it bones and use them as a ladder

J51A1.name_eng: Helpful girl is dismembered and revived
J51A1.definition_eng: When it is necessary to get an object from a place that is difficult to reach, a girl asks to cut her into pieces (or only to cut off her fingers and toes) and then to put pieces together again. She revives

J51A2.name_eng: The cut off finger instead of the chicken bone
J51A2.definition_eng: A girl must get into an inaccessible place using the chicken bones. Because a bone is lost or their number is insufficient, she cuts off her own finger and achieves her aim using it

J51B.name_eng: One piece is missing: the revived Moon
J51B.definition_eng: The Moon is eaten or died and disintegrated. He is revived by a small piece (a bone) is missing. From this peculiarities of the Moon or of human anatomy

J52.name_eng: Two animal persons and their children
J52.definition_eng: A person (usually zoomorphic and female) treacherously kills her (his) companion. The victim's children revenge on the murderer killing her own children

J52A.definition_eng: A bear-person (usually Bear-woman) kills her or his female companion who is associated with a weaker animal – not a predator or a weaker predator. The victim's children revenge on the antagonist killing her own children and / or run away and escape

J52B.definition_eng: A girl, a young woman, or children who are associated with a hare or rabbit are heroines or successful tricksters

J53.definition_eng: Children of the ungulate animal person (deer, doe, antelope) become the enemies of a predator or bigger ungulate animal person. They kill her (him) and (or) successively escape from her (him)

J53A.name_eng: To involve in a game and to kill
