J53A.definition_eng: A child suggests another to play. The one who has been invited follows the rules but the initiator does not do it and kills the other

J53A1.name_eng: A way of the revenge: to lure into the smoke and fire
J53A1.definition_eng: The victim’s children kill the murderer’s children luring them in a place where the die of smoke or heath

J53B.definition_eng: Two women live together, each one has children. When they are outdoors, one of them kills another and brings home her flesh. The victim’s children gets to see their mother’s breasts (in California: eyes or liver) or their mother’s breasts speak with them

J53C.name_eng: One of two female companions kills another
J53C.definition_eng: Two co-wives of female companions live together, both have children. Once when they go to work outdoors (usually to gather wild plants), one of them kills and devours another. The victim's children escape

J53C1.name_eng: The grizzly-bear and the black bear
J53C1.definition_eng: Two women live together, both have children. One of them kills and (later) eats another. The murderer is associated with the grizzly-bear and the victim with the bear of the smaller species

J54.definition_eng: Animals of particular species that were enemies of the heroes are exterminated besides the only pregnant female (rare a female and a male). Thanks to this, these animals still exist

J54A.name_eng: The calf and the tiger cub
J54A.definition_eng: Two women (usually female animal persons) live together, both have children, one of them kills and devours another or wants to do it. The son of the murderer kills his mother and becomes a companion of the victim's son, or the victim’s and the murderer’s children escape together

J54B.name_eng: Enemy of his mother, friend of his brother
J54B.definition_eng: Son of the antagonist and the hero have the same father or mother (or they are nephew and uncle). When the antagonist conspires against the hero his (her) son becomes friend and companion of the hero

J55.definition_eng: Hero comes across different creatures or persons who do not recognize him. Everyone tells that he is waiting for the Hero to kill him. The hero easily kills or transforms them himself

J56.definition_eng: Twin heroes (or one boy) come to their divine father. He puts them under trials to get know if they are really his children and possess supernatural power

J56A.definition_eng: Brothers turn into cooking pots or griddles which are put on fire. Only the eldest is strong enough to stand this trial

J57.definition_eng: A virgin girl is impregnated by the Sun and gives birth to a son or twin boys. When her son (or the twins) grows up, he (they) comes to his father

J58.definition_eng: Persons shoot arrows (darts) which hit each other’s end forming a chain (rope, ladder). Persons climb by this chain to the sky or (rare) across an obstacle

J58A.name_eng: Three magicians at the bank of a river
J58A.definition_eng: Each of three companions uses his own magic way to cross a river

J58B.definition_eng: Chain of arrows is used to pull or push the sky or the Sun lower or higher or to break a hole in the sky

J58C.definition_eng: Transformation: chain of arrows to bridge

J59.name_eng: Following arrow to get to the sky
J59.definition_eng: To climb to the sky, person must first to shoot an arrow that reaches the sky and sticks to it

J59A.definition_eng: Shooting and an arrow (rare: throwing a ball), person flies on it, after it or ahead of it or sends on the arrow another person

J59B.name_eng: An arrow falls down, a dead one revives
J59B.definition_eng: To revive the dead, person shoots an arrow into the sky (it is suggested that the dead would be afraid of the arrow falling, jump aside and become alive)

J59C.name_eng: To revive the dead with a whiplash
J59C.definition_eng: Person revives the dead beating the bones of corpse with the whip

J59D.name_eng: To revive the dead stepping over his remains
J59D.definition_eng: Person revives the dead stepping or jumping over his remains

J6.name_eng: Children of murdered woman grow up with her murderers
J6.definition_eng: Pregnant woman is killed (and eaten up). Twins are cut off from her womb. They should be eaten too but survive, live (unrecognized) in the house of the antagonists and revenge on them

J60.definition_eng: A woman is impregnated by two different males and gives birth to twin sons who have different fathers

J61.definition_eng: Person is able to move or to hover in the air like a feather or a bit of fluff

J62.definition_eng: Person transforms people who come to him or her into inanimate objects, usually stones

J62A.definition_eng: Person transforms people who come to him or her into trees (or flowers). Hero escapes transformation and revives the victims

J62B.definition_eng: Person transforms people who come to him or her into animals. Thanks to the hero, victims are disenchanted

J62B1.name_eng: The mistress of an island transforms men into animals
J62B1.definition_eng: The sorceress who lives an island transforms men into animals

J62C.name_eng: Sister asks her brother to obtain impossible
J62C.definition_eng: To get rid of a young man, his female antagonist uses a stratagem. She tells his sister (rare: tells directly him) about some wonderful objects and the girl is overcome with the desire to have them. An attempt to obtain these objects entails a risk for one’s life. The youth sets off to obtain the objects

J63.definition_eng: Enemies attack household. The master's wife agrees to live with the enemies' leader, her former husband lies alive but tied up. Somebody (usually his daughter) refuses to release him, but other person (usually his son) does it. The man kills the enemies and usually cruelly kills his wife (and daughter)

J64.name_eng: Person moves on clouds of smoke
J64.definition_eng: Not being burned in a fire, person ascends to the sky or gets across a river on clouds of smoke

J65.definition_eng: A lonely woman with her daughter are the only survivors after enemies' attack. The woman rejects a series of animal-persons who come to ask her daughter in marriage but accept a sky-person for her son-in-law. Children of the sky-person and woman's daughter revenge on the enemies

J66.definition_eng: Hero or his helpers cut or gnaw through bow- and other strings of the enemies, make holes in their canoes in order to forestall pursuit

J67.definition_eng: At night person puts light stones (shells, fruits) on his eyes. The antagonist believes that his eyes are opened and does not dare to attack or takes off the stones and not the eyes

J68.name_eng: Ever fresher dung on a path
J68.definition_eng: Persons who during a long time pursue an animal get to see ever fresher dung on a path and ultimately overtake their game (usually the dung every time answers how old it is); or the pursuers see gardens on which the sowing was had place ever more recently

J69.name_eng: The mock and the real beheading
J69.definition_eng: Person is killed (with the cold weapon, with water of death) and then revived. Another person asks to be exposed to the same procedure but is not revived

J6A.name_eng: Woman is eaten up, her daughter escapes
J6A.definition_eng: Pregnant woman and her small daughter get to ogres. The ogres find the woman and devour her but her daughter and her baby that was extracted from her womb survive and escape

J7.definition_eng: A woman or a girl is in search of her husband (lover) or kinsmen or a man sets out on a journey to his bride. She (he) loses her (his) way because signs that should direct her or him to the right place had been changed

J7A.name_eng: To bring a lunch for the father
J7A.definition_eng: A girl (rare: a boy) has to carry the lunch for her father or brothers who work in the field (in the forest) but gets to the ogre

J8.definition_eng: A woman or a girl is in search of her husband or other person. Bird feathers at the cross-road or near the person's dwelling mark the correct or the wrong way

J9.name_eng: Unborn children talk from the womb
J9.definition_eng: A woman is in search of her husband or other person or object. Her unborn children speak from her stomach and shows her the correct way

K10.definition_eng: Monstrous bird (giant bat) predates on humans. Heroes fight with it

K100.definition_eng: A man gets to know about dangers that threaten another man (and often about turning into stone of anybody who would warn about these dangers). He helps the man to escape the dangers though his behavior seems strange or hostile

K100A.definition_eng: A young man lets free a fish or an animal that was caught or he or his father renders a help to somebody. When the young man sets off for a journey, the grateful creature or person in guise of a stranger or animal becomes his companion and protector

K100B.definition_eng: A young man helps to bury a man (pays the debts of the dead man, honors a saint). When the young man sets off for a journey, the grateful dead (the saint) in guise of a stranger becomes his protector

K100C.name_eng: Girl’s bridegrooms are bitten by a snake
K100C.definition_eng: The hero or his companion eliminate the source of danger

K100D.definition_eng: At the end of the tale helpful animal (horse, lion, etc.) turns himself or herself into a prince (princess)

K100E.definition_eng: Stories act as particular persons: become harmful because they think that a certain person does not treat them in a correct way

K100F.definition_eng: When an unusual fish (rare: bird or some water being) is caught, the (young) man lets it go. His father (the king) drives him away or the man goes away by his own initiative. The saved fish (bird) helps him

K100F1.definition_eng: A man (usually a king) catches a strange (anthropomorphic) creature. His son frees the prisoner, is afraid of his father’s anger and leaves home or is driven away. The released prisoner helps him

K100F2.name_eng: After quenching his thirst, person breaks his chains
K100F2.definition_eng: The imprisoned supernatural person breaks his chains and escapes after they give him some water (or wine, etc.)

K100G.definition_eng: To revive or to cure his friend (rare: himself) or to fulfill a vow person is ready to sacrifice his small (young) son (children). The son revives or the supernatural powers are satisfied with the very willingness of the person to commit sacrifice

K100H.definition_eng: Supernatural person grants wishes of a man (or several men) and later visits him (each of them) again. The man or most of them demonstrate ingratitude and drive the person away. In response to this he deprives them of all that they got thanks to his generosity

K100I.name_eng: Strong person who is made drunk is deprives of his strength
K100I.definition_eng: When mighty person or animal loses his strength (self-control) after being made drunk he recognizes the superiority of the alcoholic intoxication over him

K101.definition_eng: Every morning girl' or (rare) boy’s clothes are in disorder, the boy looks very tied. People spy on her (or on him) and discover that she or he spends nights in the non-human world

K101A.definition_eng: A man has to send several nights near the girl who died and became a dangerous demonic being. After this the girl is disenchanted

K101B.definition_eng: A girl or a youth are disenchanted because the hero bravely spends three nights in a certain place being tortured or terrified by demons. The girl (youth) herself is helpful and not dangerous for the hero

K101B1.definition_eng: The enchanted person (a palace where he or she is) changes his (her, its) appearance gradually as far as the spells dissolve: becomes more human, turns white from black, beautiful from ugly, etc.

K101C.name_eng: In the palace by day, on the sky by night
K101C.definition_eng: A girl agrees to marry a man only if she would be allowed to spend days with him but return for the night to her parents. The husband gets to know that at night she joins company of sky maidens (and usually ascends to the sky to dance). He follows her. After all she remains with her husband on earth

K102.name_eng: Woman associated with the hero conspires in favor of his enemy
K102.definition_eng: A woman who initially is friendly to the hero (his mother, sister, more rare his wife, sexual partner) begins to cooperate with his enemy. For this she provokes the hero to do something that is mortally dangerous for him

K102A.definition_eng: A person gives order to kill the young man’s sister (mother, wife). The young man saves her but later regrets about it

K102A1.definition_eng: To hide truth, person buries an animal or an object and tells that it is the burial of a bride (wife, sister, children, etc.) of another

K102A2.definition_eng: Mother tries to kill her son (children) because he interferes with her love affair

K102A3.definition_eng: Somebody (usually his sister or mother) puts a poisonous tooth (bone, nail, etc.) into the bed of the hero. The young man dies but is revived

K102A4.definition_eng: Hero’s enemy is on the other bank of the river. Hero’s sister or mother helps him to cross the water and becomes his paramour

K102A5.name_eng: To fill a vessel with tears
K102A5.definition_eng: A woman must fill a vessel or two with her teas (rare: blood). Usually after this the time of her punishment will come to the end or the punishment depends on which of the vessels will contain more tears

K102B.name_eng: To ride for the last time
K102B.definition_eng: To kill a boy (a girl), the antagonist first needs to get rid of his or her horse. When they are ready to kill the horse, the boy (the girl) rides on his horse away saving his or her life

K102C.name_eng: Changing his appearance, the hero returns magic object that was stolen from him
K102C.definition_eng: The adversary receives magic object that protects the hero and kills him. The hero is revived, changes his appearance and provokes the adversary to put the object on the ground. He takes it back and kills the adversary

K102C1.definition_eng: The adversary destroys in succession objects and creatures in which the hero is incorporated. The hero wins after he turns from a chip of wood into a waterfowl (a duck or a goose)

K102D.definition_eng: Pretending to be seriously ill, a woman puts dry twigs, bark etc. under her sheets to make other people believe that her bones crunch

K103.definition_eng: Cow (ox, bull) helps an orphan child or a young woman who got into trouble

K103A.definition_eng: A plant (tree, vine, lotus) that has grown up rapidly does not let anybody besides the hero or the heroine to climb it or to pick its fruits (flowers)

K103A1.definition_eng: A tree that has grown up rapidly lets only her mistress to pluck its fruits and follows her when she is moving to live in another place

K103B.definition_eng: A cow (goat) magically spins or weaves: eats the yarn and extracts the thread, suggests to wind the yarn over its horns, etc.

K103C.name_eng: Helpful bull fights in the forest of copper
K103C.definition_eng: Riding a bull or an ox, a lad or a lassie run away from the stepmother’s house. On the way the bull fights with the other bull (monsters) and is usually killed by the last of them

K103D.name_eng: To enter an ear of the horse, to take something from an ear of the cow
K103D.definition_eng: An animal (a demonic being) asks the hero or heroine to take objects necessary for him (her) from its ear or to enter its ear to make himself or herself handsome, to sleep. etc.

K104.definition_eng: The youngest of several brothers remains at home, wounds a red swan or duck, goes away following the bird's trace

K105.definition_eng: A despised wife gives birth to wonderful human children, other wives give birth to animals

K106.definition_eng: To get rid of a baby child or of the magic cock, they throw him into enclosure for animals, but cows or other animals do not trample the child or cock down

K107.definition_eng: A woman is abandoned by her magic husband. She finds him and becomes his wife again

K107A.name_eng: Iron shoes to be worn out
K107A.definition_eng: Wandering to the purpose of her or his travel person has to worn out her or his iron shoes or staff

K107A1.name_eng: Head of the household is asked to bring presents
K107A1.definition_eng: When the head of the household goes for a journey his daughter, those who remain at home ask to bring them presents. The elder ones want something practical (usually clothes or decorations) while the younger one asks for something unusual (a flower, a bird, etc.). Thanks to this object, the younger one attains great success though after overcoming great difficulties

K107A2.name_eng: Shepard’s daughter instead of the princess
K107A2.definition_eng: Being forced to promise his daughter (son) to a demon (monster, predator animal), a noble man (king) tries but in vain to replace his child with another girl or boy

K107A3.definition_eng: When a man sets off for the journey, his daughter asks him to bring her a certain flower (leave, etc.). The man picks it up in a garden of the enchanted prince who has monstrous appearance. The monster claims from the man his daughter and thanks to her acquires his real guise

K107A4.name_eng: Daughter asks to bring magic bridegroom
K107A4.definition_eng: When a man sets off for the journey, his daughter asks him to bring her an object or creature which is the incorporation of the magic bridegroom, or she asks to find somebody, and this man is her magic bridegroom. The man does not understand well what does it mean

K107B.definition_eng: One of the spouses prohibits another to see him or her. When the other breaks the taboo (intentionally or by chance) the first one disappears (is in trouble)

K107C.name_eng: Knives on the windowsill (the prince as bird)
K107C.definition_eng: Magic bridegroom who comes as bird or other guise and then changes into a man meets regularly with a young woman. Her jealous sisters (stepmother, brother, etc.) wound him (usually putting knives of broken glass around the window). He disappears, the girl goes to find him.

K107D.name_eng: The girl cannot wake her fiancé
K107D.definition_eng: Failed attempts to wake magic husband

K107D1.name_eng: Magic wife’s failed attempts to wake a youth
K107D1.definition_eng: A youth has a date with a woman who belongs to supernatural world but he falls asleep and she is unable to wake him

K107E.definition_eng: Woman is pregnant for many years and gives birth not until her enchanted husband who had abandoned her or somebody else let her do it

K107E1.definition_eng: When supernatural husband abandons his human wife, his shirt becomes stained with blood and only his wife when she comes to him is able to make the shirt clean

K108.name_eng: A revived wife betrays her husband
K108.definition_eng: Wife dies, husband revives her, she abandons him for another man and is punished

K108A.name_eng: After murdering his wife, the man loses everything
K108A.definition_eng: A man acquires a magic wife. Another woman agrees to marry him if he abandons or kills his first wife. The man does it and loses everything

K109.definition_eng: A man is advised to ask for his service rendered to a powerful being a puppy or a small object (a beaker). The puppy or object turns into beautiful girl who is a daughter of a deity. Other person makes attempts to take the woman away

K10A.name_eng: Battle with a bird: a shelter
K10A.definition_eng: Heroes kill a dangerous bird. During or before confrontation they hide inside a shelter (hut, cage, vessel, bag, hollow log) or cover themselves with a protective object

K10B.definition_eng: A giant bird carries away to its nest a cage or bag with people inside

K10C.definition_eng: Hero (or twins) hangs on his body a bag with animal bowels full of blood. Breaking them with its claws, the bird thinks that its victim is killed and brings the man to its nest. He kills the adult bird, kills or transforms its nestlings

K10D.name_eng: Bird carries man to an island
K10D.definition_eng: A flying monster carries a man to a far away island. There he gets to kill the monster. To return, he uses a boat, a bridge or a rope made of parts of the monster's body

K10E.definition_eng: Getting to a nest of a monstrous bird, a man finds there kidnapped people, helps them to return home

K10F.definition_eng: Hero transforms nestlings or monster bird into common eagles or owls

K10G.name_eng: The man uses a fledgeling to descend to the earth
K10G.definition_eng: A man gets into the nest of a giant bird on a high rock or tree. He descends to the earth killing the bird and fixing its feathers or wings to his body or (more often) using the bird’s nestling (riding on its back, holding its feet, fixing its feathers or wings)

K10H.name_eng: A bird feeds but does not release its prisoner
K10H.definition_eng: A giant bird carries a woman or a boy to its nest. It supplies them with food but does not release. The prisoner escapes

K10I.name_eng: A tree that opens its trunk
K10I.definition_eng: A tree opens its trunk to provide a refuge for a hero pursued by the monstrous bird. When the bird follows the hero the tree crushes it squeezing its trunk again

K11.name_eng: Eyes of a monstrous bird: metamorphosis
K11.definition_eng: Two brothers (brother and sister) kill monstrous bird. It eyes turn into the Sun and Moon (Oaxaca Indians) or in something else (Yokuts: common condors)

K110.definition_eng: Person must get a treasure from the bottom of water body. He understands that what he sees is a reflection in water while the treasure is high in a tree

K111.name_eng: Animal suitors rejected, a man from the sky accepted
K111.definition_eng: Mother of a girl rejects in succession birds (and animals) who come to ask her daughter in marriage, but accepts a man from the sky (the Sun) as her son-in-law

K112.definition_eng: A poor man condemns the Sun and other supernatural personages responsible for weather, wild animals, etc. that because of them he lost his property. He finds them and punishes them

K113.definition_eng: Several young men (usually three brothers) decide to choose wives (usually shooting arrows or throwing objects on the off-chance). The wife of the youngest initially is ugly or non-human (a frog, a snake) but proves to be beautiful enchantress. She and her husband triumph. Or girls choose their husbands and the youngest one gets a youth who has guise of a snake

K113A.name_eng: To take wife where arrow falls
K113A.definition_eng: A young man shoots an arrow or throws an object on the off-chance He finds the girl to be married or something that helps to obtain her at the place where his arrow (other object) falls

K113B.name_eng: The frog-princess is the mistress of thunderstorm
K113B.definition_eng: The younger prince marries a frog. When she is riding to his parents for the first time, thunderstorm begins. The rain means that she is bathing, the lightning that she is decorating herself, the thunder that she is coming, etc.

K114.name_eng: Brothers leave home after their sister is born
K114.definition_eng: Several brothers leave home immediately after their mother gives birth to a girl. Usually they do not want to have another brother and hope that this time a girl will be born but chance or by evil intent a signal is given that not a girl but a boy is born again. The brothers are disappointed and leave, the girl grows up and travels in search of them

K115.name_eng: Person saved thanks to the spider web
K115.definition_eng: A man escapes from his (her, theirs) pursuers and hides in a cave. A spider spins its web over the hiding place. When the pursuers see the spider web they think the cave is unoccupied and do not enter it

K116.definition_eng: To choose a companion, the youth suggests each of the candidates to make something simple (to eat the served food, to set off). The chosen one demonstrates that he cares for the hero while others keep in mind only their own interests

K116A.name_eng: King is killed after putting on a strange attire
K116A.definition_eng: A powerful person abducts or is going to abduct a poor man’s wife. She tricks him to put on a strange attire (often her husband’s clothes). After this his men or dogs kill him taking for the poor man (fool, devil)

K116B.name_eng: The girl in the box is replaced with ferocious dog
K116B.definition_eng: To get a girl in his possession, the antagonist creates a situation when her relations must put her in a box (barrel, bag, etc.) and then abandon, throw it into the river or give it to him. The girl is imperceptibly replaced with a ferocious dog or other animal. Usually when the antagonist opens the box, the animal kills or injures him

K116C.name_eng: Father is persuaded to put his daughter into the box
K116C.definition_eng: To get a girl, a minister of religion persuades her father to put her into the box (barrel) and throw it into the river or abandon in a wilderness

K117.definition_eng: A woman should marry a man who would be able to make her laugh; a man promises a reward to the person who would make laugh his daughter, mother or son

K117A.name_eng: To make a mute woman speak
K117A.definition_eng: A girl who keeps silence is promised to one who would make her speak; a man with much difficulty makes his magic wife speak

K117B.definition_eng: Using a magic object or spell, hero makes people (and animals) attached to the object or to each other

K117C.definition_eng: As soon as a person plays his flute (fiddle, horn, etc.), people and animals become to dance and cannot stop without the person’s permission

K117C1.name_eng: To play his fiddle before the death
K117C1.definition_eng: A person sentenced to death asks to give him something of his belongings, usually a musical instrument. As soon as he gets it, he becomes powerful and escapes

K117D.name_eng: Two bridegrooms in one bed with a princess
K117D.definition_eng: A princess who lies or stands between two pretenders for her hand must choose one of them without seeing him. The bridegroom of low social position tricks the noble one to be smeared by filth and the princess turns to one who smells aromatically

K118.definition_eng: Master of the house allows person to feel himself (herself) free bit not to look into particular place. The person breaks prohibition

K118A.name_eng: A portrait of an unknown beauty
K118A.definition_eng: After seeing a portrait of an unknown beauty, a man is eager to meet her

K119.name_eng: Animal helper marries a poor boy to a princess
K119.definition_eng: To make a poor man rich (usually to marry him to a rich girl or to marry a poor girl to a prince), an animal makes other people believe that the groom is rich already. The man becomes prosperous indeed

K119A.definition_eng: An animal saves a man or helps him but the ungrateful man humiliates the animal, kills or tries to kill it

K119B.name_eng: Wild animals presented to the king
K119B.definition_eng: Helpful trickster (usually the fox or the cat) deceives wild animals and brings them to the king saying that they are presented to him by a rich person

K119C.name_eng: The Thunder king and the Lightning queen
K119C.definition_eng: The antagonist believes that he is attacked by the commander of thunder-storm (who married his daughter to a poor boy thanks to a stratagem of a helpful animal; see k119)

K119D.definition_eng: A cat marries a poor boy to a princess (poor girl to a prince)

K119E.name_eng: A success story of a miller
K119E.definition_eng: A poor boy whom his animal helper has made rich passing him off as a rich man at the king’s court, is a miller or son of a miller

K11A.name_eng: Feathers turn into birds or men
K11A.definition_eng: Feathers of (giant) bird turn into different present day birds (in their plumage) or into the men

K11A1.name_eng: Birds emerge from the monstrous bird
K11A1.definition_eng: Pierces of flesh or feathers of monstrous/unusual bird turn into common birds (or into their plumage)

K11B.definition_eng: Bones of a giant bird turn into reeds or bamboo from which arrows or blowpipes are made

K12.definition_eng: By trick or by force, a rival or adversary kidnaps hero's wife or bride. The man gets her back

K120.definition_eng: A man is going to marry his daughter (rare: his stepdaughter; sometimes certain conditions are put on his future marriage and only his daughter complies with them). The girl gets to escape

K120A.definition_eng: A man is going to marry his sister (often puts certain condition on his future marriage, only his sister complies with them). The girl gets to escape

K120A1.definition_eng: In order to delay a wedding with an undesirable suitor (her own brother or father, a monster), a girl asks him to give her a dress (often three dresses in succession) of unusual material (like gold, of fly wings, etc.). He does it but the girl runs away

K120A2.name_eng: Not my mother but my mother-in-law
K120A2.definition_eng: Members of the girl’s family want to marry her to a man who should not be her marriage partner (usually it is her own brother). They ask her to name them as her in-laws or the girl herself tells that they are not anymore her mother, sister, etc. but her mother-in-law, sister-in-law, etc. or her worst enemies

K120A3.definition_eng: Person gets a nut with valuables inside (precious clothes, jewelry, animal helpers, etc.) or he or she himself or herself puts valuable into a nut to use them later

K120A4.name_eng: To fill a vessel with tears
K120A4.definition_eng: Person must fill a vessel (to cover a floor) with tears

K120A5.name_eng: Luring a woman to a ship
K120A5.definition_eng: To trap a desired woman, person lures her to a ship (boat, flying machine, etc.) and carries away

K121.definition_eng: It is written at a crossroad that following one of the paths person will safely return and following another it will not return (there is often a third path following which person either returns or not). Hero follows the dangerous path

K122.name_eng: Queen of the other world comes to identify the hero
K122.definition_eng: A man gets to the powerful woman who lives in the world unreachable without the supernatural helpers, and then returns back. An imposter claims hero's deeds for himself. The powerful woman comes and finds the real hero, punishes (rejects) the imposter

K123.definition_eng: A youth or (rare) girl offends a woman who older than he (usually quite old) or is a cripple. Her words make him or her to be overcome by desire to undertake something dangerous (usually to get a particular marriage partner)

K123A.definition_eng: A youth breaks or overthrows a vessel of a woman or girl. This episode is a trigger for the narrative

K123B.definition_eng: A youth spoils an elder woman’s distaff or yarn. This episode is a trigger for the narrative

K124.definition_eng: An animal killed by a hunter revives. The animal itself or somebody else tells the hunter that there was a greater wonder (sorrow) with such and such a person. The story follows

K125.definition_eng: An enemy asks house utensils or personal objects where their master hid himself or herself or what direction he or she ran away. One of the objects, not treated by the master in a proper way, betrays him or her

K126.name_eng: Wolf pays for the eaten up horse
K126.definition_eng: A wolf (lion, etc.) or a demon eats up hero's horse but gives him a fair compensation (usually provides a wife)

K127.definition_eng: A girl has many (more than three) brothers, they turn into birds or animals (rare: into plants; killed by magic), ultimately become human again

K127A.definition_eng: A girl or young woman is bewitched to be mute or must keep silence for a period of time. Just when she has to be put to death, the period of her muteness is over and she is saved

K127B.definition_eng: Several brothers are transformed into bulls (oxen) but ultimately disenchanted

K128.name_eng: Grazing animals to be preserved by a herdsman
K128.definition_eng: A man had to graze animals or birds. If at least one is lost, the master would kill (not reward) him. Cf. K128B (ATU 570)

K128A.definition_eng: Each of three brothers carry to the princess some fruits (rare: fish, etc.). She will marry a man whose fruits are better (more numerous) or can cure her. On their way two brothers treat roughly a person who possesses supernatural power and are punished while the youngest brother is polite and rewarded. He (after additional tests) marries the princess

K128B.definition_eng: King offers his daughter in marriage to whoever can herd (catch, tame, train) a particular number of rabbits (roosters, sheep, goats, geese, partridges) without losing any. A poor boy receives a magic whistle or other device with which he can summon the rabbits. In order to avoid the marriage, members (deputies) of the royal family (in disguise) try to but pne of his rabbits. The young man demands a degrading humiliating act and after the demands are fulfilled, the rabbit comes back to him.

K129.definition_eng: Because of the female antagonist, a girl faints and is taken for dead but her body is not decomposed. A valuable marriage partner breaks the charms, she revives

K129A.name_eng: Half alive lady in the burial chamber
K129A.definition_eng: A young woman (in the burial chamber) is now alive and now dead but after all she is disenchanted

K12A.definition_eng: An unrecognized hero comes to a place where his bride or wife has to marry another man or is tuned into a slave. Despite expectations, he gets to strain a tight bow killing his rivals

K12B.name_eng: Husband of magic wife breaks her taboo
K12B.definition_eng: Getting to the world that is beyond the world of the human beings, a man marries there a woman. She gives him permission to visit his home but he must avoid particular words or deeds. He breaks the taboo triggering an (irretrievable) trouble

K130.definition_eng: A woman (rare: a man) asks if she (he) is the most beautiful among female (men) folk and always receives a positive answer. It continues till she or he receives the negative one

K130A.name_eng: Girl in house of several brothers
K130A.definition_eng: A group of young men live apart. A girl comes to them or is born magically. The men keep her as their sister. After some time she is separated from them and is in danger but ultimately she is rescued

K131.definition_eng: A man on a journey meets tree or two persons who are quarreling over the division of magic objects (a flying carpet, seven mile boots, etc.). The man promises to render a judgment, but he asks first to try our the objects or suggests the owners to run a race and uses opportunity to escape with the objects

K131A.definition_eng: Several animals (often a lion, an eagle, an ant) argue because of an animal carcass or a living place. A man settles their argument, they give him capacity to acquire their form (their qualities)

K131B.name_eng: Magic objects are exchanged and returned
K131B.definition_eng: A man loses a magic object that he got before but gets it back thanks to another object (a cudgel, a box with soldiers, etc.) that is exchanged for the first one or obtained by the man’s brother. The episode can be repeated several times

K131C.name_eng: The abducted woman escapes while the men are involved into shooting competition
K131C.definition_eng: Being abducted, a woman promises to marry the man who is the best shooter and escape while they are in search of their arrows

K131D.definition_eng: The boots (shoes, sandals) which allow the person wearing them to move with extraordinary speed are mentioned

K132.definition_eng: Person of a small size (often a chicken) overcomes powerful adversary despite all attempts to destroy him thanks to objects and animals met on the way and preserved in his bag or inside his body

K132A.definition_eng: Husband (rare: wife) sends his cock to earn money and the cock brings it. Wife (husband) sends her hen (cat, her half of a cock, etc.) and it brings filth. Or the cock brings to the wife not money but something bad or does not bring anything

K133.definition_eng: Every morning a horse is exhausted because animals or demonic creatures ride it at night

K134.definition_eng: To accuse a guest of theft, a host plants a treasure into his guest’s bag

K135.definition_eng: A weak and timid man or boy overcomes accidentally powerful enemies and gets high esteem

K135A.definition_eng: A coward or lazy-bones irritates his household so much they expel him home. He travels and overcomes mighty enemies thanks to his ingenuity or good luck

K136.definition_eng: A lad becomes a master and a leader of great amount of cattle (cows or buffaloes) and meets a princess (usually after she finds his hair fallen into a river)

K136A.name_eng: Girl’s hair picked up from a river
K136A.definition_eng: A man finds the woman’s hair that was carried by water and decides to marry its owner

K136A1.name_eng: Youth’s hair picked up from a river
K136A1.definition_eng: A woman finds the youth’s hair that was carried by water and decides to marry its owner

K136B.definition_eng: Person finds precious stones or miraculous flowers (usually in a river) and gets to know whence they originate

K136C.definition_eng: Every time when a demonic person goes away he kills or puts asleep a woman reviving her when he comes back

K136D.definition_eng: Young man receives a flute (pipe, horn) from cows (buffaloes) to inform them on his condition. Usually the animals give two musical tools with different sounds (joy and grief, piece and danger)

K137.name_eng: Sister tricks women to come and revive her brother
K137.definition_eng: When her brother is killed, a girl puts on his clothes and in a guise of a man wins competitions and gets women who are able to revive the dead. She puts the clothes back on her brother and the women come and revive him taking him for their husband. Or a sister is killed and her brother after winning wives tricks them to revive her

K137A.name_eng: A girl in her brother’s guise gets a wife for him
K137A.definition_eng: A young man is killed. His sister puts on his clothes and pretending she is a man gets a wife for him. This woman beliefs that the girl’s brother from the very beginning was a man whom she married

K138.name_eng: Exchange of bodies (king and his minister)
K138.definition_eng: Person gets an ability to enter a dead body and revive it. His own body remains dead for this time. Another person takes it for himself while the first one remains in an animal’s body

K139.definition_eng: Roasting meat or baking bread for his master, a servant sees a girl (rare: small boy) and is so impressed with her (or his) beauty, that the meat or bread get burnt

K13A.name_eng: Person with cut off leg ascends to the sky
K13A.definition_eng: Person's leg (rare: both legs) is cut, torn, bitten off, injured. He (rare: she) ascends to the sky: to the Moon; turns into the Moon, Sun, star, constellation; blood from the injured leg makes the sky red

K13B.definition_eng: A caiman ferries a man across water body, bites his leg off. The maimed man is transformed into a constellation or into an animal

K13C.name_eng: Ogress’ daughter avenges death of her mother
K13C.definition_eng: A man marries an ogress' daughter, kills her mother. The wife revenges on him, gets to cut off his leg

K13D.definition_eng: A group of boys gets to the sky. The leg of the last one is cut or torn off

K14.definition_eng: A man gives his last money for simple advices. Each of them saves his life or helps to achieve success or he does not follow the advices and gets into trouble

K140.definition_eng: Travelling with his sibling, a youth regularly kills those who help him and save him creating for himself ever more problems

K141.definition_eng: Supernatural women make harm to people. Hero overcomes them and usually marries them

K142.definition_eng: Person kills several people. asks somebody to bury only one and then tells that the dead man has returned. The grave-digger buries several people but believes that it was one and the same corpse

K143.definition_eng: Protagonist of the story is a bird-catcher (bird-hunter) or a son of a bird-catcher (bird-hunter)

K144.name_eng: The predestined death because of an animal
K144.definition_eng: A certain animal or (rare) man is predicted to become a cause of death of a certain person. When this animal (man) is already dead himself or itself or is faraway, its (his) remains or image becomes the cause of the person’s death

K145.name_eng: The predestined death because of the wolf
K145.definition_eng: A wolf is predicted to become a cause of death of a person or the person must die at his wedding day. The prophesy becomes true. If it is about the marriage, the bride herself turns into a wolf and kills her bridegroom

K145A.name_eng: Not the animal but its picture kills
K145A.definition_eng: It is foretold that the person will die because of the animal. The person dies when the animal’s representation becomes alive or a statue representing the animal falls on him

K145B.definition_eng: When a girl and a man remain alone (usually during their wedding night), the girl turns into a predator animal or a monster and devours the man

K146.name_eng: Life-medicine brought by the hero is used to revive him
K146.definition_eng: The hero is sent to bring a life-medicine. On his way back a friendly woman replaces the real medicine with a useless one or keeps part of it for herself. Using the medicine she revives the hero when he is treacherously killed

K147.name_eng: Hero's horse brings his remains and he is revived
K147.definition_eng: Enemy cuts hero’s body into pieces and ties them to his horse or the horse itself picks them up and brings to his master’s friends. They revive him.

K148.definition_eng: Every night or every year a mare gives birth to a colt but every time it is stolen

K149.definition_eng: Person receives a rope, reins or the like with three knots. If untied, person can move more or less rapidly. Usually untying the first two knots he makes his ship or his horse move more rapidly but, besides warning, he (being near to his destination) unties the third knot too and because of it he looses his ship or his horse, does not reach his destination, etc.

K14A.definition_eng: An antagonist orders to kill the first one who will come in the morning to a certain place. The hero becomes late by chance, the antagonist or his wife or son come and are thrown into the fire

K14B.name_eng: A charge of stealing the knife
K14B.definition_eng: A man receives good advice never to act before he is insistently asked to do it. When he decides to be helpful and gives his knife (rare: other weapon) without being insistently asked for it, he is accused of a crime

K14B1.name_eng: When you travel, take a companion
K14B1.definition_eng: A man receives good advice not to travel alone. He takes an animal for companion, and at night it saves his life

K14C.name_eng: Man mistakes his son for his wife’s lover
K14C.definition_eng: Coming home after a long absence, a man understands that there is another man in his house but keeps patience and discovers that it is his own son or a close kin of his wife

K14C1.definition_eng: A man who sets off to earn money sends to his wife a pomegranate without knowledhe of its real value. The wife find treasure inside

K14D.definition_eng: To test his wife (friend, member of his household), a man pretends to commit a crime or his behavior seems to be strange and deserved to be punished. At the last moment he presents evidence that proves his innocence

K14E.definition_eng: Sons of a man neglect their father (daughters-in-law neglect their father-in-law). He pretends to be hiding something (counts money conspicuously, etc.). The sons believe that their father has considerable inheritance and become to look after him carefully. When the father finally dies they find nothing valuable in his chest

K15.name_eng: I embraced nobody besides this beggar
K15.definition_eng: A woman swears that she never embraced anybody besides (her husband and) the beggar who is among the people. The people do not know that her lover assumed the beggar’s image

K150.definition_eng: Magic horse eats (hot) coals, nails, etc. or they try to feed the horse with such a staff

K151.definition_eng: Supernatural creature fulfills a poor man’s moderate request. After this he or his wife asks for ever bigger gifts till the angry helper punishes them (usually takes all his gifts away)

K152.name_eng: The devil is frightened and runs away
K152.definition_eng: A man saves a devil (snake, dangerous animal) who suffers from proximity of certain object or person. The grateful devil promises to enter a princess and abandon her as soon as the man comes to cure her. The man will get a reward but he should not try such a trick again. The man scares the devil forever telling him that the object or person of which the devil is afraid will be near soon

K152A.name_eng: The evil woman and the devil in one pit
K152A.definition_eng: A man throws his evil wife into the pit or well. The devil (snake, predator animal, etc.) who had been there before is grateful when the man pulls him to the surface or jumps our himself: even he is afraid of the shrewish woman

K153.definition_eng: Человек оказывает услугу нескольким (потенциально опасным) животным и другому человеку. Благодарные животные помогают ему, а человек предает и вредит

K154.definition_eng: A man picks up a skull with an enigmatic and ominous inscription on it. Later its meaning becomes clear

K154A.definition_eng: Solving a riddle, a boy or youth unmasks a daughter (wife, minister) of a powerful person: house-maids (or some of them) are men, the minister plans to kill his master)

K155.definition_eng: A man (usually a king) isolates his son (daughter) in a closed room, Once the boy (girl), usually because of some chance event gets to see the world outside and his (her) isolation comes the end

K155A.definition_eng: A man (usually a king) keeps his daughter (rare: his son) in a closed room, servants bring the girl (boy) meat without bones. Once she or he finds a bone in the meat, uses it to make an opening in the wall and gets to see the world outside

K155B.name_eng: Climbing up to the girl by her hair
K155B.definition_eng: A girl lets down her long hair and another person uses it as a rope to climb up to her

K155C.definition_eng: Father regularly puts his daughter on the scales and understands that she is pregnant because she is heavier than before

K156.name_eng: Will flowers wither undeer the pillow?
K156.definition_eng: A girl conceals her real identity and pretends to be a young man. To identify real sex of the person, flowers are put under his/her pillow or the mattress. If it is a man, the flowers should remain fresh and if a girl, wither (or, if it is a woman, milk in a pot under the bed will be fermented)

K156A.name_eng: Tests to reveal the sex of a person
K156A.definition_eng: People suspect that a young man is a disguised girl and suggest tests to identify the real sex of this person

K156B.name_eng: Dog helps the girl to remain unmasked
K156B.definition_eng: People suspect that a young man is a disguised girl and suggest tests to identify the real sex of this person. Her dog (rare: cat) listens to people’s plans and the girl avoids all the traps

K157.definition_eng: Person tricks his enemies to come or to leave their enclosure one by one and cuts off their head as soon as the next one appears. In rare cases the multi-headed enemy thrusts his heads on by one and the hero cuts them off

K157A.name_eng: Vanished husband recognized by keeping inn
K157A.definition_eng: For finding the lost husband (wife, benefactor), person regularly assemble together the chance people to hear what they are saying (usually sets up an inn, bakery, bathhouse and the like where guests are stimulated to talk). One of the people proves to be the lost one or his or her story helps to find the lost one

K158.name_eng: Who is the woman on a portrait?
K158.definition_eng: To find the lost husband (and other men who were helpful or cruel to her), a woman demonstrates her portrait in a public place and calls to her everybody whose reaction shows that they recognized who was represented

K159.definition_eng: When two persons are fighting, somebody wants one of them fall (while another be firm on his feet) and for this throws something under his feet

K15A.definition_eng: Hero substitutes powerful person's weapon or amulet with a fake

K15B.definition_eng: Because containers with alive and dead water (one makes one stronger, another weaker) are imperceptibly exchanged, during the battle the hero drinks the alive water and overcomes his enemy who drinks the dead water

K15C.definition_eng: The owner of the stone (ice) clothes kills people. The hero hides these clothes or substitutes them with a fake and kills the owner

K16.name_eng: To get access to a girl in guise of a bird or an animal
K16.definition_eng: Disguised as a bird, small animal or insect, a man penetrates into the place of a girl (into her father’s house)

K160.name_eng: Three hairs from the devil’s beard
K160.definition_eng: Hero must bring hairs, feathers, scales, etc. of a dangerous person and does it thanks to the helps of a wife or (grand)mother of this person

K160A.name_eng: Demon’s answers to his wife’s questions
K160A.definition_eng: A woman who lives in the house of a supernatural person conceals the man who had come to her and puts questions to this person. The answers that are received and became known to the man are of great importance for him

K161.definition_eng: Person imprisoned a dragon (demon, Thunder, etc.) and warns the other not to open a certain room (not to give water to the prisoner, etc.). The instruction is broken and the demon liberates himself that has undesirable consequences

K162.name_eng: The robber gets into the sleeping room
K162.definition_eng: The antagonist (robber, wizard, witch) penetrates into the house of a girl or young woman hiding in a state (in cupboard, etc.) and/or putting her husband (guards) to sleep using a medicine. At the last moment he is destroyed

K163.definition_eng: A magician orders a boy to fetch a magic object (often a lamp). The boy finds the object (but refuses to give it to the magician), and the object fulfills the boy’s wishes

K164.name_eng: Wife is not the best friend
K164.definition_eng: A man himself or somebody else creates situation that demonstrates that his wife is not his best friend. Often a treacherous wife is contrasted with a true dog

K165.name_eng: The youth who wanted to learn what fear is
K165.definition_eng: A youth who does not know what fear is tries various frightful experiences without becoming afraid

K166.definition_eng: A group of girls forms a community or an armed contingent and acts independently from the men

K167.definition_eng: A boy who plays making believe that he is a king demonstrates wisdom and/or magic capacities

K167A.name_eng: The son of the king and the son of the smith
K167A.definition_eng: The king’s wife hates her son whom she should give birth and decides to get rid of him. As a result, the baby prince and the son of a commoner are interchanged. The prince is smart and inherits his father throne anyway

K167B.name_eng: How does the lamb in the ewe’s womb look like?
K167B.definition_eng: The boy is able to determine the sex and the color of a baby-animal in its mother’s womb

K168.name_eng: An illusory life as long as a second
K168.definition_eng: Person gets to live a long life rich in events but eventually finds himself in the same place and moment from which the story begins.

K168A.name_eng: Food turns into cut off limbs
K168A.definition_eng: A man believes that he holds something edible in his hands (a head of an animal, bread, melon, etc.) but these objects turn into cut off human heads or limbs

K168B.name_eng: Man is made to believes he is a bear
K168B.definition_eng: A man makes another believe that he is bear, gets into the forest, etc. Being conjured up, the dreamer finds himself on the same place where he was

K169.definition_eng: A hunter spares life of an animal when he understands that it is pregnant female who reminds him his own wife, also pregnant

K16A.definition_eng: Being eager to show that he is a successful hunter, a man walks in front of a girl carrying a game (deer, birds). The girl makes him slip, he drops the false game that proves to be a dummy stuffed with ashes or a termite nest

K17.definition_eng: An ornitomorphic hero impregnates a girl magically or imperceptibly for her

K170.name_eng: Water without frogs, land without flies
K170.definition_eng: Person goes in search of a place where there are no living beings that usually are widespread (water without frogs, air without flies)

K171.definition_eng: Somebody from the enemies’ camp is constantly weaving (forging) ever new warriors (rare: weapons)

K172.name_eng: Deaf bride without hands and feet
K172.definition_eng: When a potential bridegroom comes to a man, the latter tells that his daughter is a deformed cripple. The bride proves to be a beauty

K173.definition_eng: A powerful and rich man loses everything that he has, is separated with his wife and children and they with each other. Later he obtains everything back, his family is united again

K174.definition_eng: A person puts (usually inconspicuously) his or her fingering or other small personal object into a pitcher with which a servant (girl) has come to take water. The servant's mistress or master finds the ring and understands that the person is nearby

K175.name_eng: The wind blows the flour away
K175.definition_eng: A person carries some flour, the wind blows it away. The person appeals to a powerful person and usually gets compensation

K176.name_eng: A man in search of the woman
K176.definition_eng: A (young) man sets off to find or to return his bride or his wife

K176A.definition_eng: Hero is in search of his lost magic wife. One of the winds is just going to fly there because he must do there some work. The hero joins him

K176B.definition_eng: When a man or a woman travels in search of his or her marriage partner, only the wind knows the way and/brings them to their destination

K177.definition_eng: A girl or young woman sets off to find or return her fience or her husband or she escapes from a fanger and ultimately marries happily

K178.definition_eng: A young woman follows an enchanted man to his underground place, becomes pregnant but breaks a taboo and is chased away. She finds lodging in a rich house, her husband finds her and is disenchanted

K179.name_eng: Bride purchased for her weight in gold
K179.definition_eng: An object (usually the bride) purchased for the sum of money equivalent (or bigger) than its weight in gold (silver) or a heap of valuables as high as the corresponding person

K18.name_eng: Infant picks out his unknown father
K18.definition_eng: A boy is born whose father or (rare) mother is unknown. He himself points at his parent who as a rule occupies the lowest social position. Usually many men (women) come together and everyone hopes that the boy points at him (her)

K180.name_eng: The time of wolf and the time of fox
K180.definition_eng: A ruler has a dream and demands to explain it. A snake tells a man that this dream signals the beginning or a time period when people act in particular way. The episode repeats with different dreams. Every time the man’s behavior towards the snake proves that the corresponding period really has begun

K181.definition_eng: The hero finds the horse that fits his needs in a cellar (cave, tower, etc.) where it had been preserved for a long time

K181A.name_eng: To put the arm on the back of a horse
K181A.definition_eng: When a man puts his arm on the back of a horse, the horse gives way, falls. It is a sign of the man’s unusual strength

K182.definition_eng: Supernatural person comes to help every time when he hears a signal of alarm but refuses to do it since the signal was given without a reason

K182A.definition_eng: Mighty hero is retired to the cave (tomb etc.) will come back to the world (to help his people) or he could come but decided not to do it

K183.name_eng: In what fish is the swallowed one?
K183.definition_eng: Person cuts open all water creatures (vultures) or looks into their mouths to find the swallowed one or a part of his body

K184.name_eng: When the forest will get in motion
K184.definition_eng: Person associates the arrival of an event that he considers impossible with the time when trees of the forest will get in motion like people

K18A.name_eng: Infant takes father’s bow and arrows
K18A.definition_eng: When a small boy has to recognize his father among many men, he comes to him and takes father's bow and arrows

K18AA.name_eng: Pregnancy because of the non-sexual contact
K18AA.definition_eng: A girl becomes pregnant without her knowledge thanks to the contact with body liquids of a male person or with objects touched by him (not because of the normal sexual contact, or a wish expressed by the father of her future child, or her mistical contact with a deity). The happy marriage of the girl with her child’s father follows

K18B.name_eng: Baby boy does not cry anymore
K18B.definition_eng: A baby boy has to recognize his father or mother among many people. When his parent takes him, the boy ceases crying

K18C.definition_eng: A baby boy has to recognize his father among many men. When his father takes him, the boy urinates at his arms

K18D.name_eng: A lazy boy and a fish
K18D.definition_eng: A lazy (stupid) boy releases a fish (frog, serpent, supernatural being) which gives him a power of making all his wishes come true; he marries a princess

K19C.name_eng: Non-human lover in man’s bed or bag
K19C.definition_eng: A man brings home a small being with whom he makes love at night. His mother, sister or wife discovers his non-human lover in his bed or bag

K19D.definition_eng: When a man who has married a star gets to the sky, he suffers severe cold and dies either of cold or after touching a forbidden fire

K19E.definition_eng: When a woman or two sisters descend from sky back to earth, they get to the top of a tree. Some animals who walk by cannot help them or do not want to help. Wolverine gets women down because he plans to marry them but they escape from him

K19F.definition_eng: Star person or persons descend to earth to work at the garden plot

K19G.name_eng: Two stars of different color and brightness
K19G.definition_eng: Two stars are men, an old and a young ones. They look different as about their color or brightness but these characteristics do not correlate (the bright star can prove to be an old man and vice versa. Usually two girls wish these stars for husbands and express different preferences (one prefers bright blue star, another wants small and red one, etc.)

K1C.name_eng: One who comes to look at adversary’s bones dies himself
K1C.definition_eng: A man is marooned on an islet, a rock but survives thanks to helpful birds and animals. The next time the hero and the antagonist exchange roles. Usually the antagonist comes to the islet to see the bones of the abandoned man but the man takes the canoe of the antagonist and paddles away. The antagonist dies

K1D.definition_eng: Brothers of a man's wife hate him and maroon on an islet

K1E.definition_eng: Person is marooned on an islet or on another side of a sea or wide river

K1F.definition_eng: A man maroons another because of jealousy or because he plans to take hold of his wife

K1G.definition_eng: Hero turns into stag or creates a stag to charge his kinsman who sent hi into a trap

K1H.definition_eng: Person is imprisoned in a tree-hollow or inside a rock and is released by somebody who makes a hole from outside

K1I.name_eng: Tree to descend from a rock
K1I.definition_eng: A tree or vine quickly grows up near the rock or in the bottom of a pit where the hero was marooned. He gets to the ground climbing down (or up) this tree (vine)

K1J.name_eng: A marooned man returns home before his adversary
K1J.definition_eng: A man marooned on an islet or rock in the sea turns into a bird and flies home. When the man who marooned him comes home, the hero is already there

K2.definition_eng: Hero climbs up (e.g. to a tree) or down (e.g. into a deep cave) by ladder, rope, from branch to branch, etc. The rope etc. breaks or is intentionally destroyed and the hero cannot return to the ground. (All cases of motif K2A, besides the Koreans, also contain motif K2)

K20.name_eng: Wish for star-husband or wife realized
K20.definition_eng: A human person admires a star or (rare) the Moon in the sky, expresses desire to marry it or (rare) to get a star-object. Star descends to him or to her or takes him or her to the sky

K21.name_eng: Woman gets to the sky and marries a sky-dweller
K21.definition_eng: Woman gets to the sky and marries a sky-dweller

K21A.definition_eng: A sky-dweller marries a woman. Being eager to return home, she secretly descends to the earth

K22.definition_eng: Different from (common) people inhabitants of a distant land fight from time to time with non-human enemies who periodically attack them

K22A.definition_eng: Birds or other creatures which not dangerous for common people attack dwarfs who live in another world

K22AA.name_eng: Humans in the south, birds in the north
K22AA.definition_eng: Inhabitants of the far away country are those migratory birds who live with us in summer but turn into humans after returning to their land

K22B.name_eng: Man helps inhabitants of other world
K22B.definition_eng: Inhabitants of a distant land who have different nature than (normal) human beings struggle from time to time with some non-human enemies. Man helps local dwellers because their enemies are not dangerous for the human beings

K22C.definition_eng: Inhabitants of a distant land who are birds (the bird-people) are afraid of birds or animals, which are not dangerous for humans and which usually attack them regularly

K23.definition_eng: Birds attack the inhabitants of a distant land or a man who had got to this land

K23A.definition_eng: Birds use their feathers as arrows or their arrows and down stick mouth openings of them enemies

K24.definition_eng: Women (rare: men) who possess supernatural power and usually come from a non-human world (from sky, from under the water, they are winged beings, bird- or animal-persons; rare: a girl of higher social status than the hero) take off their clothes (feather skins and the like) or part of it. Because a person hides the clothes (of one of them), their owner(s) have (has) to marry him or help him (rare: her)

K24A.name_eng: Supernatural male hides clothes of human girl
K24A.definition_eng: Supernatural male person (often a snake, a dragon) hides clothes of a human girl or sits on it. To return her clothes she had to become his wife

K24B.name_eng: To dance in her magic clothes
K24B.definition_eng: Magic wife tricks her naive mother-in-law to give her back her supernatural clothes or other object thanks to which she is able to escape from the human world

K24C.name_eng: An old man helps to obtain the bird-wife
K24C.definition_eng: A youth comes to an old man (rare: old woman) who instructs him how to obtain magic wife hiding her feather-clothing. For the first time, the youth usually gives her her clothes back, the girl disappears and he lives with the old man till the next opportunity

K25.definition_eng: A man consciously marries a woman related to the non-human world

K25A1.definition_eng: Magic wife abandons her mortal husband when she finds her clothes (often, her feathers if she is a bird-woman), makes herself the new clothes, receives them from her kin or her husband gives her her clothing believing that she will not abandon him. (Versions with magic wife abandoning her husband because she feels herself offended is not alternative to the “found clothes but in most of the texts these motifs are not combined)

K25A2.definition_eng: Person flies (makes attempt to fly) away after sticking feathers to his or her body dropped by migratory birds that fly above in the sky

K25A3.definition_eng: Magic bird-wife flies away after she had picked up many feathers and made of them her new bird-clothes

K25A4.definition_eng: A man (rare: woman) gets into power of a demonic person related to the lower world (usually a siren, fish, sea monster, rarely wizard). The antagonists raises the prisoner above water (or earth) a restricted number of times (usually being provoked or bribed to do so) and thanks to this the prisoner escapes (usually flies away turning into the bird)

K25A4A.name_eng: Saved from the underwater imprisonment (the cut through chain)
K25A4A.definition_eng: Young woman finds herself in power of water dweller and if permitted to visit her home, a chain is tied to her leg. She can be released if the chain is cut through

K25A5.definition_eng: The elder brother is a hunter, the younger brother (rare: sister) stays at home. When the elder gets to know that the bird-maidens visit the younger, he instructs him what he should do to catch one of the girls. The elder brother marries her but she finds her feathered clothes and flies away (in many versions the younger brother is a simpleton and tells his sister-in-law where her clothes are hidden). The elder brother goes away in search of his lost wife

K25A6.name_eng: Magic wife does not forgive the unfaithfulness of the man
K25A6.definition_eng: A wife from the non-human world agrees to live with the mortal man but abandons him when he becomes unfaithful to her (when he visits his mortal wife)

K25A7.name_eng: Two brothers and the winged maiden
K25A7.definition_eng: The elder brother is a hunter, the younger one is a housekeeper. When the elder brother gets to catch the winged maiden, the younger foolishly gives her winged back and she flies away. The elder brother sets off to return his wife

K25B.name_eng: Woman pursues a porcupine and gets to the sky
K25B.definition_eng: Pursuing a porcupine, woman climbs a tree and gets to the upper world

K25C.definition_eng: Digging roots or gathering sea food on a beach, a woman finds baby-boy. Usually her mother warns her not to dig a certain bulb or not to do it in a certain way. Breaking taboo, the woman finds or conceives baby-boy

K25D.definition_eng: Person gets to the sky, makes hole through the firmament digging out a root. Usually woman's husband or his kinsmen warn her against digging out a special bulb or tuber; breaking taboo, she gets to see the earth, decides to descend

K25E.definition_eng: All humans, members of a particular ethnic or social group or a ruling dynasty are believed to descend from a mortal man and a woman of supernatural origin

K26.definition_eng: Finding a hole in the ground or making it, person gets to see below another world. Usually the earth is seen from the sky

K26A.name_eng: Sky opening covered with a stone
K26A.definition_eng: Opening in the firmament is covered with a flat stone. When person puts the stone aside, he or she gets to see the earth

K27 (MOTIF IS NOT IN THE CORRELATION TAB.definition_eng: Person is suggested to fulfill tasks that are mortally dangerous or cannot be fulfilled without supernatural helpers or capacities. The person fulfills the tasks and remains alive. A contest between persons has form of a competition or game in which the loser is deprived of his status or life

K27A.definition_eng: An ordeal: to survive cold (frosty night outdoors, chamber with ice, cold water and snow)

K27B.definition_eng: An ordeal: to smoke a huge or poisonous pipe or to remain alive in poisonous smoke

K27C.definition_eng: An ordeal: to remain alive after contact with sharp points or blades

K27D.definition_eng: An ordeal: to remain alive in a closed room full of beasts of prey, poisonous or other dangerous creatures

K27E.definition_eng: Person or animal must eat (drink) enormous quantity of food (beverage) or eat or drink poisonous beverage or food

K27F.name_eng: The task: to get a woman
K27F.definition_eng: A task-giver asks the hero to get for him a particular woman

K27F1.definition_eng: Person builds a bridge (usually of gold etc.) during a very short time

K27F2.definition_eng: A man should acquire a pair of shoes (or other objects) that would be identical to those in possession of a girl. These objects are either unique or it is not known how they look like. Making himself invisible, the man steels the objects (and the owner must acquire the new ones for herself) or becomes informed concerning their appearance

K27F3.definition_eng: Person must quickly get many feathers, enough to fill a feather-bed or a pillow

K27G.name_eng: Ordeal: to bathe in a boiling liquid
K27G.definition_eng: Person is ordered to bathe in a (boiling) milk or other hot liquid or to jump into fire. He remains unharmed but his adversary usually dies

K27G1.definition_eng: Person must quickly clean a stable or cattle-shed from dung accumulated there for a long time

K27G2.definition_eng: Person has to build a house of the birds’ feathers or to make roof of feathers

K27G3.name_eng: When one tree is felled, all the other fall after it
K27G3.definition_eng: When person fells a tree (slightly touching it with an axe), all trees of the forest fall after it

K27G4.name_eng: To plow, to sow and to reap in one day
K27G4.definition_eng: During impossibly short time person must to realize all works of agricultural cycle and to present food made of new crops

K27G5.definition_eng: Person tries or must try to cut or to dig with the wooden (plumb, felt) tool instead of the iron one

K27H.name_eng: To represent the head that is permanently concealed
K27H.definition_eng: The hero has to carve the representa-tion of the head of a person who never opens his face. Usually such a representation decorates the wooden bench

K27H1.definition_eng: A task-giver asks person to bring fruits of a tree that is difficult to be reached

K27HH.definition_eng: A task: to sort a large amount or small particles of different kind (usually seeds of different plants) mixed in container or to count such particles or to pick up the spilled grains

K27I.name_eng: Task: to dry a body of water
K27I.definition_eng: A task: to dry a body of water

K27K.definition_eng: A contest: to dive deep or for a long time

K27L.definition_eng: When hero dives, the antagonist covers the water surface with ice or net

K27L1.name_eng: To be frozen in the ice
K27L1.definition_eng: Person agrees to test his strength being frozen in the ice but fails to break it and to get free

K27M.name_eng: To get an animal of unusual color
K27M.definition_eng: The hero must kill and bring an animal of special (often unusual) color or form

K27N.definition_eng: A man must fulfill difficult tasks (to win competition) to receive the permission for a marriage. Or the tasks of father-in-law for his son-in-law are chosed with the obvious aim to kill the youth

K27N1.name_eng: Task-giver is a king or a chief
K27N1.definition_eng: Person who gives difficult tasks to the hero and/or person who demands the fulfillment of certain conditions from those who want to marry his daughter is a prominent figure in social hierarchy. He is a head of the socio-political unit of community or super-community level and is neither a member of the hero’s household nor a mythical being

K27N3A.name_eng: Task-giver is the Sun, Moon, Thunder, or Wind
K27N3A.definition_eng: Person who gives difficult tasks to the hero is associated with the Sun, Moon, Thunder, or Wind (Cloud, Rain)

K27N3A1.definition_eng: In course of his matchmaking, hero comes into conflict with persons (more than two) who embody the elements, celestial bodies and parts of the universe

K27N3B.name_eng: Task-giver lives in the sky but is not the Sun, Moon, Thunder or Wind
K27N3B.definition_eng: Person who gives difficult tasks or tests to the hero or heroine lives in the sky but is not associated with the Sun, Moon, Thunder or Wind

K27N3C.definition_eng: Person who gives difficult tasks to the hero is associated with an animal, a bird or a fish

K27N3C1.definition_eng: Inhabitants of the village of the polar bears who are relations of the hero’s wife give him difficult tasks and tests

K27N3C2.name_eng: The antagonist is father-in-law in guise of a bear
K27N3C2.definition_eng: The task-giver is the bear who is the hero’s father-in-law

K27NN.definition_eng: Not the powerful person himself but his official or adviser tries to get rid of the hero and suggests that the person should give the hero difficult tasks

K27O1.definition_eng: Severed human heads are compared with balls or used as balls

K27O2.name_eng: To play with a dangerous ball
K27O2.definition_eng: To kill the hero, his enemies involve him into a game with a dangerous ball (or ice, stone, bone, iron, a walrus head, a biting skull, etc.)

K27O3.definition_eng: Two groups of participants compete in fulfilling difficult tasks or are engaged into the game in which one team plays against another (at least two episodes with different participants from both sides). The participants are either anthropomorphic who possess different extraordinary qualities or they are different animals (natural phenomena, elements, etc.). {Texts in which the main participants are anthropomorphic and competitions are win by animals who accompany the hero are not included}

K27P.name_eng: Antagonist mourns loss of his helpers
K27P.definition_eng: The antagonist sends the hero to the place where he is attacked by dangerous creatures. The hero kills them and brings to the antagonist. The creatures are the antagonist's relatives, pets, or helpers, therefore he or she mourns their death or revives them

K27P1.name_eng: Antagonistic father-in-law acquires guise of an animal
K27P1.definition_eng: When father-in-law (rare: mother-in-law) asks the hero to killl or to tame a dangerous animal or not to kill certain animal during a hunt, he (she) turns into this animal himself or transforms into it his daughter(s) or wife (husband)

K27P2.name_eng: Antagonistic father-in-law acquires guise of a bear
K27P2.definition_eng: When father-in-law (rare: mother-in-law) asks the hero to kill a bear, he (she) turns into the bear himsel or tranfforms into the bear his daughter or wife (husband)

K27Q.definition_eng: Hero is sent to bring milk of a wild animal or milk in possession of a dangerous creature or person

K27Q1.name_eng: Lion’s milk in the lion’s skin
K27Q1.definition_eng: Hero is sent to bring milk of a lioness in a skin of another lion, usually the lioness’ cub

K27Q2.definition_eng: Hero is sent to get musical instrument, usually a (self-playing) psaltery

K27R.name_eng: To visit the world of the dead
K27R.definition_eng: A task: to bring object or news from the land of the dead

K27R1.name_eng: The burnt person proves to be unharmed
K27R1.definition_eng: The antagonist believes that the hero was burned but returned from the other world alive and prosperous therefore he asks burn him (her) or his representatives

K27R2.definition_eng: A task: to bring objects (usually fruits) that act like people, i.e. dance, sing and the like

K27SS.name_eng: To win a race with an (old) woman
K27SS.definition_eng: A strong man has to race with a woman (often with an old woman). He cannot surpass her or does it with much difficulty

K27T.definition_eng: A contest: to climb a pole or tree

K27U.definition_eng: Hero and his adversary play hide-and-seek. The hero finds his adversary but the adversary cannot find him

K27U1.name_eng: One day from conception to birth
K27U1.definition_eng: A demand is brought up that a baby would be born the next day after conception or would talk immediately after the birth

K27U2.definition_eng: Powerful person asks the hero to get know where the tumbleweed goes or what are its news

K27V.name_eng: To hit a bird with an arrow (stone)
K27V.definition_eng: Person must kill a bird with an arrow or a stone

K27V1.definition_eng: Person must hit a needle with an arrow (to shoot an arrow though the eye of a needle)

K27V2.name_eng: To hit an object of copper
K27V2.definition_eng: Person must hit the copper object or the creature whose body consists of copper

K27V3.name_eng: To shoot an arrow though the ring
K27V3.definition_eng: Person must shoot an arrow through a small ring or several rings

K27W.name_eng: Monster brought by the hero kills the task-giver
K27W.definition_eng: Task-giver asks to bring him dangerous being or object possessed by a moster or deity. Hero fulfills the task. The beast, monster, deity or the object itself kills the task-giver

K27X.definition_eng: A man marries a non-human woman. In her world, she has another husband or suitor. She returns to her world, human husband follows her. He stands tests and/or fights with local inhabitants, gets his wife back

K27X1.definition_eng: Hero receives a difficult task (usually to bring an object or creature that have no particular indications and properties) and comes across an invisible person who is a powerful and well-disposed servant to anybody who becomes his master. The hero is kind with him and the person helps him

K27X2.name_eng: To steal an egg from under the bird
K27X2.definition_eng: Person is able to steal an egg (a nestling, to put it back) from under the bird (to change the bird’s feather; to steal an embryo from animal’s womb, etc.)

K27X3.name_eng: The man persecuted because of his beautiful bride
K27X3.definition_eng: A powerful person coverts a beautiful bride or wife of a man and gives him impossible tasks to get rid of him

K27X3A.definition_eng: When the hero goes to fulfill a difficult task, his magic wife gives him her towel or handkerchief and orders to use only them (usually her relatives recognize him as their son-in-law when they see the object in question)

K27X4.name_eng: Climb a tree with a full glass in hand
K27X4.definition_eng: Person must climb a tree (pole, rock) with a full open vessel in hand and not a drop should be spilled

K27X5.definition_eng: Setting off for a search of a woman or magic objects, a man comes across several (usually three) supernatural (often demonic) persons who help him. All the persons are similar but usually every next one is older (younger) than another

K27X6.name_eng: The Sun, the Moon and the Wind direct the hero
K27X6.definition_eng: Travelling in search of the marriage partner, the hero (heroine) comes in succession to several supernatural persons related to luminaries and atmospheric phenomena (the Sun, the Moon, Stars, Wind). The last of them gives him or her necessary information

K27X6A.name_eng: Person gets to the mother of the Sun
K27X6A.definition_eng: Travelling person gets to the house of the Sun where he or she meets his mother

K27X6B.definition_eng: When the man happens to meet the Sun, the Moon (Frost) and the Wind he greets only the latter of them

K27X7.name_eng: Master of animals calls them together to question them
K27X7.definition_eng: Person in search of the remote and inaccessible place comes to the master (mistress) of animals (birds, fish) or demons who summon all of them and asks about the way to this place. Only (the last) one knows the way

K27X8.name_eng: The frog directs to the aim
K27X8.definition_eng: The hero (heroine) is in search of the place that is not achievable for common people. Only the frog (toad) knows the way (and helps to achieve destination)

K27X9.name_eng: To bring an object from the sea bottom
K27X9.definition_eng: The hero must bring a small object (often a finger ring) from the bottom of a deep waterbody (often the sea)
