K27XY.name_eng: (Animal-)persons with different qualities in the camp of their adversaries
K27XY.definition_eng: Each of several men (male animals of different species) surpasses all others in some kind of activity. They get to the place of their adversaries and thanks to their special qualities win different competitions and survive in dangerous situations. The tale is not related to the quest of a marriage partner

K27Y.name_eng: To get material for making bow and arrows
K27Y.definition_eng: Hero is sent or sets off by his own will to get two or more different materials needed for making bow and arrows (wood or reed for shafts, feathers, tendons for string, flint for points, paint to paint the shafts, gum to stick points to the shafts)

K27Y1.definition_eng: Person believes or pretends that the arrow points should be of coal, bark, grass and the like.

K27YY.name_eng: To come near a dangerous tree
K27YY.definition_eng: Hero is sent to a tree which must fall on him

K27YY1.name_eng: To get feathers of a dangerous bird
K27YY1.definition_eng: Hero brings a feather (feathers) of a dangerous bird

K27YY2.name_eng: To get a nestling of a dangerous birds
K27YY2.definition_eng: Hero is sent to bring a nestling of a dangerous bird

K27YY3.name_eng: To get fruits of a dangerous tree
K27YY3.definition_eng: Hero is sent to bring fruits which grow on a tree that is dangerous to those who come near it

K27YY4.name_eng: To get bark of particular tree
K27YY4.definition_eng: Hero is sent to get bark of a tree that is dangerous to those who come near it

K27Z.name_eng: Game of chance for life and death
K27Z.definition_eng: Person becomes a master of another after winning a game (game of chance or Intellectual game but not a sport tournament)

K27Z1.definition_eng: Helpful animal instructs the hero how to steal an object he needs to get but not to take anything else (bird, but not cage, horse but not bridle, etc.) The hero breaks prohibition, is caught but released on condition that he brings another wonderful object. Situation is repeated and the last task is to bring a girl. Ultimately the hero gets both the girl and all the objects

K27Z2.name_eng: Princess separated from her son averted incest with him
K27Z2.definition_eng: A noble young woman or girl who had to abandon her home gives birth to a son and is separated from him. The youth becomes adult and is going to marry a woman. At the last moment he understands that she is his mother. The woman gets back her high social position

K27Z2A.name_eng: A man and a girl who spent one night together
K27Z2A.definition_eng: A young man and a girl live far away from each other. Supernatural beings transfer the man to the girl or vice versa and carry him or her back before morning. They do not understand what happened with them and are eager to be together again

K27Z2A1.name_eng: Innocent woman is believed to be wanton
K27Z2A1.definition_eng: When a young woman becomes pregnant, her own kin or relations of her husband blame her for her improper behavior because they are sure that she had no opportunity to be impregnated by her husband or fiancé. After a lot of suffering the woman is united with the man who is her son’s father

K27Z2A2.definition_eng: A man marries a woman but abandons her without consummating his marriage. She visits him in disguise and ultimately he gets to know who was his beautiful companion. Usually the wife gives birth to his son (three sons) and upon seeing the boy, the man realizes that it is his own child

K27Z2B.definition_eng: Complicated relations between a poor girl and a prince lead to his attempt to kill his bride in the nuptial night. The girl puts a doll in her bed, the prince pierces it with a sword and takes the sweet juice (honey, sugar) with which the doll was filled for the blood. He repents his deed but the real girl appears and the couple is happy

K27Z2C.name_eng: Prince marries a girl to lock her up
K27Z2C.definition_eng: A prince marries a poor girl only to lock her up in her room. She outwits him

K27Z2D.name_eng: An argument between female sparrow and her husband
K27Z2D.definition_eng: A conflict breaks out among a pair of birds (sparrows, doves, etc.) in which the male bird is (to some extent) guilty. This episode forms the outset of a story in which noble persons participate

K27Z2E.name_eng: The stolen jewelry and the final uniting
K27Z2E.definition_eng: During the first meeting(s) between the prince and the princess one of them (sometimes adopting an unusual guise) takes objects (decorations) in possession of another. Either the girl of the boy falls ill. Thanks to the new meeting the sick ones become healthy again, the disappeared objects are recognized and the couple married

K27Z2F.definition_eng: A poor girl receives a doll (goose) that defecates money. An envious neighbor steals or borrows the doll but it soils her house and the doll is thrown out. The king (prince) uses the doll (goose) to wipe himself and it sticks to his backside (or bites him when he passes by). He announces that anyone who can release him will get a reward. Only the girl is able to do it and he marries her

K27Z2G.definition_eng: There are several sisters. A youth easily acquires favours of elder ones but the youngest mocks him and plants him babies born from him by the elder ones

K27Z3.definition_eng: A man trains a cat (monkey, dog) to hold lighted candle (lamp) on its head or to extinguish the light by a signal. When a mouse (a rat) runs through the room, the cat drops the candle (forgets about the lamp) and chases the mouse

K27Z4.name_eng: The trained animal of the gambler
K27Z4.definition_eng: Person always wins a game thanks to a cat (or a mouse) who carries the lamp (or puts the light out in a certain moment). The hero releases a mouse (or correspondingly a cat), the cat runs after it and the person loses the game

K27Z4A.name_eng: A cripple claims his leg back
K27Z4A.definition_eng: A cripple tells that he lost his leg (eye) because of his visitor’s father. The visitor’s wife (or he himself after receiving a good advice) asks the cripple to give him another leg (eye) for comparison or brings him a leg of a dead person claiming money for it

K27Z4B.name_eng: Wife disguised as a man saves her husband
K27Z4B.definition_eng: A man goes away, comes across a deceiver and loses freedom and property. His wife comes unrecognized in the man’s guise, punishes the deceiver and saves her husband

K27Z5.name_eng: An agreement to marry the would be born children
K27Z5.definition_eng: Two men agree to marry their future children if a girl and a boy will be born. The girl’s parents evade the given obligation. The boy grows up and finds his bride

K27Z6.definition_eng: Being a victim of the injustice and after much suffering, a young woman speaks with a certain inanimate objects (often it is “the stone of pity”) telling it her sad story or her husband does it. The woman is rescued and the justice reinstated

K27Z7.name_eng: To get know what is the rose of the heart
K27Z7.definition_eng: A person promises to fulfill somebody’s request if another gets to know why certain man or woman acts regularly in a strange way

K27Z7A.name_eng: One who gets to know an intimate secret should die
K27Z7A.definition_eng: Person is going to kill anyone who gets to know why he punished his former wife so brutally

K27Z8.definition_eng: The riddle refers to extraordinary or accidental events that happened to the person setting the riddle, and thus is unsolvable to outsiders

K27Z8A.name_eng: Young man suggests a riddle to the princess
K27Z8A.definition_eng: A young man suggests a riddle to the princess, the answer is known only to him. If the princess is unable to solve it, she must marry him

K27Z8B.name_eng: A woman suggests a riddle to her husband
K27Z8B.definition_eng: A woman suggests her husband a riddle, the answer being known only to her. If the husband is unable to solve the riddle, the wife gets a right to kill him

K27Z9.definition_eng: A (dried) fish (water-spirit, satyr, etc.) laughs, smiles or spits because a man disguised as a woman lives in the house

K27ZY.definition_eng: A youth (a girl) lives in the house of an ogress. To get rid of him (her) the ogress asks him (her) to bring some object from other ogres (often from her mother) who must kill him or her. The hero or heroine escapes and kills all the ogres

K27ZZ.name_eng: The witch and the blinded queens
K27ZZ.definition_eng: A man does not know that his (new) wife (rare: mother) is an ogress/witch/evil woman. Thanks to her intrigues (former) wives (wife) are blinded and/or confined in an underground hole. A son of one of them overcomes the ogress and returns sight to his mother and aunts

K27ZZ1.name_eng: Only the youngest queen's child survives
K27ZZ1.definition_eng: Several imprisoned (driven out) co-wives give birth but only the son of the youngest woman survives. The boy saves the women

K27ZZ2.name_eng: All queens are blind, one is half-blind
K27ZZ2.definition_eng: Several young women who are co-wives or sisters loose both eyes but the youngest only one eye

K27ZZ3.definition_eng: Father or step-mother (who is usually a demon in human guise) pushes several girls (a girl and her maids) into a hole (confines them in a hole). The heroin gets to climb out and she overcomes her antagonists

K27ZZ4.name_eng: The wife who should not be beaten
K27ZZ4.definition_eng: A prince (merchant’s son) beats his wife each day (says he will marry only a woman who will submit to a beating each day). When he is married his wife saves him demonstrating her superiority

K28.name_eng: Father or uncle is rival and enemy
K28.definition_eng: Maternal uncle or father (or grandfather if he replaces father who is not mentioned) of the young man is his rival or enemy and tries to kill him

K29A.definition_eng: Hero demonstrates his supernatural abilities remaining alive in a burning hot chamber, stove, bonfire, among burning vegetation

K29B.definition_eng: Hero is asked to climb into a hole or pit. When he does it, they fill it with soil or throw down a post, a stone, etc. The hero demonstrates his magic capacities coming back uninjured

K29C.name_eng: Brings tree that was fallen on him
K29C.definition_eng: To kill a strong man, others fell a tree and hope that the man will be crashed when it falls on him, or they tie him to a tree. The man remains unharmed and brings the tree home

K29D.definition_eng: When water in a spring is replaced with alcohol, honey, etc. or bottles of alcohol seem to be left without supervison, a creature of person becomes drunk and is caught

K2A.definition_eng: Hero is sent to the lower world though a well, precipice, etc. After he obtains valuables (young women), his envious companions cut the rope to get rid of him but he succeeds in returning back

K2A1.name_eng: Simple man gets to see how the princess has been abducted
K2A1.definition_eng: A simple man becomes a chance witness of the abduction of the princess by the demonic being or finds an evidence of the abduction. The girl’s father sends him to bring her back

K2A2.name_eng: The abducted princess drops her shoe
K2A2.definition_eng: A monster carries a princess away. A youth gets to see it and picks up a shoe dropped by her. Or he shoots and finds her lock of hair. The youth sets out in search of the princess, descends underground and saves her

K2A3.definition_eng: To maroon hero on a mountain, his companions destroy the rope or chain by which he climbed there or which he let down from there

K2B.definition_eng: The pastimes or only names of the hero’s companions are unusual and different but their specific qualities that they must possess considering their names are irrelevant for the plot. Cf. motif K66, “Extraordinary companions”

K3.definition_eng: Hero climbs up a tree or rock to get eggs, nestlings, fruits, honey, etc. Another person makes the tree (rock) grow higher or thicker and the hero is unable to descend back

K30.definition_eng: Flying person or creature abducts a woman but is ultimately killed or the woman escapes from him

K30A.definition_eng: Wife of a chief abandons him with vultures (usually by her own will being untrue to her husband). The chief (Witoto: her own brother) brings her back

K30B.name_eng: Abducted as soon as she went to the courtyard
K30B.definition_eng: A girl or a woman is prohibited to go outdoors and is abducted by the flying creature as soon as she does it

K31.definition_eng: Person makes a sea mammal or fish of wood, it carries another person or persons into the open sea or kills him or them

K32.definition_eng: An ugly, old, lazy, etc. woman or (in Chaco) a male trickster comes to man under disguise of his wife or bride who is driven out, confined to the underworld, killed, etc.

K32A.name_eng: Travelling man leaves his wife or daughter for a short time
K32A.definition_eng: A man travels with his wife or daughter. Another woman or a demonic person replaces her when the man goes away for a short time or (rare) falls asleep

K32B.definition_eng: Mother-in-law of a man takes the appearance of her daughter to replace her

K32B1.definition_eng: Mother-in-law of a man takes the appearance of her daughter to replace her

K32C.definition_eng: When the imposter takes place of the real wife, the latter turns into owl

K32D.name_eng: Sister sent to feed geese, servant taken for the sister
K32D.definition_eng: A girl (rare: boy) is walking to her or his relations or to her bridegroom. On the way the imposter lures her (him) to exchange clothes and takes her (his) place while the real girl (boy) is sent to look after crops or fee domestic fowl or animals. People hear her (his) song in which all the story is told. The deception is disclosed, the imposter killed

K32E.name_eng: The gold, the silver, the wood
K32E.definition_eng: Negative person, object or place is contrasted with one or two positive ones as wood with silver and gold

K32F.definition_eng: An evil spirit abandons a girl or a young woman in a tree or islet. She takes care for a nestling of bird of prey, he grows big, rescues her

K32G.definition_eng: To punish an antagonist, he or she is tied to a horse (camel, bull) and dragged or he or she is torn apart (usually by horses)

K32G1.definition_eng: Person is asked to choose between objects that have utilitarian value, often forty (seven, etc.) horses or forty knives. Usually the person does not understand that the question is about different kinds of execution

K32G2.name_eng: The executed dauther’s meat is sent to her mother
K32G2.definition_eng: When powerful person marries a girl, an evil woman replaces her with her own daughter. The false wife is exposed and executed, and her cooked meat is sent to her mother as a special gift

K32G3.name_eng: What punishment deserves one who did it?
K32G3.definition_eng: The evel doer is asked what punishment should be allotted for the corresponding crime? He (she) does not understand that they speak about him (her) and determines the way of his (her) execution

K32H.definition_eng: To punish an antagonist, he or she is buried alive

K32H1.name_eng: Punishment: rolled down a hill in a barrel
K32H1.definition_eng: To kill a person, he/she is put in a (nailed) barrel which is rolled down a slope or is tied to the tail of a horse

K32H2.definition_eng: To tortures his wife to death, a man ties her up at an anthill

K32H3.definition_eng: To punish an antagonist, he or she is burned alive. (Episodes in which the burning of the dangerous being is not a punishment but an effective way to get rid of him or her are not considered)

K32I.name_eng: Two sitters at the bed of a sleeping prince
K32I.definition_eng: A girl finds a body of a sleeping youth who will wake up at a certain time and marry the girl who would sit nearby. Usually at the last moment the girl goes away for a time and the impostor takes her place.

K32J.name_eng: Sister replaced by an ugly girl, brother accused of deception
K32J.definition_eng: A ruler gets to know from a young man that this man’s sister is extraordinary beautiful. On the way to the ruler beautiful girl is replaced by the ugly one. Usually the ruler thinks that the young man is a deceiver and throws him in prison

K32K.name_eng: The false wife is a bug or a grub
K32K.definition_eng: The false wife who acquired guise and place of the real one is a smelling bug or a grub

K32L.name_eng: Horses handed out among people to feed them
K32L.definition_eng: The king hands his horses (cows) among people to feed them. Only the heroine returns her horse well fed

K32M.name_eng: The heroine is transformed into animal (not drownd)
K32M.definition_eng: The heropine’s rival transforms her into an animal or bird and not pushes her into the water. Cf. motif k33

K33.definition_eng: When a young woman is pushed into the water by her rival, she drowns or loses her human guise but ultimately is returned to the people, Cf. motif k32n

K33A.definition_eng: Siblings (most often younger brother and elder sister) leave their home. One of them (most often the brother, most rare several brothers) turn into animal (usually an ungulate) or (rare) a bird but (in the most cases) ultimately acquires his or her human form again

K33A1.definition_eng: A woman is thrown into a well (pond, hole, etc.) or transformed into a water bird. Being in water, she gives birth to a son (children) or she had been thrown together with her baby. Ultimately she and her children are saved

K33A1A.name_eng: The heroine in the belly of a whale
K33A1A.definition_eng: A woman who was thrown into the water is swallowed by a fish (whale, crocodile) but ultimately saved

K33A2.name_eng: A witch distorts what was told
K33A2.definition_eng: Young man carries his sister to her fiancé. The girl does not hear well what her brother tells her. The witch distorts his saying (she must jump into the water; must be blinded, etc.). After getting rid of the heroine, the witch replaces her with her own daughter

K33A3.name_eng: Heroine's mother is transformed into a turtle
K33A3.definition_eng: Because of a conflict with her rival or with her husband the heroine’s mother or the heroine herself turns into a turtle

K33A4.name_eng: The heroine is transformed into a forest animal
K33A4.definition_eng: After the heroine’s rival transforms her into a forest animal of medium size (lynx, wolf, deer), she makes attempts to contact her children or husband

K33A5.name_eng: The heroine is transformed into duck
K33A5.definition_eng: The heroine’s rival transforms her into a duck (goose). The duck makes attempts to contact her children or husband

K33A6.name_eng: They sharpen knives and boil water already
K33A6.definition_eng: A kid (lamb, gazelle, etc.) comes to a well (see, etc.) where his mistress was pushed down and says that they sharpen knives and boil water to kill and cook him

K33A7.name_eng: The widower, his daughter or son and their teacher
K33A7.definition_eng: After the death of her or his mother, a girl or a boy suggests her or his father to marry another woman who is her or his teacher, neighbor etc. and who usually persuaded the girl (boy) to give such an advice. As soon as she is married, the step-mother becomes to persecute her step-daughter (stem-son)

K33A8.name_eng: The heroine is transformed into a dove
K33A8.definition_eng: The heroine’s rival transforms her into a dove. The dove makes attempts to contact her children or husband

K33B.definition_eng: A girl goes with her friends to a river, into a forest, etc. Other girls return home but the heroine has to remain or to go back to the forest, etc. She has a narrow escape from a dangerous creature. marries a supernatural being or a chief, or dies but is avenged

K33C.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who, before he met her, was (permanently or periodically) inside of a fruit or (rare) a flower, a stem or an egg

K33C1.definition_eng: Person is thrown into the water and becomes a flower (usually lotus)

K33C2.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside a fruit of the pomegranate

K33C2A.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside of the coconut

K33C3.name_eng: Girl from citrus or bel (Aegle marmelos)
K33C3.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside citrus fruit (orange, lemon, bergamot etc.) or in bel (Aegle marmelos, related to citrus family)

K33C4.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside of the pumpkin, eggplant or cucumber

K33C5.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside the egg

K33C6.definition_eng: Young man obtains several (usually three) fruits (eggs, pieces of reed). When he opens the first one, a girl who comes out from it immediately disappears because something was wrong (usually the drinking water for her is not available). Only the girl who has come out of the last fruit remains with the man. Cf. motif k33c7

K33C7.name_eng: One fruit with a girl inside
K33C7.definition_eng: Young man obtains a fruit from which a girl comes out (rare: two girls from two fruits, both remain with the man). The episode of the loss of girls who were inside other fruits is absent, Cf. motif k33c6

K33C8.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside of the nut (walnut or hazelnut but not the cocos)

K33C9.definition_eng: Young man gets a girl who is inside of the apple

K33D.definition_eng: A man discovers that a beautiful girl hides herself under a guise of an ugly and dirty servant, under a skin of an animal or in an object that is brought into his house

K33D1.definition_eng: The youth does not know that a beautiful girl hides inside an object that is brought to him

K33E.definition_eng: Babies disappear but are ultimately returned to their mother or father grown up and in good health

K33F.name_eng: Basin of honey and basin of oil
K33F.definition_eng: Two or more different kinds of valuable edible liquids like oil, honey, milk, etc. are available or imaginable. Cf. motif n34

K33F1.name_eng: Fountain of oil is promised to be created
K33F1.definition_eng: Person promises to create a fountain from which a valuable product (usually oil) is flowing and really creates it (rare: promises to share a large amount of such a product)

K33G.definition_eng: One who eats certain fruit (leave, etc.) gets horns (long nose, etc.) or turns into an animal. After eating another fruit (leave) person recovers his or her normal body

K33H.name_eng: The cat, the dog and the magic object
K33H.definition_eng: A man obtains an object that fulfills his wishes. The object is stolen but brought back by the animals (which had been saved by the man before)

K33H1.name_eng: To exchange the old ring for the new one
K33H1.definition_eng: The hero’s wife (mother, servant) does not know about the magic qualities of an object in their house and exchanges it for something that looks likes more expensive but actually has low value

K34.definition_eng: Person kills others inviting them to sit on a swing and launching them into water, on rocks, etc.

K34A.name_eng: Rival woman lures the heroine to the swing
K34A.definition_eng: A rival woman lures the heroine to a swing to throw her into the water and get rid of her. The heroine (almost) drowns or temporarly loses her human guise but ultimately gets to return to the human world

K35.definition_eng: An imposter pretends to be the hero to take his position and/or to marry or to violate his woman

K35A.definition_eng: In exchange for temporal advantages, person agrees to be maimed or branded

K35A1.name_eng: The pick up a feather of fire-bird
K35A1.definition_eng: On his way a man picks up a precious feather (often despite the warning of his magic horse). When a powerful person gets to know about the feather he tells the man to fulfill difficult tasks

K35A2.name_eng: An animal with the shining hide
K35A2.definition_eng: A man kills an animal with the shining hide. When a powerful person gets to know about the hide he tells the man to fulfill difficult tasks

K35A3.definition_eng: To obtain privileges of his master, his servant creates situation that results in exchange of their social positions

K35A4.definition_eng: To get rid of the hero and to get his social and family position, the imposter pushes him into the sea or maroons him on a faraway island. The hero survives and comes back {The circum-Pacific versions which are geographically remote from the Western European ones are excluded. See motif K1E}

K35A5.name_eng: Token to be shown to the protector
K35A5.definition_eng: Powerful person leaves a token (letter) for a small boy to demonstrate it when he becomes adult and comes to him

K35A6.definition_eng: Person finds an objects (usually a feather) with which he illuminates his room

K35A7.definition_eng: Person finds a feather that has a quality to make alive beings healthy and handsome

K35B.definition_eng: Hero gives his rivals the food provided by him by order of the king but the king finds this food poisonous, useless or tasteless while the food presented by the hero is excellent even if it looks not so good

K35C.definition_eng: An ogre (a dragon, king of the sea) has not killed a man who descended to him as other people had thought but rewarded because the greeted him and/or gave a correct answer to his question

K35C1.name_eng: The best is one whom you love
K35C1.definition_eng: A mighty person asks a man which of two women is prettier, what is the most beautiful thing, and the like. Giving a correct answer, the man is not killed like those who were before him but receives a reward

K35C2.name_eng: Man descends to the sea bottom
K35C2.definition_eng: A man rides a ship that stops suddenly and does not move for a long time. The man agrees to descend to the bottom, behaves himself in a proper way with the sea dwellers and returns to the ship

K35C3.definition_eng: Because of the reason that for some time remains unclear a ship stops in the middle of the sea (rare: a horse stops on the road)

K36.definition_eng: Person is temporary transformed into animal (usually into a dog or coyote or into donkey, ox, etc.). When he acquires his human guise again, the antagonist suffers similar transformation. In some texts only the hero or only the antagonist is transformed

K37.definition_eng: To return or to get his or her son, wife, husband, domestic animal or (rare) object, person must recognize her, him or it among several identical persons, animals or objects

K37A.definition_eng: Person must recognize her (or his) son or husband among several identical persons or animals

K37B.name_eng: To recognize a woman by her missing finger
K37B.definition_eng: A man must recognize blindly the woman that he is eager to marry. He does it knowing that one of her fingers is absent or injured

K37C.name_eng: To recognize an object or an animal
K37C.definition_eng: Person must recognize a particular object or animal among several similar objects or animals

K37D.definition_eng: One person gets to know about the presence of another seeing traces of his teeth or nails on a fruit or leaf

K37E.name_eng: The iron bird with three legs
K37E.definition_eng: The clairevoyant is unable to pinpoint a person who betrayed a secret because doing this, the latter is covered with objects which normally are never found together

K38.definition_eng: For helping its children, their powerful mother or father who is a giant bird or (rare) other flying being helps the hero

K38A.definition_eng: Getting to the underworld, hero should take a white ram (horse) which would carry him back to earth. By chance, he takes the black one which carries him even deeper to the lower level of the underworld. Or the hero grabs not the right but the left horn of the animal and because of this gets to the wrong place

K38B.name_eng: The nestlings and the aggressive snake
K38B.definition_eng: A serpent or water monster regularly devours or injures children of a bird or other flying creature (almost always nestlings of giant bird). The hero kills the serpent (monster)

K38B1.name_eng: Bird steals colts, hero kills the serpent
K38B1.definition_eng: Every time when a horse gives birth to wonderful colts, they are stolen by a giant bird. A hero goes to get the colts and kills a serpent that regularly devours nestlings of the giant bird

K38B2.name_eng: Birds carries hero to its place, hero kills the monster
K38B2.definition_eng: Somebody (almost always a giant bird) carries/brings a man to its place where he kills a monster who regularly devoured his children (usually the nestlings)

K38B3.definition_eng: Mighty bird or other flying creature helps a man because he took care of its youngs feeding them, warming, decorating, etc.

K38B3A.definition_eng: Mighty bird helps a man because he had given food to its nestlings

K38B3B.name_eng: Hero warms and covers the nestlings
K38B3B.definition_eng: Mighty bird (more rare other creature/mythological person) helps a man (rare: a woman) because he (she) warms/covers from bad weather its/hers nestlings (children)

K38B3C.name_eng: Hero protects sleeping ones from the sunshine
K38B3C.definition_eng: When a man gets to see creatures of beings sleeping under the hot sun, he coveres them with a cloth, leaves etc. The beings are grateful and make somethig good for the man

K38B4.name_eng: Serpent comes out of the water
K38B4.definition_eng: Powerful bird has its nest on the tree that stands in or nearby the body of water. The serpent (reptilian monster) comes out of it to devour the nestlings

K38C.name_eng: Bird brings the hero to his destination
K38C.definition_eng: After the hero helps a powerful bird (usually does good to her nestlings), the grateful bird brings him to the place where he is eager to get or tells to do it one of her nestlings. (It is not the vertical movement between layers of the world. According to the Sumerian variant, the bird endows the hero with capability to move with extraordinary speed and directs him to his destination)

K38D.definition_eng: A monster blocks sources of water (or sends floods) and usually gives some (promises not to send floods) in exchange for human victims or valuables. Hero kills the monster

K38D1.name_eng: A girl sacrificed to a dragon
K38D1.definition_eng: To appease a water monster (water spirits, gods) or to put an end to the drought or flood, a girl is sacrificed or descends into the water by her own will

K38E.name_eng: Of copper, of silver, of gold
K38E.definition_eng: Loci or objects of three (rare – four) different materials are mentioned in such a way that all of them have positive connotations though unequal value (copper, silver and gold; silver, gold and diamonds, etc.)

K38E1.definition_eng: Person travels across a forest with trees of two or more kinds of metal (copper, silver, etc.)

K38E2.definition_eng: Coming from the underworld to the earth, princess puts objects that she used (clothes, house, “kingdom”) into a small container (an egg, a ball, etc.) and brings them with her

K38E3.definition_eng: In a series of three (rare: four) loci or objects that have high but different value the highest value is related to the precious stone (usually a diamond; crystal, glass)

K38E4.name_eng: Palace of gold and silver bricks
K38E4.definition_eng: A palace (castle, crypt, church, bridge) made of gold and silver modules (usually bricks, more rare planks) is mentioned in narratives (in different context)

K38F.definition_eng: A reptile monster demands humans (usually virgins) as a sacrifice or abducts a girl or closes sources of water. Hero kills him. Monster’s victims do not play an active part in the plot

K38F1.definition_eng: Killing a monster or an animal, the hero cuts of and hides a piece of its body, usually a tongue. (In most of the cases, the imposter claims the deed to himself and when he cannot demonstrate the cut off piece, the hero unmasks him)

K38F2.name_eng: Stains of the dragon’s blood on the hero’s body
K38F2.definition_eng: Hero kills the dragon and saves the girl who had to be sacrificed. She smears the youth with the dragon’s blood. The imposter claims the deed to himself but is exposed when the hero demonstrates stains of the dragon’s blood on his body

K38F3.definition_eng: In order to kill a dragon, a hero digs a pit and hides in it. When the dragon crawls close to or over the pit, the hero deals the death blow with his sword

K38F4.definition_eng: From the mouth of a monstrous creature or person who is the enemy of the hero fire is coming out; its breath is fire

K38F5.definition_eng: From the mouth of a horse fire is coming ot the horse itself is of fire

K38F6.definition_eng: A creature that consists of fire is mentioned

K38F7.definition_eng: Person obtains some wild animals (of two or more different species) who serve him like dogs

K39.name_eng: Man feeds his own flesh to a creature who helps him
K39.definition_eng: Person has to feed powerful creature (usually a giant bird) giving it regularly pieces of meat. When meat supply is exhausted, he cuts off a piece of his own flesh

K4.definition_eng: Person climbs up a tree or rock or descends to a cave to get eggs or nestlings from the bird's nest. Another person remains on the ground. They get into conflict and/or the first person is unable to get back to the ground

K40.name_eng: One will be eaten today and another tomorrow
K40.definition_eng: Two (rare more) persons or creatures think that they are doomed but one whose death is slightly delayed is happy while one who will be killed earlier is in grief

K41.definition_eng: Thunder or giant bird fights against a reptile, big water animal or other big and strong creature who lives in water or under the earth

K42.definition_eng: Bird-woman is energetically searching a man whom she likes, takes him by force for her husband. Turning into a monster, she kills men but is ultimately destroyed

K43A.definition_eng: People abandon a boy, a girl, brother and sister, a group of children, or a young family without fire and food. A compassionate person conceals hot coals for the outlaws in the abandoned camp

K43B.definition_eng: People abandon a boy, a girl, brother and sister, a group of children, or a young family without fire and food. The outlaws demonstrate supernatural powers or protectors providing food and lodging. While the abandoned persons have plenty of food other people starve. A person (often a bird like crow, magpie, sea-gull, etc.) visits the abandoned ones and brings from them some food home. This way people get to know that the abandoned ones prosper

K43C.definition_eng: Abandoned children are tied to a tree. Helpful dog or other animal unfastens them

K44.definition_eng: A demonic or animal person steals a boy and pretends to be his real mother or father. The boy gets to know the truth, leaves the false parent

K44A.definition_eng: An amphibian (frog, toad, rare newt) steals or finds a boy, lies him that she is his real mother

K44B.name_eng: Returning after long absence, person throws food to his mother
K44B.definition_eng: Coming home after a long absence, the hero (rare: heroine) peeps into his house and sees his mother (his parents, her husband) who suffers hunger. He or she throws food inside, extinguishes the fire, pushes aside, etc. Usually those who are inside do not understand what is happening

K45.definition_eng: A man rides away from a woman or girl in a boat (on raft, sledge). When she tries to snatch a border of the boat (raft, sledge), he cuts her fingers off

K45A.definition_eng: A man rides away from a woman or girl in a boat (on raft). When she tries to snatch a border of the boat (raft), he cuts her fingers off. The fingers turn into water animals

K45B.definition_eng: A man and a woman of different generations (the father and the daughter, the son and the mother) get into conflict which results in the woman's transformation into the sea mammal. the sovereign of the sea mammals or into the frog (toad)

K46.name_eng: Woman throws herself into the ocean
K46.definition_eng: Giving way to a burst of horror or shame, woman or girl runs to the ocean, throws herself into the water or remains on the beach. Her husband or suitor pursues but cannot catch her

K47A.definition_eng: After having sexual contact with a dog, a woman gives birth to his children. The puppies turn into humans and usually become ancestors of particular groups of people

K47B.definition_eng: A girl marries a handsome man whom she had first seen in guise of a dog

K47C.definition_eng: A woman marries a dog, gives birth to the ancestors of present dogs who are people's helpers and friends

K47D.definition_eng: A girl marries a dog because only the dog fulfilled the condition of marriage put by the girl's father

K47E.name_eng: A girl and a dog on an island
K47E.definition_eng: A girl marries a dog or has relations with a dog. They are sent to the sea (down a river) in a boat (abandoned on an island). Or the girl which was sent to the sea and the dog meet on the island. A particular ethnic or social group descends from them

K48.definition_eng: An antagonist wants that a wonderful bird of the hero sing but it remains mute or cries differently. The bird begins to sing when the hero triumphs over his adversaries

K48A.definition_eng: Alive birds and beasts decorate hero's costume and headgear. Imposter steals hero's attire, takes his place but the birds and beasts are mute or cry differently

K49.name_eng: The dead mother visits her child
K49.definition_eng: A woman who is transformed into animal or driven out of the human world comes periodically to her child (usually to her baby to feed him)

K5.definition_eng: To lure the hero into a trap or to send him far away, the antagonist makes a bird or nestlings of excrements or guts

K50.definition_eng: A man disguised as a woman comes to his enemy and kills him at night (usually cuts off and carries away his head)

K51.definition_eng: A Man disappears or goes away for long time. His wife sets off, comes to a house where her husband lives now or first sends her son there. She gets to know that he has married another woman

K51A.name_eng: Woman pushes her rival into the boiling pot
K51A.definition_eng: A woman comes to her rival and kills her pushing her head into boiling liquid or pouring it into her ear

K51B.definition_eng: Bodies of the killed ones are put in such a position as if they are in a good mood (smile, laugh, dance)

K52.definition_eng: When a woman or a lad comes to the sea bank, she or he is carried away by sea predators (killer-whales, sharks, swordfish). Man descends to the bottom and rescues the woman or lad using his shaman's power

K52A.definition_eng: A man descends to the bottom of the sea to rescue his wife. He makes arrangements with a slave who pours water on fireplace producing steam. Hidden behind the steam, the man escapes with his wife

K52B.definition_eng: A man comes to the non-human beings to get a woman. He secures the help of a slave repairing his adze or axe

K52C.definition_eng: A shaman, wizard or other character with magical powers demonstrates his skill. The dwelling in which he and other people are situated begins to fill with water. It is sometimes said that this water is an illusion and that the people also see animals (waterfowl, fish or marine mammals) swimming around

K52C1.definition_eng: A shaman, wizard or other character with magical powers demonstrates his skill. The dwelling in which he and other people are situated begins to fill with water. It is sometimes said that this water is an illusion. One of the episodes: the character tells the people to take the waterfowl or fish that have appeared with the water or they start to catch them on their own initiative; when the water disappears, the people see that they hold in their hands not those animals, but their own penises or something else

K53.definition_eng: Person temporarily turns into bird or animal putting on corresponding skin or animal skins are amulets that become alive and help the person

K54.definition_eng: A man meets a dangerous giant (or serpent) who proves to be friendly to him. When another giant fights with the first one, the man helps his friend

K54A.definition_eng: A man and a friendly giant live together. The friendly giant fights with another one and asks the man for help. This help proves to be crucial because the man badly injures a foot of another giant

K55.definition_eng: A powerful supernatural wants to check if his guest made love with his wife or daughter. The person is impotent or (successfully pretends to be) chaste and is rewarded or at least gets no harm. Usually the same episodes repeats with another person who is dissolute or unable to control himself. This person is punished

K56.name_eng: The kind and the unkind girls
K56.definition_eng: One of (step)sisters, co-spouses or young female neighbors meets a being that is able to reward and to punish. She behaves herself properly and is rewarded. Another (other) girl comes to the same being but behaves in a wrong way and is punished (not rewarded).

K561.name_eng: The wise carving of the fowl
K561.definition_eng: A poor man brings his master a chicken (goose, etc.) as a present. The master asks him to divide the bird appropriately among the members of his household. The poor man does it considering the symbolic meaning of particular parts (gives the master the head, his daughters the wings, etc.) and receives rich compensation. A neighbor brings the master five chickens but is unable to divide them approppriately. The first man does it again.

K56A.name_eng: The unworthy girl fails, the worthy one succeeds
K56A.definition_eng: Two or three sisters are sent in succession to powerful person. The first or the first and the second sister behave in a wrong way, perish or do not succeed. The last one behaves correctly, gets a reward

K56A1.name_eng: Mother-in-law helps the girl to fulfill a task
K56A1.definition_eng: Coming to powerful man, a girl must make work that she is unable to do. His mother makes the work for her, and she marries the man

K56A2.name_eng: If asked to do in a bad way, do otherwise
K56A2.definition_eng: Person (usually a girl) gets to the powerful person (usually an old woman) who asks her to act in a strange and harsh way (to put room in disorder, to bring unclean water, and the like). The person does not according to order but in a rationale and polite way and is recompensed. Another person acts according to the direct sense of the words and is punished

K56A2A.name_eng: To wash herself in the red water
K56A2A.definition_eng: The girl becomes beautiful or ugly after washing herself in the water of particular color

K56A2B.definition_eng: Supernatural person asks a girl to bath (to feed) his or her children. These are lizards, bugs, or wild animals. The girl does it well and is rewarded

K56A3.name_eng: Not to fix laces on clothes and shoes
K56A3.definition_eng: Though laces on her clothes or shoes get loose, a girl on her way to the powerful persons or back should not tie them up

K56A4.definition_eng: When the kind girl returns home, a dog barks saying that everything is well with her and when the unkind girl returns (or her dead body is brought home), the dog barks that everything is bad

K56A4A.name_eng: The girl sends the demon to bring her new clothes
K56A4A.definition_eng: At night a girl remains alone in an isolated house (mill, bath-house, etc.). When a demon comes, she asks him to bring her ever new pieces of attire, jewelry, etc. till it dawns and the demon disappears

K56A4B.name_eng: Yarn is gone with a wind
K56A4B.definition_eng: A girl is told to clean (to spin) yarn (to weave, etc.). The yarn (spindle, a piece of fabric, etc.) is carried away by the wind. In search of it the girl comes to a person who makes her beautiful (gives precious gifts and the like)

K56A4C.name_eng: To wash something black making it white
K56A4C.definition_eng: Person must wash something black making it white or vice versa (yarn, clothes, board, etc.)

K56A4D.definition_eng: The stepmother sends her stepdaughter to the house in the forest and gives, instead of edible products, ash, sand and the like. When the stepdaughter becomes to use them, they turn into flours, cereals, etc.

K56A4E.definition_eng: After meeting the supernatural person, the good human person receives valuables but the bad one after coming back home is burned

K56A4F.definition_eng: The supernatural person does not like the behavior of the unkind girl and punishes her making her ugly (disfigured)

K56A4G.name_eng: The ugly girl: outgrowths on her face
K56A4G.definition_eng: After her visit to the supernatural person, ugly outgrowths appear on the face or head of the unkind girl (tail, horns, warts, etc.)

K56A5.name_eng: Old woman becomes a young beauty
K56A5.definition_eng: An old or ugly woman is transformed into a young beauty or becomes rich. Usually another old woman tries to imitate her but dies or suffers a reverse

K56A5A.definition_eng: Old or ugly woman wants to be flayed alive to become a beauty. Cf. motif H4

K56A5B.definition_eng: A person speaks friendly with embodiments of the weather peculiar for particular times of the year (praises the corresponding weather) and is rewarded. Another person scolds them and is punished

K56A5C.definition_eng: A person speaks friendly with embodiments of the weather peculiar for particular months and is rewarded. Another person scolds them and is punished

K56A5D.definition_eng: A person answers friendly to questions of the embodiment of the cold, praises him, is rewarded. Another person expresses his or her discontent and is punished

K56A6.definition_eng: On the way to the non-human world people or objects ask a child (a young girl) to taste certain food or to fulfill some work. The child (girl) does (rare: does not) what she was asked to do and thanks to this achieve his or her destination and safely returns

K56A7.definition_eng: In the winter time a girl (rare: a boy) is sent to bring something that is available only in summer. She brings it

K56A8.name_eng: An animal is taken for a bridegroom by mistake
K56A8.definition_eng: A girl marries an animal (brings it with her), it turns into a handsome man. Another girl tries to do the same but perishes or suffers a reverse

K56A8A.name_eng: Kind girl returns with a handsome man
K56A8A.definition_eng: A girl goes to the other world, acts correctly and brings back an animal or a box with a handsome man inside. Usually another girl acts wrongly and suffers a reverse

K56A8B.name_eng: Girl’s hand in the snake’s den
K56A8B.definition_eng: A kind girl who usually is a daughter of a bitch wants to suicide and puts her hand into the den of a poisonous snake. The snake does not bite her but gives her a valuable gift

K56A8C.name_eng: The youth married to a dog
K56A8C.definition_eng: A young man brings to his place an animal, it turns into a girl. Another man marries a dog (pig) but it is nothing but an animal

K56A9.definition_eng: Using a bell (drum, etc.) an animal (usually a mouse) produces sounds which the antagonist who is blind or is outdoors takes for the sounds produced by the hero (heroine). Thanks to this the hero escapes

K56AA.definition_eng: Two or three girls in succession become brides of the dog. The first one or two act in a wrong way, perish or do not succeed. The last one behaves correctly, gets a reward

K56AB.name_eng: Girl sheds her shirts, snake sheds his skins
K56AB.definition_eng: A girl marries monster and challenges him to shed (one of) his skin(s) every time she takes off (one of) her shirt(s). The girl remains alive and the monster turns into handsome man (usually because she has more shirts than he has skins)

K56AC.name_eng: A row of stones and a row of logs
K56AC.definition_eng: A girl gets to the house in the forest. The bear comes and tells her to prepare him a bed of stones and logs

K56B.name_eng: Two male persons: a successful one and a failure
K56B.definition_eng: First one, then another male person (humans or primeval ancestors) gets into a difficult situation or meets a powerful person or persons. The first one behaves adequately and is save (rewarded), the second one tries to imitate him but does it in a wrong way and gets into trouble

K56B1.name_eng: The old man with the live coals
K56B1.definition_eng: A poor man looks for a light for his fire. An old man gives him embers. When he takes them home, they turn to gold. An envious wealthy neighbor (brother) purposely extinguishes his fire and asks the old man to give him some coals. His homestead burns to ashes

K56B2.definition_eng: Supernatural creature (object) gives treasure to a modest man. The greedy one is eager to take more than he is allowed to take is caught and cannot release himself (for the long time). Usually the creature grasps his stretched out hand

K56B3.definition_eng: Intestine gases of a man become fragrant. His rival attempts to achieve the same effect but the result is the opposite

K56C.definition_eng: A man loses an axe. A spirit or a powerful official suggests him a golden axe but the man does not accept it. The spirit (official) gives him axes of gold and silver as a reward for his honesty. Usually another man intentionally loses his axe, claims the golden one but receives nothing

K56D.definition_eng: A man cures injured bird, it brings him a seed from which something valuable grows. Another man intentionally injures and then cures a bird, kit brings him a seed from which something harmful grows

K56D1.definition_eng: Man finds treasure in a pumpkin (water melon) that was (or which seeds were) presented to him

K56E.definition_eng: Two men have a similar defect (a hump, a lump). One spends a night in a place where spirits free him from his defect. Another comes to the same place but spirits double his defect giving him what they had taken off from the first man

K56E1.name_eng: Singers mention days of the week
K56E1.definition_eng: A man gets to see dwarfs (ghosts, witches) who dance and sing. They mention some days of the week in their song. The man joins the singing and mentions other days of the week which the dwarfs like. He receives a reward. (Usually another man tries to receive the same reward but mentions days of the week which the dwarfs do not like and is punished

K56F.definition_eng: A divides the chicken among the members of a household (and guests) considering the symbolic meaning of particular parts (gives the master the head, his daughters the wings, etc.).

K56F1.definition_eng: A poor man brings his master a chicken (goose, etc.) as a present. The master asks him to divide the bird appropriately among the members of his household. The poor man does it considering the symbolic meaning of particular parts (gives the master the head, his daughters the wings, etc.) and receives rich compensation. A neighbor brings the master five chickens but is unable to divide them appropriately. The first man does it again.

K56F2.name_eng: One woman, two men and five eggs
K56F2.definition_eng: To divide a certain (often five) number of eggs between people of different sex, a clever woman takes into consideration that every man has already two eggs

K57.definition_eng: A girl who conceals her beauty and/or is poor and oppressed by her stepmother puts on a splendid attire and comes incognito to a feast where a man of high status falls in love with her. He marries her after identifying her by an object given to her or lost by her or (rare) seeing how she changes her clothes

K57A.definition_eng: Noble youth falls in love with a beautiful girl but does not recognize her as a kitchen maid whom he gave a harsh treatment. When he asks the beauty where she is from, he does not understand her cryptic answers related to corresponding episodes. Or younger brother gives a cryptic answer when his elder brothers first beat him and then do not recognize in a guise of a handsome hero

K57B.name_eng: The girl’s shoe stuck to glue
K57B.definition_eng: To detain a beauty who runs away from the palace (church, etc.) the man who is in love with her smears the threshold (steps) with a glue (tar). The girl’s shoe remains stuck in it, all the girls are asked to put it on and it fits only to the heroine

K57C.definition_eng: Prince putы his ring on the beauty’s finger but does not know that she is the same girl who works in his kitchen. She plants the ring in a dish of food prepared for the prince and he recognizes it

K57D.definition_eng: Prince brings a shoe to marry a girl whose foot it fits. To meet such a standard, some girls cut off their toes or heel

K57E.name_eng: Young girl is provoked to kill her mother
K57E.definition_eng: Because of her simple-heartedness or by chance a young girl becomes a cause of her mother’s death

K58.definition_eng: Person builds a watercourse or digs a well as a condition of marriage. (Usually the woman breaks her promise to marry the winner and she or her bridegroom die)

K58A.definition_eng: Person makes water or fish available only if girl agrees to marry him and does not do it if the girl is unwilling

K59.definition_eng: One man puts another into a box, closes the lid (or ties him to a board, to canoe, etc.) and puts the box adrift. It floats to another land, man is released there, returns home, revenges on his enemy

K6.definition_eng: A vine grows from person's or animal's tears, mucus, urine, etc.

K60A.definition_eng: Person lets be firmly tied up when another one say that it's only a joke (e.g. a test to see can the first one break bonds)

K60B.definition_eng: Person is lured into a trap being invited to lie in a box or a hole to measure it. Being unable to liberate himself from the box etc., the person remains in power of his enemies

K60C.name_eng: Touchy with king, patient with stableman
K60C.definition_eng: King’s wife is extremely touchy and cannot suffer a slightest pain. She does not say a word, however, when her lover who is a servant or a demon is beating her

K61A.definition_eng: To get know the precise number of certain units, to select certain object among many others, to get know a name of particular person or a reason of particular phenomenon, person tries to surprise (or unintentionally surprises) the possessor of the knowledge who becomes to speak aloud and so provides the hero with necessary information

K61A1.definition_eng: Two men sleep (hide themselves) in one bag or lie with their soles touching each other. Dangerous creature or spirit takes them for an unknown monster

K61B.definition_eng: To get know names of strangers, person finds or creates situations when the strangers call each other by name

K61C.definition_eng: A demon agrees to help a person (usually to fulfill some difficult work that a girl must do herself) if a person tells him his name. At the last moment the person gets know the name by chance, the demon disappears and the person is rewarded

K61C1.definition_eng: Person will be ruined if he or she would not find an answer for a riddle of a demon. The answer is found accidentally when the person or somebody else hears how the demon talks by himself or with another demon. See motif C29

K61D.definition_eng: Young woman’s bridegroom or husband gets to believe that she is extraordinarily industrious. To conceal the deception, she herself or somebody else makes the man believe that because of hard work women become ugly or change into animals. The man prohibits his wife to work anymore

K61E.name_eng: Reward for making a supernatural laugh
K61E.definition_eng: When a powerful (supernatural) person gets to see a ridiculous situation, he or she laughs (and thus is cured from his disease). People involved into the situation are rewarded (saved from a danger)

K61F.definition_eng: Being afraid of her husband, a sterile woman pretends to give birth. In a due time the husband plans to marry his daughter or son. During the wedding ceremony a doll or an animal is in a sedan-chair but at the last moment a supernatural persons transforms it into a young woman or handsome youth

K62A.definition_eng: A mouse (rat, mole, etc.) and a small bird quarrel because they cannot divide supplies for the winter. (Usually this episode initiates the story about the war between animals and birds)

K62A1.name_eng: A man cures the wounded eagle
K62A1.definition_eng: A man saves (spares) a wounded bird. When the bird becomes strong again, it carries the man to a distant land (to the sky)

K63.definition_eng: A man gets to a country which inhabitants hunts of fish people whom they consider wild and equivalent to the real game or fish

K64.definition_eng: Person gets into dwelling of master of animals or monstrous shepherd. The host can kill him. The hero escapes sticking to hair of one of the animals who are going out

K64A.definition_eng: Person blinds sleeping ogre or ogress and escapes from him or her

K64B.definition_eng: Hero's adversary provokes him to touch an object that proves to be sticky. The hero sticks to it, sometimes has to cut off his finger

K64C.name_eng: The cyclopes is blinded by the smith
K64C.definition_eng: A man who gets to destroy the only (healthy) eye of the monstrous man or woman is a smith

K65.definition_eng: Being thrown out, put into certain places, born by primeval couple some beings turn into spirits of particular loci or into persons of particular ethnic groups

K65A.definition_eng: Being thrown down (usually from the sky), some beings get to different places and turn into spirits or animals with particular functions and names

K65B.definition_eng: Spirits or unpleasant animals (reptiles, worms, etc.) are (often: concealed from the eyes of God or deformed) children or miscarriages of the same human couple or the same primeval ancestor who produced first human beings

K65C.definition_eng: A woman conceals from God part of her children (rare: all of them) or part of domestic animals that are under her care. The concealed children become poor people or non-human beings and the concealed domestic animals become wild

K65C1.name_eng: Separating the rich from the poor
K65C1.definition_eng: A woman gives birth to many children but conceals part of them from God. The concealed children become ancestors of the people of the lower social status while those that had been shown to God become ancestors of the high status people

K65C2.name_eng: Man and tiger among several sons
K65C2.definition_eng: A woman or female animal gives birth to several sons, a man and a tiger among them

K65C3.name_eng: Eve is ashamed to have many children
K65C3.definition_eng: The woman (alone or with her husband) hides from the God part of her children because she is ashamed to have so many

K65D.name_eng: Wrong marriage ritual and the birth of spirits
K65D.definition_eng: The primeval couple is married. First wife has miscarriages or gives birth to spirits, worms or other unpleasant animals. Later, usually after the proper marriage ceremony is organized, she becomes to give birth to real human beings or gods

K65E.definition_eng: A woman is summoned to help supernatural beings as a midwife (to baptize a baby, to be a babysitter) and returns to the human world after rendering her assistance

K65E1.definition_eng: A woman is summoned to help supernatural being as a midwife (to baptize a baby). In the human world, this being has a form of a toad or frog

K65F.name_eng: With which eye do you see?
K65F.definition_eng: When person touches her or his eye with the magic substance, she or he sees supernatural beings unseen for the people. Usually the beings understand it and make this eye blind

K66.definition_eng: Several companions have extraordinary abilities (one who runs fast, one who eats great quantities, one who produces or can withstand severe frost, etc.); a hero comes across and takes for companions several men, each of them being involved into a special and unusual activity

K66A.definition_eng: The man who is able to build (to get) a ship which can fly (travel on land) marries the princess (inherits property)

K66B.name_eng: Hero presents the received princesses to his companions
K66B.definition_eng: Travelling from one place to another, hero lets his companions live there (usually presents to each one a princess that he received for his deeds) and continues his journey. When he gets into trouble, companions rescue him

K66C.definition_eng: The bear (lion) takes a woman for sexual partner or the she-bear takes a man. They have children who look like humans or bear cubs. More rare the woman gives birth to her son in the bear den because being abducted by the bear she was pregnant

K66D.definition_eng: The (adopted) human child of a bear has superhuman strength

K67.definition_eng: Two men spend a night in a forest, take their moccasins or clothes off usually to dry them near the fire. One plans to burn the moccasins or the clothes of another at night. The latter imperceptible interchange their things and the first man burns his own property

K67A.definition_eng: A man who has a low social position is a nuisance for persons of high position. He gets to know that they plan to drown him or his preperty (rare: to strangle him) and tricks them to drown instead one of them or their own property

K67B.definition_eng: Person of a low social position (a man) makes an agreement with a person of high social position (an ogre) that the master must never become angry with the servant. The servant abuses the master until the latter erupts in anger and has to be severely punished or to pay a great fee

K67C.name_eng: Skin ribbon ripped off from the back
K67C.definition_eng: Person agrees that under certain conditions another may rip off a piece of skin from his back or inflict some other body injury

K67D.name_eng: Flight of the master with his goods in the bag
K67D.definition_eng: A farmhand or a family member annoyed his master or another family member so much that the latter decides to slip away from him or her. However, the annoying person hides in his luggage and appears as soon as he stops for a rest

K67E.name_eng: The woman as cuckoo in the tree
K67E.definition_eng: The bargain between two persons is to end when a bird whose call is related to particular time of a temporal cycle will be heard. In order to hasten the contract’s end, another person imitates the bird. The first one recognizes the trick

K67F.name_eng: Slaughter any sheep that will look at you!
K67F.definition_eng: A fool (trickster) is told to slaughter any sheep (cow, ox) that will look at him, i.e. it’s all the same which one. He kills all the sheep because all of them looked in his direction

K67G.definition_eng: Pretending that he is acting according his master’s instructions, the farmhand cuts off the lips of domestic animals (because they “must smile”)

K67H.definition_eng: When the farmhand is sent to the place where he is expected to be killed by wild beasts, he subdues them, brings home and lets into the cattle-shed (stable), and the beasts destroy the master’s cattle (pigs, horse)

K67I.definition_eng: A farm-hand is told to walk along the direct line or to overcome an obstacle without breaking it. He slaughters animals entrusted to him, cuts them into pieces and throws every piece separately across the hedge or he breaks the hedge though there is an entrance nearby

K68.definition_eng: An old man abused by another (often his son-in-law) brings home a clot of blood, from which a child is born. The blood-clot boy avenges the old man

K69.definition_eng: A group of persons decide to go to the end of the world to meet the Sun or other supreme god. One (or several) of them perish on their way, some reach destination, at least one returns home using the shorter way than the one they have took before

K7.definition_eng: A man (rarer a woman) compares something with genitals of another person. The insulted one takes ravenge on him or her

K70.name_eng: Two sisters-in-law: the girl and the frog
K70.definition_eng: One brother marries a girl, another a frog or toad, both bring them to their parents, or one man takes two wives, a woman and a frog. Both wives have to pass a test. Values of the girl are highly assessed, the frog’s poor qualities are revealed

K71.name_eng: Coyote first betrays and then saves his brother
K71.definition_eng: Coyote's brother is victorious against numerous enemies as far as Coyote does not break some taboo. Enemies kill the brother. Coyote gets his remains, escapes, revives him

K72.definition_eng: Powerful person listens in conversation of three (rare: two or four) women. Each of them tells what she would do if the person marries her. One promises to bear his son (children) who would have wonderful qualities, two others promise to practice some kind of work or (more rare) marry people of lower status

K72A.name_eng: A ban to kindle any light
K72A.definition_eng: A king notices that his ban to kindle any light during the night is broken

K73.definition_eng: A young woman promises to bear a wonderful children (wonderful son). In her husband's absence other people (co-wives, mother-in-law, etc.) try to kill the mother and/or the child, usually slandering the young woman

K73A.name_eng: Baby child substituted with object or animal
K73A.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with an animal or an object (inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to an animal or an object)

K73A1.name_eng: Baby child substituted with inanimate object
K73A1.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with inanimate object and/or inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to a stone, broom, doll, etc.

K73A2.definition_eng: Rivals of the beloved wife hide or throw away her baby and substitute it with an inanimate object or (rare) a small animal (but not with a pup) and tell the husband that the woman gave birth to a broom, stone, etc.

K73A2A.name_eng: Baby child substituted with a piece of wood
K73A2A.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with a piece of wood and/or inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to a piece of wood

K73A3.name_eng: Baby child substituted with a doll
K73A3.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with a doll or statue (inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to a doll)

K73A4.name_eng: Baby child substituted with a pup
K73A4.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with a pup (inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to a pup)

K73A5.name_eng: Baby child substituted with a kitten
K73A5.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with a kitten (inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to a kitten)

K73A5A.name_eng: Baby child substituted with a monkey
K73A5A.definition_eng: Hostile women substitute baby of the newly made mother with a monkey (inform the baby’s father that his wife has given birth to a monkey)

K73A6.definition_eng: Enemies of the woman kill (throw away) her wonderful children. Trees (flowers) grow from their remains. Eventually the children acquire their human form again.

K73A7.name_eng: The wonderful children: sister and her two brothers
K73A7.definition_eng: Woman gives birth to three (and not two or more) wonderful children. They survive and triumph over their enemies

K73A8.name_eng: The wonderful children: brother and sister
K73A8.definition_eng: Woman gives birth to wonderful boy and girl. Being substituted with animals or objects and thrown away, they survive and triumph over their enemies

K73A9.definition_eng: Lying on the nuptial bed, the false wife who took place of the real one hears the voice of the latter or her children and in the morning orders to destroy the bed

K73B.definition_eng: A woman who was falsely accused of killing her new-born child or giving birth to pups and the like is punished in such a way that she must suffer from filth and be taunted by passers by

K73B1.name_eng: Mother and child in a barrel
K73B1.definition_eng: A woman with her new-born child (or a woman pregnant with a boy) or a young girl and a young boy is put into a barrel (box, skin bag, boat) and thrown into the sea (into the river, down the mountain slope)

K73B2.name_eng: To make kettle boil with a story
K73B2.definition_eng: One needs to make kettle boil telling a story that is incredible but real

K73B3.name_eng: Throw one nut as a keepsake
K73B3.definition_eng: A person must count a number of nuts in a barrel (take nuts one by one). He does it accompanying his actions with a denunciating story

K73B4.name_eng: To fill a bag with truth
K73B4.definition_eng: Person must fill a bag (bowl) with truth (falsehood, tales). He fulfills the demand telling a denunciating story

K73B5.name_eng: But the mother also could eat her baby up
K73B5.definition_eng: A woman is accused of doing something that she could not do by her very nature. To reject accusation, another example of something absurd and impossible is suggested or it is told that the person believes in impossible though rejects possibility of the possible

K73B5A.name_eng: Mother’s milk ascertains her children’s identity
K73B5A.definition_eng: Kin relations between a woman and her children is confirmed when the milk from her breast (scones made with her milk) hits their mouths (are tasted by her children). If, however, the stream of milk does not land in the son’s mouth, this indicates his imminent death

K73B6.name_eng: Hero flies to his mother’s enemies to listen to what they are talking about
K73B6.definition_eng: Wife of a powerful person gives birth to wonderful child(ren). Her envious sisters play a trick to make her husband order to get rid of her (usually to put her and her child into the barrel which is thrown into the sea). The wonderful son saves her and himself. Imperceptibly (usually in guise of an animal or an insect, or sending his brother who has guise of a puppy) he gets into his father’s house and listens in what people are are talking about

K73B7.name_eng: Hero saves magic wife from her enemy
K73B7.definition_eng: Hero saves magic wife from her enemy when both, the future wife and the enemy, have the animal guise. Later the saved one turns into a woman

K73B8.name_eng: Many children of the calumniated woman
K73B8.definition_eng: In the absence of her husband, the woman gives birth not to one, two or three but to many children (7, 20, 100 and the like); her rivals throw her babies away and replace them with animals or inanimate objects (inform her husband that her children are not human)

K73B9.definition_eng: A baby that was thrown into the water does not die but grows up in the underwater world and returns to the people

K73C.name_eng: A girl in a bird's nest
K73C.definition_eng: A girl gets into a bird’s nest (usually the bird carries away a baby-girl). The bird cares for her like her parent, the girl becomes a beauty

K74.name_eng: Hero, his companions and a dwarf
K74.definition_eng: The hero and his companion or companions live together. Every morning one stays at home while another or others go to hunt, etc. A demonic person comes, eats up all the food and beats the cook. Or the man who remained at home comes to the demon himself in search of fire and is maltreated by him. The hero kills or neutralizes the demon

K74A.name_eng: Only the hero gets to overcome the demon whose track he then follows
K74A.definition_eng: Every time a demon commits an outrage upon one of the men who remains at home. When it is the hero’s turn, he overcomes the demon and follows his track to his world

K75.name_eng: The youngest daughter is willing (The loathsome bridegroom)
K75.definition_eng: A girl (usually the youngest of several sisters) does not reject but marries a poor, sick, dirty, old, too young, non-human, etc. man who later demonstrates his supernatural qualities

K75A.name_eng: Thrown apple hits the chosen one
K75A.definition_eng: Boy or girl selects one person among many throwing an object (usually an apple) into him or her. This way a girl makes a choice of a husband, a young man of a bride, a boy identifies his father

K75A1.name_eng: The youngest son-in-law should live in the stable
K75A1.definition_eng: The sovereign orders his youngest daughter (together with a man chosen by her) to live in conditions that do not correspond to her high status. Her father does not know that her chosen one is not a poor wretch as he seems to be but a prince

K75A2.definition_eng: The unrecognized hero works as a gardener at the powerful person

K75A3.definition_eng: The unrecognized hero works as a groom for the powerful person

K75B.name_eng: Three melons from the three daughters
K75B.definition_eng: To show their father that he must marry them, his daughters of different age send him fruits of the same kind but of different degree of ripeness (or bread that is differently baked)

K75C.definition_eng: Devil is ready to make a man rich if he would not wash (and comb) himself for a long time. The man is willing, both fulfill their promise

K76.definition_eng: A boy born into a family or found by his adoptive parents has a strange guise (ball of meat, nut, bag, half of a man, an animal). He possesses magic power, becomes a handsome man and usually marries a girl of high social status. The magic spouse of a princess originally has a non-human or monstrous appearance

K76A.definition_eng: Frog or toad marries a girl or a handsome youth marries a frog or road

K76B.name_eng: Snake son and the snake husband
K76B.definition_eng: An (adoptive) son is a snake who turns into handsome man. The snake is the magic spouse of princess, lost and returned

K76C.definition_eng: An (adoptive) son (rare daughter) emerges from a gourd (rare water melon, coco nut) or is found inside it

K76C1.name_eng: Woman gives birth to a gourd
K76C1.definition_eng: Woman gives birth to a gourd which turns into person or which contains a person or people inside

K76D.definition_eng: An (adoptive) son is a hedgehog. He marries a princess, turns into handsome man.

K76E.definition_eng: An (adoptive) son or daughter is a pig. He marries a princess, turns into handsome man (she marries a handsome man)

K76F.definition_eng: A youth who initially has guise of a calf marries a girl and becomes a handsome man.

K76G.definition_eng: An (adoptive) son is a crab. He marries a princess, turns into handsome man

K76H.name_eng: Magic bridegroom threatens the girl’s father with disasters
K76H.definition_eng: A youth who temporally has a strange or monstrous guise wants to marry a princess but is rejected. He threatens the princess’ father with disasters after which the king agrees to give him his daughter

K77A.name_eng: War campaign of objects and animals
K77A.definition_eng: Different objects and animals decide to attack somebody (cf. motif k77b: the first interaction with the enemy is unexpected for the animals). Animals which are mentioned are mostly harmless in reality or if strong, they act in company with the weak ones. The participants either come to the enemy’s place or wait for the enemy in their own place. Variants with animated objects (needle, egg, stone, etc.) and with objects as tools used by a human person are difficult to select from each other

K77A1.definition_eng: When different objects and animals hide in the house of their enemy who is expected to come there, an egg (fruit, bladder) hides in hot ash and explodes scorching the enemy’s face

K77A2.name_eng: Slippery object left on the floor
K77A2.definition_eng: When different objects and animals hide in the house of their enemy who is expected to come, they leave on the floor something slippery stepping on which the enemy falls

K77A3.definition_eng: When different objects and animals set off to make harm to their enemy. One of them rides in a miniature cart

K77A4.name_eng: The egg and the chicken are among the participants
K77A4.definition_eng: When different objects and animals set off to make harm to their enemy, an egg or a chicken are among the participants (sometimes they are the leaders); the campaign against the antagonist is organized to avenge the murder of the chicken

K77A5.name_eng: War campaign of objects and animals
K77A5.definition_eng: Different objects and animals go to war with the aim to rob somebody or to attain prestige

K77B.name_eng: The animals in night quarters (Bremen town musicians)
K77B.definition_eng: Domestic animals abandon their masters. They find an empty house or build a house. Robbers or the predator animals come there. The domestic animals attack (or just frighten) them. The robbers (predators) do not understand who are their enemies, are scared and run away

K77B1.name_eng: The wolf flees from the wolf-head
K77B1.definition_eng: When domestic animals meat the predators, they – deliberately or unintentionally – behave in such a way that the predators escape in panic

K77B2.definition_eng: A predator animal asks a goat (a ram, etc.) about a purpose of certain parts of his body. The goat describes every part as a weapon able to injure his opponent or the goat really possesses weapons

K77B3.definition_eng: Goats meet a wolf. One goat has one belly, another has two bellies, the third one has three bellies, and so on. The wolf is scared or killed by the goat with the greatest number of bellies

K77C.name_eng: Ones who hide in a house attack their enemy
K77C.definition_eng: Objects and/or animals hide themselves in a place where their enemy is expected to come. They attack or frighten him in succession, he dies or runs away. Or a person who plans to make harm to his enemy puts objects and animals in corresponding loci

K77D.definition_eng: Small animated objects act like persons (keep house, travel, attack enemies etc.)

K78.definition_eng: An ogre (an ogress) swallows people, is killed but the people are not found in his or her belly or are found dead. Only when the ogre's finger is cut off, the hero finds a remedy to revive the people or the swallowed up (the swallowed hero himself) come out alive from the finger of the ogre

K78A.name_eng: To cure a person, demon swallows him
K78A.definition_eng: The demon swallows and vomits maimed and disfigured persons that makes them healthy and handsome

K78B.name_eng: Arrow shot into the sky kills the shooter
K78B.definition_eng: The hero suggests his adversary to shoot an arrow into the sky. Falling to earth, the arrow kills the shooter

K79.name_eng: Snake serves an example of resuscitation
K79.definition_eng: Person in a desperate situation gets to see how a snake or other small animal uses remedy to revive or to cure itself or other animals. The person uses the remedy, succeeds

K80.definition_eng: Person (usually a young woman) turns into different objects or creatures which another person destroys one by one. However, the person is reincarnated again and again and ultimately acquires her or his original form

K80A.name_eng: A bird or an object tell about a murder
K80A.definition_eng: An object or a creature that emerged from remains, decorations, etc. of a killed person tells about his or her fate. Usually a reed grows from the person's grave and a pipe made from the reed tells the story

K80A1.definition_eng: A bird (that usually emerges from the remains of a murdered person or being incarnation of his or her soul) punishes the murderer or tells people about the crime

K80A2.definition_eng: Body part of a murdered person or a plant that grew on the place of the crime tells people about the crime

K80A3.name_eng: One who picks up more berries is killed
K80A3.definition_eng: Members of the same household (children, young girls or women) go to the forest to pick up berries and kill one of them because she or he arouses their envy
