K80A4.definition_eng: Hair of the head of a person turns into grass (thorns, bamboo, shrub)

K80A5.name_eng: A wild boar and the fratricide
K80A5.definition_eng: Brothers who are rivals as bridegrooms or successors must kill a wild boar. The youngest does it. The elder brother kills him and takes the boar. The crime is uncovered

K80A6.name_eng: Speaking pipe made from a recently grown plant
K80A6.definition_eng: A pipe or other musical instrument is made from a plant that has grown on a place where certain person was killed (fell, touched ground). When the instrument plays, people hear a particular message

K80B.name_eng: My mother slew me, my father ate me
K80B.definition_eng: The (step)mother kills or orders to kill her small (step)son, eats him or feeds his flesh to her husband. The son revives, usually in the form of a bird who tells about the crime.

K80C.definition_eng: Person becomes a victim of a murder. Just before dying he or she calls on some birds (celestial bodies, animals, plants, etc.) to bear witness for the crime. Getting to see these birds (this plant, the Sun, the Moon, etc.) the murderer reveals himself without thinking. Or the birds, being the only witnesses, bring the investigators to the murderers.

K80C1.definition_eng: A person brings to a king or has at his home something edible. At the decisive moment fruits or meat turn into human remains. The person imprisoned (and executed)

K80C2.name_eng: The treasure finders who murder one another
K80C2.definition_eng: Three (two, more) men find (rob) a treasure. One of them goes away for a while. Those who stay kill him when he returns but die later from eating food (drinking wine) which he had poisoned

K80C3.name_eng: A name helps to reveal the murderer
K80C3.definition_eng: Before his death a man asks his murderer to go to his pregnant wife, let she gives the child certain name. Hearing an unusual name of the child, a powerful person initiates the investigation, the murderer confesses his crime

K80C4.definition_eng: In a deserted place, a man kills another. After some time he is exposed thanks to circumstances and facts that do not seem important and do not report on the crime directly (the victim’s last words; objects or live beings that were or appeared on the place of the murder). (All texts that contain motifs K80c, K80c1, K80c3, K80c4, also contain a more general motif K80c4)

K80D.definition_eng: Person is bewitched (transformed into a bird, faints) when a pin or other sharp object is stuck into her (rare his) body

K81.definition_eng: For minor offence or because of false accusation a young girl or woman is maimed and expelled from home (rare: killed or she kills herself). The maimed person magically obtains her body integrity (the dead revives)

K81A.name_eng: The handless girl in the prince’ garden
K81A.definition_eng: A girl with the cut off hands comes to the fruit tree (into the vegetable garden) to find food. A princes gets to see her there and marries her

K82.definition_eng: Wife of a man or wives of a group of brothers envy his (their) sister and tries (try) to destroy her

K82A.definition_eng: An ill-disposed elder woman makes a young woman or girl to swallow snake eggs (a snake, something else). Her stomach becomes to swell and the man believes that the victim has become pregnant because of her dissoluteness (rare: to make snakes, worms, etc. to kill her from inside)

K83.name_eng: The sons on a quest for a wonderful remedy for their father
K83.definition_eng: To cure a sick person or to make him (rare: her) young again it is necessary to bring a remedy from a distant country. The medicine is brought and the sick person is cured (becomes young)

K83A.name_eng: Where your father has never been
K83A.definition_eng: To fulfill their mission, persons sons must reach a place where he never been (or which he reached in his time)

K84.definition_eng: Young man gives his sisters to the first bridegrooms who claim them. These are demons or animals who usually later help him

K84A.name_eng: To give a sister to the first male who comes marry her
K84A.definition_eng: On his deathbed, father orders his son to give his sister(s) in marriage to the first male(s) who come(s) to take her (them)

K85.definition_eng: An antagonist possesses a horse which can overtake any other. Hero obtains the brother (sister) of this horse who is the only one to win the race with the antagonist's horse

K85A.name_eng: The thought-horse and the wind horse
K85A.definition_eng: When assessing the swiftness of a horse, the speed of thought (lightning) and the speed of wind are compared

K85B.definition_eng: A horse with a bigger number of legs or wings is faster than the horse that has lesser number of legs or wings

K85C.name_eng: The four-legged horse is faster than the three-legged one
K85C.definition_eng: A horse with a bigger number of legs or wings is faster than the horse that has lesser number of legs or wings

K85D.name_eng: A horse with a skin resistant to bites
K85D.definition_eng: Hero’s horse asks his master to cover him with skins (smear with pitch and sprinkle with sand, etc.) that makes him invulnerable to other horse’ bites

K85E.definition_eng: Magic horses live under the water

K86.definition_eng: Because a small child is ignored or punished by its parents (usually it cries late in the evening), bush spirit or animal carries it away

K87.name_eng: Marriage with an animal creates problems
K87.definition_eng: A woman becomes the wife of an animal (rare: other non-human being). Her husband cares for her but ultimately the animal, the woman, her children or her relations are killed, she turns into an animal herself, animals and humans become enemies, etc.

K87A.definition_eng: A forest woman receives or steals a small boy and brings him up to make him her paramour

K87A1.name_eng: Baby passed to the demon’s hands
K87A1.definition_eng: Mother of a baby child is asked by demonic woman to give her the baby for a short while or the demon imperceptibly replaces another person who must take the baby. As soon as the demon gets the baby she carries it away to her place

K87B.definition_eng: Gathering berries a woman steps into bear's dung and curses bears. A bear abducts her and marries her. Her human husband, her brothers, or supernatural person kill the bears

K88.definition_eng: Two men travel or argue about whether truth or falsehood (justice or injustice, etc.) is more powerful. The evil one abandons the good one robbing or blinding (maiming) him but the good one gets back his sight and becomes rich. The evil one usually perishes

K88A.definition_eng: Wicked stepmother (aunt, a rival) blinds a young woman. The heroine returns her eyes (often gets them back in exchange for some values)

K88B.definition_eng: A companion promises to share water or food with a thirsty or hungry person on condition that he or she allows to blind him or her

K88C.name_eng: The dog’s blood is a medicine for princess
K88C.definition_eng: Person gets to know that the blood (brain, etc.) of a dog who guards sheep nearby can cure the sick princess (prince). He applies this medicine and is rewarded

K89.name_eng: A girl and a witch: presents of kinsfolk
K89.definition_eng: A girl and her rival (a witch, a frog) marry two brothers. Both daughters-in-law have to bring presents from their kinsfolk. The girl finds her brother, brothers or sister who were lost or died in the beginning of the tale and they give her valuables. Presents brought by the rival are worthless

K89A.name_eng: In search of the place to abandon the sister
K89A.definition_eng: A girl with her maimed sister or brother escapes from a danger. The sister (brother) rejects some places where the girl wants to abandon her or him but agrees with her last suggestion

K89B.definition_eng: A girl becomes separated with her brothers (or brother) who die, remain in a tree, on a hill, ascend to the sky, etc. Usually after being happily married, the girl once again meets her brothers who have acquired a non-human nature

K89C.definition_eng: A girl parts with her brother or sister who marries a bear and helps the girl

K89D.name_eng: Person hides turning into a needle
K89D.definition_eng: Person who remained alone in a house or got into the house of dangerous creatures hides turning into a needle or other weaving or spinning tool

K8A.definition_eng: Person gets into the belly of water being or into the belly of giant creature which appearance and living place remain vague. He kills the monster from the inside and/or returns to earth by himself (i.e. not extracted by other people)

K8AA.definition_eng: Giant bird swallows people. The hero kills the bird and lets people free or being swallowed himself remains alive and comes out

K8B.name_eng: Woman is soul of a whale
K8B.definition_eng: Raven gets inside a whale where he sees a woman who asks him not to touch an inner organ of the whale (usually its heart) or a burning lamp. Raven touches it, woman disappears, the whale dies

K8C.definition_eng: Person gets into the belly of ground animal or bird. He kills it from the inside and/or returns to earth by himself (i.e. not extracted by other people)

K8C1.name_eng: First swallowed by herbivorous animal and then by wolf
K8C1.definition_eng: Tiny boy is first swallowed by chance by a big herbivorous animal and then carried away by a wolf began to eat the animal's offal

K8C2.definition_eng: Mouse swallowed by a big terrestrial animal cuts it open from the inside and comes out

K8C3.name_eng: Not from your mouth but through your side
K8C3.definition_eng: One (animal) person refuses to use different body parts of another besides the only one the use of which causes another’s death

K8C4.definition_eng: A mouse, a small bird, a porcupine or other animal (rare: person) of a small size gets inside a big ungulate (elk, deer, buffalo, tapir) to kill (and then usually to eat) him

K8C5.definition_eng: Animal person (mammal, bird, fish) of a small size (less than a fox) gets inside the bear and kills him from the inside (usually eat his meat)

K8D.definition_eng: Person (often an animal-person) gets into the belly of anthropomorphic being. He kills it from the inside and/or returns to earth by himself (i.e. not extracted by other people)

K8E.definition_eng: Person or animal gets into another being through its anus

K8F.definition_eng: A swallowed up person finds alive deer in the belly of the monster

K9.name_eng: God’s wife thrown down from the sky
K9.definition_eng: The sky chief discovers or thinks that his wife, sister or lover is untrue or incestuous. He throws her down from the sky. She becomes the mistress of the lower or middle world or a part of it or one of her sons gets power over the lower world

K90.name_eng: The black and the red ones
K90.definition_eng: A man gets to see two fighting monsters or animals (usually of contrasted colors like red and black, black and white). He helps one of them and/or one of them helps him

K90A.name_eng: Trying to hit the black serpent a man hit the white one
K90A.definition_eng: A man gets to see how two serpents of contrast color fight. He tries to hit one f them but injures another by mistake. The injured snake’s kinfolk come to punish the man but they give him presents after getting know that he regrets his mistake

K90B.name_eng: Stag antlers stuck in serpent’s throat
K90B.definition_eng: Antlers of a stag or tusks of an elephant who a serpent tries to swallow are stuck in its throat

K91.definition_eng: Hero's dogs or horse or (rare) he himself fight with his adversary in the underworld (under the water). Those who are waiting for the outcome of the combat understand who overcomes whom by the color of water or foam that rises to the surface, or the color animal who comes first to the surface

K92.definition_eng: A man puts his children questions that seem easy to answer (how they love him, who is the elder in the family, etc.). The elder children flatter, the youngest daughter (rare: son) is reserved and her father drives her away or deprives of inheritance. Later her noble nature becomes evident to him

K92A.name_eng: The princess responsible for her own fortune
K92A.definition_eng: A girl driven away from home or married to a poor man become prosperous

K92B.definition_eng: A girl answers her father (rare: brother) that she loves him like she loves salt (or that salt is the most valuable, etc.). He becomes angry (usually drives her away) but later satisfies himself that she was right

K92C.name_eng: Wife is weaving, husband is selling
K92C.definition_eng: A princess or a fairy becomes the wife of a poor man. She weaves or embroiders a kerchief (or something else) and sends him to sell it. This is the first step to their ultimate success

K93.definition_eng: After a series of adventures and victories, the hero gets into trouble. His twin brother or the best friend follows his traces, gets across the same persons but overcomes the last enemy and revives (liberates) the hero

K93A.definition_eng: Sleeping in one bed with a woman, man puts a sharp or thorny object between them as a sign of chastity (sometimes the woman herself puts the sword)

K93B1.definition_eng: After eating a fish, the sterile woman gives birth to a son or twins

K93B2.definition_eng: After eating a fruit (more rare a vegetable, a pea, an egg), the sterile woman gives birth to a son or twins

K93B3.name_eng: Boys, colts and puppies are born the same day
K93B3.definition_eng: To have children, a woman eats a fish, apple or something else. A mare, a bitch or other domestic animals eat part of this food (often skin, broth, etc.). The woman gives birth to a boy (twins) a mare to colts, a bitch to puppies

K93B4.name_eng: Woman, mare, and bitch birth give birth to human boys
K93B4.definition_eng: When a woman gives birth to a boy (twins), a mare (a bitch and/or other domestic animals) also gives birth to human boys. When the boys come of age. they leave for a journey

K93B5.name_eng: A stratagem: hero turns into pup or kitten
K93B5.definition_eng: Person gets into the place of his antagonists acquiring guise of a pup or a kitten. Usually one of his adversaries suspects the deception but other think that the animal is nice and harmless

K93B6.name_eng: The sword that grows in the garden
K93B6.definition_eng: A woman becomes pregnant eating a fish. The fish bones (entrails, tail, etc.) are buried in a garden, and at this place grows something related to her son: either a weapon (a sword) or an object which appearance depends on her son’s wellbeing (a plant or a spring)

K94.definition_eng: Person eats magic bird, fish, small animal, or fruit and becomes prosperous and powerful

K95.definition_eng: Two persons who loved each other (usually a man and a girl) are buried in one grave or not far from each other. After the burial something related to this event takes place (two plants grow up and stretch their branches to each other, smoke of two funeral pyres is merged, two birds flu out from the grave, two stars appear on the sky, etc.)

K95A.definition_eng: Two lovers are buried in one grave or nearby. Two plants that grow up on the place stretch their branches to each other but a thorn grows in between them as an incarnation or symbol of a person who prevented the happy marriage

K96.definition_eng: Many brothers marry or have to marry in such a way that all their wives are (were) sisters

K97.name_eng: Now you are grieved as I was
K97.definition_eng: A man is going to kill but spares a giant bird. Later when the bird carries him high in the air it pretends to drop him or to abandon him on a rock. This way the bird wants him to feel the same terror that it felt when the man was going to kill it. Or the bird first drops and picks up a man and he later makes the bird feel a similar terror

K98.definition_eng: An animal or (rare) a person that gave birth to the hero or supported him for a long time asks his master or son to kill him or her. Its (her) remains turn into a house with a household where the hero can live

K99.definition_eng: A young man or (rare) a girl has a (day-)dream that predicts his or her future triumph. The dreamer either conceals or reports its contest to his family and in both cases is punished for too high opinion of himself. In the beginning the dreamer sometimes sells his dream to another young man, who becomes the protagonist of the tale. Adventures that follow explain the contest of the dream. The youth becomes rich and happy (e.g. marries heiresses of two kingdoms, that in the dream were symbolized by two suns or a sun and a moon), the girl marries king's son

K99A.name_eng: The father will humble himself before the son
K99A.definition_eng: A lad or a girl (often after having a prophetic dream) claims that he (she) will achieve extraordinary social position (usually that his or her parents, brothers, sisters will demonstrate signs of high respect to him or her). The lad (girl) is expelled out of the family but the prophecy is fulfilled

K99A1.name_eng: Smart man is rescued from prison
K99A1.definition_eng: An imprisoned man is rescued and exalted because only he gets to resolve problems that trouble the king or to save the princess (prince, the king himself)

K99A2.definition_eng: Person has a dream, another person buys it and acquires the fortune that the dream promised

K99A3.name_eng: The happy dream: Sun, Moon and stars
K99A3.definition_eng: A young man has a dream: he sees the Sun, the Moon and a star (all of them or some of these luminaries). When the narrative come to the end, the man understands the meaning of the dream: these are people who love or adore him

K99A4.name_eng: A young boy becomes the Pope
K99A4.definition_eng: A young man (teenager) demonstrates his wonderful powers, comes to Rome and is made the Pope despite his young age

K99B.definition_eng: At night a girl’s lover has to carry her away but falls asleep or is late. She is carried away by another man who happened to be on the place

K9A.name_eng: Punished person is hanged between heaven and earth
K9A.definition_eng: Punished person is hanged on a chain or a metallic thread between heaven and earth

L10.definition_eng: A monster kills victims with his or her sharp or stinging tail or protrusion on his or her back

L100.definition_eng: A youth and a girl who run away from pursuer transform themselves into a pair of persons, creatures or objects (pond and duck, church and priest, etc.) in order to escape detection by the pursuer

L100A.name_eng: A pursuer throws ahead the transformed fugitive
L100A.definition_eng: A fugitive turns into small object (stick, stone) or hides himself inside it. A pursuer picks it up and throws ahead in anger, thus unwillingly helping the fugitive to escape

L100B.definition_eng: The hero and his bride get to escape from the pursuer. The youth goes to visit his home, leaving his bride behind for a time and forgets her. When the youth is going to marry another girl, the forgotten fiancée reawakens his memory by performing magic actions. Or the girl herself forgets her magic husband as soon as she gets to her parents’ home

L100B1.name_eng: Dialogue between the male and the female pigeons
L100B1.definition_eng: The young man forgets his magic bride and meets another woman. At the last moment a bird tells the story about his real bride and he recalls everything. Usually two birds, a male and a female, have a dialogue in which the female can tell the male that he will be as cruel with her as this youth who has forgotten his bride.

L100C.name_eng: Duped visitors of a chaste woman
L100C.definition_eng: When a man comes to a beautiful woman she tricks him by asking to finish some trivial task, keeping him by her magic in an awkward or ridiculous position until daylight. Episode is repeated next nights with other or (rare) the same suitor. Usually the first suitor being ashamed tells the other that everything was nice, so all of them are humiliated the same way

L100D.definition_eng: A pretty, faithful wife is courted by one or several men, one of them usually a clergyman. With her husband’s consent, she invites the suitor(s) to a private rendezvous. Before the first man’s wishes are gratified, the next one arrives and then the husband himself. The suitor or suitors are caught in an uncomfortable position and then killed, punished in some other manner, ridiculed, made to pay ransom, to work, etc.

L100D1.definition_eng: A cleric or administrator visits a woman after the dark. When her husband knocks at the door, the woman, according to the scenario elaborated by her and her husband, tells the guest to lie in the cradle. She answers the husband that it is their baby son. The husband becomes or shams to become transform the adult into the baby (shaves his beard off, knocks out his teeth, grasps an axe to cut his feet off). The disgraced guest runs away

L100E.name_eng: The lover, the husband and the guest
L100E.definition_eng: Before coming in, a guest gets to notice that the housewife is with her lover. When the husband comes home, the guest pretends to possess magic object or the like that helps him to reveal where the good food and the lover are hidden

L100F.name_eng: Guest runs away from the host
L100F.definition_eng: In the absence of the host, the guest is told that the host is going to kill or to maim him. The guest runs away, the host runs after him with good intentions but the guest believes that the received warning had a reason

L100F1.name_eng: Lover runs away from the husband
L100F1.definition_eng: A farmhand (a young son of the peasant) arranges a situation a series of tricks to the love affair between the wife of his master and another man. The wife is going to bring food outdoor to her lover but gets to her husband. Seeing the master coming with an axe (stones, etc.), the lover believes, that he is going to attack him and runs away

L100G.definition_eng: The servant is asked to prepare a goose (chicken, etc.), eats one leg and maintains that the goose had only one leg enforcing his point by showing geese who stand on one leg. The master shoots away the geese so that they use both legs. Usually the servant replies that if he had frightened the roasted goose, it would have showed its second leg as well

L101.name_eng: Pieces of clothes thrown to pursuer
L101.definition_eng: Pursued by demonic creature (usually a whale or walrus), people throw behind piece by piece children’s or woman’s clothes. These attract the pursuer’s attention, he loses time, the runaways escape

L102.definition_eng: Seriously of for fun, a girl or a woman names an animal or remains of an animal as her husband or steps on the animal’s bones. The animal (revives and) carries her away. Her human husband or brother comes after her and they run away. The animal husband pursues them but abandons the chase or dies

L102A.definition_eng: The sea-gull abducts a girl or a woman but she gets to return to the people

L103.definition_eng: Treasure, or the like, is thrown back to tempt pursuer to delay

L103A.name_eng: Relatives do not open the door for the girl
L103A.definition_eng: A girl or young woman runs away from the demonic person, knocks at the door of her house but her relatives do not open the door and she is devoured by the demon. (Musical instrument is made from her hair or bowels)

L103B.name_eng: Animals carry hero away from a demon
L103B.definition_eng: A girl or a boy gets to demonic person. Sitting on the back of domestic animal (usually a calf, a bull) the girl (boy) escapes from the demon who pursues her (him). Usually several different animals in succession try to carry the girl away but the demon overtakes them and only the last animal brings her home

L103B1.name_eng: A spurt of dung into the pursuer’s face
L103B1.definition_eng: The Hero (heroine) flights from a demon riding a domestic animal (often a calf or a bull). When the demon is near, the animal spurts a portion of dung or intestinal gases into the face of the pursuer and the latter turns back

L103C.name_eng: A dog tries in vain to defend its masters against the ogres
L103C.definition_eng: A dog (cat, hare) tries to drive away a demon (usually an old ogres). The demon (or her victims themselves being unaware of the danger) cut off or break one by one the animal’s body parts and ultimately kills it that gives her the power over her victims

L104.definition_eng: A fugitive turns in succession into different animals or objects. A pursuer does the same, every time becoming an animal or a person who is dangerous for the fugitive in his given guise

L105.definition_eng: Animal, fish or person wounded by hero runs or swims away, usually with the man's projectile in his or her body. Local doctors are not able to cure the wound (usually because they do not see the projectile). The hero or his companion comes to the place where the wounded one lives and cures him or her (usually extracting his projectile from the wound)

L106.definition_eng: An antagonist makes a demand to the hero which is correct in form but really is unjustified. The hero fulfills the claims or is punished. Now antagonist takes an object or animal possessed by the hero, is unable to give it back and is punished

L106A.definition_eng: An antagonist makes a demand to the hero which is correct in form but really is unjustified. The hero fulfills the claims or is punished. Now antagonist takes an object or animal possessed by the hero, is unable to give it back and is punished

L106B.name_eng: Journey to the other world in search of the lost object
L106B.definition_eng: In search of a lost object, usually carried away by water or wind, a girl or (rare) a boy comes to a powerful person, gets the object back and/or is rewarded. The object is related to the everyday life, it has no ritual significance and is not a weapon

L107.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic beings have huge ears (use them for blankets, umbrellas, etc.)

L108.name_eng: The enemy imitates the friend's voice
L108.definition_eng: An (animal) person gives a signal (special song, etc.) to his relative or friend who lets him or her in. Antagonist imitates the person's voice or guise and the relative lets him in

L108A.definition_eng: A predator animal (ogre, ogress) swallows people or animals. The goat (rare: the sheep) punishes him or her and usually saves the victims (most often opens the ogre’s belly open and the swallowed ones come out alive)

L108B.definition_eng: To make himself unrecognizable by the victim, a predator or ogre modifies his throat or tongue mechanically (oils or burns it, asks blacksmith to remake it, etc.)

L108B1.name_eng: A smith makes the voice thin
L108B1.definition_eng: Person asks the smith to make his voice thin

L108B2.definition_eng: To get a thin voice, person lets the ants to bite his tongue

L108C.definition_eng: To make himself unrecognizable by the victim, a predator or ogre demonstrates clothes, limb, etc. that look like clothes or limb of his victim's mother, etc.

L108D.name_eng: Stones sewed up in the belly
L108D.definition_eng: Person who swallowed his prey alive falls asleep and does not feel anything when his belly is cut and the prey is replaced with stones

L108E.definition_eng: The fox has a child or children (usually she adopts a lamb, foal, etc.), cares for it. The wolf finds and eats it, the fox revenges on him

L108F.definition_eng: A person (a girl, a small boy) gets into the water and remains there. Antagonist lures him out imitating his father's or sibling's voice

L108G.definition_eng: Person is or becomes black and has to sit in the water till becomes white. An antagonist carries him or her away

L109.definition_eng: A gourd proves to be a cannibal or grows from remains of a monster

L10A.definition_eng: A hunter spends night in a desolate place. A demon comes to his fire. When the demon falls asleep or goes away for a while, the hunter puts his clothes over a log and hides nearby. When the demon attacks the log taking it for the man, the hunter wounds or kills the demon

L11.definition_eng: In a non-human world objects of everyday life have appearance of animals and monsters, mainly fish, amphibians and reptiles

L110.definition_eng: A demonic being swallows a multitude of people and animals. When it is killed and cut open, the swallowed ones come out alive or are revived

L110A.definition_eng: A demonic being swallows a person or (in African versions) a multitude of people and animals. Hero kills the monster but cutting open its body, injures a person who was inside. Usually this person is offended and finds opportunity to kill the hero

L110B.definition_eng: A stomach (spleen) cut out of the body of a domestic animal or fowl becomes a voracious monster

L110C.definition_eng: Old man and woman make a child of clay (wood, straw). The doll becomes alive, devours everybody who comes across. Usually a goat (sheep) breaks it, swallowed people come our alive

L111.definition_eng: The sky dwellers fish human beings who live on earth with a line and a hook

L112.definition_eng: A boy is born having only half of a body or only a head. Ultimately he obtains normal body

L113.definition_eng: A girl (rejects suitors for a long time but at last) falls in love with a handsome man who proves to be a demon or animal. Usually she eventually escapes from him

L114.name_eng: The youngest one saves siblings from demon
L114.definition_eng: A group of young people comes to a demon. The youngest brother of sister or a person whom others take for a sick, unpleasant, invalid one and who often accompanies the others against their wish saves them all

L114A.definition_eng: A member (usually the youngest) of a group of boys or girls gets with them to a cannibal. The cannibal plans to kill people when they fall asleep. The youngest boy or girl every time answers the cannibal why he or she is still awake and forces him or her to be engaged into different activities instead of killing the sleeping people. Brothers (sisters) run away and return home. (Tulu: girl is saved by her speaking cat)

L114B.definition_eng: Getting a task or by his own initiative, a trickster several times comes to a person (usually an ogre) and steals in succession objects in his possession or members of his family

L114B1.name_eng: A task: to bring the ogre
L114B1.definition_eng: Person has to bring a certain ogre and does it luring the ogre into a cage, a box, etc.

L114C.name_eng: To exchange clothes with ogre's daughters
L114C.definition_eng: Children or youths (usually a group of brothers) exchange clothes (headgears, ornaments, blankets, sleeping places) with their enemy’s children. The enemy kills his or her own children by mistake. Usually brothers get to the ogre or ogress and the youngest advices to exchange places (clothes, etc.) with ogre’s daughters). Outside of Europe the actors can be animals

L115.definition_eng: A girl who rejected suitors finds at last a really handsome man. He escorts her to his place and distributes on the way all his clothes and body parts that he loaned before. Only his skull (head) remains

L116.definition_eng: A cannibal (old man, Gipsy, etc.) carries away a girl. He walks from village to village forcing her sing or dance. People recognize her (or her voice) and release her

L116A.definition_eng: Hunting a doe (a deer), hero gets to the place of a magician or demon; the doe is a bewitched person or demon

L117.definition_eng: When a man goes to marry, an evil spirit joins him, helps him in the village of his bride, etc. but then claims at least half of the bride for himself. (In Gola story a man gets a wife for a spirit and claims a half of her)

L118.definition_eng: (Animal) person provokes another to put a part of his body into a split log (between two planks, etc.) and removes the wedge

L118A.name_eng: To cut his throat imitating a man
L118A.definition_eng: To get rid of a dangerous but stupid demon or animal, a man commits certain acts. His adversary repeats them without understanding their meanings and makes harm to himself

L119.definition_eng: Hero and antagonist fight in the air tearing off each other limbs. Usually their allies on earth preserve limbs of their leader and destroy limbs of the adversary

L12.definition_eng: Vultures bring to the sky a being who has lost part of its body members or is reduced to the head or skull

L120.definition_eng: Hero listens in conversation of demonic beings who plan to turn into something edible, attractive, etc. and to destroy those who touch them. The hero neutralize the demons beforehand

L120A.name_eng: Tongue of dragoness and the smith’s pincers
L120A.definition_eng: Hero hides in a smithy from a dragoness who pursues him. She destroys the door or wall (with her tongue) but the hero (smith) burns her (usually grips tight her tongue with his hot pincers or throws hot iron club in her mouth)

L120B.name_eng: Fighting hero is waking his brothers
L120B.definition_eng: The hero is fighting with a dragon and calls for help but he is not heard but when he throws his shoe (mitten) and his brothers (his horse) come and save him

L121.name_eng: Demonic woman marries hunter to kill him
L121.definition_eng: A wild animal, ogress or ogre turns into woman and marries a hunter with a special aim to kill him. Usually she goes with the hunter to the forest and acquires there her real guise

L121A.definition_eng: A hunter can transform himself into different objects. His demonic wife tries to identify them and kill the hunter

L122.definition_eng: A (demonic) person is riding a cock

L122A.name_eng: Stitching up cracks in the earth
L122A.definition_eng: A (demonic) person is stitching up cracks in the earth with a giant needle and thread

L123.definition_eng: To confuse pursuer, person many times runs away in different directions and comes back

L124.definition_eng: Person pulls out a sinew (spinal cord, intestine, ribbon of skin) from the body of a demon or receives from the demon a belt as a gift. He applies it not to his own or other person’s body but to a tree. The tree is cut to pieces or burnt

L124A.definition_eng: Being applied to a tree or a person, a girdle (sinew, intestine, etc.) cuts it or him through or burns

L125.definition_eng: A man marries a beauty but catches her in a situation when her not human nature is revealed. After this their marriage breaks down

L125A.definition_eng: A man marries a woman who is really a demon. Her real nature is revealed when in the night being thirsty and unable to find any water inside the house she turns into a snake (flies away letting her body members, etc.)

L125B.definition_eng: Spying on his wife (her husband), the man (woman) gets to see that she (he) goes to eat the dead bodies

L126.definition_eng: A small bird makes a powerful anthropomorphic person lose his temper. The bird cannot be annihilated, cries from inside person's stomach, the person suffers or dies

L127.definition_eng: In the other world person sees separate body parts or other strange creatures that dance, etc. He or she should neither express his or her surprise, laugh, nor name the God

L128.name_eng: You are Deo but I am Mahadeo
L128.definition_eng: When a demonic person or a predator animal gives his name, the hero or a herbivorous animal invents such a name for himself that suggests his superiority over his opponent

L129.name_eng: Why so big teeth? (Little Red Riding Hood)
L129.definition_eng: Person or animal is asked why his or her body parts or tools are such as they are. He or she gives the answers (or one who is asking answers for him). Ultimately one of them kills or badly injures the other

L129A.name_eng: A person asks, the wolf gives explanations
L129A.definition_eng: Wolf or demon is asked why his body parts do look like they are. Every time the wolf gives the explanation

L13.definition_eng: A small creature is reared up by people. When it is grown up, it becomes harmful and dangerous

L130.definition_eng: Two or more persons have only one eye for all

L131.name_eng: Your house is on fire! (all versions)
L131.definition_eng: To get rid of a (female) demon or to make a (lady)bird fly away, they are told that their house and/or children are on fire

L131A.name_eng: Your house is on fire! (appeal to a demon)
L131A.definition_eng: To get rid of a (female) demon, she is told that her house and/or children are on fire

L131B.name_eng: Your house is on fire! (appeal to a bird or ladybird)
L131B.definition_eng: To make a (lady)bird fly away, she is told that her house and/or children are on fire

L132.name_eng: The theft of food: a family conflict
L132.definition_eng: When a member of a small (family) group secretly eats the food reserved for others, a serious conflict (often a murder) follows

L133.definition_eng: Person is capable to preserve his limbs apart from his body and use them when needed

L134.definition_eng: Hero’s enemy (often a demonic woman) hides inside a sea wave or is associated with it

L135.definition_eng: Male person leaves his home and gets to unfamiliar places. On his way, he comes across different strange creatures. After all, he returns home or leaves the earth for the other world. (Rather often a long string of episodes breaks off or the story lacks the beginning and does not explain why the hero is travelling)

L14.definition_eng: A small creature (often a worm or a reptile) is brought home and reared up or it becomes to live by itself in an artificial body of water. When big, it goes out of human control or becomes something huge and/or dangerous. Cf. motif L13A (The reared up monster attacks people)

L15A.definition_eng: The only vulnerable spot is near the surface of person’s or creature’s body and not in his inner organs

L15A1.definition_eng: Vulnerable place on the body of a person or creature is on his or her foot (toe, heel, sole, ankle)

L15A2.name_eng: Made invulnerable but not the entire body
L15A2.definition_eng: The body of a person is made invulnerable (in a furnace, etc.) besides a particular spot

L15B.definition_eng: Person can be killed only with a particular plant that normally is not used as a weapon

L15B1.name_eng: Deer horn is a weapon against the evil
L15B1.definition_eng: During a fight between the good and the evil creators the good one chooses a deer horn for a weapon (because his adversary is afraid of it most of all)

L15C.definition_eng: Dangerous person tells simple-heartedly what he is afraid of giving the hero a good opportunity to scare him

L15C1.name_eng: The antagonist is defeated because he tells truth
L15C1.definition_eng: Dangerous person tells simple-heartedly what he is afraid of or what particular object is the receptacle of his life giving the hero a good opportunity to scare or to kill him

L15D.definition_eng: Life of a person or creature is preserved outside of his (her, its) body. Person or creature dies after the corresponding object is destroyed

L15D1.definition_eng: Being asked where his soul (death) is located, person initially gives a false answer. The inquirer usually becomes to show concern to corresponding object or locus (decorates it, etc.)

L15E.definition_eng: Hero's life is in certain object, usually in his weapon. When antagonist steals the object, the hero dies but revives after his friends or brothers find the object and bring it back

L15E1.name_eng: The sword thrown into a lake
L15E1.definition_eng: A powerful person tells his son, warrior or people depend on him to throw his blade (sword or sabre) into a sea or lake. The one to whom it was entrusted does not fulfil the order but declares that the blade was thrown into the water. The powerful person asks what happened when the blade had fallen and hears in response that there were no supernatural phenomena. He understands that his order has not been fulfilled and demands to do it. This time or after the situation was repeated the blade is really thrown into the sea / lake. The powerful person dies / moves into another world

L15E2.name_eng: What happened when you had thrown the sword into the lake?
L15E2.definition_eng: One person tells another to throw certain object (often a sword) into the water. Another tells that he had fulfilled the order but is unable to say what happened as a result, and it becomes clear that lies

L15F.name_eng: Heroine’s life in her necklace, ATU 412
L15F.definition_eng: A young woman or (rare) a youth falls dead when her necklace (rare: an organ) is stolen from her and revives again as soon as she gets it back or when the antagonist takes it off

L15G.definition_eng: Life of a man depends on an object that can be burned. He dies as soon as the object is burned

L15G1.name_eng: Knowing the secret of his family member, person kills him
L15G1.definition_eng: Person knows the secret on which depends life of his or her husband, son or wife. After a quarrel, he or she commits an act that looks insignificant but causes an immediate death of another

L15H.name_eng: The external soul: three or more objects one inside the other
L15H.definition_eng: An object that contains the life (soul) of a person is inside two or more creatures or other objects (like an egg in a duck, a duck in a hare, etc.) or the zoomorphic soul container tries to escape and turns in succession to other animals (three or more transformations)

L15H1.name_eng: Person’s soul is in the egg
L15H1.definition_eng: An object that contains certain person’s soul / death is inside other object, the latter is in the third one (etc.). The last receptacle of the life is an egg

L15H2.name_eng: Person’s soul is in a bird
L15H2.definition_eng: An object that contains certain person’s soul / death is inside other object, the latter is in the third one (etc.). The last receptacle of the life is a (small) bird (a nestling, several nestlings of birds)

L15H3.name_eng: Person’s soul is in an insect (worm)
L15H3.definition_eng: An object that contains certain person’s soul / death is inside other object, the latter is in the third one (etc.). The last receptacle of the life is an insect or a worm

L15H4.name_eng: Person’s soul is in a needle
L15H4.definition_eng: An object that contains certain person’s soul / death is inside other object, the latter is in the third one (etc.). The last receptacle of the life is a needle, the hero breaks it

L15I.definition_eng: A man dies or loses his strength (or pretends that it is so) if (some) hair on his head is cut off

L16B.definition_eng: All the body of a person is covered with eyes

L17.definition_eng: There is a headless anthropomorphic being who has eyes and/or mouth on his or her breast

L17A.name_eng: Eyes on the back of the head
L17A.definition_eng: Person or creature has another pair of eyes (or one eye) on the back of his head or (rare) on his back

L17A1.definition_eng: Persons or creatures with ever bigger number of eyes guard a man or a woman. The latter makes eyes asleep one by one but forgets about the last one

L17A2.name_eng: Rival woman with the odd number of eyes
L17A2.definition_eng: Instead of a beautiful woman, a man marries a demonic person with an odd number of eyes

L17B.definition_eng: Person or creature has another face (another mouth) on the back of his (her, its) head

L18.definition_eng: A bird with two or more heads on top of one body is described in tales or represented in art

L19A.name_eng: Beings with even number of heads
L19A.definition_eng: Beings (any besides birds) with even but not more than ten number of heads are described in tales or represented in art. Beings that with even number of heads named in a row with other multi-headed beings and the highest number is even or bigger than ten are not considered

L19B.name_eng: Beings with odd number of heads
L19B.definition_eng: Being (any besides birds) with more than ten heads or with odd (but more than one) number of heads are described in tales or represented in art. If beings with ever more number of heads are named, the row ends with a being that has odd (or more than ten) number of heads

L19B1.definition_eng: A monster (usually a reptile) with seven heads is described or is represented in art. If beings with ever more number of heads are named, the last number in a row is seven

L19B2.definition_eng: A monster with nine heads is mentioned either alone or at the end of the row of creatures with ever bigger number of heads

L19B3.definition_eng: A monster with twelve heads is mentioned either alone or at the end of the row of creatures with ever bigger number of heads

L1A.definition_eng: A young woman turns into the bear (in Asia, into the tiger) and attacks her husband or close relatives

L1B.definition_eng: A young woman turns into monstrous bear. She kills most of the people besides her younger sister (Ojibwa: younger sister of her former husband). Their brothers return from a hunt, kill the bear or she dies pursuing them

L1B1.definition_eng: A woman gets into conflict with her brothers and turns into dangerous demon

L1C.definition_eng: A young woman turns into monstrous bear. She kills most of the people besides her younger sister (Ojibwa: younger sister of her former husband). Their brothers return from a hunt, kill the bear or she dies pursuing them

L1C1.definition_eng: To escape from a demonic person, a group of men who are relations of a girl ascend to the sky and remain there

L1C2.definition_eng: Pursued by a demon, persons hide their younger brother or sister or children in a pit under the hearth

L1D.definition_eng: A were-jaguar kills most of the people but is killed itself thanks to a woman who remained alive

L1E.definition_eng: A monstrous bird is created from small amount of the flesh of a human being or animal (usually a heart) or from manioc starch

L1E1.definition_eng: A huge bird created or reared by the hero and friendly to him turns into a cannibal

L1F.definition_eng: A young woman turns into monster and kills her brothers avenging the death of her husband or lover

L2.definition_eng: Mask or costume stick to the person who put them on, and he is transformed into animal

L20.definition_eng: Two persons hunt or fish. One of them is or becomes a cannibal. He or she reveals his or her nature eating the quarry raw

L20A.definition_eng: A man climbs a tree, throws down bird nestlings to a woman. She eats them raw and then kills or tries to kill the man

L21.definition_eng: A cannibal under a tree plans to eat up a man who has climbed the tree. The man throws down and afar his pray or some object and escapes while the cannibal rushes to this object or is eating the pray

L22.definition_eng: After breaking some taboo, coming across a strange object or person, people fall asleep. They do not feel when at night spirits come and injure or kill them

L22A.definition_eng: After breaking some taboo, coming across a strange object or person, people fall asleep and awake blind

L23.definition_eng: Person gets hold of another. Trying to free himself, the latter turns into different materials, elements, animals or (Urarina and Setebo) orders different dangerous creature to attack the person

L23A.definition_eng: Being seized, person changes his or her guise in succession, one of the transformations is into the fire (and also into the water)

L23B.definition_eng: Being seized, person changes his or her guise in succession, the last transformations is into a spindle

L23C.name_eng: To break an object in two
L23C.definition_eng: Being seized, person changes his or her guise in succession, the last transformations is into a small wooden object (usually a spindle). As soon as this object is broken in two, person acquires forever the human guise

L23D.name_eng: Metamorphosis of the caught female person
L23D.definition_eng: Being seized by a person, a female person turns into different materials, elements or animals (Urarina and Setebo: sends different dangerous creature to attack the one who caught her)

L23E.name_eng: Metamorphosis of the caught male person
L23E.definition_eng: Being seized by a person, a male person turns into different materials, elements or animals

L24.definition_eng: Demons (or one of them) attack people and return to their den (usually a cave or tree hollow). People make suffocating fire around the den killing most or all of the demons

L25.definition_eng: People adopt a demonic child, girl or woman but discover that this being kills people (in particular babies left in its charge) sucking out their brains or taking out their eyes

L26.definition_eng: During the (first) initiation supernatural beings teach boys the rituals and kill them for breaking rules related to consumption and distribution of food

L26A.definition_eng: During the (first) initiation the men kill the supernaturals (and since then reproduce their appearance and/or voices during the male rituals)

L27.definition_eng: Two girls or young women meet a demon. One or both are not aware of danger. One is eaten up, another escapes

L27A.name_eng: One is eaten up, another escapes
L27A.definition_eng: Two or three children get to the house of a demon or the latter comes to their house. They do not know that the person is a cannibal or are not sure about it. The demon eats up one of the children. Another child (children) escapes, the demon pursues him or them and perishes. Usually the demon is a female, and if he is male, his victims do not arouse in him sexual interest

L28.definition_eng: Person who have eaten a prohibited meat or fish turns into monstrous snake or fish

L28A.name_eng: Eating of snake meat triggers flood
L28A.definition_eng: Because people (or certain person) eat the meat of a snake (dragon, strange fish), a flood begins or a landslide occurs, or a river (lake) appears

L29.definition_eng: Person catches fish in a place where it should not be, i.e. in a forest pond or in a tree hollow isolated from other water bodies; or he drinks water in such a place. After eating or drinking he dies, is transformed and/or attacked by monsters

L3.definition_eng: A demon takes appearance of a man and comes to his wife or (rare) to other woman. The woman (alone or with her child) runs away and/or kills the monster (herself or with somebody's help)

L30.name_eng: Eating of snake meat triggers thirst
L30.definition_eng: Person who breaks some sort of taboo (usually has eaten a prohibited food) is thirsty and drinks enormous quantity of water

L31.definition_eng: People against their will must follow an object, a creature, or a person (usually stick to it) who/which leads or carries them far away, usually into the water or to the sky

L31A.name_eng: Children carried away to the sky
L31A.definition_eng: An object descends from the sky. Playing children climb on it or stick to it, it carries them away to the sky

L31B.name_eng: Reptile carries people into the water
L31B.definition_eng: People find a snake or a turtle on a dry ground. They touch it or sit on it, stick to it, it carries them into the water

L32.definition_eng: Stone swallows, bites or transforms people

L33.definition_eng: Stone chases people to crash them

L33A.definition_eng: Trickster takes off an object (often a blanket) that lies on or near a rock or other seemingly inanimate object and that has been presented to it. The object pursues or otherwise punishes the stealer

L33B.definition_eng: Person suggests to another who looks like being unable to move (rock, stump, fire) a race competition or provokes this object to roll towards him. The competitor becomes to move, burns or crashes the person or runs away with his clothes

L33C.definition_eng: Trickster and rock agree to race down slope. The rock rolls with ever greater speed and crashes the trickster

L33D.definition_eng: Rolling rock kills people, hero destroys it

L33E.definition_eng: Trickster takes a blanket or decorations which are a property of Rock or other seemingly inanimate object (usually the same trickster presented this blanket to Rock before)

L33F.definition_eng: Rolling rock pursues person. The person cries for help, and goatsucker breaks Rock to pieces

L33G.definition_eng: A tree, a creature in a tree, a rock, etc. kills (severely injures) everyone who climbes it, names it in a certain way, etc. Person provokes others to do it and devours the killed ones. The last of the invited ones deceives the provoker

L34.definition_eng: Person kills or injures his enemy putting fire on his or her straw costume, mask, headgear, hair or object on his or her back

L35.definition_eng: At night, a shaman or a bush spirit comes and inserts his hand into the hut to steal food or to make this way love with a sleeping woman. A man who is in the hut cuts the hand off or breaks it

L36.name_eng: Woman attacks man who climbs a tree
L36.definition_eng: When a man climbs a tree (escaping from persecutor; to get bird nestlings, honey, fruits, etc.), his wife (rare: her brother) kills, injures him or turns into demonic creature who pursues him

L37A.name_eng: To get know causes of problems
L37A.definition_eng: On his way to a powerful person (God), a man comes across some persons or animals who ask him to put questions to this person from their part too (usually to ask what is the reason of their troubles)

L37A1.definition_eng: A man travels to get know why he is poor (unlucky). Other persons, animals, plants ask him to investigate the reason of their own misfortunes. God (fate) tells that the wolf (bear, lion) should eat the most stupid man. Other problems can be resolved if the queen gets a husband, a treasure is taken from under the fruit tree, etc. The man does not use opportunity to become a king, to receive gold, etc. because did not receive direct instructions to do it. The wolf decides that the man is a real fool and he must eat him

L37A2.definition_eng: Person comes to God (Fate, Sun, etc.) and puts questions that asked him to put those whom he met on the way. Somebody wanted to know for how long he must fulfill his duties. The answer: he or she must put other person on his or her place

L37B.definition_eng: Person accidentally overhears secrets of animals or demons and thus gets to know the causes of his and other people's misfortunes

L37B1.definition_eng: To cure a sick person or to save a household from misfortunes a toad or frog hidden in (nearby) the house should be killed (found, removed)

L37B2.name_eng: The overheard secret: a snake inside a person
L37B2.definition_eng: Overhearing conversation of two snakes or raven, person gets to know the cause of a sickness of another person: a snake has crawled into him. He snake out and the person regains his health

L37B3.name_eng: The magic medicine is in the body of the speaker
L37B3.definition_eng: Overhearing conversation of birds or demons, person gets to know that their bodies or body secretions have magic effect

L37B4.name_eng: The magic medicine is in the body of a dog
L37B4.definition_eng: Overhearing conversation of animals or ghosts, person gets to know that the meat (brain, blood) of a dog of a nearby shepherd has magic effect

L37C.definition_eng: A man comes across persons who incorporate his own or somebody’s else Bad and Good Lucks. He gets to influence their behavior and change course of events (for himself) for better

L37C1.name_eng: Luck (good or bad) as a person
L37C1.definition_eng: Good or bad luck of a man are particular persons with whom the man meets

L38.definition_eng: A demon puts a trap to catch people, hero gets into it

L38A.definition_eng: Person sticks to an object, usually touching it one by one with his body members. The object is a trap of demonic creature or is a non human creature itself

L39.name_eng: Hero is compelled to descend from a tree
L39.definition_eng: By trick or by force, one persom makes another to descend from a tree to harm him or her

L39A.definition_eng: A demon comes from the underworld and attacks a man who has climbed a tree

L39B.definition_eng: A tree grows from a doughnut (scone etc.) and usually brings doughnuts instead of fruits

L39C.definition_eng: A boy (rare: girl) climbs a fruit tree that is recently grown up (usually from a seed thrown by the boy) to eat fruits. An ogress tries to make him (her) descend to the ground

L39D.name_eng: To pass an apple from hand to hand
L39D.definition_eng: A boy climbs a tree to eat fruits. A demon asks him to share the fruits with her (him) but not to throw them to the ground but give them from hand to hand. The demon grabs the boy and carries him away

L3A.definition_eng: A woman remains alone and calls for somebody who could help her with her housework. A demon comes, kills the woman or her child

L4.definition_eng: Person kills girls (rare: his nephews, younger brothers of his wife, husbands of his daughter) in succession (usually the male person kills his wives). The last of potential victims escapes, usually after finding remains of those who had been killed or imprisoned earlier

L40.definition_eng: Person discovers (rare:still fails to discover) another getting to see his or her shadow or reflection in water

L40A.name_eng: Woman takes reflection of a youth for her own
L40A.definition_eng: An ugly woman gets to see in water a reflection of a youth who is up in a tree. She takes it for her own reflection and thinks that she has become beautiful

L40B.name_eng: Absurd actions to lure person out
L40B.definition_eng: Somebody acts in absurd way to lure person out of his or her place. The person does not understand the deception and comes to explain how to act correctly

L40C.name_eng: Pays for the bridle and claims the camel
L40C.definition_eng: Thanks to ambiguity of the saying, person pays for a cheap object but claims the much more valuable

L41.definition_eng: An ogre or ogress catches a person and carries his or her prey home but the person escapes on the way or immediately after reaching the ogre's house

L41A.definition_eng: Hero escapes from the demon's basket or bag letting stone (a piece of wood, some sand) instead of him

L41A1.definition_eng: When demon tries to empty his bag, stones and not the hero fall out and break the cauldron

L41B.definition_eng: An ogress puts her victims into a basket which is filled or smeared with pitch

L41C.name_eng: Children caught when sliding down a slope
L41C.definition_eng: Ogre catches children when they play sliding down a slope

L42.definition_eng: An ogre or ogress catches a person and brings him to his or her home where he or she plans to cook and eat him. The hero escapes

L42A.definition_eng: An ogre steals fresh corpses from graves and devours them

L42B.definition_eng: An ogre's child or (rare) wife believes in what hero tells him (or her) and releases him. Usually the hero kills the child and puts its meat to cook in the very pot where the ogre planned to cook the hero

L42B1.definition_eng: Person abducted by a demon suggests him or her to make a ladder of pots, pans and other kitchen utensils by which the demon could climb up to catch the person. The ladder is collapsed and the demon injured or killed

L42C.definition_eng: Person hides from the powerful one now in his house, now outdoors, the powerful cannot catch him

L42D.definition_eng: Person escapes from an ogre, runs over frozen water body and spills some blood on ice. The ogre rushes to lick the blood, his tongue freezes to ice. Or the ogre slips on ice, falls, is badly hurt, dies

L42E.definition_eng: An ogre catches a person and carries his or her prey home but the person escapes on the way. The ogre comes back, this time carries the person to his home. Or the ogre catches a group of children, most of them escape on the way, one is brought to the ogre's place

L42F.definition_eng: Person that has to be eaten up imperceptibly runs away. The master of the house thinks that his wife had eaten the food alone and cuts her belly open

L42G.definition_eng: Step mother or more often father (persuaded by his wife) abandons children in a desolate place. Getting to the ogre or ogress, children (or at least one of them) survive and ultimately achieve success

L42G1.name_eng: Chops are heard, woodcutter is gone
L42G1.definition_eng: Father (step mother) abandons children in the forest. He (she) hangs a plank (gourd, shoe, etc.) on a tree that is striking trunk under the wind. Children believe that he is still nearby cutting woods

L42G2.definition_eng: Walking person creates a trace behind him or her throwing seeds, stones, etc. or the trace is produced because blood drops behind the person. The traces is destroyed unintentionally by birds, animals, wind etc.

L42G3.definition_eng: In a far-away place person comes across a house that is made, completely or partly, of edible matter

L42G4.name_eng: Give me your finger to feel it
L42G4.definition_eng: An ogre (ogress) puts a person (usually a child) in the cage and feeds him to make him fat. To see if the prisoner is fat enough, the ogre asks him (her) to show his finger and feels it. Instead of the finger, the prisoner stretches something tough and thin (a stick, a bone, a rat’s tail)

L42H.name_eng: Ogres who come to a feast devour the host
L42H.definition_eng: An ogre brings the hero to his house to feast on him together with other ogres. When the guests get to know that the hero has escaped, they devour the host

L42I.name_eng: Sister sets out to save her little brother
L42I.definition_eng: A demon carries away a little boy but his sister finds him, takes and back escapes from the pursuer. Usually the boy has three sisters but only the youngest one is successful

L42I1.definition_eng: A boy (rare: girl) rides in a boat. The witch lures him (her) to the shore and carries away. The boy (girl) escapes

L42J.name_eng: Tree bends down (mice in the ogre’s bag)
L42J.definition_eng: An ogre puts children (usually they are mice) into his bag, tell a tree (post, etc.) to bend down, hangs the bag on the tree and tells the tree to straighten itself back. Another animal person (usually the fox) releases the children

L42K.definition_eng: To cut a tree, an ogre coughs up an axe (anze)

L43.definition_eng: Persons who are dangerous for the hero (demons, robbers, merchants) take for something pleasant and edible those objects, creatures or matters (excrements, snakes, insects, etc.) that are disgusting (not edible)

L44.definition_eng: A man hides in a shelter. An ogre wants him to demonstrate certain parts of his body. The man demonstrates or parts of the body of an animal or some objects. The ogre believes that his adversary is a powerful creature

L44A.definition_eng: A man hides in a shelter. An ogre wants him to give certain parts of his body. The man gives the ogre instead parts of the body of a killed animal. The ogre does not understand the deceit, gives in response parts of his own body and dies

L44A1.definition_eng: A man and a demonic person agree to compare their lice. When the man demonstrates a tortoise (a frog), the demon believes that the man is the strongest of them

L44B.name_eng: The blind got his sight, the lame got his legs
L44B.definition_eng: A blind man and a lame man live together and help each other. When they got mortally scared or became to fight with each other, their eyes and legs were cured

L45.definition_eng: An ogre or a stronger animal catches a man or a weaker animal or drives him into a small enclosure and goes away for a time leaving a watchman. The hero dupes the watchman, escapes. (Most, though hardly all American cases can have post-Columbian African origin)

L46.definition_eng: Person ascends, descends, walks head downward or sees the world upside down

L47.definition_eng: Hero's enemy ascends a tree or rock head downward or walks backward letting the hero better possibility to kill him or to escape

L48.definition_eng: A man kills (usually in a tree, on a rock, at the edge of a well, of a precipice) and/or throws down one of his enemies. The other enemies do not recognize their comrade and think that their prey is falling down

L49.definition_eng: Body parts of a person or pieces of his flesh are thrown down one by one. (In American Indian versions those who are on the ground usually take them for game, honey, fish)

L4A.definition_eng: A demon orders the hero (heroine) to eat some food that is prohibited for him. When the hero answers that he has eaten the food the demons asks it where it is at the present moment and the food answers him

L4B.name_eng: The stain of blood is impossible to wipe off
L4B.definition_eng: Person gets to know that the heroine has broken his or her prohibition to enter a certain room because the corresponding evidence is preserved on her body or on an object given to her (e.g. the blood on the key)

L50.definition_eng: A person kills those who are passing by him. Usually he does not attack them all of a sudden but first distracts their attention. Usually he throws down his victims into a precipice, lake, etc.

L51.definition_eng: A cannibal, a bush spirit or a dangerous animal throws his victims into the precipice where water creatures devour them

L52.name_eng: Hero escapes from top of a tree
L52.definition_eng: Hero hides in a tree from an ogre. Before the ogre gets to fell the tree, the hero flies away or a bird helps him to escape

L53.definition_eng: A monstrous being is killed or neutralized by (burning hot) stones (pieces of metal, heavy fruits, etc.) thrown into its maw or anus or the being retreats when they menace to throw a stone into its maw

L54.definition_eng: To overcome a disaster, hot stones or ashes are thrown into the water

L55.definition_eng: To kill a dangerous animal or monster, acrid or hot liquid (boiling water, resin, soup, etc.) is poured into one of his body orifices

L56.definition_eng: A monster or a big animal dies when fire is kindled in its belly

L57.name_eng: Person gets his body part back
L57.definition_eng: Person loses his organ or body part, it is carried away. He finds its new owner, gets his property back

L57A.name_eng: Hero's body part is returned by his companion
L57A.definition_eng: The antagonists acquire person’s organ or body part (his remains) . Another person gets back what has been stolen and the first one revives (becomes strong again)

L57B.name_eng: Demon comes to get his body part back
L57B.definition_eng: Person cuts off and uses for his own needs a part of the body of predator animal or demonic creature. The demon (the animal) comes after it and usually kills or maims the person

L58.definition_eng: A man does not share food with his wife or kinsfolk. He or his food is transformed (turns into a bird, into worms, etc.) in punishment

L59.definition_eng: Man's wife, sister or mother eats all the nest food alone, she is transformed in punishment

L59A.definition_eng: People who treated badly the hero or his son are pulled into the sea and turn into sea animal or into parts of its body or into parasites on its hide

L5A.name_eng: Human head turns into celestial object
L5A.definition_eng: Anthropomorphic head that has no body turns into the sun, moon, stars or meteor

L5B.name_eng: The demonic woman pursues her children
L5B.definition_eng: A woman who had changed into demon pursues her own children

L5C.definition_eng: Human skull or head that has no body is a frightful demonic being

L5E.name_eng: Wife’s headless body pursues her husband
L5E.definition_eng: The beheaded woman pursues her husband while her head pursues her children

L5F.definition_eng: A bodiless head, face, or skull is a woman's husband, suitor or son. He is not dangerous but a good provider, saves people from hunger, etc.

L5G.name_eng: Elder sister’s head rolls after her younger sister
L5G.definition_eng: Only head remains from a girl. It rolls after her younger sister or sisters or they take it with them. Ultimately the head finds a place to stop

L5H.name_eng: Person stuck in an opening, head is torn off
L5H.definition_eng: Two sisters or two brothers get into demon's house. One crawls out through a tiny opening, another sticks there. Brother or sister pulls him or her by the head but tears it off

L6.definition_eng: A demonic being demands that a person would carry it permanently, clings to his shoulder or back

L60.definition_eng: Two or more sisters pick up a baby boy. In their absence he turns into adult man but when they come back they find him again in guise of a baby lying in its cradle

L61.definition_eng: Person devours his or her own flesh or disembowels himself or herself

L62.definition_eng: Stone man kills people but ultimately is killed himself

L63.name_eng: Person eats with vagina or anus
L63.definition_eng: Person eats food with her toothed vagina or with her or his anus

L64.definition_eng: Person removes part of his or her body (head, scalp, lungs) and then puts it back

L65.definition_eng: A baby or small child proves to be a demon, devours or injures people

L65A.definition_eng: A girl born to the family or found proves to be a monster, devours people. Her brother escapes, (usually marries and returns home, finds that everybody had been eaten up), runs away, she pursues him but cannot get

L65A1.definition_eng: A demonic person devours in succession parts of the hero’s horse, each time coming back to the hero and returning again to the horse. (Often asking the hero, if he has ridden on a three-. two-. one-legged horse)

L65A2.definition_eng: Person shoots off (injures) a finger of a demonic person and then sees that his baby-sister’s finger has a similar injury

L65B.definition_eng: A demonic woman or (rare) her paramour or a monster is going to kill a man usually after driving him up a tree. At the last moment the man's dogs or other animals or birds who are the man's pets come and kill the demon

L65B1.definition_eng: A man exchanges his sheep (goats) for dogs. The deal looks like unprofitable but the dogs help him to reach success

L65B2.definition_eng: Hero’s dogs have names that tell about their strength and deftness

L65B3.definition_eng: Persons climbs a tree and thanks to this escapes from a demon (who usually tries to fell the tree)

L65B4.definition_eng: Person extracts his or her tooth to use it as a weapon or a tool (often an axe)

L65B5.name_eng: Hero’s dogs at the princess’ marriage party
L65B5.definition_eng: Despite obstacles, dogs of the hero or other animals who are his helpers come to the princess at the very moment when she is forced to marry a deceiver

L65C.definition_eng: The eldest of three or more sisters becomes a cannibal and devours her sisters and other people

L65D.definition_eng: When the elder sister becomes a cannibal, the younger one (temporarily) escapes. Cf. motifs L1B, L65C

L66.definition_eng: A small animal digs an underground hole to the place where the monstrous stag, elk, antelope, or buffalo lies. Hero climbs along the tunnel and kills the monster

L67.definition_eng: After digging a tunnel under a lying monstrous animal, a small animal (usually a mouse) bites off the monster's hair at a certain place. Hero kills the monster thrusting his spear or arrow through the hairless place into the monster's heart

L68.definition_eng: Person turns into monster at night when he remains alone with his companion in the wilderness

L69.name_eng: Puma rescues man from a monster
L69.definition_eng: A man is attacked by a monster but puma or jaguar fights with the monster and rescues the man

L6A.name_eng: Sticking demon asks to be carried
L6A.definition_eng: Person that looks weak and feeble asks a man to carry him or her on his back and refuses to leave him

L7.definition_eng: Instead of chasing a person, a bush spirit, a monster or a dangerous animal follows by mistake an object or animal that moves nearby

L70.definition_eng: Person or animal is killed or injured with a heavy object dropped from a tree (or rock, etc.). The person or the animal knows that the objects will fall but has falls ideas about its character and weight

L71.definition_eng: Person has killed an animal. A trickster attempts to appropriate all the meat. The person gets to carry the meat to the top of a tree and helps the trickster (or trickster's child) to get there too to share their meal. After eating, the trickster wishes to defecate or (rare) to drink. The person points to the tip of a thin branch as a right place for doing it. The trickster climbs there, falls and dies

L72.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws small objects behind him or her which turn into mighty obstacles on the way of the pursuer

L72A.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws a comb (a brush) that turns into mighty obstacle (usually a thicket) on the way of the pursuer. (In South America the motif is probably of European origin)

L72B.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws objects that turn into mighty obstacles on the way of the pursuer. One of the thrown objects is a whetstone which turns into a mountain

L72C.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws a pair of scissors behind him or her creating an obstacle on the way of the pursuer

L72D.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws a pair of scissors behind him or her creating an obstacle on the way of the pursuer

L72E.name_eng: Pursuer goes back to take his axe
L72E.definition_eng: The pursuer cannot break with his hands obstacles created by heroes and must return home after the needed tools

L72E1.definition_eng: The pursuer uses tools to destroy obstacles created by heroes. Before he continues the chase, he is wasting time hiding these tools or carrying them back to his home because birds and animals can steal them

L72F.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws entrails or contents of the stomach of an animal creating an obstacle on the way of the pursuer

L72G.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws salt creating an obstacle on the way of the pursuer

L72H.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws a tool (fire-stone, matches, tinder) creating an obstacle on the way of the pursuer. (A flint is considered as a fire-producing tool and ignored as a hard stone that turns into mountain or rock)

L72I.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws a piece of soap creating an obstacle on the way of the pursuer (a slippery mountain, a river, etc.)

L72J.name_eng: Obstacle flight: the thrown awl (needle) turns into many awls (needles)
L72J.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws an awl or a needle which turn into many awls (needles)

L72K.name_eng: Obstacle flight: the thrown bottle with oil
L72K.definition_eng: Running away from a dangerous being, person throws a small vessel with oil. The oil turns into the lake or river. (Only North American variants are considered. In the Old World the motif is rare and is not restricted to particular region. In North America the oil to anoint the haur is probably meant in all cases).

L73.name_eng: Ogre tries to drink a river dry and bursts
L73.definition_eng: The antagonist tries to drink a river or sea and bursts

L73A.definition_eng: Fugitives create darkness behind them to trouble the pursuer (and light in front of them)

L73A1.definition_eng: Fugitive throws an object behind himself and thus creates fog or darkness in front of pursuer

L73B.name_eng: Drawing a line on the ground
L73B.definition_eng: Person draws a line on the ground creating an obstacle that the pursuer is unable to cross

L73C.name_eng: A towel opens or blocks the pass
L73C.definition_eng: Waving a piece of cloth (throwing it on the ground, putting on water, etc.) person creates obstacles (on the way of the pursuer) or a means to overcome them (bridge, dry path between waters, etc.)

L74.definition_eng: A bear or other dangerous being tears off and carries away a hand of a person and holds it at his sleeping place. Another person steals the hand, gives it back to the owner

L74A.definition_eng: An antagonist carries away the hero or rips off and carries away his limb and hangs the prisoner or the limb (usually over the fire). The hero is suffering from pain. Another personage saves the hero or brings his limb back

L75.definition_eng: One of twin brothers is evil. Being still in the womb, he does not want to be born in a normal way and bursts through his mother’s side killing her

L76.definition_eng: An ogress attacks her male victim devouring or pulling off his testicles

L77.name_eng: Girl seen as a fruit eaten up
L77.definition_eng: Person sees or smells people as delicious objects and devours them

L78.definition_eng: Mixed traits of toad and jaguar in iconography; a toad or frog transforms into a jaguar; a toad or frog is a jaguar's mother or wife

L79.definition_eng: A girl marries a powerful benevolent man. His first wife is a monster. The man kills her or is glad that she is killed by his human wife

L7A.name_eng: Sticking demon: first to person and then to animal
L7A.definition_eng: A demon who sticks to other creatures and refuses to get down sticks first to a person and then to an animal or first to an animal and then to a bird

L7B.definition_eng: Instead of chasing a person, a bush spirit, a monster or a dangerous animal follows by mistake a gourd vessel that floats downriver

L80.definition_eng: A demonic person or animal is killed but revives or can revive if a small piece of its flesh or blood goes out of control

L81.definition_eng: Person sets off in search of fire and finds it in the house of a demon. The demon makes (attempts to make) harm to the person

L81A.definition_eng: Because a girl or young woman offends a cat (rare: a dog, a cock), it plays a trick that brings the girl a misfortune (usually extinguishes the fire and in search of it the girl gets to a demon)

L81A1.definition_eng: Person takes for alive coal a red bead (stone) that fell into the hearth and does not understand that the fire is extinguished

L81A2.name_eng: Demon comes to drink blood of a girl
L81A2.definition_eng: While the men of the household are not at home, a demonic person comes to drink blood of a girl or young woman or make her harm other way. Initially the men do not understand why the girl becomes thin

L81A3.definition_eng: A girl meets a demon who is disgusting and terrible. When the demon gets to see her again, he (or she) asks her what had she told about him (what had she seen). The girl answers that the demon was beautiful (clad in gold, etc.). Usually at the last meetings the girl tells the demon truth. He is enraged and the men who hide nearby kill him

L81B.definition_eng: Hero’s companions cut off his legs and abandon him (usually they put a sword in front of his tent and when the hero runs out in a hurry, he is wounded by the blade)

L81C.definition_eng: A man whose feet were cut off lives with two others, one of whom lost his hands and another eyes (or with one of them). Acting in cooperation, they become health again

L81D.name_eng: Two cripples fight and become healthy
L81D.definition_eng: Two cripples with different injuries quarrel and fight after overcoming a demon that makes them unexpectedly healthy

L82.definition_eng: Intentionally or not, a man burns his foot or his whole body in a fire, then turns into demon

L83.definition_eng: A rolling head or a man who has burned off his foot turns into or produces thunder or lightning

L84.definition_eng: Bush spirits and the like try to cut down a tree. The attempt fails because their axes are good for nothing being made of turtle shells, clay, etc.

L85.definition_eng: One-sided people have one leg and/or also one arm, one half of a head, etc. The second leg is not cut or burned off, preserved as a stump but is absent completely
