M204.definition_eng: When a deity (powerful person) attempts to pass some money to a certain man, he either gets it or not thanks to his fate while all other factors play no role

M204A.name_eng: One does not see money because he closes his eyes
M204A.definition_eng: Money is intentionally thrown in front of a man to be used by him. At this moment he closes his eyes and passes by

M205.name_eng: Birds set a city on fire
M205.definition_eng: Warriors lay siege to a city or palace. They catch or receive as a tribute the birds that live there, oil them or tie combustibles (tinder, wood chips, nutshells filled with pitch, etc.) to their bodies and sets them on fire. When released, the birds fly back to the city or palace. The fire starts there and the warriors achieve their objective

M206.definition_eng: A guard (courtier) agrees to open a man an access to a powerful person after a promise to share with him the expected reward. The man asks to be bitten (from the very beginning expected the punishment)

M207.definition_eng: A poor married couple (a poor man) bemoans life’s harshness and blame Adam and Eve who through their disobedience and curiosity brought sin into the world. A powerful person hears their complaint and put them into the place where they can live in luxury. He stipulates only that they must not break certain taboo (usually to open a covered vessel). They break taboo and are returned to their old way of life

M21.definition_eng: The protagonist pursued by an enemy comes across a person, an animal or an object to help him and receives help

M21A.name_eng: Zoomorphic protector hides fugitives on/in his body
M21A.definition_eng: Person is pursued by an enemy. A bird or animal hides him or her in its mouth, on its body (e.g. under a wing) or swallows him or her

M21B.name_eng: Every deception is the beginning of the next one
M21B.definition_eng: One animal person makes harm to others in such a way that every of his victims is used to injure the next one

M22.definition_eng: A long-necked bird living near water (stork, heron, bittern, swan) saves person from dangerous pursuer

M22A.definition_eng: A long-necked bird living near water (stork, heron, swan) is a guard in a strange house or land where hero comes

M23.definition_eng: Person or creature pretends to be afraid of a particular sort of treatment that really cannot do him any harm

M23A.definition_eng: A turtle explains that before to be eaten he has to be soaked in water in order to soften his shell. When he gets into water, he swims away

M24.definition_eng: Turtle goes to war and/or is captured by enemies

M24A.definition_eng: Turtle goes to war, kills people (usually a woman), is caught and killed but continues to live in its animal guise

M25.definition_eng: To take part in a feast or to visit God or celestial object, person ascends to the sky. To return, he either uses a rope but falls before reaching ground or jumps (falls) down from the sky and is badly hurt, dead, and/or transformed

M26.name_eng: Ducks rise hunter into the air (he caught them by leg)
M26.definition_eng: Person attempts to hunt ducks or geese catching them by the legs. They rise him into the air, he falls down

M26A.name_eng: Ducks rise hunter into the air (threaded on a string)
M26A.definition_eng: Person catches birds by tying a bait to a string which they swallow and become tied one after another to the same string; or he immobilizes many birds with one bullet; or gives them liquor and ties to a string. Usually the birds all fly up at once and lift the man up in the air

M27.definition_eng: A tree or a chain of reeds by which people have ascended to the sky is destroyed. On their way back they fall to the ground. Some of them remain in the sky for ever or longer than others

M28.name_eng: Icarus (failed attempt to fly on artificial wings)
M28.definition_eng: Acquiring possibility to fly, person ultimately falls to the ground or remains in a faraway place being unable to fly any more

M29A.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is raven

M29A1.definition_eng: In three or more different episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is raven (crow)

M29B.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is fox, jackal or coyote

M29B1.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the wolf suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29B2.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity or unsocial behavior, the bear suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29B3.name_eng: The fox (jackal, coyote) is a failure
M29B3.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the fox, jackal or coyote suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29C.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is Canada jay

M29D.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is mink

M29E.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is skunk

M29F.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the wolverine suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29G.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is hare or rabbit

M29G1.name_eng: Hare or rabbit as the main trickster
M29G1.definition_eng: In most of the episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is hare or rabbit. Not considered are traditions in which 1) trickster hare/rabbit is rare while other trickster (usually fox/jackal/coyote) typical; 2) Mesoamerican traditions in which episodes with trickster rabbit are not many and could be borrowed in post-Columbian time being of African origin

M29G2.name_eng: A crab wins thanks to his smartness
M29G2.definition_eng: Being smart and witty, the crab overcomes strong adversaries

M29GG.name_eng: The hedgehog wins thanks to his smartness
M29GG.definition_eng: Being smart and witty, the hedgehog overcomes overcomes strong adversaries

M29H.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is owl

M29I.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is hawk

M29J.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a water bird

M29K.name_eng: The turtle (tortoise, toad, frog) wins thanks to his smartness
M29K.definition_eng: Being smart and persistent, the turtle (toad, frog) overcomes strong adversaries

M29K1 NOT USED IN STATISTICS.name_eng: The turtle (toad, frog) is a tricky failure
M29K1 NOT USED IN STATISTICS.definition_eng: A turtle (tortoise, toad, frog) behaves foolishly creating serious problems for himself

M29L.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is an opossum

M29M.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a rat

M29N.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a mouse

M29NN.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a ground squirrel (Xerux sp.)

M29O.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a monkey

M29O1.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the monkey suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29P.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a spider

M29Q.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a racoon

M29QQ.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is an anteater

M29R.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a porcupine

M29V.name_eng: The duiker (mouse-deer) wins thanks to his smartness
M29V.definition_eng: Being smart and witty, a small ungulate overcomes strong adversaries. The hero is a duiker, a mouse-deer or other small even-toed ungulates that are not very close biologically but look similar. In some publications on African folklore it is difficult to say what species is meant in particular case

M29W.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the jaguar (ocelote, puma) suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29W1.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the leopard (panther) suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29W2.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the tiger suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29W3.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the lion suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29X.definition_eng: Because of its stupidity and unsocial behavior, the hyena suffers a reverse, is injured or dies

M29X1.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a badger

M29Y.definition_eng: In episodes related to deception, absurd, obscene or anti-social behavior the protagonist is a wren

M29Z.definition_eng: Person named as the Beardless (Kusa, Kesa, Kose, Kysa, Kusu, etc.) acts in narratives

M29Z1.definition_eng: A bald person acts in narratives (thence his usual name: Taz, Tazchi, Kal, Keloglan, Kechal etc.)

M29Z2.name_eng: The Gipsy wins thanks to his smartness
M29Z2.definition_eng: Being smart and witty, the Gipsy overcomes strong adversaries

M29Z3.name_eng: The Gipsy is an enemy or a failure
M29Z3.definition_eng: The Gipsy (more often a female than a male) is an enemy overcome by the hero (heroine) or (rare) a weak failure

M3.definition_eng: Person crosses a water or air space along the chain of many animals, birds or fish

M30.definition_eng: Person or creature who has no wings or is unable to fly on a long distance attempts to ascend to the sky or to fly far away but falls down or, deprived of his wings, remains in a place from which he is unable to return

M30A.definition_eng: Trickster who flies over a village falls to the ground. They bind him and defecate on him

M30B.name_eng: Birds give and take back their feathers
M30B.definition_eng: Birds first give their feathers to a certain person to make him be able to fly or to make him beautiful and then take them back

M30C.name_eng: Flying person falls down after breaking taboo
M30C.definition_eng: Person flies across the air but falls down when, despite warning, looks down to earth, flies above villages, becomes to talk, etc.

M30D.name_eng: The tortoise lets itself be carried by birds
M30D.definition_eng: An animal (usually a tortoise) is carried up into the air by two birds who hold onto a stick which the tortoise holds in its mouth

M31.definition_eng: Animal person who cannot swim asks a good swimmer to carry him. The latter agrees only to throw his rider into the water

M32.definition_eng: Food or liquid that person swallows are immediately pouring out from his bottom part

M32A.name_eng: Eating pieces of flesh that fall out
M32A.definition_eng: Person's intestines or pieces of flesh from his bottom part fall out. He eats them up taking for a good meat or fat

M33.definition_eng: Person himself or somebody else stitches up or firmly stops his anus (with wax, clay, grass, etc.)

M34.definition_eng: An object thrown into person becomes his tail and the person himself an animal

M35.definition_eng: Two animal persons compete to see who could withstand cold all the night. At dawn one is dead

M36.name_eng: Dismantles himself to crawl through an opening
M36.definition_eng: Person is imprisoned inside a tree, stone, a ball of ice, etc. He or somebody else makes the opening but it is too narrow. The person puts himself to pieces (or turns into fog), inserts them into the opening, outside puts the pieces together again

M37.definition_eng: Person or person's head is split with the blow of an axe. Person remains (or must remain if the procedure is realized in correct way) uninjured

M38.definition_eng: Person sees how others act using magic or according to their animal nature. He or she imitates their actions and gets into trouble. Actions are not heroic deeds, competitions or tests and refer to everyday activity, mostly to providing and cooking food

M38A.definition_eng: Being on a visit to other people or (more often) animals, an (animal)-person sees them act using magic or according to their animal nature. Back at home, he imitates their actions and gets in trouble. Actions are not heroic deeds, competitions or tests and mostly refer to providing and cooking food

M38A1.definition_eng: Person imitates actions of his son- or brothers-in-law or (among Comox and Halcomelem) of his wives

M38A2.definition_eng: The hen (other bird) cooks her own eggs and serves them to other animal persons (who imitated her with disastrous consequences)

M38B.name_eng: Stupid wives imitate magic one (the daughter of the Sun)
M38B.definition_eng: The first and rejected or taken later wife acts using magic. Other wives try to imitate her but perish are maimed or disgraced

M38B1.name_eng: Young wife is mute until her husband pronounces particular words
M38B1.definition_eng: After the wedding a wife does not speak with her husband until he says particular words related to her origin (the name of her adoptive father, her own name that reveals her superhuman nature, and the like)

M38B2.name_eng: Three daughters-in-law at the king's banquet
M38B2.definition_eng: In the feasting hall, the heroine who has magic capacities throws food around (puts it under her bodice, etc.) but arouses admiration among the guests. Other women try to imitate her but only make the room and themselves look unsightly

M38C.definition_eng: A blacksmith is (seems to be) able make people young, cure maimed people and animals

M38C1.name_eng: Old people forged into young ones: unhappy imitation
M38C1.definition_eng: Person changes (forges, boils, cuts into pieces and joins them back) old (sick, dead) people into the young (healthy, alive) ones or pretends to do so. Another one unsuccessfully tries to imitate him

M38C2.name_eng: Cuts the horse’ leg off to iron it
M38C2.definition_eng: To iron a horse or a donkey, Jesus (a saint) cuts its leg off, irons it and puts the leg back, the horse is not injured. Another person imitates him with no success

M38C3.definition_eng: A conceited smith attempts to rejuvenate an old woman (man). His magic helper tries to save the victim but all that he do is to transform the woman into an animal, usually a monkey

M38D.name_eng: Animated objects perish one after another
M38D.definition_eng: Two or several animated objects or small animals and live or travel together and perish one after another when they make the most simple acts

M38D1.definition_eng: Persons whose body parts are obviously vulnerable (head like a bladder, neck like a hair, leg like a straw, etc.) attempt to behave normal people and perish one after the other.

M38D2.name_eng: The bean, the straw and the coal
M38D2.definition_eng: Several (usually three) small animated objects travel but fail to cross a river (usually perish attempting to cross it)

M38D3.definition_eng: An animated object who is a clod of earth (flour, salt) melts away when he gets wet under the rain or going to fetch water

M38D4.definition_eng: Several persons who are the embodiments if small artifacts (and a squirrel with them) are travelling. A needle penetrates into the body of a big animal and kills it. (In the beginning of the Baltic Finnish versions the needle finds objects which its companions consider worthless but after the killing of the animal they prove to be useful for cooking the meat)

M38D5.name_eng: The grains talk with one another
M38D5.definition_eng: Two or three different grains talk with one another, act together, etc.

M38D6.definition_eng: Several characters who are the embodiments of small objects die one after another. The last of them laughs so much that he bursts (breaks his head, etc.)

M38D7.definition_eng: Person who represents something fat (a sausage, a piece of fat, etc.) prepares a rich soup adding to it its own fat. Another person tries to repeat the trick and dies

M38E.name_eng: The mushroom reviles the young oak
M38E.definition_eng: The mushroom (gourd) imagines himself to be as lasting and durable as a tree

M39A.name_eng: Fool takes off boots from animals’ legs
M39A.definition_eng: Two or three brothers live together (with their mother). One of them makes stupid actions like (all or some of them): lets free animals that got into a snare but kills his mother; cuts off the legs of domestic animals or flays them; thinks that a certain place on a head of a baby is a tumor, sucks baby's brains out; cuts a cloth into pieces and ties them to reeds of to branches of a tree; hearing a murmur of water throws food into the water; tries to build a hut not on a river bank but in the river

M39A1.definition_eng: Fool follows instructions that were reasonable in every previous episode but become absurd in every next one

M39A2.name_eng: Fool puts a needle into the hay
M39A2.definition_eng: Fool puts a small sharp object (needle, pin, nail) in a place when it is impossible later to find it (a cart-load of hay, a bag of flour. etc.)

M39A2A.name_eng: A fool buys spoons and a table
M39A2A.definition_eng: A fool buys wooden spoons and a table. He orders the table to walk because it has legs and throws the spoons away because they rattle when he is walking. Both episodes are usually found in the same story

M39A2B.definition_eng: A fool buys salt or sugar but throws them into a river to salt or to sweeten the water

M39A2C.definition_eng: Fool (or a person who pretends to be mad) sows salt (small objects) like grain

M39A2D.definition_eng: Fools plant pieces of meat, horns or bones and believe that animals will grow from them

M39A2E.definition_eng: A fool forgets his name but it comes back to his mind when he hears some word by chance

M39A3.definition_eng: Fool kills a person, throws the body into a pond or a well. His relation throws there a dead goat. Searching for the corpse in the pond, the fool asks if the killed person had horns, etc. People see that he is really crazy and do not suspect him of a crime

M39A3A.definition_eng: Fool gets to see objects that are cracked (stumps, ground, ice) and oils them with sympathy

M39A3B.definition_eng: Fool thinks that tree stumps need caps and put pots on them

M39A4.definition_eng: Fool takes his own shadow for a person who pursues him and gives it his possessions

M39A4A.name_eng: Fool’s customer is an animal or an object
M39A4A.definition_eng: A fool gives meat, a domestic animal, cloth etc. to an animal (plant, inanimate object) and thinks that the latter will pay him later or asks an animal to do some work. Claiming money or products of the work, he finds treasure

M39A4B.definition_eng: A fool (woman or man) throws valuables into the water believing that will be useful for frogs

M39A4B1.name_eng: Foolish woman throws her yarn away
M39A4B1.definition_eng: Foolish woman throws her yarn ways (into the water, into the bush) and believes that somebody with weave it

M39A4C.name_eng: Conversation of the fool with a bird
M39A4C.definition_eng: Hearing the cry of a bird (often, an owl) and thinking that the bird speaks with him, the fool eventually finds treasure

M39A4D.definition_eng: Fool sells property a lizard and believes it will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

M39A4E.definition_eng: Fool sells property to a tree (stump, pole, a cross in the countryside) and believes that it will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

M39A4F.definition_eng: Fool sells property to the statue and believes that it will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

M39A4G.definition_eng: Fool sells property to the dogs and believes that they will pay him. Trying to get his money, he finds treasure

M39A4H.name_eng: The lost camel of the king
M39A4H.definition_eng: A smart man (using a naive person) gets to acquire treasure that was on the back of a lost camel

M39A4I.definition_eng: Fool sees fontanelle on a baby’s head, takes it for abscess and squeezes off. The baby becomes silent, the fool thinks that he fell asleep

M39A5.name_eng: Fool kills goats for eating pears
M39A5.definition_eng: Fool brings his goats to a fruit tree and kills them when they become to eat fruits that he has thrown down from the tree

M39A5A.definition_eng: Because telling the truth a stupid son (wife, husband)) can bring misfortune upon the family, his mother (wife; her husband) mystifies him (her) making him or her describe events that are definitely impossible. People take him (her) for a fool and let alone.

M39A5A1.definition_eng: Husband (mother) understands that his stupid wife (her son) can report about certain deeds of the family members and inflict a severe punishment. The fool is put into a hole (barrel, etc.), covered with a skin and the domestic fowl is let to pick up the grain above it. The fool takes the knocking for the attack of the birds, the rain of stones, etc. See motif m39a5a A woman plants fish in the field where her husband is sure to plow them up. He finds them and believes that the fish got there by itself. People take him for mad.

M39A5A2.definition_eng: Husband found a treasure. He knows that his talkative wife will not keep a secret and tells her that during this time the judge (king, etc.) got his face injured (usually lost his eye) because of a hail (because of hot soup pouring from the sky). The wife repeats this story before the judge who becomes angry and drives her out. The treasure remains in the family

M39A5A3.definition_eng: A man understands that if his wife let out the truth, it would bring them trouble. He tells her that sounds that she hears are screams of the landlord (official, etc.) because devils (or somebody else) beat him (carry him to the hell, etc.). Being summoned to the official, she repeats what her husband had told her and considered mad

M39A5B.definition_eng: A woman plants fish in the field where her husband is sure to plow them up. He finds them and believes that the fish got there by itself. People take him for mad.

M39A6.name_eng: Misunderstood instructions: to cut a road
M39A6.definition_eng: A wayfarer asks his companion in an allegorical for to tell a story. The companion takes his words in the direct sense and acts stupidly or thinks that his companion is a fool

M39A6A.name_eng: Clever daughter-in-law of the imprisoned khan
M39A6A.definition_eng: After an extensive search powerful man finds a smart wife for his son. Being caught by his enemies he sends some a message to his daughter-in-law, the messengers being chosen among the enemies. The young woman understands the real meaning of the received text, destroys the enemies and releases her father-in-law. (In Malagasy version the youngest wife is insyead of the daughter-in-law)

M39A6A1.name_eng: The harvest is eaten up? The corpse is alive?
M39A6A1.definition_eng: One man asks another if the grain that they see is already eaten up? Is the dead body alive? It becomes clear that his questions have sense

M39A6B.name_eng: A leaned tower and the builder’s daughter-in-law
M39A6B.definition_eng: A master builder gets to know that the king is going to kill or maim him. He asks to send a messenger to his home to bring an ostensibly forgotten tool or something else. His daughter-in-law understands the real meaning of the message, takes the messenger as a prisoner and saves her father-in-law

M39A6C.definition_eng: A poor girl agrees to marry a prince only if he learns some craft. He does it, marries the girl and then gets into hands of some criminals. He promises them to produce valuable object that they can sell for good money. His wife or (rare) his father recognize his work (or read signs of the object). He is released, the criminals killed

M39A6D.definition_eng: A person sends to his or her kinsmen or spouse through other persons a text or an object. Only the receiver understands the real meaning of words or of the object, saves the sender and/or destroys his enemies

M39A6F.name_eng: To sell a sheep and to bring the sheep and the money
M39A6F.definition_eng: Father tells his son to sell a sheep (goat) and to bring back both the sheep and the money. Usually a girl teaches the boy to sell the wool

M39A6G.name_eng: Four coins (The sharing of bread and money)
M39A6G.definition_eng: Man explains that one part of his incomes he puts out at interest while another part is used to pay debts, i.e. he cares for his children and keeps up his parents

M39A6H.definition_eng: King asks a commoner to pluck (skin, milk, cut) a goose (geese, other birds, animals) that he sends him. The commoner understands correctly that he is allowed to fleece a courtier

M39A6I.definition_eng: Person asks a servant to bring another some food or object and to pass certain words which for the servant have no meaning. Hearing these words, the recipient understands that the servant had appropriated part of what he had to bring

M39A6J.definition_eng: A girl mildly (allegorically) reproaches the person who suddenly entered the house or expresses her regret for having no dog to warn about the coming guest

M39A7.name_eng: Misunderstood instructions: to wash with the boiling water
M39A7.definition_eng: A fool is told to wash an old person with a warm water. He uses a boiling water killing the person

M39A8.name_eng: A fool carries a door on his back
M39A8.definition_eng: A fool or a buffoon takes the door of the house and carries it on his back

M39A8A.name_eng: Fool drops an object from a tree
M39A8A.definition_eng: A person (often a fool or buffoon) drops a (heavy) object from a tree or says something. Those who are under the tree (usually robbers or demons) are frightened and run away abandoning their goods and valuables

M39A8B.name_eng: The cut off tongue of a robber
M39A8B.definition_eng: Using a stratagem, someone who hides in a tree cuts (bits) off the tongue of a dangerous person and the latter is unable to describe situation to his partners

M39A9.definition_eng: One person asks another to cook a soup with parsley and onions. The latter understands (pretends to understand) that he must cook a child or a dog whose names sound similarly

M39B.definition_eng: Person does not put attention in which direction his canoe goes. As a result he returns to his own dwelling and attacks its inhabitants killing his own kin

M39B1.definition_eng: Persons sitting in a canoe paddle in opposite directions and the canoe does not move

M39C.name_eng: Pumpkin sold as a donkey’s egg
M39C.definition_eng: A numskull finds or buys an unknown fruit (pumpkin, melon, etc.). He mistakes it for an egg of a donkey (mare. camel, etc.). When he drops it or throws it off he scares a hidden hare (rabbit, fox, mouse, etc.). The fool thinks the fugitive is a young animal hatched from the egg

M39D.definition_eng: In succession and unintentionally a man causes a series of accedents. The injured parties bring him before a judge. In each case the judge makes decisions that are formally logical but patently unacceptable and saves the man

M39E.definition_eng: Asking about minor details of the case, a judge demonstrates that the plaintiff (or the defendant) lies because he does (not) know about them

M39E1.name_eng: The eaten up iron and the kidnapped child
M39E1.definition_eng: A man steals money or property. The owner gets his property back after he or his helper puts the theft in such a position when the best choice for him becomes to return what he has stolen (usually the first man kidnaps a child of the second one)

M39E1A.definition_eng: Person claims that iron or gold disappeared being eaten by mice

M39E2.definition_eng: Two men hide a treasure together but one of them steals it and accuses another. He suggests the judge to interview the tree and asks his father to hide in the hollow of the tree and to tell that another man is the thief. When the tree is ordered to be burned and the old man cries, the real thief is exposed

M39F.name_eng: He had a hat, had he a head?
M39F.definition_eng: A fool loses his head (usually bitten off by a bear). His wife or companions cannot say had he his head before but remember that he certainly had a hat (beard)

M39G.name_eng: Girl bewails the loss of her child before she has any (Clever Elsie)
M39G.definition_eng: Girl bewails the loss of her future child before she has any; thinking about an event that could have been tragic; is jealous of her sisters before any of them have fiancée; thinks out the name of her child that does not exist instead of coming to meet her fiancée.

M39G1.definition_eng: A fool does not know how to pull on his breeches (boots) and jumps down into them from a high place

M39G2.definition_eng: Numskulls try to shovel nuts with a pitchfork. F stranger shows them how to do this work more easily with a shovel (a basket)

M39H.name_eng: Husband pretends to become blind (The faithless wife)
M39H.definition_eng: A married woman is eager to get rid of her husband and usually asks a spirit (God, saint, etc.) to make him blind. The husband hides in a tree, behind the alter, etc. and usually tells her that good food will make her husnad blind, or the husband himself tells his wife that the good food is dangerous for him. He pretends to become blind, kills the love (and his wife)

M39I.name_eng: The treasure of the hanging man
M39I.definition_eng: When he spends his entire fortune, a man is going to hang himself but finds treasure (intentionally put in the corresponding place by his father)

M3A.definition_eng: Animal who does not swim well suggests animals who live in water to count their number. For this, they should make a chain and he would run along it. It is but a trick to cross a body of water

M3B.definition_eng: Another animal tries to catch the hare but only tears (cuts) off its tail. Since then it is short

M4.definition_eng: Crossing a body of water or descending a tree, person steps on an certain part of a body of an animal or on a certain animal that have made a chain (usually despite warning that he should not do it) and falls down or drowns as a result

M40.definition_eng: Person is sent to receive something of relatively low value. He asks to give him quite different object (to provide a service) and asks one who had sent him to confirm the demand. Usually a person or animal comes to a wife or a son of a powerful one and tells her or him that her (his) husband or father tells to give him food, to make love to him, to marry him, etc.

M41.definition_eng: Person plays throwing his eyes or (Alaska Athabascans) his tooth up or away. Eyes or tooth first come back to eye sockets or mouth but eventually are lost

M42.name_eng: Eyes: taken out of orbits and lost
M42.definition_eng: Person loses his eyes because of his playfulness or negligence. He makes new eyes of some substance or/and takes eyes of another person

M42A.definition_eng: Person (usually after losing his own eyes), makes new eyes of berries and is able to see again

M42B.definition_eng: Person loses his eyes, makes new ones of gum and is able to see again (though usually not well)

M42C.name_eng: Animal person eats his own marrow
M42C.definition_eng: Breaking or cutting his leg, animal person becomes to eat his own bone marrow

M43.definition_eng: To kill or catch a monster, human figure of wood or clay or alive woman is exposed as a bait. Usually monster's claws or sharp leg get stuck in the wood

M44A.name_eng: Thieves of food: the first people
M44A.definition_eng: Person discovers that somebody steals game or fish from his trap or devastates his garden. He or his guards catch the thieves who prove to be the first humans beings or the first men

M44B.definition_eng: Person discovers that somebody steals game or fish from his trap or devastates his garden. He or his guards catch the thieves who prove to be (the first) women or the thief is the water being whom the hero lets go after receiving a woman for ransom

M44C.name_eng: Thieves of food: a young hero
M44C.definition_eng: A boy or young man comes to steal food of a person who is elder than he. Usually he is caught but not punished and invited to live with the elder person

M45.name_eng: A predator tricks animals to gather around him
M45.definition_eng: An ogre or a stronger animal catches a man or a weaker animal or drives him into a small enclosure. He goes away for a while leaving a watchman. The watchman is unable to fulfill his duty and the man (the weak animal) escapes (usually he dupes the watchman). Most, though hardly all American cases can have post-Columbian African origin

M45A.definition_eng: A man falls asleep or pretends to be sleeping or dead. Animals take him for dead: mourn, carry to bury, are going to eat up, etc. The man kills a lot of animals or obtain valuables otherwise

M45B.name_eng: An old man carrying a kneading trough
M45B.definition_eng: An old man goes through the forest, lies down to rest, and draws a trough over himself. Animals admire the fine little table and bring food. Then the man moves, the animals run away and the man gets all their food

M45C.definition_eng: Person gives advice that the right way to plant seeds or tubers is to cook them before

M46.definition_eng: Planning to get or to return valuables, person turns into baby or in a small objects that has power to impregnate a woman. The picked up or the born baby steals the valuables and acquires his real guise (including cases according to which the girl herself is the desired valuable)

M46A.name_eng: A stratagem: the picked up baby
M46A.definition_eng: Person turns into baby, is picked up by the owner of valuables, steals the valuables or makes love to a woman. The baby is not a demonic creature and does not plan to kill those who picked him up (cf. motif L60)

M46B.name_eng: A stratagem: baby born by woman
M46B.definition_eng: Person turns into tiny object or creature. Touching or swallowing it, the woman conceives and gives birth to a baby-boy. The boy steals valuables or make love to the woman

M46C.definition_eng: Person turns into conifer-needle, a tiny particle, a small insect. Swallowing it by chance, the woman becomes pregnant and gives birth to a boy

M46D.definition_eng: A small child cries and becomes satisfied only when he gets a particular object to play with. This object is of high value and is hidden in the house. As soon as the object is given to him, the child or a person related to him carry it away

M46E.definition_eng: They (promise to) give a child the Sun (and or the Moon) to play with

M47.definition_eng: Punishing a person or animal or restoring his or its body after its disin­teg­ration, a powerful being intentionally or by chance puts head to bottoms

M48.definition_eng: Trickster asks an animal to transform him but breaks condition of transformation and acquires his original guise. Usually he asks a big horned animal (buffalo, elk) to turn him into buffalo (elk) too. Animal charges, trickster is scared. Next time he remains on the place, turns into buffalo but trying to transform the same way another person, turns back into his own self

M49.name_eng: Man in a skin of another
M49.definition_eng: Hero comes across a (animal-)person from an enemy group and takes his or her appearance, usually dressing himself in a skin of his victim; after this he penetrates the enemy camp

M49A.definition_eng: The hero has to come unrecognized to the meeting place of his enemies. He meets an old woman (usually a shaman, a medicine-woman) who goes there, puts on her skin and acquires her appearance

M5.definition_eng: Being in a situation when his life depends on a good will of a demon or animal, person either resists or does not resist the temptation to insult or to beat, bite, etc. the latter

M50.definition_eng: A man tries to join a group of persons who are or become stars (usually the Pleiades) but suffers a reverse; or he pursues the stars to have sexual contact or to be reintegrated with members of his family

M51.definition_eng: One of two animal-persons kills game. In the absence of the stronger one, the weaker one hides the meat to eat it alone later

M52.definition_eng: A small animal (not a predator) or a weak person kills a big game. He asks another (animal-)person to skin or butcher the carcass. The latter is willing but takes or tries to take all the meat for himself

M53.definition_eng: Person invites birds or animals (usually geese and ducks) to dance or stand around him and concentrate their attention on some activity (usually to dance with their eyes shut), kills them, usually one by one. Or (rare) he dances himself with his eyes shut and then kills water fowl who gather around him

M53A.definition_eng: Raven tricks seals or other water mammals to gather around him and kills them by deception

M53B.definition_eng: Trickster pretends to have songs in his bag

M53C.definition_eng: Trickster suggests water fowl to dance around him with their eyes shut, kills them one by one. He warns that eyes of a bird who would open them become red. In some versions, the bird who opened its eyes got them really red

M53D.definition_eng: Person creates figures that look like enemies or pretends that enemies come. People run away, person gets all valuables for himself

M53E.definition_eng: Person (always a raven) kills a whale. When people come, he tells them about some circumstances that can make the meat dangerous. People do not dare to touch the meat and the deceiver eats it alone

M53F.name_eng: Disguised trickster eats up all the food
M53F.definition_eng: Taking part in storing up food, person pretends to go away for some reason, returns disguised as a monster or predator, people are scared and run away, the deceiver eats up all the food but is ultimately unmasked

M54.name_eng: Runway awakes in the same house
M54.definition_eng: A man runs away from the house of powerful person but in the morning awakens in the same house again

M55.definition_eng: A man or a weaker animal leads the stronger one to a place that is allegedly dangerous (hot coals, ashes, sticks, etc. can fall there at night). When his companion is asleep, man throws sticks, sprinkles hot ashes or coals on him pretending that they fall on them both

M56A.definition_eng: A man or an animal beats alligator but it remains unharmed and says that he would be killed if stricken in one special place on his body. The next time the same person strikes alligator this way and kills it

M56B.definition_eng: A weak person's demand will be granted if he brings a skin (paw, tears, etc.) of animals stronger than he. He fulfills the task using tricks (but usually does not receive the promised reward)

M56C.definition_eng: Person promises to bring a snake. The snake agrees to let him measure it. He ties the snake to a measuring stick or during the measuring finds a vulnerable place on the snake’s body

M56D.definition_eng: Person promises to fill container with small flying creatures which are alive. When he expresses his doubts that the creatures are numerous enough to fill the container, they fly in and he closes the lid

M57A.definition_eng: Instead of common body discharges a man or a woman urinates, spits, etc. beads, flowers, gold and other valuables; valuables are produced by the very presence of particular person

M57A1.name_eng: Flowers blossom where she puts her feet
M57A1.definition_eng: Where the beautiful woman steps, treasure appears, flowers blossom, etc.

M57A2.name_eng: Male person is the producer of valuables
M57A2.definition_eng: Instead of common body discharges a a man urinates, spits, etc. beads, flowers, gold and other valuables; valuables are produced by the very presence of particular male person. See motif m57a

M57A3.name_eng: Female person is the producer of valuables
M57A3.definition_eng: Instead of common body discharges a a woman urinates, spits, etc. beads, flowers, gold and other valuables; valuables are produced by the very presence of particular female person. See motif m57a

M57B.name_eng: Sweat of the Sun and tears of the Moon
M57B.definition_eng: Beads or metals are discharged by bodies of deities

M57C.definition_eng: An animal (ass, cow, horse, goat, bear, leopard) extracts gold or food from its body or person makes others believe that it is so

M57C1.definition_eng: A man enters into a fight with a bear or (among the Malayali) leopard and makes another person believe that this animal defecates gold

M57D.definition_eng: Person gets one by one magic objects that bring food or treasure. Other people replace them with common objects or take them away by force. The person takes his property back (usually beating the thieves with magic cudgel or whip)

M57D1.name_eng: Bird presents objects and fulfills wishes
M57D1.definition_eng: A bird gives a man several magic objects in succession (or one object which helps to get others) or fulfills in succession a series of his wishes

M57D2.definition_eng: When a man is going to fell a tree, the tree itself or the being who lives in (on) it asks him not to do it and grants the man’s wishes

M57D3.definition_eng: Wind person grants a wish to a man

M57D4.definition_eng: Frost grants a wish to a person

M57D5.name_eng: Ghosts are afraid to be eaten
M57D5.definition_eng: On his way, a man takes a rest and ponders over the units of food to be eaten now: one, two, three etc. Ghosts (snakes, fairies) who live nearby mistake his words for intention to eat them and bribe him giving him magic objects

M58.name_eng: Plant or trail saves from fire
M58.definition_eng: World is ablaze, fire pursues a person. Some objects or elements do not resist the heat and cannot hide him. The last named gives protection. Earth becomes cool, person continues his travel

M59.definition_eng: A small animal asks bigger one to bring him across the stream, rejects one by one all possible places to sit; finds the position that lets him kill the big animal after crossing the stream

M59A.definition_eng: Porcupine asks other animal to ferry him across river, rejects different places to sit, occupies a place where he can easily kill the animal after crossing the river and really kills him

M5A.definition_eng: Small animals ride a canoe, it sinks, all try to save their lives in their own way

M5B.definition_eng: An animal (often the rat) who cannot swim well is brought to the shore by another one but pays him with ingratitude

M5C.definition_eng: The octopus or star-fish was covered with hair but the rat had eaten it up

M5D.definition_eng: The squirrel and the creeping fish are smart and get medicines for each other

M6.definition_eng: A young man or girl spends night in the forest. The forest partridge (Tinamus sp.) provides him or her a fire, a shelter and/or a hammock but takes them away and flies away itself when the person does something wrong

M60.definition_eng: Hero wounds dangerous enemy (a monster, a robber) and then, in guise of a doctor, comes to him and kills his patient instead of curing him

M60A.name_eng: A hunter comes to one whom he wounded
M60A.definition_eng: An animal or a supernatural creature is wounded but escapes. Local doctors are helpless. The hero or his companion, masked as a doctor, comes to the wounded one and either cures or kills him.

M60A1.definition_eng: To come unnoticed to his adversaries, the hero takes the guise of a servant (usually a herdsman) and before that gets know from the real herdsman how to act and to speak with his masters (usually what should be said to ferry the cattle across a river)

M60A2.definition_eng: A servant has to lick soles or a wound of his master or mistress. The hero comes disguised as the servant and instead of licking the soles rubs them (rubs the wound) with a cut off animal tongue

M60A3.name_eng: Sham doctor: punishment of a scoundrel
M60A3.definition_eng: When a scoundrel takes away person’s property (it is a domestic animal or bird), the person comes to him under different guise (a girl, a doctor, etc.) and treats him cruelly

M60B.name_eng: False doctor: a finished off victim
M60B.definition_eng: The deceiver who promised to cure a sick or wounded person or animal devours him or suggests a remedy that makes the sick one to feel ever worse

M60B1.name_eng: The crow eats up the fish
M60B1.definition_eng: The crow promises to cure a sick fish but easts her up

M61A.definition_eng: To obtain valuables person provokes a quarrel between their owners. When the owners become to fight with each other, the valuables fall out

M61A1.name_eng: Person provokes a quarrel between two birds
M61A1.definition_eng: To provoke a quarrel between a gull and another bird, person (always a raven) tells each one that the other was insulting him

M61A2.name_eng: Person provokes a quarrel between two stones
M61A2.definition_eng: To provoke a quarrel between two different stones, person (always a raven) tells each one that the other was insulting him

M61A3.name_eng: Person provokes a quarrel between two fish
M61A3.definition_eng: To provoke a quarrel between two different fish, person tells each one that the other was insulting him

M62A.name_eng: Quarrel provoked by action [not in correlation table]
M62A.definition_eng: Hero imperceptibly causes detriment to two persons or creatures. They accuse each other and fight

M62B.name_eng: Trying to hit the hero hit each other
M62B.definition_eng: Two or more personages direct their weapons against the hero who is between them but hit each other

M62C.definition_eng: A weak animal-person agrees separately with two strong ones to pull a rope with him. They do not know that are engaged into tug-of-war with each other or that the rope is tied to a tree. (In New World motif borrowed from Afroamericans)

M62D.definition_eng: Trickster puts on a rotten hide of an animal and, being unrecognized, pretends to be victim of hare’s magic. Animals are frightened and decide not to pay the hare back for his tricks

M62E.definition_eng: A weak person makes a separate agreement with two strong ones to cultivate a field. The strong ones do not know about each other, and ultimately the weak one takes all the harvest himself.

M62F.name_eng: Every next assistant kills previous one
M62F.definition_eng: Person invites others to help him in his work. Every next one is stronger than the one who came before and eats him up, the last two perish when they begin to fight

M63.definition_eng: Before finding a part of the body that is the best for some particular function, other parts are proven or enumerated

M64.definition_eng: To get valuables (food, fire) concealed by their owner, person pretends that the valuables are already in his possession

M65.definition_eng: Trickster cooks meat that he got by deception but is unexpectedly jammed between trees or stuck to a stone. An animal (usually fox, wolf or coyote) steals all the meat

M65A.definition_eng: Trees squeak in the wind. Trickster hears a noise, climbs up the tree and is caught between limbs

M65B.definition_eng: Person kills game (usually by deception), gets to see how thieves carry it away but is unable to intervene

M66.definition_eng: After eating certain plant, small animal, or rubbing it over his body, person suffers from itch, diarrhea, or from breaking wind

M66A.definition_eng: After eating certain food, person produces a hill of excrements that is bigger than he himself

M67.definition_eng: Imprudent trickster produces wind that carries him away

M68.definition_eng: Because of his own obstinacy, person suffers of breaking wind permanently and starves because a loud noise produced by him scaring game

M69.name_eng: Getting fast in an animal skull
M69.definition_eng: Small animals or insects dance or feast inside a big animal skull or food is there. Person inserts his head into the skull and cannot take it out for a long time

M6A.name_eng: Overnight with the fire in the forest
M6A.definition_eng: A person spends a night in the forest. One of the forest dwellers has fire. After the person does something wrong, this fire is lost

M6B.name_eng: Coming across aguti before reaching home
M6B.definition_eng: Person who lost his or her way comes across different creatures. When he or she comes to aguti (Dasyprocta), it becomes clear that the home is nearby

M7.name_eng: Hero waiting to be picked up
M7.definition_eng: Getting into the lower or upper world, to an island, a country at the horizon, etc. a man is unable to move further and waits for somebody who could bring him to his destination. Some animals, birds or celestial bodies pass by, the last one (often the Sun or the Moon) picks him up and brings to the place he is eager to go

M70.name_eng: An elder person poisons a younger one with intestinal gas
M70.definition_eng: Old person tricks a young man into smelling her or his intestinal gas

M70A.definition_eng: An old woman defecates or breaks wind over a man. He kills her inserting a cutting object into her anus or vagina

M71.definition_eng: Trickster floats down the river or falls from the height and turns into a piece of wood or into a wooden object. Somebody picks it up. Eventually, the trickster acquires his real self, usually in the host's absence

M72.definition_eng: Person puts (for different reasons) his or her hand into the anus of a tapir or other herbivorous animals and is unable to extract it back. Animal starts to run and drags the person behind him for a long time

M73.name_eng: Exchanged excrements or vomits: who is stronger
M73.definition_eng: Two (animal) persons compare their feces or vomits to know about the diet and habits of each other (who is the strongest). The weaker one gets to exchange the feces (vomits)

M73A.definition_eng: Two (animal) persons compare their feces (with different purpose). One of them gets to exchange them

M74.definition_eng: Two animals or persons compare their vomits to know about the diet and habits of each other. The weaker one gets to exchange vomits, to swallow the unusual food before, or to swallow his partner's vomits

M74A.definition_eng: An animal person pretends to be invited to be godfather or he gives names to different places along which he travels in a sledge, boat, etc. The names look strange but become understandable when other people or animals get to know that their companion has devoured all the supplies

M74AA.name_eng: Theft of food by playing godfather
M74AA.definition_eng: An animal person pretends (several times) that he has to make a visit (that he has been invited to be godfather at a baptism or invited to a funeral or wedding) but instead eats secretly food supplies

M74AB.definition_eng: Travelling in a boat or on a sledge, animal person (always the fox) steals food supplies or ruins objects and accordingly to his deeds, names different places. These names seem strange to the person’s companions (“River of broken arrows” and the like)

M74B.name_eng: Who has eaten up the fat?
M74B.definition_eng: To demonstrate that the thief who had eaten food supplies is somebody else or to declare somebody else as a victim to be eaten up, animal person smears his sleeping companion with remains of the food or body excretions (exchanges the excretions)

M74C.definition_eng: The bear (wolf) notices beautiful plumage of the woodpecker and believes that it was the fox who had painted him. He asks the fox to make him handsome too. The fox burns him alive

M74D.definition_eng: While travelling on earth, God (a saint) asks his companion to prepare a slaughtered animal (chicken). The companion secretly eats liver (heart, etc.) and explains that the animal did not have such an organ. He confesses his wrong deed when God (a saint) promises him a treasure

M74E.name_eng: To divide the cheese biting from both parts
M74E.definition_eng: Two animals ask the third one to divide a piece of food in two halves equally. The divider bites alternatively from both pieces that remain ever unequal until eats it all

M75.definition_eng: Person attracts and catches the carrion-eaters (usually some birds) and thanks to this obtains valuables retrieves valuables (fire, woman, animals, etc.)

M75A.name_eng: Revenge for falling from the sky
M75A.definition_eng: Vulture suggests person to carry him in the sky but drops to earth. The person attracts vulture to revenge on him. Or the vulture drops the person (or abandons him on a high rock) to revenge on him for his attempt to catch him

M75B.definition_eng: A man hides in a skin or carcass of a big animal. A bird carries it to its nest without knowing that the man is inside

M75B1.definition_eng: A respected man gets to know that a poor boy must inherit all his property or become a king and tries to prevent it, but the fate cannot be changed

M75B1A.definition_eng: A man (usually of high social position) learns by a prediction that a (newborn) girl will be his future wife or a girl from rich family gets to know that her future husband is a poor man. The man (the girl, something else) attempts to kill the predestined marriage partner but only wounds her or him. After the wedding it becomes clear that the prediction is fulfilled

M75B2.name_eng: Bird tries to avert predetermined marriage
M75B2.definition_eng: When a boy and a girl are still small children, a bird gets to know about their predetermined marriage. All its attempts to prevent the marriage fail

M75B3.name_eng: The Trojan Horse: victory over enemies
M75B3.definition_eng: A life-size or larger than life-size figure of a horse or a bull is demonstrated to enemies. They do not understand that this is a stratagem and carry the figure to their territory. As a result, the invasion becomes possible and the enemies are defeated

M75B4.name_eng: The Trojan Horse: gaining of the woman
M75B4.definition_eng: To gain a woman, a man hides inside a hollow figure or a carcass of a big animal (horse, bull, etc.). Person who guards the woman brings it to her. The man comes outside and becomes the woman’s lover. Or a woman hides inside the figure of the horse that is brought into the room of a man

M75C.definition_eng: A man sends another one to top of a mountain or a tree to obtain treasure for him. To go back is impossible but the man survives

M75D.definition_eng: A man bereaves vultures of their hunting weapons or amulets

M76.name_eng: Person climbs a tree, leg is cut off
M76.definition_eng: When a man climbs a tree, a woman cuts his leg off or when a woman climbs a tree, a man cuts her leg off

M77.definition_eng: While person is asleep, another smears with excrements or something that reminds excrements his or her bed or clothes. The ashamed person runs away or agrees to make what the trickster wants in exchange of his silence

M78.definition_eng: Tiny boy as small as a thumb, a pea and the like taunts people, predator animals, ogres

M78A.definition_eng: A wee boy is a transformed tail of a sheep or goat

M78B.definition_eng: A woman who is eager to have a child gives birth to a great number of tiny boys. She or her husband kill them or throw them away but one remains and helps his parents

M78C.definition_eng: A cut off finger or thumb turns into a wee boy

M78D.definition_eng: A pea (bean, grain) or a pellet of cheep’s dung turns into a tiny boy (rare: girl); a child is as small as a pea. Or his mother conceived him after eating a pea

M78E.definition_eng: An ear of an animal turns into a tiny boy or his size is compared with the size of an ear or his name is “Ear”.

M78F.definition_eng: When a woman falls asleep, the trickster (usually a tiny boy) puts animal embryo or entrails (or something that looks like this) near her to make her or other people believe that she has had a miscarriage or her own entrails have fallen out

M78G.definition_eng: When household members fall asleep, the trickster (usually a tiny boy) ties them in pairs to make a mess when they get up

M79.definition_eng: Person joins dancers but then understands that these are trees or reeds moved by the wind

M7A.definition_eng: Birds or an animals takes (animal) person into their boat but acquire their animal guise and leave him in water (when he breaks a taboo)

M7A1.name_eng: Celestial bodies move above the hero
M7A1.definition_eng: Person gets to a place from which he is unable to come out. Several (more than two) different celestial bodies rise and move near him or above him. He puts attention to them (and asks their help)

M7B.definition_eng: Person gets to a place from which he cannot come out. He asks to help him different animals (fish) who pass by or come to him and choses the last one

M7C.definition_eng: Animal person wants to be transported across a body of water or lowered down. Different animals or fish suggest their help. The person accepts the help of the last one, he was waiting for him to eat him

M8.definition_eng: Non-human persons work hard to destroy a strong and durable obstacle that blocks access to some place or object

M80.definition_eng: Person insults a partridge-like bird, kills or injures her chickens. The partridge scares him, he falls, usually into a river or lake

M81.definition_eng: A man travels and comes to two or several blind (usually old) persons

M81A.definition_eng: A man meets two blind women, makes them see, they are or become birds (geese, ducks, grouses or the like)

M81B.name_eng: Not to climb after an arrow stuck in a tree
M81B.definition_eng: Despite a warning not to do so, person climbs in a tree to get his arrow that was stuck and gets into trouble (Cf. Tree, from which an arrow is supposed to be fetched, grows up high and thus carries the arrow’s owner into the sky, Boas 2002: 662)

M81C.definition_eng: Getting to the sky or (rare) to the lower world a man comes across one or two blind persons, then returns to the earth. Usually he cures their eyes

M81D.definition_eng: A man comes across (often in the sky) one or two blind persons and cures their eyes

M81E.name_eng: Not to graze animals on the ogre's land
M81E.definition_eng: The young man takes the job of grazing animals and is warned not to cross the border of the ogre’s land. The hero ignores the warning and overcomes the ogre

M81E1.name_eng: The hero brings to the old man his stolen eyes
M81E1.definition_eng: Young man lives with an old man whose eye(s) were stolen by an ogre. The youth comes to the ogre, kills him, brings the stolen eyes and the old man gets to see again

M81E2.name_eng: Attracting persons and animals from a distance
M81E2.definition_eng: Playing a musical instrument or otherwise person is able to pull to himself other persons or animals even if they are far from him

M81F.definition_eng: A blind trickster steals from (does not return some money to) a harmless man. The injured man follows the blind man and steals his whole hoard of money. Often he robs (tricks) several blind men

M82.name_eng: Animal person ties rattles to its tail
M82.definition_eng: An animal person sees that another has something tied to his tail, wants the same tail for himself and has a trouble as a result

M82A.name_eng: Rattles tied secretly to the tail
M82A.definition_eng: One animal person inconspicuously ties rattles to the tail of another. The latter thinks that he is pursued and runs in panic

M83.definition_eng: Somebody claims that he has been born before present world came into being. His opponent claims the same, and they argue who of them is the older

M83A.definition_eng: Persons or animals argue who of them is older, some claim that they lived in such and such time, but the last one says that he remembers this day because a certain event had taken place at this time

M83B.definition_eng: Two (or more) (animal)-persons agree that whichever of them has the most wonderful dream may eat all the food. The first one tells about a feast that he participated in his dream. His companion answers that he was sure that after such a feast (after getting into the paradise, etc.) the first one would not need the food, so he has eaten it alone

M83C.definition_eng: Animals argue who of them gets drunk easier. The last one falls down because he becomes drunk as soon as somebody talks about alcohol

M84.definition_eng: Person, animal, fish or (rare) a fruit is eaten up and then revived, usually after all bones (all seeds) being put together

M84A.definition_eng: Supernatural beings kill and eat an animal and then put all the bones together (in the animal's skin). After the feast the animal becomes whole (and usually revives)

M84B.definition_eng: Butchered and eaten animal, bird or fish revives after its bones are thrown into the water

M84B1.name_eng: A journey to the land of the fish
M84B1.definition_eng: A man visits the place from there the salmons come to the human world

M84B2.definition_eng: Person preserves bones of the eaten up migratory birds (not fish or animals) and the birds revive. (Episodes with the eaten up and revived cock or goose in realistic tales not considered)

M84C.definition_eng: A man spends a night in a forest or desert where spirits live. One of them explains to the others that he has a guest (i.e. this same man) tonight

M84D.definition_eng: A man listens in conversation of trees one of which is mortally ill

M85.definition_eng: An animal person (usually a fox or a jackal) threatens to cut down a tree on which mother bird (squirrel) made its nest unless she will throw down one of her nestlings (squirrel children) or eggs. Another bird lets the mother bird know that the predator is unable to realize his threat

M86.definition_eng: Rock chases or otherwise punishes person who has offended it (usually deceived it or has taken objects that belong to Rock)

M87.definition_eng: Person enters a seemingly empty house and attempts to take certain things. Invisible beings prevent him from doing it or objects themselves hurt him

M88.definition_eng: A man joins a group of dancing women and is killed or injured as a result

M89.definition_eng: Person dies or is humiliated after some object that he or she made of wax, resin, excrements and/or took for something worthy are melted down

M89A.definition_eng: Only horned animals are invited to a feast. Hyena makes itself false horns but is disguised

M8A.name_eng: Birds peck a rock to release prisoners
M8A.definition_eng: Birds and sometimes also animals work hard to break from the outside or from the inside a rock, a tree truck, bonds, etc. to release some beings or themselves from confinement in a small enclosure or trap

M8B.name_eng: Birds break an obstacle to get water
M8B.definition_eng: Birds or (rare) animals work hard to break a rock or a cane and get water or honey concealed inside

M8C.definition_eng: Birds peck through a layer of clay, wax, pitch etc. with which person’s eyes or anus are stuck up

M8D.definition_eng: Birds work hard to peck through the substance that covers some beings' body or to reach its entrails

M9.definition_eng: Person who puts her or his head or hand into a tree hollow or (rare) other hole is stuck fast in it or falls into the hollow and dies or undergoes a metamorphosis

M90.name_eng: Snake gives a correct answer of what material the object is made
M90.definition_eng: Somebody suggests to guess what sort of material a certain object is made of or from what substance a tree has grown (what is the name of an unusual tree). Another person (usually a monster) gets to know the secret and the hero or the heroin must do what they have promised. (Usually a girl must marry this person)

M90A.name_eng: To marry a man who would give a correct answer
M90A.definition_eng: A girl is promised to a man who would know her name or whose finger would fit her ring, or who would guess a material from which certain object is made or grown. Person finds a correct answer by deception

M90A1.definition_eng: It should be guessed the nature of a big animal or its skin, the content of a box. The correct answer is that the animal is a louse (or a flea), a louse is in the box

M90A2.name_eng: From what did the plant grow?
M90A2.definition_eng: Person must guess from what substance a certain plant grew or what is its name

M90A3.definition_eng: A plant grows from a killed snake or part of snake’s body

M90A4.definition_eng: A tree which has gems or adornments instead of fruits is described; particular parts of the tree are made of different metals or precious stones

M90A5.definition_eng: Golden fruits (in rare cases only leaves) of a certain tree are mentioned in tail. Usually these are golden apples

M90A6.definition_eng: Certain apples make their owner eternally young

M90B.definition_eng: Person was wrong being sure that the Sun cannot rise from the West

M90C.definition_eng: One man promises another that he can take anything in his house if he touches i with his hand. The guest is going to take the other man’s wife but when he touches a ladder he is told to take it and go away

M91.definition_eng: Person pretends that a person (often his or her mother, spouse or lover) who recently died is alive, claims that the death of the false alive resulted from negligence of others and gets a reward

M91A.definition_eng: Person pierces a bladder with blood or red juice, simulates murder or suicide

M91B.definition_eng: Using trick, a man sells or exchanges for treasure ashes. Another person tries to sell ashes and is ridiculed

M91B1.definition_eng: A man goes to sell a skin of domestic animal and on his way, by trick or thanks to chance, gets a big sum of money. Usually coming back he explains that this was the price of the skin but when other people kill their animals they cannot sell skins for such a sum. (In India the hero sometimes pretends to sold cow meat to brahmins for whom it is forbidden)

M91C1.definition_eng: Person gets other person’s possessions by trick (or pretends to get it; usually another person is drowned instead of him) and then demonstrates his possessions (usually a herd) and explains that he had received everything at the river bottom. His enemies believe him

M91C2.definition_eng: Person is put into a bag (a cage, tied up, etc.) to be drowned, burned, etc. He pretends to be in this situation by his own will or because he refuses to marry a princess, to become a chief and the like. Another person is willing to take his place and is killed

M91C3.definition_eng: Person pretends that an animal or a bird in his possession is able to understand and deliver messages. Usually after warning his wife about the planned trick, person lets free a wild animal or bird asking it to pass a message to his wife. Seeing the same (actually another) animal or bird in his companion’s house another man buys the animal for a lot of money

M91C4.name_eng: Pot that does not need fire to cook
M91C4.definition_eng: Man takes a pot from the fire but it is still boiling or he cooks the food beforehand and tells that his pot cooks it in no time (or that his stick touching ground creates the food). Another man buys the pot (the stick)

M91C5.name_eng: The wager that sheep are hogs
M91C5.definition_eng: A man (a boy) drives his cow (or any other domestic animal of a big size) to market. A trickster who would like to buy the animal cheaply tries to convince him that it is a sheep (or any other smaller and cheaper animal). Trickster’s accomplices confirm his opinion and the man sells his cow for the price of a sheep

M91C6.definition_eng: A man pays in advance and invites his enemies to eat with him. When he turns his hat (throws it on the floor, rings a bell, and the like), they believe that the hat (bell) that the innkeeper say that the bill has been settled

M91C7.name_eng: Tell them that I have died
M91C7.definition_eng: When enemies come to deal with a man he pretends to be dead

M91D.definition_eng: Person deceives the other (giving out a corpse for alive person, accusing incent people of murder, etc.). When a shaman (almost) gets to know the truth, the trickster kills her or him and gets to avoid any punishment

M92.definition_eng: Girls stick something red to old man's eyebrows and he thinks it is a fire

M93.definition_eng: Before falling asleep, person tells his eyes (which he extracts and puts aside) or his anus to awake him in case of danger. Eyes or anus do not make an alarm or person himself does not react to it. As a result he suffers a damage

M93A.definition_eng: Person punishes the part of his body which he selected as his guard for the time of his sleep or absence (he burns his buttocks, breaks eyes)

M94.definition_eng: One person or animal suggests another to slide downhill to kill or harm him or her

M94A.definition_eng: A demonic person provokes his victims to slide downhill and kills them

M94A1.definition_eng: Being irresponsible and light-minded, animal person slides downhill and dies or gets into trouble (falls on sharp pole, into the water, etc.)

M94B.definition_eng: Person tricks another to crawl into a basket and closes it. One in a basket is killed or badly injured (usually rolled down a hill)

M94B1.definition_eng: Animal person is tricked to creep under the mill wheel, he is killed or badly injured

M95.name_eng: To bring a present for person's kin
M95.definition_eng: A weaker person asks the stronger one to take present to his or her kin and hides himself or herself in a bag. The stronger one brings the bag to the weaker one's relatives thinking that there are but some objects inside. Usually a girl deceives the ogre into carrying her sisters and then herself in a sack (chest) back to their home

M96.definition_eng: Person does not want to share his meal with his close relatives and pretending to have many guests, eats food alone

M97.name_eng: The blind is directed by trees
M97.definition_eng: Person is lost or becomes blind. He walks asking different trees their names and makes decisions according to their answers reaching ultimately his destination

M97A1.name_eng: The blind person asks trees their names to get the new eyes
M97A1.definition_eng: The blind person walks asking different trees their names till he finds one that is needed to make (receive) the new eyes

M97A2.name_eng: The blind person asks trees their names to find his was to the water
M97A2.definition_eng: The blind person walks asking different trees their names and thus finds his way to the water

M98.definition_eng: Person reckons up number of members in two enormous and alternative multitudes (alive trees and dead trees, men and women, etc.). Usually numbers prove to be equal but one member possesses the qualities of the both multitudes. Adding it to one of them, person demonstrates his case

M99.definition_eng: Person is going to exterminate birds but decides not to do thanks to a wise adviser

M99A.definition_eng: Person is going to build a palace (tower, etc.) made of bird bones

M99A1.definition_eng: Person is going to make holes in the beaks of birds (to thread them)

M9A.definition_eng: Person who sucks honey greedily from a tree hollow and/or is stuck in it turns into tree-frog

N1.name_eng: Initial formula: when Altai was but a small tussock
N1.definition_eng: Epics and folktales begin with an initial formula in which it is claimed that objects that are huge now were tiny

N10.definition_eng: A woman (rare: a man) with transparent body is described. This transparence is an evidence of the beauty

N10A.definition_eng: A woman (rare: a man) with transparent body is described: bones are seen through the skin and marrow through the bones. This transparence is an evidence of the beauty

N10B.definition_eng: A girl (rare: a youth) with transparent neck is described, food or drinks swallowed by her or him are seen. Such a neck is an evidence of the beauty

N10C.name_eng: Inner organs are seen through the body
N10C.definition_eng: Inner organs of a girl or food that she swallowed are seen through her body. This transparence is an evidence of the beauty.

N11.definition_eng: Person is eager to get a child (spouse) who would be likened to blood and snow (milk)

N12.definition_eng: A powerful person makes or orders to make for him a cloak or a mantle from human beards and/or moustaches

N13.definition_eng: Girl is associated with scissors (and boy with a knife or an axe)

N14.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller represents himself as being present at the wedding and/or feast, which were organized by characters of the tale

N15.name_eng: It ran down onto my moustache, but didn’t get into my mouth
N15.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller ate some food and/or drank some alcohol but it did not get into his mouth and/or stomach

N16.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller had a horse and/or harness of wax, ice, flax, vegetables, etc. Usually they are melt, eaten, etc.

N17.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller met characters of the tale and had clothes made of paper, glass, butter, etc.

N18.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller received food, drinks, money or other real-world objects from characters of the tale, but lost them because of a meeting with dogs or people (robbers, youths, children or his neighbor)

N19.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: one or two people who met the teller after the tale feast or were present at this party became bald and/or lame because of a hot food get on the head and/or a thrown bone or bowl

N2.name_eng: Initial formula: when a goat was a colonel
N2.definition_eng: Epics and folktales begin with an initial formula in which it is claimed that animals fulfilled social or economic roles of the people

N20.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller says that the characters attained their desires, goals and/or happiness or that God satisfied their desires

N21.definition_eng: The warrior-hero was made of dough and then became alive (his name is “The Dough”)

N22.name_eng: If they are not dead, they are still alive
N22.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller says that the characters are still alive if they are not already dead

N23.name_eng: They stayed there, and I came here
N23.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: the teller says that the characters stayed there (i.e. at the place where the action happened) or were left there by him, and that he returned home and/or came here (i.e. to the place of the performance)

N24.definition_eng: Light is seen that looks like the second Moon or the second Sun. It’s source is a beautiful woman

N25.name_eng: The length of a needle as a long distance
N25.definition_eng: It is said that tale characters have been on the road for a long time (days, weeks, months, years), but passed in the end a distance no more than a grain, needle or another small object

N26.name_eng: When wheat grew on the ice
N26.definition_eng: It is said that an action took place when cultivated plants (wheat, cotton) grew on the ice or on the salt

N27.definition_eng: Bird’s (hen’s) milk is mentioned in fairy tales, riddles and proverbs as something very rare and difficult to obtain

N27A.name_eng: You can find even bird’s milk there!
N27A.definition_eng: It is said that somewhere there is (or was) even bird’s milk

N27B.name_eng: The only thing missing is bird’s milk
N27B.definition_eng: It is said that someone is only lacking bird’s milk or that somewhere the only thing missing is bird’s milk

N27C.definition_eng: It is claimed that the bird has no milk and/or breasts

N28A.definition_eng: Roots (belt) of rocks (stones, mountains) are mentioned in myths, riddles, proverbs, charms and songs as something that does not exist

N28A1.definition_eng: Among the things that do not exist in the world, a belt of mountains is called

N28B.definition_eng: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a ladder or stairway to the sky (variant: a ladder in the sky) is mentioned

N28C.definition_eng: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a pillar of the sky is mentioned

N28D.definition_eng: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a lid or covering for the sea, ocean or river are mentioned

N28E.definition_eng: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a bridge across the sea, ocean or lake is mentioned

N28F.definition_eng: It is said that water has no boughs or twigs

N28G.definition_eng: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, a gall of horse or ass is mentioned

N28H.definition_eng: In a list of things that do not exist in the world, horns of the horse are mentioned

N28I.definition_eng: Among the things that do not exist in the world, a whisk for the sea is called

N29.name_eng: Before the water starts to boil
N29.definition_eng: The time required to perform an action or the time that has passed since the described event is estimated by comparing with the time required to boil the water and / or to cook a food

N3.definition_eng: One of the fingers says that he is hungry and/or suggests to steal something. Other fingers express their opinion on this behalf.

N30.name_eng: Crying while looking in one direction and laughing while looking in another
N30.definition_eng: The formula that describes the confusion of feelings: when a person looks in one direction, he or she cries, when in another – begins to laugh or smile; or one eye of a person laughs and another laughs; or person laughs looking at one object and weeps looking at another; or one of two persons who share the same fate laughs and another smiles, etc.

N31.definition_eng: Coming of the late fall and then winter is signaled by successive migration to the South of two or three species of birds which fly wedge-like (Zugvogel)

N32.definition_eng: It is told about an ornithomorphic person or creature that he is sitting on several (three or more) trees

N33.definition_eng: The hero presses his adversary into the ground or both of them press each other (ankle-, waist-, breast-deep and the like)

N34.definition_eng: Streams of honey and oil (oil and milk, milk and blood) instead of streams of water are mentioned as a sign of generosity and prosperity. Cf. motif K33F

N35.definition_eng: In a remote country rivers of milk have banks of kissel. It is a sign of abundance

N36.name_eng: Above the forest, below the clouds
N36.definition_eng: Tale and epic formula: a horse is galloping above trees (grass, surface of the earth) and below the sky (clouds)

N37.name_eng: Covering himself with the sky like a blanket
N37.definition_eng: It is said that a hero sleeps covering himself with the sky like a blanket

N38.definition_eng: Person asks which object (usually a key) is better: the old one (that was lost and found) or the new one. By this the marriage partner is meant (rarely this question is asked directly)

N39.definition_eng: The image of a three-ply rope is used to describe the invincibility of two close-knit friends

N4.definition_eng: Strong men have ribs grown together to form a kind of an armor or shell

N40.name_eng: The liver sank and the lungs floated away
N40.definition_eng: A fairy tale or epic text ends with the formula announcing that the liver sank and the lungs floated away (floated up, remained safe, etc.)

N5.name_eng: They recognize winter by rime, summer by rain
N5.definition_eng: Long trips, campaigns, flights or battles are described using cliché which contain expressions like “they get to know that it is winter seeing rime, that it is summer, seeing rain” and the like

N6.name_eng: Horse tells to whip him strongly
N6.definition_eng: A horse tells his rider to whip him with such force that his blood would splash out, skin would come off, flesh would be gashed to the very bone, etc. The rider follows these instructions

N7.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: three apples fell from heaven or a tree; the storyteller got at least one of them. Or it is said that somebody gives / ought to give to the storyteller one or three apples

N8.definition_eng: Closing formula of the folktale: characters put the storyteller into a cannon or rifle and made the shot or he jumped onto a cannonball that has been shot from a cannon and so arrived at the place of performance

N9.definition_eng: Two persons see a horseman who is ever nearer to them. One of the higher social position explains that what seems to be crows are clods flying from under the hooves of the horse and what seems to be snow, cloud or fog are lather dripping from the horse’ mouth or its breath
